## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

### 12.1 Evidence chain

```text
Phase 0 foundation
  → public EEG source selection and dataset-status declaration
  → source/version/license/provenance capture
  → metadata normalization and label-map fixation
  → preprocessing configuration and fit-scope registration
  → split/protocol and low-calibration budget declaration
  → trial/window generation with overlap and split lineage
  → artifact/channel-quality annotation where supported
  → schema, metadata, label, preprocessing, split, leakage, exclusion, and matched-key validation
  → DatasetRecord / WindowRecord / SplitRecord / PreprocessingRecord / LabelMapRecord / ArtifactFlagRecord
  → ValidationReport, DatasetCard, ProtocolCard, Layer1Manifest, layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json
  → downstream Phase 2–15 source-lineage, evaluation-readiness, dashboard-readiness, and claim-safety handoff
```

### 12.2 Phase-owned transformations

Phase 1 owns only transformations that make public-data source evidence standardized, versioned, split-safe, and traceable:

- source dataset registration into `DatasetRecord`;
- source metadata normalization without changing downstream evidence meaning;
- original-to-normalized label mapping into `LabelMapRecord`;
- preprocessing configuration registration into `PreprocessingRecord`;
- split membership and low-calibration budget assignment into `SplitRecord`;
- trial/window materialization into `WindowRecord`;
- artifact/channel quality annotation into `ArtifactFlagRecord` where supported;
- validation/leakage/missingness accounting into `ValidationReport` and supporting reports;
- source and protocol explanation into `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard`;
- record bundle packaging into `Layer1Manifest`;
- matched-key and ablation-readiness status into `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json`.

### 12.3 Forbidden hidden transformations

Phase 1 must not:

- tune preprocessing, labels, splits, label budgets, or exclusions using test-set outcomes;
- use downstream decoder correctness, calibration quality, IHARQ decisions, policy rewards, stress outcomes, embodiment outcomes, or dashboard preferences to modify clean source records;
- silently discard subjects, sessions, runs, trials, windows, channels, labels, or datasets;
- infer artifact cleanliness from missing artifact flags;
- promote public EEG to clinical validation, real patient-safety evidence, real deployment readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, or real stimulation-control evidence;
- treat the readiness artifact, cards, dashboards, or claim-safety audit as performance evidence.

### 12.4 Evidence-plan boundary note

Dataset-specific loader details, file-download commands, preprocessing code, function signatures, command-line runs, and debugging steps belong to a future implementation build book or execution playbook. This Execution and Evidence Plan records what evidence must be produced, validated, preserved, and handed off.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Pass condition | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schema gate | All Phase 1 records/artifacts conform to Phase 0 schemas or marked candidate schema status where unresolved | Validators pass on real Layer 1 outputs | Block promotion to validated source record |
| Source/provenance gate | Public source, source version, license/access note, dataset status, cache/mirror note where applicable | `DatasetRecord` complete enough for reproducibility and claim scope | Exclude dataset, mark optional/future, or diagnostic-only |
| Metadata completeness gate | Required dataset/subject/session/run/channel/sampling/timing metadata present or missingness documented | Completeness report contains no unresolved blocking gaps | Diagnostic-only or dataset/task exclusion |
| Label-map gate | Every included original label maps to a normalized label or documented exclusion | `LabelMapRecord` validates and includes proxy-intent note | Exclude affected label/task or mark downstream comparisons diagnostic-only |
| Preprocessing fit-scope gate | Preprocessing config hash stable; normalization/fit scope legal; no held-out test fit leakage | `PreprocessingRecord` validates | Block downstream decoder/calibration claims or rerun with new version |
| Window-generation gate | Window timing, duration, stride, overlap group, labels, preprocessing ID, split membership, and `trial_id`/`parent_trial_id` fields validate | `WindowRecord` validates | Block downstream use of affected windows or mark diagnostic-only |
| Split-disjointness gate | Train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation memberships valid and non-overlapping as required | `SplitRecord.leakage_checks_passed` true | Block evaluation claims until repaired with new split version |
| Subject/session/run leakage gate | Split level and membership do not leak subject/session/run/trial/overlap information contrary to protocol | Leakage-audit report passes | Diagnostic-only or blocked; no silent repair |
| Low-calibration budget gate | Label budgets, calibration memberships, adaptation memberships, and split roles are consistent | Budget table and `SplitRecord` validate | A0–A4 and later comparisons diagnostic-only or blocked |
| Exclusion accounting gate | Dropped/excluded datasets, subjects, sessions, runs, trials, windows, labels, or channels have reasons | Validation report lists exclusions and reasons | Downstream claims diagnostic-only or blocked if untracked |
| Artifact/channel flag gate | Artifact flags validate where available; missing flags are warning state, not clean proof | `ArtifactFlagRecord` validates where present; missingness warning emitted | Quality/artifact claims downgraded |
| Matched-key completeness gate | Required keys for A0–A13 and especially A0–A4 are present or diagnostic-only reasons logged | `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` reports readiness or explicit missing-key status | Matched comparisons diagnostic-only or blocked |
| Manifest/path/hash gate | `Layer1Manifest` paths, hashes, seeds, config files, validation status, source record IDs, and readiness path are valid | Manifest validates | Reproducibility incomplete; downstream phases blocked from thesis-ready claims |
| Card limitation gate | `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard` reflect source records, validation state, limitations, and non-claims | Cards validate against records/manifests | Cards cannot be used in thesis/dashboard exports |
| Claim-safety tag gate | Public-data, proxy, non-clinical, non-deployment, and diagnostic-only tags propagate | Layer 0-compatible tags present | Claim downgrade or blocked publication claims |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 1 is done only when one or more selected public EEG datasets have:

1. validated `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, and applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord` outputs;
2. a `ValidationReport` that explicitly reports schema, metadata, label, preprocessing, split, leakage, exclusion, matched-key, and warning status;
3. a `Layer1Manifest` with paths, hashes, seeds, config references, source record IDs, validation status, readiness status, and known limitations;
4. a validated `manifests/layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` with matched-comparison key completeness, missing-key warnings, and diagnostic-only downgrade reasons;
5. `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard` that state what the public data can and cannot support;
6. no unresolved split leakage, label ambiguity, preprocessing leakage, untracked exclusion, or missing matched-comparison key unless explicitly marked diagnostic-only in the readiness artifact and validation report;
7. stable handoff fields for Phase 2 baseline decoders and for downstream evaluation/dashboard/claim-safety use.

If multi-dataset coverage is infeasible, the accepted fallback is one primary dataset with a fully validated split protocol, cards, manifest, and readiness artifact before adding secondary datasets. This fallback can support an initial C0 path but must be labeled accordingly and must not be represented as broad multi-dataset robustness.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

### 14.1 Phase 1 matched-key responsibility

Phase 1 is the first phase that materializes the keys later required for A0–A13 matched comparisons. It must preserve stable identity fields and prevent downstream phases from fabricating missing keys.

| Key or key family | Phase 1 source | Required for | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `Layer1Manifest` | All comparisons and source grouping | Required |
| `subject_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord` where applicable | Subject-level splits and matched comparisons | Required where dataset supports subject identity |
| `session_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord` where applicable | Session-level leakage control and temporal analyses | Required where dataset supports sessions |
| `run_id` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, manifests where applicable | Run-level reproducibility and source grouping | Required where applicable |
| `trial_id` and `parent_trial_id` | `WindowRecord` | Trial/window lineage, overlap leakage, replay, stress pairing | Required where trial/window structure exists; standalone `TrialRecord` remains unresolved |
| `window_id` | `WindowRecord` | Decoder inputs, calibration, IHARQ, policy context, simulation replay, stress, embodiment, dashboard | Required |
| `split_id` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord`, manifests | All split-safe evaluations | Required |
| `split_role` / `split_membership` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord` | Train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation legality | Required |
| `label_budget_id` / `calibration_budget` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord` | Low-calibration comparisons A0–A4 and downstream | Required |
| `preprocessing_id` / `preprocessing_version` | `PreprocessingRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `DatasetRecord` | Matched preprocessing comparisons | Required |
| `label_map_id` | `LabelMapRecord`, `WindowRecord` where applicable | Label consistency and proxy-intent limitation | Required |
| `artifact_flags` / `channel_mask_id` | `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `WindowRecord` where applicable | Artifact/channel subgrouping, warnings, stress/quality analyses | Required where source supports it; missingness is warning, not clean proof |
| `config_hash` | All configs/records/manifests where applicable | Reproducibility and hidden-drift detection | Required |
| `seed` | `SplitRecord`, manifests where applicable | Split reproducibility | Required for generated splits |
| `schema_version` | All canonical records/artifacts | Schema compatibility | Required |
| `validation_status` | All canonical records/artifacts | Dashboard, claim-safety, diagnostic-only treatment | Required |
| `claim_boundary_tags` | `DatasetRecord`, manifests, cards/readiness artifacts | Claim limitation inheritance | Required |

### 14.2 Key preservation across future phases

Phase 1 must prepare the key envelope so later phases can add their own keys without changing source meaning:

- Phase 2 adds `model_id`, `decoder_id`, prediction IDs, and seed/model lineage.
- Phase 3 adds `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, and uncertainty/selective-prediction IDs.
- Phase 4 adds IHARQ decision/evidence IDs.
- Phase 5 adds regime/trust state IDs.
- Phase 6 adds policy/context/action IDs.
- Phase 7 adds transition/session/reward/rollout IDs.
- Phase 8 adds stress profile/schedule/run IDs.
- Phase 9 adds embodiment mode/state/outcome IDs.
- Phase 10 and Phase 11 add policy-update and adaptive-policy identifiers where applicable.
- Phase 14 adds dashboard/export IDs only as derived/read-only outputs.
- Phase 15 adds final claim-evidence links without mutating evidence records.

If any Phase 1 key is missing, unmatched, stale, or non-unique, later comparisons must be marked diagnostic-only or blocked according to validation status. No downstream layer may repair a missing Phase 1 key by overwriting a validated source record.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 A0–A13 linkage

A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata, not artifact owners. Phase 1 enables or strengthens them by producing clean source records and matched keys.

| Ablation/evaluation context | Phase 1 role | Evidence-action status | Required Phase 1 artifact linkage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A0 — raw decoder` | Direct source-record basis for raw decoder evaluation | `enabled_later` | `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `Layer1Manifest`, readiness artifact |
| `A1 — calibrated decoder` | Provides legal calibration/test split roles and label budgets | `enabled_later` | `SplitRecord`, calibration membership, label budgets, `Layer1Manifest` |
| `A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline` | Provides split roles and matched operating context for later threshold selection | `enabled_later` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord`, readiness artifact |
| `A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction` | Provides source/split lineage and score/label visibility needed for later uncertainty and selective-prediction comparisons | `enabled_later` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord`, preprocessing lineage, readiness artifact |
| `A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls` | Provides matched window/source/split keys for fair multi-window and ensemble controls | `enabled_later` | `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, label budget, config hash |
| `A5 — IHARQ-lite` | Provides source windows/splits/labels and limitation tags consumed through decoder/calibration evidence | `prepared_later` | Layer 1 source lineage and readiness status |
| `A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator` | Provides source/proxy/quality context but no evidence-quality model | `prepared_later` | Source lineage, artifact flags where available |
| `A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk` | Provides temporal subject/session/run/window ordering and artifact context | `prepared_later` | `WindowRecord`, `DatasetRecord`, optional `ArtifactFlagRecord` |
| `A8 — learning-to-defer` | Provides split-safe source context and proxy labels for later deferral evaluation | `prepared_later` | `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, readiness artifact |
| `A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ` | Provides protocol identity, label-budget context, and source limitations | `prepared_later` | `Layer1Manifest`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord` |
| `A10 — contextual bandit` | Provides source IDs and split/adaptation boundaries for later simulation-only online adaptation | `prepared_later` | Split/adaptation membership and limitation tags |
| `A11 — reinforcement-learning policy` | Provides source lineage and split boundaries for later simulated sequential evaluation | `prepared_later` | `SplitRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `Layer1Manifest` |
| `A12 — StressForge stress tests` | Provides immutable clean source records for matched clean/stressed comparisons | `prepared_later` | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, preprocessing/label/source hashes |
| `A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo` | Provides source/proxy lineage indirectly through policy/transition records | `prepared_later` | Source IDs and non-clinical/proxy tags inherited by later records |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts produced or prepared

| Evaluation artifact | Phase 1 action | Canonical status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | Produced and validated | Canonical readiness artifact with exact full schema requiring confirmation | Contains validation status, matched-key completeness, required paths, known limitations, diagnostic-only reasons |
| Matched-comparison key completeness report | Produced as readiness/validation support | Supporting evaluation artifact unless later canonicalized | Must feed readiness artifact and future `MatchedComparisonReport` generation |
| Split-leakage report | Produced as validation support | Validation artifact under Layer 1 report family | Must preserve pass/fail/warning status and failure list |
| Metadata-completeness report | Produced as validation support | Validation artifact | Must preserve missingness and diagnostic consequences |
| Low-calibration budget table | Produced as protocol support | Supporting artifact | Must include label budgets, calibration/adaptation memberships, split IDs, config hashes, and seeds |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` | Prepared only | Required downstream evaluation artifact; MC-008 unresolved | Phase 1 must not invent metric formulas; it preserves keys needed for later metrics |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | Prepared only | Required downstream evaluation artifact | Phase 1 provides keys; later phases produce comparison reports |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Prepared/triggered where protocol exclusions or validation failures affect evaluation | Evaluation/claim-safety artifact | Phase 1 failures must be visible and may seed later negative-result notes |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Produced/triggered where Phase 1 validation/readiness is incomplete | Evaluation/claim-safety artifact | Must be visible in readiness artifact, validation report, cards, dashboard inputs, and claim-safety review |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` / claim-evidence placeholder | Prepared only | Candidate/confirmation-dependent final-evidence artifact | Phase 1 supplies public-data/proxy limitation tags and source lineage for later claim linkage |

### 15.3 Evaluation boundary

Phase 1 is evaluation-readiness production, not evaluation-result production. It can say that A0–A13 are enabled or prepared by source records and matched keys. It must not say that any ablation produces Layer 1 records or that Phase 1 proves decoder/calibration/IHARQ/policy/stress/embodiment performance.

### 15.4 Frozen/update separation and `PolicyUpdateTrace` applicability

`not_applicable_with_reason`: Phase 1 is not an adaptive-policy, simulation, stress, contextual-bandit, reinforcement-learning, or embodiment-feedback phase. It does not produce `PolicyUpdateTrace`, update-enabled training curves, disabled-update audits, held-out frozen-policy evaluation curves, reward traces, policy-action records, or simulator transition records. Its responsibility is limited to preserving split roles, adaptation memberships, held-out identifiers, seeds, config hashes, and validation status so later phases can separate update-enabled training/adaptation evidence from frozen-policy evaluation evidence without mutating Layer 1 clean source records.

## 16. Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Obligations

### 16.1 Dashboard-readable source records and artifacts

Layer 10 may later read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, card, export, and package the following Phase 1 outputs:

| Dashboard-readable Phase 1 output | Layer 10 allowed use | Layer 10 forbidden use |
|---|---|---|
| `DatasetRecord` | Source summary, dataset provenance, dataset status, limitation display | Change dataset status or claim source validation |
| `WindowRecord` | Window counts, timing summaries, overlap warnings, source lineage views | Rewindow data or repair split/window leakage |
| `SplitRecord` | Split membership summaries, calibration/adaptation budget display, leakage warnings | Retune splits or promote leaked splits |
| `PreprocessingRecord` | Preprocessing summaries and fit-scope warnings | Retune preprocessing or hide illegal fit scope |
| `LabelMapRecord` | Label mapping displays and proxy-intent warnings | Relabel or convert proxy labels into clinical intent |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` | Quality/artifact warnings where available | Treat missing flags as clean proof |
| `ValidationReport` | Pass/fail/warning panels, blocked/diagnostic-only status | Hide failures or silently repair records |
| `DatasetCard` | Render/export card and limitation summary | Rewrite limitations or treat card as performance evidence |
| `ProtocolCard` | Render/export split/protocol/budget summary | Retune thresholds/splits or hide diagnostic labels |
| `Layer1Manifest` | Reproducibility/export source manifest input | Fabricate missing paths/hashes |
| `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | Ablation-readiness view and warning surface | Promote unmatched comparisons to thesis-ready claims |

### 16.2 Dashboard-warning inputs

Phase 1 must expose warning inputs for:

- source/version/license/access ambiguity;
- missing subject/session/run/trial/window identifiers;
- split leakage or split-disjointness failure;
- overlap leakage or parent-trial leakage;
- missing calibration/adaptation memberships;
- missing low-calibration budget definitions;
- label-map ambiguity or unmapped labels;
- illegal preprocessing fit scope;
- missing artifact/channel-quality flags;
- untracked exclusions;
- stale manifest paths or config hashes;
- missing matched-comparison keys;
- readiness artifact missing or false;
- missing public-data/proxy/non-clinical limitation tags.

### 16.3 Dashboard-generated derived outputs

Layer 10 may later generate derived outputs from Phase 1 source artifacts, including dataset summary views, protocol summary views, split/leakage warning panels, ablation-readiness views, reproducibility exports, dashboard cards, figures/tables, and export manifests. These outputs must remain derived, traceable, non-primary, and linked back to Phase 1 source records, configs, validation reports, cards, and manifests.

### 16.4 Dashboard-export manifest inputs

Phase 1 must make the following available for future export manifests:

```text
Layer1Manifest
DatasetCard
ProtocolCard
ValidationReport
layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json
record paths and hashes
config files and config hashes
seed values
schema versions
source record IDs
validation status
known limitations
claim boundary tags
diagnostic-only flags where applicable
```

### 16.5 Not-dashboard inputs

Raw public EEG files, external dataset mirrors, internal cache artifacts, loader internals, and dataset-specific preprocessing intermediate files are not dashboard evidence by themselves. They may be referenced through manifests and source metadata, but Layer 10 must not expose or reinterpret them as primary findings without validated Layer 1 records.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types for Phase 1

Phase 1 may support bounded claims about:

- use of public EEG/public benchmark data as the empirical source substrate;
- existence of a standardized, validated, split-safe public-data protocol;
- reproducible dataset/source/protocol lineage;
- low-calibration budget definitions and split memberships;
- source metadata, label mapping, preprocessing, windowing, and split-disjointness traceability;
- readiness of source records for downstream A0–A13 evaluation contexts when validation passes;
- validity-boundary disclosure for public healthy/public benchmark EEG as a proxy.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types for Phase 1

Phase 1 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real online closed-loop control;
- actual decoder, calibration, IHARQ, policy, stress, or embodiment performance.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 1 outputs must carry or enable the following limitation tags where applicable:

```text
public_eeg_only
not_clinical_validation
not_medical_device_evidence
not_real_patient_safety_evidence
not_rehabilitation_efficacy_evidence
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
offline_public_benchmark
proxy_or_pseudo_intent_labels
low_calibration_protocol_only
evaluation_readiness_only
source_record_only
validation_support_only
diagnostic_only_if_missing_keys
diagnostic_only_if_validation_incomplete
missing_artifact_flags_not_clean_proof
```

### 17.4 Diagnostic-only cases

Phase 1 evidence becomes diagnostic-only, or causes downstream evidence to become diagnostic-only, when:

- source/provenance/license/version is unresolved;
- required metadata are missing and cannot be validated;
- label mapping remains ambiguous;
- split leakage is detected;
- preprocessing fit scope is illegal or unclear;
- windows overlap across prohibited split boundaries;
- low-calibration budget definitions are inconsistent;
- exclusions are untracked;
- matched-comparison keys are incomplete;
- readiness artifact is missing, stale, or false;
- limitation tags are missing;
- artifact/channel flags are missing for analyses that require quality subgroups.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 must be able to review Phase 1 outputs for:

- public-data/proxy limitation propagation;
- no clinical/deployment/real-control claims;
- no missing diagnostic-only labels;
- traceability from cards/manifests to source records and validation status;
- matching between claim wording and validation/readiness status;
- no use of excluded, optional-only, future, or diagnostic-only datasets in confirmatory claims.

Layer 0 may add stricter claim-safety tags or downgrade claims. It must not mutate Phase 1 source records or become the empirical owner of the data.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 are capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels. They are not implementation phases, ablation IDs, artifact owners, or substitutes for Phase 1 validation.

| Capability tier | Phase 1 linkage | Claim-maturity effect |
|---|---|---|
| `C0` | A single primary public EEG dataset with validated source records, fixed splits, low-calibration budget definitions, cards, manifest, and readiness artifact may support an initial C0 path | Supports core public-data/protocol readiness only; does not prove decoder reliability until Phase 2/A0 evidence exists |
| `C1` | Phase 1 enables broader baseline/calibration reliability evidence by preserving keys and splits for Phases 2–3 | Cannot mature without decoder/calibration outputs and metric dictionary entries |
| `C2` | Phase 1 provides source lineage and proxy/limitation tags for IHARQ/RegimeRisk evidence later | Cannot mature without Phases 4–5 |
| `C3` | Phase 1 provides source/split/adaptation boundaries for adaptive policy/simulation evidence later | Cannot mature without Phases 6–11 and strict frozen/update separation |
| `C4` | Phase 1 provides public-data/proxy lineage that must remain visible in stress/embodiment/dashboard/final claims | Cannot mature without later stress, embodiment, dashboard, and final integration validation |

Phase 1 cannot by itself advance claims beyond public-data/protocol readiness. If only one dataset is validated, the capability-tier statement must identify the scope as one-dataset C0 readiness rather than broad robustness.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative-result handling in Phase 1

Phase 1 negative or unfavorable protocol findings must be preserved, not hidden. These include:

- dataset source/access/license ambiguity;
- exclusion of datasets, subjects, sessions, runs, trials, windows, channels, or labels;
- missing metadata;
- label-map ambiguity;
- split leakage or split infeasibility;
- preprocessing fit-scope failure;
- low-calibration budget inconsistency;
- missing artifact/channel flags;
- missing matched-comparison keys;
- failure of one or more validation gates.

These outcomes must appear in `ValidationReport`, cards, manifests, and readiness artifacts as applicable. Where they affect downstream evaluation claims, a `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` and, when supported by the evaluation framework, a `NegativeResultNote` must be prepared or emitted so later phases do not omit the limitation.

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency

Phase 1 establishes data/protocol sufficiency for baseline evaluation, not baseline performance sufficiency. Baseline decoder sufficiency is a Phase 2 responsibility. Phase 1 sufficiency means:

- at least one selected public EEG dataset has validated source/protocol records;
- windows and splits are stable and readable by downstream decoders;
- low-calibration budgets are defined;
- matched-comparison keys are complete or diagnostic-only status is explicit;
- cards/manifests/validation reports are present;
- public-data/proxy/non-clinical limitation tags are preserved.

If multi-dataset validation fails, Phase 1 may still be sufficient for an initial one-dataset C0 path only if the primary dataset is fully validated and the fallback scope is explicit. Secondary or stretch datasets that fail validation must not be silently counted toward robustness or generalization.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure/missingness condition | Required status | Phase 1 handling | Downstream consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Missing public source/version/license | Blocking or diagnostic-only depending on dataset status | Exclude or mark diagnostic-only; preserve reason | Dataset cannot support confirmatory claims |
| Missing required metadata | Diagnostic-only or blocking | Record in metadata-completeness report and cards | Affected subject/session/run/window comparisons blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Standalone `TrialRecord` requested | Unresolved candidate | Do not promote; use `trial_id`/`parent_trial_id` inside `WindowRecord` | Later trial-level schema may need confirmation |
| Label ambiguity or unmapped label | Blocking for affected label/task | Exclude or version label map before use | Decoder/evaluation for affected labels blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Illegal preprocessing fit scope | Blocking | Require new preprocessing version/config; preserve failed validation | Downstream evidence invalid until repaired |
| Split leakage | Blocking for confirmatory claims | Fail split gate; create new split version if repaired | Downstream evaluation claims blocked; diagnostic-only if retained |
| Missing calibration/adaptation membership | Blocking for affected low-calibration/adaptive evaluations | Mark readiness false for affected contexts | A1–A4 or adaptive contexts blocked/diagnostic-only |
| Untracked exclusions | Blocking until accounted | Add exclusion reasons or mark diagnostic-only | Thesis evidence not ready |
| Missing artifact flags | Warning, not proof of clean data | Add warning/limitation tag | Quality/artifact subgroup claims downgraded |
| Missing matched-comparison keys | Diagnostic-only or blocking | Record in readiness artifact and completeness report | A0–A13 comparisons diagnostic-only or blocked |
| Missing `Layer1Manifest` | Blocking | No downstream thesis-ready handoff | Phase 2 may not make traceable claims |
| Missing readiness artifact | Blocking for ablation readiness | Generate or mark Phase 1 incomplete | A0–A13 evaluation readiness absent |
| Stale path/config hash | Blocking or reproducibility-incomplete | Fail manifest/path/hash gate | Layer 10 export and Phase 15 reproducibility incomplete |
| Missing claim-boundary tags | Blocking for claim use | Add tags through supported claim-safety fixtures; do not invent unsupported claims | Layer 0 downgrades/block claims |
| Dashboard tries to repair source record | Forbidden | Treat as Layer 10 boundary violation | Dashboard output invalid for thesis evidence |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` or update-enabled policy evidence is requested from Phase 1 | Not applicable / boundary violation | Do not create policy-update records in Phase 1; preserve only split/adaptation/frozen-evaluation identifiers for later phases | Policy-update claims blocked until the appropriate later phase produces validated update traces under Phase 0 governance |
| Downstream phase mutates clean Layer 1 record | Forbidden | Require derived/new-version record and audit note | Downstream evidence invalid or diagnostic-only |

Diagnostic-only status must be preserved in records, validation reports, readiness artifacts, cards, dashboards, and final claim-evidence links. It must not be erased by later positive results.

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

All repository paths below are registry-supported planned/conceptual homes unless the final repository layout confirms them under `MC-009`. `Layer1Manifest` must record actual generated paths and hashes.

| Artifact/record | Planned or registry-supported storage expectation | Path-status caveat |
|---|---|---|
| `DatasetRecord` | `records/dataset_records/` | Use actual path in manifest; final layout confirmation required under `MC-009` |
| `WindowRecord` | `records/window_records/` | Use actual path/hash in manifest |
| `SplitRecord` | `records/split_records/` | Use actual path/hash in manifest |
| `PreprocessingRecord` | `records/preprocessing_records/` | Use actual path/hash in manifest |
| `LabelMapRecord` | `records/label_map_records/` | Use actual path/hash in manifest |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` | `records/artifact_flag_records/` | Present where available; missingness warning required |
| `ValidationReport` | `reports/layer1_validation/`, `reports/leakage_audits/`, `reports/metadata_completeness/` | Report family may include multiple files; manifest must reference them |
| `DatasetCard` | `cards/dataset_cards/` | Layer 1 card artifact; Layer 10 later reads/renders/exports |
| `ProtocolCard` | `cards/protocol_cards/` | Layer 1 card artifact; Layer 10 later reads/renders/exports |
| `Layer1Manifest` | `manifests/layer1_manifest_l1_v1.json` | Required handoff manifest |
| `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | `manifests/layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | Required evaluation-readiness artifact |
| Low-calibration budget table | Supporting protocol/evaluation location recorded in `Layer1Manifest` | Do not create unsupported canonical record name |
| Matched-key completeness report | Supporting validation/evaluation-readiness location recorded in `Layer1Manifest` and readiness artifact | May be embedded or separate; must be traceable |
| Split-leakage report | Supporting validation/leakage audit location recorded in `Layer1Manifest` | Must preserve pass/fail/warning status |

Storage expectations:

- every saved record/artifact must include schema version, phase ID, producer module, validation status, config hash, seed where applicable, and source IDs;
- versioned repairs must create new versions rather than overwriting validated source records;
- manifests must include path, hash, validation status, known limitation, and dashboard/export-readiness status;
- excluded/diagnostic-only artifacts must remain discoverable and must not be deleted from reproducibility evidence;
- raw data storage or external mirrors must be referenced only through source metadata and manifests, respecting public dataset access and licensing constraints.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Required package contents for Phase 2

Phase 2 may begin only when the Phase 1 handoff package includes:

- validated `WindowRecord` files readable by the decoder pipeline;
- validated `SplitRecord` files with train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation memberships and leakage status;
- validated `LabelMapRecord` files with normalized labels and proxy-intent notes;
- validated `PreprocessingRecord` files with stable config hashes and legal fit scope;
- `DatasetRecord` source/provenance records;
- applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord` files or explicit missing-flag warnings;
- low-calibration budget table;
- `ValidationReport` with no blocking unresolved errors;
- `Layer1Manifest` with paths/hashes/seeds/configs/status;
- `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` with matched-key completeness status;
- dataset/protocol cards with public-data and non-clinical limitations.

### 23.2 Required package contents for later phases

| Downstream phase | Required Phase 1 handoff |
|---|---|
| Phase 3 | Split roles, calibration/adaptation memberships, labels, preprocessing lineage, readiness status |
| Phase 4 | Window/source lineage, artifact flags where available, split/legal-use status, claim tags |
| Phase 5 | Subject/session/run/window ordering, artifact context, public-data/proxy limitations |
| Phase 6 | Protocol identity, label budgets, split roles, source limitation tags, readiness status |
| Phase 7 | Replay-compatible windows, split/protocol identity, trial/window ordering, proxy labels, limitations |
| Phase 8 | Immutable clean source records for matched clean/stressed comparisons |
| Phase 9 | Source/proxy limitation tags inherited through policy/transition/embodiment records |
| Phase 10–11 | Split/adaptation boundaries and source limitations for simulated update-enabled and frozen-evaluation separation |
| Phase 12–13 | Source/proxy limitation tags and trial/window lineage inherited into embodiment/replay records |
| Phase 14 | Dashboard-readable records/cards/manifests, warning inputs, validation status, diagnostic-only flags |
| Phase 15 | Final claim-evidence source lineage, cards, manifests, readiness status, limitation tags, and unresolved issue ledger |

### 23.3 Handoff validity rules

- Downstream phases may consume Phase 1 source records only when `validation_status` permits the intended use.
- Downstream phases may not overwrite Phase 1 records; changes require new versioned records or derived records with explicit lineage.
- Downstream phases must inherit diagnostic-only and limitation tags.
- If a downstream phase cannot find required source IDs, path hashes, split roles, or matched keys, its results must be marked diagnostic-only or blocked.
- The handoff package must be reproducible from `Layer1Manifest` without relying on hidden local knowledge.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 1 is complete only if all of the following are true:

1. The supplied Phase 0 foundation has been inherited and no blocking Phase 0 gap exists.
2. At least one selected public EEG dataset is registered with a validated `DatasetRecord` and explicit source/version/license/status/claim-scope metadata.
3. `LabelMapRecord` validates for all included original labels and documented exclusions, including proxy-intent limitation notes.
4. `PreprocessingRecord` validates with stable config hash, legal fit scope, and version linkage to windows.
5. `SplitRecord` validates with train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation memberships, seed, split level, label budgets, leakage checks, and split version.
6. `WindowRecord` validates with dataset/subject/session/run/trial/window identity, timing, labels, split membership, overlap grouping, preprocessing linkage, and config hash.
7. `ArtifactFlagRecord` validates where artifact/channel-quality annotations exist, and missing flags are explicitly warned as missingness rather than clean proof.
8. `ValidationReport` records schema, source/provenance, metadata, label, preprocessing, split, leakage, exclusion, matched-key, card, manifest, and claim-tag validation status.
9. `DatasetCard` and `ProtocolCard` are created, validated against source records, and include required limitations and non-claims.
10. `Layer1Manifest` validates with paths, hashes, config files, config hash, seed, source IDs, output paths, validation status, ablation-readiness path, and known limitations.
11. `manifests/layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` validates with readiness status, matched-key completeness, required record paths, known limitations, and diagnostic-only downgrade reasons.
12. No split leakage, label ambiguity, illegal preprocessing fit scope, untracked exclusion, stale path/hash, or missing matched-comparison key remains unresolved unless explicitly marked diagnostic-only or blocking.
13. Layer 10 can read Phase 1 source records/cards/manifests and warning inputs without recomputing hidden protocol logic or repairing source evidence.
14. Layer 0 can audit Phase 1 outputs and verify public-data/proxy/non-clinical limitation tags.
15. Downstream Phase 2 can consume the validated `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `DatasetRecord`, applicable `ArtifactFlagRecord`, validation reports, and manifests without renaming or redefining them.
16. All carried open issues are listed rather than silently normalized.

```yaml
phase_definition_of_done_status: complete_when_all_gates_pass
phase_blocks_downstream_if:
  - Layer 1 source records are missing or invalid
  - split leakage remains unresolved
  - label maps are ambiguous
  - preprocessing fit scope is illegal
  - exclusions are untracked
  - Layer1Manifest is missing or stale
  - layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json is missing or falsely reports readiness
  - matched-comparison keys required by downstream evaluations are absent without diagnostic-only status
  - claim-boundary tags are missing
phase_allows_downstream_with_diagnostic_only_if:
  - missingness is explicit
  - readiness artifact records diagnostic-only reasons
  - validation report and cards expose limitations
  - downstream phases preserve diagnostic-only labels
  - no confirmatory thesis claim relies on diagnostic-only evidence
next_phase_unlocked_when_done: Phase 2 — Baseline decoders
```

# Phase 2 — Baseline decoders

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 2 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 2` |
| Official phase name | `Baseline decoders` |
| Phase status | `measurement_spine_gate` |
| Primary layer ownership | `Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine` |
| Supporting layers | `Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor` as immutable source-record producer; `Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction` as immediate downstream consumer; `Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance`; `Layer 10 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility` as read/export consumer only |
| Implementation-order role | First decoder-evidence phase after Phase 1 public-data/split protocol validation |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Evidence-production logic for fair decoder outputs, model registry, prediction records, baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject profiles, ensemble controls, failed-run visibility, and downstream readiness; not a function-level training playbook or command-run guide |
| Scientific-output status | Produces decoder/baseline evidence and comparison spine records; does not produce calibration evidence, IHARQ decisions, RegimeRisk trust states, policy actions, simulated consequences, stress profiles, embodiment results, dashboard conclusions, or final clinical/deployment claims |
| Thesis role | Supports baseline tables, low-calibration curves, subject difficulty profiles, model-family comparisons, ordinary ensemble/longer-window controls, and the argument that later reliability modules operate on a fair decoder spine rather than a cherry-picked model |
| Previous phase dependency | Hard dependency on Phase 0 schemas/configs/validators/run conventions and Phase 1 validated public-data/protocol source records |
| Downstream dependency effect | Phase 3 consumes raw probabilities, logits, decision scores, labels where evaluation-only use is legal, score type, class order, split IDs, model IDs, and prediction identifiers; Phases 4–15 consume prediction identifiers, A0/A4 evidence, model registry links, baseline summaries, and diagnostic/limitation tags |

Phase 2 is the measurement spine gate. It creates fair, reproducible, inspectable decoder outputs for all later reliability, calibration, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, adaptive policy, simulation, stress, dashboard, ablation, and final thesis phases. It prevents unfair model comparisons, hidden model reruns, missing raw scores for calibration, inconsistent seed handling, incomplete low-calibration evidence, and downstream policy work built on unstable or undocumented predictions.

Phase 2 is not a readiness-decision phase. It predicts and measures; it does not decide whether a prediction is trustworthy, safe, sufficient, clinically meaningful, or deployment-ready. Any stronger interpretation is reserved for later layers and remains bounded by Layer 0 claim-safety governance.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 2 establishes the baseline decoder measurement spine. It produces the raw prediction and baseline evidence that all later reliability and readiness modules consume. Its central purpose is not to maximize a single decoder score; it is to make decoder evidence fair, complete, traceable, reusable, and downstream-compatible.

Phase 2 controls the bottleneck between Phase 1 clean public-data/source records and Phase 3 calibration/uncertainty. Without Phase 2, later phases would have no grounded `PredictionRecord` family, no model registry, no low-calibration curves, no subject difficulty profiles, no ordinary ensemble controls, and no reliable way to prove that IHARQ or adaptive-policy results are not built on cherry-picked or hidden decoder runs.

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 2 explicitly controls:

- unfair model-family comparisons caused by different splits, preprocessing, label budgets, reporting units, or missing-run policies;
- hidden model reruns that would prevent downstream evidence traceability;
- missing probability vectors, logits, decision scores, score types, or class-order mappings needed by Phase 3;
- inconsistent seed/config handling;
- unsupported use of test labels for training, calibration, budget selection, or threshold selection;
- hidden failed/skipped/unsupported model runs;
- weak-baseline criticism in later IHARQ, RegimeRisk, and policy evaluation;
- ambiguity between IHARQ evidence verification, A2 confidence-threshold rejection, and A4 ordinary longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, or ensemble controls;
- unsupported promotion of decoder performance into readiness, clinical, deployment, safety, or rehabilitation claims.

### 4.3 Thesis-evidence role

Phase 2 supports:

- baseline decoder tables;
- low-calibration / low-label budget curves;
- subject/session difficulty profiles;
- model-family comparisons;
- A0 raw-decoder evidence;
- A4 ordinary-combination, longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble-control summaries;
- failure and missingness evidence;
- decoder/model cards or card source bundles;
- reproducibility appendix material;
- the argument that later reliability modules operate on a fair decoder spine rather than a single selected model.

## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

### 5.1 Layer ownership

| Layer | Phase 2 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Primary producing layer | Owns decoder prediction evidence, model registry, baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject profiles, ensemble controls, failure-case index, and Layer 2 readiness report |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Upstream source-record producer | Owns immutable clean public-data/protocol records consumed by Phase 2; Phase 2 may validate, reference, or reject them but must not overwrite them |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Immediate downstream consumer | Consumes Phase 2 prediction records and model registry links for calibration, uncertainty, selective prediction, thresholding, reliability audits, and high-confidence-error diagnostics |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Downstream consumer | Consumes predictions, model identities, disagreement/control evidence, and later calibrated/uncertainty outputs; does not own Layer 2 records |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Downstream consumer | Consumes time-indexed prediction logs, recent performance histories, subject profiles, and error-burst indicators where available |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Downstream consumer through derived context | Later consumes Layer 2 lineage through calibrated/IHARQ/RegimeRisk readiness contexts; Phase 2 does not learn policies |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Downstream replay consumer | May consume prediction histories for replay-style simulated sessions; Phase 2 does not define rewards, transitions, or safety-event proxies |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Downstream stress consumer | May stress-condition Layer 2 prediction histories while preserving clean-source lineage; Phase 2 does not create stress profiles/schedules |
| Layer 9 — Embodiment demo/replay | Downstream provenance/input consumer only | May use decoder-derived readiness/provenance inputs through later layers; Phase 2 does not claim embodiment safety or real control |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility | Read/export/derived-output owner | Reads Phase 2 records and source bundles; renders views/cards/figures/exports as derived outputs only |
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Claim-safety auditor | Applies limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, non-claim boundaries, and final claim review; does not produce empirical decoder evidence |

### 5.2 Module participation

| Module/submodule | Phase 2 participation | Evidence output |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline trainer | Trains/runs selected decoder families under fixed Phase 1 splits and low-calibration budgets | model artifacts/checkpoints, training logs, `ModelRegistryRecord` entries |
| Prediction logger | Exports per-window/per-trial decoder outputs in canonical form | `PredictionRecord` |
| Baseline metric builder | Computes declared baseline metrics under matched split/budget/model/seed keys | `BaselineMetricRecord`, baseline comparison tables, confusion-matrix lineage |
| Low-calibration curve builder | Evaluates declared label-budget / low-calibration conditions | `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, low-calibration budget summaries |
| Subject difficulty profiler | Summarizes subject/session heterogeneity, instability, low-label fragility, model-family sensitivity, and difficult cases | `SubjectProfileRecord`, difficult-subject index, subject/session profile summaries |
| Model-family registry | Standardizes model IDs, decoder IDs, hyperparameters, seeds, artifacts, paths, score types, class order, status, and failure reasons | `ModelRegistryRecord`, failed/skipped-run table |
| Ensemble comparison builder | Produces ordinary longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, probability-averaging, and ensemble-control evidence; preserves confidence-threshold evidence under A2 | `EnsembleControlRecord`, A4 control summaries, delay-burden notes |
| Compact SSL adapter | Optional/stretch baseline adapter when legal, feasible, compatible, and stable | adapter-produced `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord`, feasibility/skipped-run notes |
| Downstream readiness validator | Verifies that Phase 2 outputs can be read by downstream layers without hidden reruns or invented fields | `Layer2ReadinessReport`, missing-field list, consumer-compatibility matrix, diagnostic-only downgrade list |

### 5.3 Boundary rules

Phase 2 must not:

- calibrate raw confidence as trust evidence; calibration is Layer 3;
- select final thresholds; threshold governance is Layer 3;
- make IHARQ accept/wait/request/combine/fallback/unsafe decisions; that is Layer 4;
- compute RegimeRisk temporal trust states; that is Layer 5;
- train readiness policies, contextual bandits, or RL policies; that is Layer 6 / Phase 10 / Phase 11;
- produce simulated transitions, rewards, or safety-event proxies; that is Layer 7;
- create stress profiles or stress schedules; that is Layer 8;
- claim embodiment validity, muscle stimulation control, or deployment readiness; those claims are forbidden;
- treat Layer 10 cards/views/exports as primary empirical evidence;
- treat Layer 0 claim-audit artifacts as empirical decoder evidence.

| Run identifier conventions | Yes | Available | Every Phase 2 record carries `run_id` where applicable |
| Config hash conventions | Yes | Available | Every model/run/output uses `config_hash`; model config hash must be recorded |
| Seed conventions | Yes | Available | Every trained model or stochastic process carries `seed` |
| Manifest conventions | Yes | Available | Phase 2 creates a downstream handoff manifest using Phase 0 conventions |
| Repository skeleton expectations | Yes | Available conceptually; `MC-009` remains | Store under architecture-supported conceptual paths and mark final path reconciliation open |
| Metric dictionary placeholders | Yes | Available but `MC-008` remains | Required for thesis-facing `BaselineMetricRecord` and low-calibration curves; missing entries trigger diagnostic-only status |
| Claim-evidence placeholders | Yes | Available | Phase 2 supplies evidence inputs and limitation tags, not final claim-audit outputs |
| Dashboard/export-readiness placeholders | Yes | Available | Phase 2 marks dashboard-readable source records and warning inputs; Layer 10 later generates derived outputs |

### 9.1 Required input contract

| Input | Producer | Class | Required fields / content | Phase 2 use | Missing/invalid handling |

| `DatasetRecord` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Primary source record | dataset ID, subject/session/run information, channels, sampling rate, task labels, preprocessing metadata, split membership, source/license notes | Dataset identity, compatibility checks, model input validation, subject/session aggregation | Block or diagnostic-only if identity/provenance is incomplete |
| `WindowRecord` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Primary source record | trial/window IDs, segment pointers, time boundaries, channel mask, artifact flags where available, task label, split membership | Training/inference units; prediction alignment; ensemble/replay/stress lineage | Block affected windows or mark outputs diagnostic-only if window/trial alignment is invalid |
| `SplitRecord` / split manifest | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Protocol source record | train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation membership, split role, split version, label-budget linkage, leakage-control policy | Split-safe training, validation, test reporting, calibration-ready outputs, matched comparisons | Block if leakage or illegal membership remains unresolved |
| `LabelMapRecord` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Protocol source record | canonical class labels, class order, label-map version, inclusion/exclusion mapping | Prediction field mapping, probability/logit class order, model compatibility | Block affected model outputs if class order cannot be resolved |
| `PreprocessingRecord` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Protocol/source record | filtering/resampling/windowing/normalization/channel handling/artifact policy and fit scope | Model input reproducibility and leakage prevention | Block or diagnostic-only if preprocessing fit scope is illegal or ambiguous |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` where available | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Quality/source record | artifact/channel flags, affected windows/channels, flag provenance | Quality context, exclusion or flag-aware reporting, limitation tags | Missing flags do not prove clean data; carry warning and restrict quality-dependent claims |
| `ValidationReport` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Validation report | schema, metadata, split, label, preprocessing, leakage, matched-key status | Phase-start eligibility | Block or diagnostic-only according to severity |
| `Layer1Manifest` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Manifest | record paths, hashes, schema versions, validation status, limitation tags | Source package for Phase 2 runs | Block if stale, unreadable, or hash-inconsistent |
| `manifests/layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Readiness/diagnostic artifact | A0/A4 readiness, matched keys, diagnostic-only reasons | Controls which Phase 2 comparisons can be final vs diagnostic | Affected ablations remain diagnostic-only if readiness is incomplete |
| Low-calibration budget table/config | Phase 1 / experiment config | Protocol artifact | budget IDs, budget definitions, label counts/fractions/session fractions, split linkage | Low-calibration training/evaluation and curve production | Sparse/invalid budgets must be marked; no test-driven budget selection |
| Model configs and selected baseline family list | Phase 0 config family and Phase 2 selection | Phase config | model family, hyperparameters, training protocol, score output requirements, failure policy | Model training and registry creation | Unsupported families must be marked skipped/unsupported; do not silently omit |
| Seed registry / seed policy | Phase 0 | Reproducibility config | seed IDs/values and scope | Fair comparison, stochastic reproducibility | Missing seed blocks thesis-ready comparison |
| Metric dictionary placeholders/entries | Phase 0 / evaluation architecture | Evaluation artifact | metric ID/name, aggregation, split role, reporting scope | `BaselineMetricRecord`, low-calibration curves, A0/A4 comparisons | Missing entries trigger diagnostic-only metric status |
| Training-resource constraints | Phase 2 declared context | Operational constraint | compute/availability/licensing constraints for selected families | Coverage/fallback decisions | Must be recorded; optional/stretch omissions must have reasons |

### 9.2 Input validation before evidence production

Before training or inference, Phase 2 verifies:

- every selected `WindowRecord` maps to a validated `DatasetRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, and `LabelMapRecord`;
- dataset ID, subject ID, split ID, split role, trial ID, window ID where applicable, label, preprocessing version, and split membership are present;
- windows from the same trial are not leaked across incompatible splits;
- label mappings and class order are consistent across models and outputs;
- artifact/channel flags are handled or explicitly warned according to protocol;
- channel count, sampling rate, and preprocessing are compatible with each selected model family;
- label budgets do not use held-out test labels;
- seed policy and config hashes are fixed before training;
- model-family selection is declared before results are interpreted;
- missing probabilities, logits, decision scores, score types, and class-order fields are planned for explicit reporting rather than silent repair.

### 9.3 Not-dashboard inputs

The following are not dashboard inputs at the time Phase 2 consumes them:

- raw external public EEG files;
- internal training arrays/tensors;
- temporary model-fitting objects;
- optimizer state unless saved as model artifact provenance;
- local aliases such as `y_true`, `y_pred`, or `prob_vector` before export mapping;
- test labels used outside evaluation-only contexts;
- compute-resource notes not linked to model registry entries.

Layer 10 may later read only saved, validated records, cards/source bundles, logs, manifests, and metric artifacts.

### 10.2 Minimum `PredictionRecord` output fields

Phase 2 exports canonical field names rather than local aliases. Required or conditionally required fields include:

```text
schema_version
record_id
producer_module
producer_layer
phase_id
validation_status
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id where available
run_id where available
trial_id
window_id for windowed data
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
decoder_id
model_family
label_budget_id
seed
config_hash
predicted_class
probability_vector strongly recommended
logits where available
decision_score if applicable
score_type
class_order
label_true as evaluation-only where permitted
time_start and time_end where available
timestamp_or_order where temporal/replay use is planned
artifact_flag where available
latency where available
source_record_ids
claim_safety_tags
notes for missing/unsupported fields
```

Forbidden exported field names include unsupported final aliases such as `y_true`, `y_pred`, and `prob_vector`. They must be mapped before export to `label_true`, `predicted_class`, and `probability_vector`. Evaluation-only correctness helpers may be stored only in protected evaluation contexts and must not become decision-time policy features.
