## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 2 evidence production follows this record-level chain:

```text
Phase 1 validated source records
→ Phase 2 input validation and split/model/budget eligibility checks
→ fixed model-family and seed/config selection
→ decoder training/inference under declared splits and label budgets
→ canonical prediction export
→ model registry and model-artifact provenance
→ baseline metric and low-calibration summaries
→ subject/session profile summaries
→ ordinary ensemble/longer-window/multi-window controls
→ failed/skipped/missing-field visibility
→ conditional leakage warnings when invalid split use is detected
→ downstream readiness validation
→ A0/A4 evaluation source artifacts
→ Layer 10 readable source package and Layer 0 limitation/diagnostic inputs
```

### 12.1 Evidence actions by submodule

| Submodule | Evidence action | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline trainer | Trains/runs declared baseline families using fixed Phase 1 splits, label budgets, preprocessing records, label maps, seeds, and configs | model artifacts/checkpoints, training logs, `ModelRegistryRecord` |
| Prediction logger | Converts model outputs into canonical per-window/per-trial records | `PredictionRecord` |
| Split/schema validation and leakage warning path | Checks that Phase 1 split roles and memberships are legally used by decoder training/evaluation; does not repair Layer 1 records | `LeakageWarningRecord` when invalid split use is detected; blocking or diagnostic-only status for affected outputs |
| Baseline metric builder | Computes declared metrics with metric dictionary linkage and matched keys | `BaselineMetricRecord`, baseline tables |
| Low-calibration curve builder | Aggregates performance by declared label-budget conditions | `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, budget curves/tables |
| Subject difficulty profiler | Builds descriptive subject/session profiles from prediction and metric records | `SubjectProfileRecord` |
| Ensemble comparison builder | Constructs ordinary controls only from aligned, compatible prediction records | `EnsembleControlRecord`, A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries, delay-burden notes |
| Failure logger | Records failed/skipped/unsupported runs, missing outputs, sparse budgets, missing probabilities/logits, convergence failures, and compatibility problems | `FailureCaseIndex`, failed-run logs, negative-result triggers |
| Downstream readiness validator | Checks schema, lineage, score fields, class order, model registry links, split roles, matched keys, and consumer-specific completeness | `Layer2ReadinessReport` |

### 12.2 Core/fallback model-family evidence

Phase 2 should attempt the architecture-supported model-family ladder without overpromising coverage:

| Family/status | Phase 2 expectation | Evidence handling |
|---|---|---|
| Sanity baselines | Core lower-bound and pipeline sanity checks | Produce prediction/metric/registry records or explicit failure notes |
| Classical CSP plus LDA/SVM-style pipelines | Core where compatible | Produce matched predictions and baseline metrics |
| Riemannian / tangent-space baselines | Strongly recommended where data format and channel consistency allow | Produce matched predictions and metrics or skipped/unsupported notes |
| Compact neural baselines such as EEGNet or ShallowConvNet / temporal convolutional models | Recommended if compute allows | Produce matched records where feasible; document compute/coverage limits |
| Compact SSL or foundation-style adapters | Optional/stretch | Include only if legal, compatible, stable, and feasible; otherwise mark skipped/unsupported |
| Ordinary controls: longer-window, multi-window majority vote, probability averaging, and ensemble summaries; confidence-threshold rejection is kept under A2 | Core A4-style longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls where alignment permits | Produce matched `EnsembleControlRecord`/A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries and delay-burden notes; incompatible groups diagnostic-only |

If full model-family coverage is infeasible, the fallback minimum is one classical baseline, one Riemannian or robust classical baseline, and one compact neural baseline where feasible, with all skipped or unsupported families explicitly documented. Phase 2 remains valid as measurement evidence if limitations are transparent; it does not become invalid merely because optional stretch baselines are absent.

### 12.3 Clean-source immutability

Phase 2 must not overwrite Phase 1 `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, `ArtifactFlagRecord`, `ValidationReport`, `Layer1Manifest`, dataset cards, protocol cards, or ablation-readiness artifacts. Any discovered upstream issue must be recorded as a warning, blocking condition, diagnostic-only condition, or cross-phase issue. Repair of source records belongs to a controlled upstream correction workflow, not silent downstream mutation.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Phase-start gates

| Gate | Requirement | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 foundation gate | Schemas, configs, validators, run/hash/seed conventions, metric placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, and dashboard/export placeholders exist | Block if missing; carry open issues if non-blocking |
| Phase 1 source-record gate | Required Layer 1 source records validate and remain readable | Block affected dataset/split/window if invalid |
| Split-disjointness gate | No train/validation/test/calibration/adaptation leakage for intended comparisons | Block or diagnostic-only for affected outputs |
| Label-map/class-order gate | `LabelMapRecord` and class order are consistent across outputs | Block affected model outputs |
| Preprocessing-fit gate | No illegal fit scope or test-set leakage in preprocessing | Block affected records |
| Low-calibration budget gate | Budgets are declared before training and linked to split roles | Sparse or invalid budgets marked; no test-driven budget selection |
| Seed/config gate | Seed policy and config hash are fixed before training | Block thesis-ready comparison if missing |
| Model-family declaration gate | Selected baseline family list and feasibility constraints are declared before interpretation | Unsupported/skipped families must be logged |

### 13.2 Phase-output validation gates

| Gate | Requirement | Output affected |
|---|---|---|
| `PredictionRecord` schema gate | Required fields, canonical aliases, schema version, producer module/layer, phase ID, validation status, dataset/subject/session/trial/window/split/model/seed/config lineage present | `PredictionRecord` |
| Score availability gate | Probability vector, logits, or decision score available or explicitly marked with `score_type` | `PredictionRecord`, Phase 3 eligibility |
| Class-order gate | Probability/logit vectors align with `class_order` and `LabelMapRecord` | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord` |
| Evaluation-only label gate | `label_true` and correctness helpers remain evaluation-only and are not exported as decision-time features | `PredictionRecord`, `FailureCaseIndex` |
| Model registry gate | Every prediction file links to a validated `ModelRegistryRecord` | `PredictionRecord`, all metrics |
| Metric dictionary gate | Thesis-facing metric records reference `MetricDictionaryEntry` where required | `BaselineMetricRecord`, `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` |
| Matched-key gate | A0/A4 comparisons match dataset, subject/session, split, preprocessing, label map, budget, seed, model family/aggregation unit where applicable | A0/A4 evaluation artifacts |
| Low-calibration curve gate | Budget IDs, budget definitions, split roles, seed summaries, and budget-failure notes are present | `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` |
| Subject-profile coverage gate | Subject/session coverage is sufficient or profile is marked ambiguous | `SubjectProfileRecord` |
| Ensemble/control alignment gate | Model/window/class-order alignment exists; delay-burden notes present where controls add time/windows | `EnsembleControlRecord`, A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries |
| Split-leakage warning gate | Invalid split use, train/test/calibration/adaptation leakage, or illegal label-budget use discovered during Phase 2 validation is recorded and blocks or downgrades affected outputs | `LeakageWarningRecord`, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, affected `PredictionRecord` and metric artifacts |
| Failure transparency gate | Failed/skipped/unsupported/missing-field cases are recorded and not hidden | `FailureCaseIndex`, training/inference logs |
| Downstream readiness gate | Consumer-compatibility matrix marks each downstream path as ready, diagnostic-only, or blocked | `Layer2ReadinessReport` |
| Claim-safety gate | Limitation tags and diagnostic-only conditions are preserved | All Phase 2 outputs |

### 13.3 Exit condition

Phase 2 is complete when per-window or per-trial `PredictionRecord` outputs exist for every selected dataset, subject, split, model family, seed, and label budget intended for downstream comparison; every prediction file can be traced to a `ModelRegistryRecord`; missing logits, probabilities, decision scores, score types, or class orders are explicitly marked; A0/A4 evidence is matched on Layer 1 comparison keys or downgraded to diagnostic-only; baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject profiles, ensemble/ordinary controls, longer-window or multi-window controls, delay-burden notes, failure logs, any required `LeakageWarningRecord` artifacts, and a `Layer2ReadinessReport` are produced; and downstream layers can consume the decoder evidence spine without rerunning hidden model code.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

### 14.1 Required matched-comparison keys

Phase 2 must preserve all keys needed to compare A0/A4 and later A1–A13 evidence fairly:

```text
source_record_ids
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
producer_module
phase_id
ablation_id where applicable
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id where later applicable
threshold_registry_id where later applicable
policy_id where later applicable
stress_profile_id where later applicable
embodiment_mode_id where later applicable
label_budget_id
decoder_id
model_family
score_type
class_order
aggregation_unit
comparison_key
metric_dictionary_id where metrics are reported
```

`calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `policy_id`, `stress_profile_id`, and `embodiment_mode_id` are not produced by Phase 2, but Phase 2 records must be structured so those downstream identifiers can later attach without breaking lineage.

### 14.2 Matching requirements by output type

| Output | Matching requirement | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `PredictionRecord` | Same dataset, subject/session, trial/window, split, preprocessing, label map, budget, model family where applicable, seed/config policy | Missing source IDs, split role, label map, score type, class order, or model registry link |
| `BaselineMetricRecord` | Same dataset, subject/session, split role, aggregation level, label budget, metric dictionary entry, seed/config policy | Missing metric dictionary, unmatched aggregation level, or incomplete source prediction coverage |
| `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` | Same budget family, split role, subject/session grouping, model family, seed summary, metric dictionary | Sparse/missing budget conditions not disclosed |
| `SubjectProfileRecord` | Same source prediction coverage, subject/session IDs, split roles, budget family, aggregation rules | Insufficient coverage or unstable categories not labeled ambiguous |
| `EnsembleControlRecord` | Aligned trial/window IDs, class order, model-family membership, aggregation rule, delay-burden lineage, source prediction IDs | Incomplete model alignment, missing class order, hidden delay burden, or unfair member selection |
| `LeakageWarningRecord` | Affected split IDs, dataset/subject/session/window/model/budget IDs, severity, and required action are linked to the affected source and output records | Missing affected-record linkage, silent repair, or unresolved leakage hidden from evaluation |
| A0 evidence table | Matched Layer 1 comparison keys and metric definitions | Missing matched keys or unvalidated source records |
| A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summary | Matched ordinary-control and raw-decoder keys | Missing alignment between control and base decoder records |

### 14.3 Protection against hidden comparisons

Phase 2 must not compare models, budgets, aggregation rules, or controls unless their matched keys are explicit. If any key is missing, the comparison may remain useful for diagnostics or implementation debugging, but it must be labeled `diagnostic_only` and excluded from final thesis evidence until repaired or bounded as a limitation.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 A0–A13 treatment

A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata, not artifact owners. Phase 2 produces records used by A0 and A4, and it prepares upstream source evidence for A1–A13. It does not allow an ablation ID to own or produce a canonical record.

| Ablation/evaluation context | Phase 2 role | Produced/prepared artifacts | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 — raw decoder | Phase 2 directly produces source evidence used by this evaluation context | `PredictionRecord`, `ModelRegistryRecord`, `BaselineMetricRecord`, A0 raw-decoder evidence tables | Raw decoder baseline only |
| A1 — calibrated decoder | Prepared | Raw probabilities/logits/decision scores, score type, class order, model IDs, split roles for Phase 3 `CalibrationRecord` | No calibrated claim in Phase 2 |
| A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Prepared | Prediction records, labels where evaluation-only legal, confidence-score fields, matched keys for Phase 3 thresholds | No threshold claim in Phase 2 |
| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | Prepared through score/confidence fields, prediction lineage, class-order metadata, and split-safe inputs for Phase 3 uncertainty/selective evaluation | Prediction records, score/probability/logit fields where available, model/split/class-order lineage for Phase 3 `UncertaintyRecord` and `SelectivePredictionRecord` | No uncertainty/selective claim in Phase 2 |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Phase 2 directly produces compatible ordinary-control evidence used by this evaluation context | `EnsembleControlRecord`, ordinary-control summaries, disagreement tables, A4 matched reports | Ordinary combination control only; not IHARQ |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Prepared | Prediction identifiers, ensemble controls, failure cases, model registry links for later comparison | Phase 2 does not produce IHARQ decisions |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Prepared | Decoder lineage, subject profiles, failure case diagnostics for later evidence-quality contexts | No learned quality in Phase 2 |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Prepared | Time-indexed predictions, subject/session profiles, recent performance/error histories where available | No RegimeRisk trust state in Phase 2 |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Prepared | Decoder lineage through later readiness contexts | No deferral policy in Phase 2 |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Prepared | Prediction/model/budget lineage for later supervised policy training/evaluation | No adaptive policy in Phase 2 |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Prepared as lineage only | Frozen prediction histories for later simulation-only bandit context | No bandit policy/update evidence in Phase 2 |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Prepared as lineage only | Frozen prediction histories for later simulation-only RL context | No RL policy evidence in Phase 2 |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Prepared as lineage only | Prediction records and model IDs that can be stress-conditioned later | No stress profile/schedule in Phase 2 |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Prepared as provenance only | Decoder-derived inputs can later appear through readiness/policy/embodiment mappings | No embodiment validation in Phase 2 |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts

| Evaluation artifact | Phase 2 responsibility | Required fields / linkage | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 raw-decoder evidence table | Produce | source prediction IDs, model IDs, split IDs, label-budget IDs, metric IDs, matched keys, limitation tags | Missing matched keys or metric dictionary |
| A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summary | Produce where compatible | source prediction IDs, aggregation rule, member model IDs, class-order mapping, delay-burden notes, matched keys | Misaligned windows/classes/models or hidden delay |
| `BaselineMetricRecord` | Produce | metric dictionary ID, source prediction IDs, split IDs, seed/config, aggregation level | Missing metric dictionary or source lineage |
| `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` | Produce | budget ID, budget definition, split role, source metric IDs, seed summaries, budget-failure notes | Sparse/invalid budget without warning |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` inputs | Prepare | comparison keys and source record IDs for later reports | Missing key completeness |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Consume/validate | metric ID and definition for each thesis-facing metric | Missing entry |
| `NegativeResultNote` triggers | Prepare where applicable | failed runs, poor baselines, sparse budgets, missing scores, skipped families, diagnostic-only reason | Negative result hidden or omitted |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` triggers | Prepare where applicable | affected artifact IDs, reason, severity, final-claim block | Missing validation status |
| `Layer2ReadinessReport` | Produce | consumer-compatibility matrix and downstream pass/block/diagnostic states | Missing consumer requirements or unresolved source lineage |

### 15.3 Evaluation constraints

Phase 2 must preserve training, validation, calibration, threshold-selection, adaptation, and test split separation. Test outcomes must not drive model-family selection, budget selection, preprocessing revision, score-field repair, ensemble membership selection, or threshold-like control selection unless explicitly tagged as oracle/diagnostic and excluded from final claims.

## 16. Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Obligations

### 16.1 Dashboard-readable source records

Layer 10 may read the following Phase 2 records/artifacts as source inputs:

- `PredictionRecord`;
- `ModelRegistryRecord`;
- `BaselineMetricRecord`;
- `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`;
- `SubjectProfileRecord`;
- `EnsembleControlRecord`;
- `FailureCaseIndex`;
- `Layer2ReadinessReport`;
- training logs;
- inference logs;
- failed/skipped-run logs;
- model/checkpoint artifact provenance;
- `ModelCard` / `BenchmarkCard` source bundles or exported card inputs;
- A0 raw-decoder evidence tables;
- A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries;
- delay-burden notes;
- Phase 2 manifest/handoff package.

### 16.2 Dashboard-warning inputs

Layer 10 must surface, not suppress:

- missing probabilities, logits, decision scores, score type, or class order;
- failed/skipped/unsupported model runs;
- sparse or invalid low-calibration budgets;
- split leakage or unresolved Phase 1 validation issues;
- missing metric dictionary linkage;
- unmatched A0/A4 comparison keys;
- incomplete subject/session coverage;
- ensemble/control incompatibility;
- stale model artifact or prediction paths;
- diagnostic-only labels and negative-result notes;
- inherited claim-safety limitation tags.

### 16.3 Dashboard-generated derived outputs

Layer 10 may later generate:

- raw decoder baseline views/tables;
- model-family comparison views;
- low-calibration curve figures/tables;
- subject profile views/cards;
- ensemble-control and A4 comparison views;
- failure/missingness warning panels;
- model cards / benchmark cards / decoder cards rendered from source bundles;
- reproducibility export packages and manifests.

These outputs are derived, non-primary evidence. They must preserve source record IDs, metric dictionary references, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, validation statuses, export manifest IDs, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result notes, and claim-safety tags.

### 16.4 Dashboard-export manifest inputs

Phase 2 must prepare export-manifest inputs for Layer 10:

```text
source_record_ids
output_paths
model_artifact_paths
training_log_paths
inference_log_paths
failed_run_log_paths
metric_record_paths
card_source_bundle_paths
manifest_id
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
validation_status
diagnostic_only_flags
negative_result_note_ids where applicable
claim_safety_tags
metric_dictionary_ids where applicable
matched_comparison_keys
```

### 16.5 Layer 10 prohibited actions

Layer 10 must not:

- retrain decoders;
- recompute hidden experimental logic;
- retune model-family selection, thresholds, budgets, or ensemble membership;
- silently repair missing score fields or class-order mappings;
- hide failed/skipped/unsupported runs;
- erase diagnostic-only labels;
- hide poor baseline results;
- promote optional compact SSL/stretch outputs into core evidence;
- treat dashboard views/cards/exports as primary source evidence.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 2 may support bounded claims about:

- public EEG decoder-baseline measurement;
- fair, split-safe baseline comparison;
- reproducible decoder prediction records;
- low-calibration / low-label benchmark behavior;
- subject/session heterogeneity in public EEG data;
- ordinary voting/averaging/longer-window/multi-window/ensemble controls;
- availability or missingness of score fields for later calibration;
- failure transparency and diagnostic limitations;
- readiness of saved decoder records for downstream reliability analysis.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 2 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- calibrated confidence or uncertainty reliability;
- IHARQ readiness decisions;
- RegimeRisk temporal trust;
- adaptive-policy improvement;
- contextual-bandit or RL performance;
- stress robustness;
- embodiment validity.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 2 outputs inherit and may add:

```text
public_eeg_only
offline_public_benchmark
low_calibration_protocol_only
decoder_measurement_only
not_calibrated_confidence
not_readiness_decision
not_clinical_validation
not_medical_device_evidence
not_real_patient_safety_evidence
not_rehabilitation_efficacy_evidence
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
proxy_or_pseudo_intent_labels
evaluation_only_labels_protected
diagnostic_only_if_missing_scores
diagnostic_only_if_missing_metric_dictionary
diagnostic_only_if_unmatched_keys
diagnostic_only_if_validation_incomplete
optional_stretch_if_compact_ssl
ensemble_control_not_iharq
dashboard_derived_not_primary
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Claims must be downgraded or blocked if:

- `PredictionRecord` lineage is incomplete;
- model registry linkage is missing;
- split leakage is unresolved;
- test labels influenced model/budget/control selection;
- score type or class order is missing;
- probability/logit/score fields required by downstream calibration are absent;
- metric dictionary entries are missing for thesis-facing metrics;
- A0/A4 comparison keys are unmatched;
- failed/skipped/unsupported model runs are hidden;
- optional stretch outputs are presented as core evidence;
- dashboard-derived outputs are used without source record lineage;
- limitations inherited from Phase 1 are removed or weakened.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 must later verify that:

- Phase 2 claims are measurement/reproducibility/baseline claims only;
- every thesis-facing metric links to a metric dictionary entry and matched comparison key;
- poor results and failed/skipped runs are not hidden;
- diagnostic-only outputs are not promoted;
- clinical/deployment/rehabilitation/patient-safety/medical-device claims are absent;
- Layer 10 views/cards/exports are not treated as upstream evidence.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 are capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels. They are not implementation phases, ablation IDs, record owners, or substitutes for Phase 2.

| Capability tier | Phase 2 contribution | Claim-maturity effect |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Strengthens public-data/protocol readiness by adding decoder-baseline evidence after Phase 1 | Can support a minimal baseline-measurement path if Phase 2 validates on at least one primary dataset; still no readiness claim |
| C1 | Prepares calibration and uncertainty work by providing raw probabilities/logits/scores and model registry links | Enables later reliability evidence but does not itself prove calibration quality |
| C2 | Provides baseline and ordinary-control comparators for IHARQ and RegimeRisk | Prevents later IHARQ/RegimeRisk claims from lacking raw/ordinary-control baselines |
| C3 | Provides decoder/provenance lineage for adaptive policy and simulated closed-loop phases | Supports later policy evaluation inputs but no adaptive-policy claim matures in Phase 2 |
| C4 | Provides provenance for stretch stress, bandit/RL, embodiment, dashboard, and final integration contexts | Stretch-tier claims remain downstream, simulation/proxy-only, and claim-safety bounded |

Phase 2 can improve the evidence maturity of C0/C1 groundwork, but it does not mature C2–C4 claims by itself. Optional compact SSL or stretch baselines may enrich later comparisons but must not be required for a lower-tier valid thesis stop if documented as skipped/unsupported.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative-result handling

Negative or weak Phase 2 outcomes are evidence, not merely failures. The phase must preserve:

- poor raw decoder performance;
- high subject/session variability;
- weak low-calibration performance;
- failed, skipped, unsupported, or non-convergent model runs;
- missing probabilities, logits, or decision scores;
- incompatible channel layouts, sampling rates, or input shapes;
- sparse label-budget conditions;
- ensemble/control incompatibility;
- A0/A4 controls that outperform later methods, if that occurs;
- diagnostic-only comparisons caused by missing keys or metric dictionary gaps.

These outcomes must be reflected through `FailureCaseIndex`, failed-run logs, `Layer2ReadinessReport`, `NegativeResultNote` triggers, diagnostic-only flags, limitation tags, and dashboard-warning inputs.

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency rules

Phase 2 is sufficient for downstream progression when it provides a fair and traceable decoder spine, not when every optional model family succeeds. Baseline sufficiency requires:

- at least one sanity/classical baseline for pipeline validity;
- one classical CSP/LDA/SVM-style baseline where compatible;
- one Riemannian or robust classical baseline where feasible;
- one compact neural baseline where feasible;
- explicit failed/skipped/unsupported reasons for missing families;
- A0 raw decoder evidence for selected datasets/splits/budgets;
- A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls evidence where compatible;
- model registry linkage for every prediction file;
- metric dictionary linkage or diagnostic-only status for thesis-facing metrics;
- low-calibration budget reporting;
- subject/session profile reporting where coverage permits;
- downstream-readiness validation.

If full model-family coverage is infeasible, Phase 2 should not fabricate missing evidence. It should document the coverage limitation, preserve negative results, and use fallback coverage honestly.

### 19.3 Strong-baseline honesty

If A4 ordinary longer-window/multi-window/ensemble controls or A2 simple confidence-threshold controls perform strongly, Phase 2 must preserve that result. Later IHARQ or adaptive-policy claims must be compared against these controls rather than hiding them.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure or missingness condition | Severity | Required handling |
|---|---|---|
| Missing or invalid `WindowRecord` / `SplitRecord` | Blocking | Return to Phase 1 repair path; do not train on affected data |
| Split leakage | Blocking for final evidence | Block or mark affected records diagnostic-only; no final claim use |
| Missing `LabelMapRecord` or class-order mapping | Blocking for affected outputs | Do not export thesis-ready probabilities/logits; repair mapping |
| Missing `PreprocessingRecord` or illegal fit scope | Blocking | Block affected model run |
| Missing seed or config hash | Blocking for thesis-ready comparison | Produce only diagnostic outputs until repaired |
| Missing model registry entry | Blocking for affected predictions | Orphan predictions cannot feed downstream phases |
| Missing probability vector/logits/decision score | Conditional | Mark `score_type`; exclude from calibration-dependent use or diagnostic-only |
| Label-only prediction records | Conditional | May support limited raw accuracy diagnostics but not calibration/uncertainty claims |
| Missing metric dictionary linkage | Diagnostic-only for thesis-facing metrics | Carry `MC-008`; no final metric claim |
| Missing matched comparison keys | Diagnostic-only | No final A0/A4 comparison claim |
| Sparse or invalid label budget | Diagnostic-only for affected budget | Record budget-failure note |
| Unsupported model family | Non-blocking if fallback coverage exists | Record skipped/unsupported reason in `ModelRegistryRecord` and failed-run logs |
| Failed/convergence error | Non-blocking if visible | Record in `FailureCaseIndex`; do not hide from denominator/coverage tables |
| Incompatible ensemble/control alignment | Diagnostic-only for affected control | Restrict to compatible groups; record missing-model/misalignment reasons |
| Incomplete subject/session coverage | Diagnostic-only for affected profile | Mark profile ambiguous |
| Compact SSL infeasible | Non-blocking/stretch omission | Record skipped/unsupported reason; do not weaken core claim |
| Dashboard source path stale | Blocking for dashboard/export only | Keep source evidence but mark dashboard/export not ready |
| Clinical/deployment interpretation appears | Claim-safety blocking | Layer 0 rejects or downgrades claim |

### 20.1 Frozen/update-enabled separation

Phase 2 does not produce adaptive policies, policy updates, stress schedules, simulation sessions, contextual-bandit updates, RL updates, or embodiment feedback. However, because its prediction records later feed frozen and update-enabled contexts, Phase 2 must preserve immutable frozen prediction histories, split roles, model IDs, seeds, config hashes, and source record IDs. Later update-enabled phases may reference Phase 2 records but must not modify them. If a future adaptive phase updates a policy based on Phase 2-derived evidence, that update belongs to downstream `PolicyUpdateTrace` governance and not Phase 2.

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

Repository paths remain architecture-supported conceptual paths until final reconciliation under `MC-009`. Phase 2 outputs should nevertheless follow the repository expectations below and record concrete paths/hashes in manifests.

| Artifact family | Expected conceptual path or role |
|---|---|
| Decoder configs | `configs/decoders/` with families for sanity, CSP/LDA, CSP/SVM, Riemannian, EEGNet/TCN or compact neural models, compact SSL where feasible, and ensembles |
| Layer 2 experiment configs | `configs/layer2_experiments/label_budgets.yaml`, `split_policy.yaml`, `seed_policy.yaml` |
| Prediction schema | `records/prediction_records/prediction_schema.yaml` |
| Prediction records | `records/prediction_records/` in CSV or Parquet, preferably Parquet for large per-window logs |
| Model registry | `records/model_registry/`, including registry tables, YAML, `model_registry_schema.yaml`, and validation reports |
| Baseline metric records | `records/baseline_metric_records/` with metric-dictionary references, matched-comparison keys, aggregation level, and diagnostic-only flags |
| Low-calibration outputs | `records/low_calibration_curves/` and `figures/layer2_low_calibration/` |
| Subject profiles | `records/subject_profiles/` and `figures/layer2_subject_profiles/` |
| Ensemble/control records | `records/ensemble_records/` |
| Failure-case index | `records/failure_case_index/` and `reports/layer2_failure_cases/` where supported |
| Layer 2 readiness reports | `reports/layer2_readiness/` or run-local validation folders |
| Conditional leakage warnings | warning/report location linked from `Layer2ReadinessReport`, `ValidationReport`, or run manifest; concrete path remains subject to `MC-009` |
| Model artifacts/checkpoints | `models/layer2_decoders/` |
| Training logs | `logs/training_logs/` |
| Inference logs | `logs/inference_logs/` |
| Failed/skipped-run logs | `logs/failed_runs/` |
| `ModelCard` / `BenchmarkCard` source bundles and rendered later cards | `cards/model_cards/` and `cards/layer2_benchmark_cards/` as source/rendered separation permits |
| Validation tests/reports | Schema, split-integrity, model-registry, prediction-record, score-availability, class-order, metric-dictionary, and consumer-readiness validation artifacts |
| Phase 2 manifest | Phase 2 handoff manifest with source paths, output paths, hashes, schema versions, validation statuses, diagnostic-only flags, and limitation tags |

Every thesis figure or table derived from Phase 2 must identify source `PredictionRecord` paths, registry version, split ID, budget ID, model IDs, aggregation rule, metric definition, generated figure/table path, config hash, seed policy, and limitation tags.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Required handoff to Phase 3

Phase 3 may begin serious calibration/uncertainty work only when it receives:

- validated `PredictionRecord` files;
- validated `ModelRegistryRecord` entries;
- probability vectors where available;
- logits where available;
- decision scores where applicable;
- declared `score_type`;
- declared `class_order`;
- evaluation-only `label_true` where permitted;
- `split_id` and `split_role`;
- `label_budget_id`;
- `model_id`, `decoder_id`, and `model_family`;
- `seed`, `config_hash`, and schema version;
- score-field missingness flags;
- model registry linkage;
- matched comparison keys;
- `Layer2ReadinessReport`;
- any `LeakageWarningRecord` affecting the prediction, model, budget, or split package.

If only label predictions exist and probability/logit/decision-score fields are missing, Phase 3 may use those records only for limited diagnostics or must exclude them from calibration-dependent evidence with documented reasons.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phases 4–15

| Downstream phase | Phase 2 handoff content | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 4 — IHARQ-lite evidence verification | Prediction identifiers, model IDs, raw score/confidence fields where later calibrated, ensemble/control summaries, failure diagnostics | Phase 2 does not produce IHARQ decisions |
| Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust | Time-indexed prediction logs, subject/session profiles, recent performance/error histories where available | Phase 2 does not produce regime/trust states |
| Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Decoder/model/budget lineage through later readiness contexts | Phase 2 does not produce policy records |
| Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer | Frozen prediction histories through later policy context | Phase 2 does not produce deferral actions |
| Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness | Prediction histories and ordering keys for replay lineage | Phase 2 does not produce transitions or rewards |
| Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite | Prediction/model/source lineage for later stress conditioning | Phase 2 does not produce stress profiles/schedules |
| Phase 10 — Contextual bandit | Frozen prediction-lineage inputs through later simulated/policy contexts | Phase 2 does not produce bandit updates |
| Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | Frozen prediction-lineage inputs through later simulated/policy contexts | Phase 2 does not produce RL updates |
| Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo | Provenance/readiness input lineage through later policy/embodiment mappings | Phase 2 does not produce embodiment evidence |
| Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison | Provenance/readiness input lineage through later replay mappings | Phase 2 does not produce OpenSim evidence |
| Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards | Validated source records, metric records, logs, card source bundles, warnings, manifest inputs | Layer 10 renders derived outputs only |
| Phase 15 — Final thesis integration | Source-to-claim evidence inputs, baseline tables, limitations, diagnostic-only statuses | Phase 2 supports bounded baseline claims only |

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 2 is done when all conditions below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Validated Phase 1 source records and manifests are readable and not overwritten.
- Selected model-family list, label-budget policy, seed policy, and configs are declared before interpretation.
- Per-window or per-trial `PredictionRecord` files exist for every selected dataset, subject, session where available, split, label budget, seed, and required model family intended for downstream comparison.
- Every prediction file links to a validated `ModelRegistryRecord`.
- Probability vectors, logits, or decision scores are exported where available; missing score fields are explicitly marked with `score_type` and diagnostic/ineligibility status.
- `class_order` and `LabelMapRecord` mapping are validated.
- `BaselineMetricRecord` artifacts exist for declared metrics and aggregation levels.
- `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` artifacts exist for declared budget families.
- `SubjectProfileRecord` artifacts exist where coverage permits; incomplete profiles are marked ambiguous.
- `EnsembleControlRecord` and A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries exist where model/window/class alignment permits.
- Longer-window or multi-window controls include delay-burden notes where applicable.
- Training logs, inference logs, failed/skipped-run logs, and `FailureCaseIndex` are produced.
- Any invalid split use detected during Phase 2 creates a `LeakageWarningRecord`, blocks affected final-evaluation use or marks it exploratory/diagnostic-only, and does not mutate validated Phase 1 records.
- A0 raw-decoder evidence tables are produced.
- A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries are produced where compatible.
- Metric dictionary linkage exists for thesis-facing metrics or the affected metric artifacts are diagnostic-only.
- Matched-comparison keys are complete for A0/A4 final comparisons or affected comparisons are diagnostic-only.
- `Layer2ReadinessReport` marks each downstream consumer path as ready, diagnostic-only, or blocked.
- Layer 10 source/derived separation is preserved.
- Layer 0 limitation tags and forbidden-claim boundaries are attached to all outputs.
- Negative results and poor baselines are visible.
- Optional compact SSL/foundation-style evidence is included only if feasible and documented; otherwise skipped/unsupported status is explicit.
- Phase 2 handoff manifest is created with paths, hashes, schema versions, validation status, diagnostic flags, and limitation tags.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 3 and later thesis-facing decoder-derived evidence must not proceed from Phase 2 outputs if any of the following remain unresolved for the affected dataset/model/split/budget:

- source records do not validate;
- split leakage exists;
- label-map or class-order mapping is ambiguous;
- preprocessing fit scope is illegal;
- model registry linkage is missing;
- seed/config hash is missing;
- prediction schema validation fails;
- evaluation-only labels leak into decision-time features;
- metric dictionary entries required for thesis-facing metrics are absent and no diagnostic-only downgrade is applied;
- matched comparison keys are missing and no diagnostic-only downgrade is applied;
- failed/skipped/unsupported runs are hidden;
- claim-safety tags are missing;
- clinical/deployment/rehabilitation/patient-safety claims are implied.

### 26.3 Completion statement

When done, Phase 2 hands forward a validated decoder evidence spine: prediction records, model provenance, baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject profiles, ordinary-control baselines, failure transparency, and downstream-readiness reports. This spine enables Phase 3 calibration/uncertainty and later reliability/readiness modules while preserving the boundary that Phase 2 provides decoder measurement evidence only, not calibrated trust, readiness decisions, clinical safety, deployment readiness, or rehabilitation efficacy.

| Indirect downstream contexts | `Phase 7`, `Phase 8`, `Phase 9`, `Phase 10`, `Phase 11`, `Phase 12`, and `Phase 13` through later readiness, policy, simulation, stress, bandit/RL, and embodiment handoffs; Phase 3 does not produce those later records |
| Evidence role | Reliability-feature gate and calibration/selective-prediction evidence producer |
| Empirical-output status | Produces derived empirical reliability evidence from already validated `PredictionRecord` inputs |
| Source-record status | Does not overwrite Layer 1 clean records or Layer 2 prediction records |
| Dashboard status | Produces dashboard-readable source metric records and card inputs; Layer 10 later renders derived dashboard/card/export outputs |
| Claim status | Supports bounded public-EEG calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, and high-confidence-wrong visibility claims only |
| Forbidden status | Does not support clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, or real deployment readiness |

Phase 3 is the architecture-defined reliability-feature gate. It converts raw decoder scores and probability evidence from Phase 2 into calibrated probabilities, uncertainty features, threshold registries, selective-prediction baselines, reliability audits, split-integrity reports, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, and matched operating-point evidence. It prevents downstream IHARQ, RegimeRisk, adaptive policy, simulation, stress, embodiment, dashboard, and thesis claims from treating raw decoder confidence as trustworthy merely because raw accuracy is acceptable.

Phase 3 is not a policy phase, not a simulation phase, not a dashboard-rendering phase, not a claim-safety evidence owner, and not a clinical-safety validation phase. It produces reliability evidence that downstream layers may consume under strict lineage, split, metric-dictionary, and limitation boundaries.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 3 converts Phase 2 decoder evidence into reliability evidence. Its purpose is to make raw decoder confidence auditable before IHARQ, RegimeRisk, Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, simulated closed-loop readiness, stress testing, bandit/RL policies, embodiment demos, dashboards, and final thesis claims use decoder outputs.

Phase 3 answers the core reliability question:

```text
Are the decoder scores trustworthy enough, calibrated enough, uncertainty-aware enough, and threshold-governed enough to serve as fair inputs and fair baselines for later evidence-verification and policy comparisons?
```

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 3 controls the following bottlenecks:

- raw confidence being treated as calibrated confidence;
- high accuracy hiding high-confidence wrong predictions;
- threshold baselines being tuned on final test labels;
- calibration methods being selected using illegal split roles;
- uncertainty features being untraceable or label-leaking;
- selective-prediction baselines being unfairly compared with IHARQ or Adaptive-IHARQ;
- later policy/context records depending on missing or ineligible calibration outputs;
- dashboard reliability figures being generated without source-record lineage;
- calibration failure or threshold sufficiency being hidden rather than recorded as negative evidence;
- A1–A3 evidence lacking matched coverage, matched cost, metric dictionary, or comparison-key support.

### 4.3 Thesis evidence role

Phase 3 supports thesis evidence that accuracy alone is not enough for readiness claims in low-calibration neural-intent decoding. It contributes:

- reliability diagrams;
- ECE-style summaries where metric dictionary entries are available;
- Brier and NLL components where label support permits;
- calibrated-vs-raw confidence comparisons;
- entropy, margin, confidence, variation-ratio, disagreement, and related uncertainty summaries where available;
- high-confidence-wrong audits;
- selective-prediction and risk-coverage curves;
- matched-coverage and matched-cost operating-point tables;
- threshold lineage and leakage-status records;
- negative-result notes when calibration fails or threshold/selective baselines are sufficient.

### 4.4 Non-purpose

Phase 3 does not:

- train new decoder families as a substitute for Phase 2;
- rewrite or repair Phase 1 source records;
- overwrite `PredictionRecord` outputs;
- produce IHARQ decisions;
- produce RegimeRisk states;
- produce readiness policies, deferral actions, simulation transitions, stress profiles, embodiment outcomes, contextual-bandit updates, reinforcement-learning policy updates, dashboard views, or final thesis claims;
- claim that calibrated probabilities are safe, clinically valid, deployment-ready, or rehabilitation-effective.

### 5.1 Layer participation

| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, negative-result visibility, and forbidden-claim boundaries | Does not produce empirical calibration evidence |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Provides immutable source lineage, split roles, labels, window/trial identifiers, label maps, preprocessing IDs, artifact flags where available, and low-calibration budget definitions | Clean source records must not be overwritten |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Provides `PredictionRecord`, model lineage, score fields, A0/A4 baseline/control evidence, and readiness reports | Decoder evidence remains Layer 2-owned; Phase 3 derives reliability evidence from it |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Primary producing layer for calibration, uncertainty, threshold, selective-prediction, reliability, leakage, and matched operating-point artifacts | Owns Phase 3 outputs |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Downstream consumer of calibrated confidence, uncertainty features, threshold registries, selective baselines, and high-confidence-wrong diagnostics | Does not own Phase 3 records |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Optional downstream consumer of temporal uncertainty signals and reliability summaries where temporal ordering is valid | Does not own calibration records |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Downstream consumer of split-safe, label-free uncertainty and threshold context for evidence-quality and policy-context preparation | Must not consume evaluation-only labels or high-confidence-wrong labels as decision-time features |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Later consumer through readiness/policy context; may replay frozen calibrated/uncertainty histories | Does not update calibration in frozen evaluation |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Later consumer through stress eligibility, matched clean/stressed comparisons, and source lineage | Does not mutate Phase 3 clean derived records |
| Layer 9 — Embodiment-state/outcome/demo records | Later consumer through policy/embodiment provenance only | No real embodiment safety claim from Phase 3 |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, Export, and Reproducibility | Reads Phase 3 records, warnings, card inputs, metrics, manifests, and renders derived views/cards/exports later | Does not recompute hidden calibration or retune thresholds |

## 6. Registry Issue Intake and Impact Assessment

| Registry issue or candidate item | Relevance to Phase 3 | Impact | Required handling in Phase 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MC-001` `TrialRecord` / trial-level source representation | Phase 3 must join predictions to trial/window identifiers and preserve matched-comparison keys | Missing or ambiguous trial identity can break calibration grouping, high-confidence-wrong traceability, matched operating points, and dashboard filters | Preserve `trial_id` where present; otherwise rely on `WindowRecord`/`PredictionRecord` linkage and mark affected comparisons diagnostic-only if matching is incomplete |
| `MC-007` `DashboardMetricRecord` boundary | Phase 3 produces dashboard-readable metric records such as `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` | Source metric records may be confused with Layer 10-generated views/cards | Treat Layer 3 metric artifacts as source inputs for Layer 10, not dashboard-generated outputs |
| `MC-008` `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema and path | Calibration metrics and risk-coverage metrics require metric definitions | Missing dictionary entries weaken thesis-ready comparison and reproducibility | Require metric dictionary references for ECE, Brier, NLL, coverage, risk, retained accuracy, wrong-accept, high-confidence-wrong, matched cost, and matched coverage; otherwise mark metric outputs diagnostic-only |
| `MC-009` repository paths and storage homes | Phase 3 stores derived records, reports, parameter files, metrics, figures, and manifests | Concrete path uncertainty can break dashboard and reproducibility loading | Use conceptual registry-supported locations while carrying path status as unresolved until repository reconciliation |
| `MC-010` lifecycle/schema maturity | Several Phase 3 artifacts are final, normalized candidate, or diagnostic-only | Candidate records could be promoted silently | Preserve lifecycle/status labels such as `canonical_record`, `normalized_candidate`, `evaluation_artifact`, and `diagnostic_only` |
| `MC-011` Layer 10 evidence boundary | Phase 3 metrics and card inputs are read by Layer 10 | Dashboard cards may be mistaken for primary evidence | Store source IDs, metric dictionary IDs, configs, seeds, schema versions, and manifests; keep Layer 10 outputs derived/non-primary |
| `MC-012` Layer 0 evidence boundary | Phase 3 limitation and claim tags are audited by Layer 0 | Claim audit artifacts may be mistaken for empirical evidence | Preserve Layer 0 as audit/governance only; Phase 3 remains the empirical reliability producer |
| `CalibrationEligibilityTable` candidate status | Determines whether a calibration method is legal under sparse/missing-class budgets | Hidden method eligibility can create unfair calibration comparisons | Produce or prepare it as `normalized_candidate`/validation-report table; do not treat as final canonical record unless registry promotion occurs |
| `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` candidate status | Required for Layer 10 reliability panels | Schema/path may not be final | Mark `normalized_candidate` dashboard-readable metric source; include source lineage and export lineage |
| `HighConfidenceWrongTable` diagnostic status | Core thesis diagnostic for accuracy hiding risk-relevant errors | Could leak evaluation labels into policy inputs if mishandled | Treat as evaluation-only/diagnostic-only; never use as decision-time feature |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` path/status | Required for A1–A3 fair comparison and downstream IHARQ fairness | Missing matched keys block fair claims | Produce only when matched keys and metric definitions are complete; otherwise diagnostic-only |
| `LeakageWarningRecord` conditional production | May be produced by Phase 2 or Phase 3 validation | Storage/ownership can be ambiguous when detected in different phases | Phase 3 produces it only when calibration/threshold/test leakage is detected; link it to affected records and block final evaluation use |
| `ReliabilityCard` source/render boundary | Phase 3 prepares reliability-card inputs; Layer 10 renders final card | Cards may become untraceable summaries | Export source bundles with limitations; Layer 10-rendered card remains derived |

| Calibration config | Phase 0 config family / Phase 3 run config | method family, calibration split ID, scope, budget, fallback rule, seed/config hash | Missing config blocks reproducibility |
| Uncertainty-feature config | Phase 0 config family / Phase 3 run config | allowed features, label-free feature rule, optional ensemble/disagreement rule, conformal/temporal flags if used | Unsupported or label-leaking features blocked |
| Threshold-selection rules | Phase 0 config family / Phase 3 run config | selection split, metric, criterion, allowed consumers, leakage status, threshold versioning rule | Test-tuned thresholds marked oracle diagnostic only |
| Metric dictionary entries or placeholders | Phase 0/evaluation framework | definitions for ECE-like summaries, Brier, NLL, coverage, risk, retained accuracy, retained error, high-confidence-wrong rate, matched cost, matched coverage | Missing entries make affected metrics diagnostic-only |
| Run metadata and manifest conventions | Phase 0 | run ID, config hash, seed, schema version, producer module, phase ID, validation status, source paths, output paths | Missing lineage blocks dashboard/final use |

### 9.2 Conditional or optional inputs

| Input | Status | Allowed use |
|---|---|---|
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` | Conditional | Auxiliary limitation/context for quality-aware calibration interpretation; absence does not prove clean signals |
| `SubjectProfileRecord` | Conditional | Group-wise reliability context where coverage is sufficient |
| `LowCalibrationCurveRecord` | Conditional | Calibration-budget analysis and sparse-budget limitation context |
| `EnsembleControlRecord` | Conditional | Model disagreement, variation-ratio, and ordinary-control comparison where class/model/window alignment is complete |
| Labels/correctness fields | Evaluation-only | Calibration fitting/evaluation only on legal splits; never decision-time features |
| Temporal ordering fields | Conditional | Past-only temporal summaries and optional Layer 5 diagnostic handoff; missing ordering blocks temporal reliability analysis |
| Conformal calibration data | Optional/stretch | Conformal proxy fields only when split-safe and declared |

### 9.3 Explicitly forbidden inputs

- Final test labels for calibration fitting, method selection, threshold selection, or threshold retuning.
- Evaluation-only correctness labels as decision-time policy features.
- Dashboard-rendered metrics or screenshots as calibration inputs.
- Layer 0 claim-review artifacts as empirical calibration evidence.
- Future simulation, stress, embodiment, bandit, RL, or policy-update outcomes as Phase 3 calibration inputs.
- Manually repaired source records unless issued as versioned upstream records with validation lineage.

### 9.4 Exported-field alias and schema-governance rule

Phase 3 may read internal or legacy field aliases only through an explicit schema-mapping step. Exported Phase 3 records must use canonical names and must preserve the mapped lineage.

| Internal or legacy alias | Required exported or canonical form | Phase 3 handling |
|---|---|---|
| `y_true` | `label_true` | Allowed only as an ingestion alias; exported labels remain evaluation-only and split-governed |
| `y_pred` | `predicted_class` | Allowed only as an ingestion alias; exported predictions must preserve model, split, class-order, and label-map lineage |
| `prob_vector` | `probability_vector` | Allowed only as an ingestion alias; exported probability vectors must carry `score_type`, `class_order`, and calibration eligibility status |
| Unmapped score or confidence aliases | Registry/schema-defined score fields or declared score fallback | Missing or ambiguous mappings make the affected decoder ineligible for calibration-dependent claims |

This rule is a correction and clarification rather than a new artifact. It preserves the registry requirement that aliases be normalized before export and prevents downstream layers or Layer 10 from reading informal notebook names as canonical evidence fields.

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 3 evidence production follows an evidence-level chain, not a function-level implementation playbook:

```text
validated Phase 1 source records
+ validated Phase 2 prediction/model records
+ Phase 0 schema/config/metric/manifest conventions
→ split and score eligibility validation
→ calibration fitting on legal calibration/validation splits only
→ calibrated probability and reliability records
→ label-free uncertainty-feature extraction
→ selective-prediction and threshold baseline evaluation
→ threshold registry with leakage status and allowed consumers
→ reliability audit, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, and group/budget summaries
→ A1-A3 matched operating-point evidence with metric dictionary linkage
→ negative-result and diagnostic-only annotations
→ dashboard-readable source bundles and Phase 3 handoff manifest
```

### 12.1 Calibration evidence chain

1. Validate that every candidate `PredictionRecord` is joinable to its source records, split roles, model registry entry, class order, label map, run ID, config hash, seed, and label budget.
2. Separate calibration fitting, threshold selection, validation, and final test/evaluation roles according to Phase 1/Phase 0 split conventions.
3. Fit only declared calibration methods on allowed splits.
4. Apply calibration mappings to eligible validation/test prediction records without changing original `PredictionRecord` values.
5. Save `CalibrationRecord` outputs with raw and calibrated probabilities/confidence, calibration method/scope, split, source IDs, metrics/components, config hash, and validation status.

### 12.2 Uncertainty evidence chain

1. Compute label-free uncertainty features from prediction/calibration outputs and optional ensemble-compatible outputs.
2. Preserve feature definitions, score type, class order, source IDs, and config hash.
3. Exclude correctness labels, true labels, high-confidence-wrong status, or future outcomes from decision-time uncertainty features.
4. Save `UncertaintyRecord` outputs for downstream IHARQ and policy contexts.

### 12.3 Selective-prediction and threshold evidence chain

1. Use registered threshold-selection rules and permitted validation/selection splits.
2. Evaluate confidence, entropy, margin, calibrated-score, and other declared threshold/selective baselines.
3. Export `SelectivePredictionRecord` outputs with coverage, rejection rate, retained accuracy, retained error, risk, high-confidence-wrong rate, and lineage.
4. Register thresholds in `ThresholdRegistryRecord` with source split, selection criterion, metric, run identifier, version, allowed consumers, and leakage status.
5. Export `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` only when matched coverage/cost keys are complete.

### 12.4 Reliability, negative-result, and dashboard-source chain

1. Produce `ReliabilityAuditReport`, reliability-bin tables, group-wise summaries, and calibration-budget analyses where coverage permits.
2. Produce `HighConfidenceWrongTable` using evaluation labels only for offline analysis.
3. Produce `NegativeResultNote` when calibration fails, uncertainty/selective baselines are sufficient, thresholds dominate later candidates, sparse budgets invalidate methods, or metric/matching limits weaken claims.
4. Produce `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` and ReliabilityCard source inputs with source IDs, metric dictionary IDs, filters, configs, seeds, schema versions, limitation tags, and export lineage.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Failure outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 foundation gate | Schemas, configs, validators, run IDs, config hash, seeds, manifests, metric placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, and dashboard/export placeholders exist | Block or diagnostic-only depending on missing item |
| Phase 1 source-record gate | Source records validate and remain immutable | Block affected outputs |
| Phase 2 prediction spine gate | `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` validate | Block calibration for affected model/split/budget |
| Score availability gate | Probability vector/logits/decision scores and `score_type` are present or explicitly missing | Missing scores create calibration ineligibility or limited diagnostics |
| Class-order / label-map gate | `class_order` matches `LabelMapRecord` | Block metrics/calibration for affected records |
| Split-role gate | Calibration, threshold-selection, validation, and test roles are legal | Leakage warning and final-claim block if invalid |
| Preprocessing fit-scope gate | Preprocessing did not fit on disallowed evaluation/test data | Block final use if illegal |
| Calibration method eligibility gate | Chosen method has enough classes/examples under declared budget | Fall back to simpler declared method or mark invalid; no test-driven method selection |
| Calibration parameter lineage gate | Calibration parameters link to config, split, seed, run, model, and source predictions | Block reproducibility if missing |
| Uncertainty feature gate | Features are label-free for decision-time use and source-defined | Remove/diagnostic-only if label-leaking or undefined |
| Threshold registry gate | Threshold selection rule, split, metric, version, allowed consumers, and leakage status are recorded | Block downstream threshold use |
| Metric dictionary gate | Every thesis-facing metric links to `MetricDictionaryEntry` | Diagnostic-only if missing |
| Matched operating-point gate | A1–A3 comparisons have matched keys, coverage/cost definitions, and source IDs | Diagnostic-only if incomplete |
| Negative-result gate | Calibration failure, threshold sufficiency, sparse budget, leakage, and missingness are not hidden | Block claim-evidence approval if hidden |
| Dashboard source-bundle gate | Dashboard-readable outputs have lineage, validation, limitations, and manifests | Not dashboard-ready if missing |
| Claim-safety gate | Forbidden claims are not implied; limitations attached | Block or downgrade affected claims |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 3 exits successfully when:

- every eligible Phase 2 decoder variant has either validated `CalibrationRecord` and `UncertaintyRecord` outputs or an explicit ineligible/diagnostic-only status;
- calibration methods are fit only on allowed calibration/validation splits;
- threshold-selection rules are registered and no final test labels are used for tuning;
- `SelectivePredictionRecord` outputs and risk/coverage curves exist for declared baselines;
- `ThresholdRegistryRecord` entries exist for every threshold used downstream;
- `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` outputs exist for A1–A3 comparisons or diagnostic-only reasons are explicit;
- `ReliabilityAuditReport`, `HighConfidenceWrongTable`, and negative-result notes are produced where applicable;
- leakage checks pass or affected outputs are blocked/diagnostic-only;
- metric dictionary linkage exists for thesis-facing metrics or affected metrics are downgraded;
- dashboard-readable metric records/source bundles are exported with lineage and limitation tags;
- downstream mock or read-only consumers in Layers 4, 5, 6, 10, and evaluation scripts can read exported records without manual reinterpretation.


### 14.2 A1–A3 comparison preservation

| Evaluation context | Required matched condition | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A1 calibrated decoder | Raw and calibrated predictions share dataset/model/split/window/seed/budget keys | Missing raw comparator, illegal calibration split, missing metric dictionary, or unmatched model/window keys |
| A2 simple registered-threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Threshold selected on legal split and evaluated against matched raw/calibrated records | Test-tuned threshold, missing threshold registry, unmatched coverage/cost keys |
| A3 uncertainty and selective prediction | Uncertainty/selective records share prediction/calibration/source keys and matched coverage/cost definitions | Label-leaking uncertainty feature, missing selective record, unmatched coverage/cost keys |
| A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls as upstream context | Phase 2 ordinary-control evidence remains matched on prediction/source keys | Reclassified A4 controls must not be called A3 by Phase 3 |
| A5+ downstream comparisons | IHARQ/policy/stress/embodiment records must reference Phase 3 source IDs and threshold versions | Missing Phase 3 lineage blocks fair downstream improvement claims |

### 14.3 Handling missing keys

If any comparison key is missing, Phase 3 must:

1. preserve the source record unchanged;
2. write the missingness in the relevant report or manifest;
3. mark the affected comparison `diagnostic_only` or `incomplete`;
4. prevent thesis-ready improvement or sufficiency claims for that comparison;
5. carry the issue to the handoff manifest and Layer 10 warning inputs.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 A0–A13 treatment

A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata only. Phase 3 produces records used by A1–A3 and prepares fair baselines for downstream A5–A13 comparisons. No ablation owns a canonical record.

### 15.2 Direct Phase 3 evaluation linkage

| Evaluation ID | Evaluation meaning in the architecture/registry | Phase 3 role | Explicit evaluation artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | Raw decoder | Consumed as upstream comparator from Phase 2 | A0 raw-decoder evidence tables, source `PredictionRecord` IDs |
| A1 | Calibration / calibrated decoder | Phase 3 directly produces/strengthens records used by this evaluation context | `CalibrationRecord`, calibration deltas, reliability tables, ECE/Brier/NLL entries, before/after metric tables, `ReliabilityAuditReport` |
| A2 | Simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Phase 3 produces/strengthens records used by this evaluation context | `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, threshold-comparison tables, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, matched coverage/cost threshold rows |
| A3 | Uncertainty and selective prediction | Phase 3 directly produces/strengthens records used by this evaluation context | `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, risk-coverage curves, accuracy-coverage curves, uncertainty summaries, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` |
| A4 | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Consumed from Phase 2 as ordinary-control context where compatible | Phase 2 A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls summaries and `EnsembleControlRecord`; not Phase 3-owned |
| A5–A6 | IHARQ-lite and IHARQ plus evidence-quality contexts | Prepared through calibrated/uncertainty/threshold evidence | Phase 3 source IDs, threshold registry IDs, negative-result notes, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics |
| A7 | IHARQ plus RegimeRisk | Prepared through temporal uncertainty/reliability inputs where legal | Past-only temporal uncertainty summaries where available |
| A8–A11 | Deferral, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, bandit, RL | Prepared through split-safe uncertainty and threshold context | Label-free `UncertaintyRecord`, threshold registry references, diagnostic-only restrictions |
| A12–A13 | Stress and embodiment demo | Prepared only through source/reliability lineage for later stress/embodiment evaluation | Phase 3 source IDs, limitation tags, matched keys |

### 15.3 Explicit evaluation artifacts

Phase 3 must produce or prepare:

- `CalibrationRecord` outputs for A1;
- calibration deltas against A0 raw outputs;
- `ReliabilityAuditReport` and reliability-bin/source tables;
- `UncertaintyRecord` outputs for A3;
- `SelectivePredictionRecord` outputs for A2 threshold / A3 uncertainty/selective-prediction contexts;
- `ThresholdRegistryRecord` entries for every threshold/operating point used downstream;
- `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` for matched coverage/cost operating points;
- `HighConfidenceWrongTable` for diagnostic analysis;
- `CalibrationEligibilityTable` for sparse/missing-class/method eligibility;
- `SplitIntegrityReport` and conditional `LeakageWarningRecord`;
- `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or missing-entry diagnostic flags;
- `MatchedComparisonReport` inputs for Phase 15 and evaluation scripts;
- `NegativeResultNote` entries where calibration fails, thresholding is sufficient, selective prediction is sufficient, or evidence is incomplete;
- `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` entries for leakage, missing score fields, missing matched keys, or missing metric definitions;
- dashboard-readable source metric bundles and figure-source manifests.

### 15.4 Frozen/update separation

Phase 3 does not perform update-enabled adaptive policy learning. Its calibrated, uncertainty, threshold, and selective records must be treated as frozen evidence inputs for later held-out evaluation unless a later phase explicitly creates a versioned downstream adaptation branch with `PolicyUpdateTrace` and disabled-update audit rules. Phase 3 calibration parameters and thresholds must not be re-fit using downstream simulation, stress, embodiment, bandit, RL, or final test outcomes.
