## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed bounded claims

Phase 3 may support bounded claims only when records validate and metric/matched-comparison requirements are met:

- Public EEG decoder confidence can be evaluated for calibration quality under declared splits and budgets.
- Calibration and uncertainty artifacts reveal reliability structure not visible from raw accuracy alone.
- High-confidence wrong predictions can be audited under evaluation-only label protection.
- Thresholding and selective prediction can be compared as fair baselines at matched coverage or matched cost.
- Reliability, calibration, and uncertainty evidence can be made dashboard-readable and reproducible.
- Negative results, including calibration failure or threshold sufficiency, are valid evidence and constrain later novelty claims.

### 17.2 Forbidden claims

Phase 3 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- calibrated probabilities guaranteeing correctness;
- uncertainty features proving safe action;
- thresholds being safety approvals;
- high-confidence-wrong labels being available at decision time;
- dashboard cards being primary empirical evidence.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 3 outputs must carry applicable tags such as:

```text
public_eeg_only
offline_public_benchmark
low_calibration_protocol_only
calibration_visibility_only
uncertainty_evidence_only
selective_prediction_baseline_only
threshold_registry_not_safety_approval
not_readiness_decision
not_clinical_validation
not_medical_device_evidence
not_real_patient_safety_evidence
not_rehabilitation_efficacy_evidence
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
proxy_or_pseudo_intent_labels
evaluation_only_labels_protected
diagnostic_only_if_missing_scores
diagnostic_only_if_illegal_split_use
diagnostic_only_if_missing_metric_dictionary
diagnostic_only_if_unmatched_keys
diagnostic_only_if_validation_incomplete
diagnostic_only_if_sparse_budget_invalid
dashboard_derived_not_primary
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Any Phase 3 reliability, calibration, selective-prediction, or uncertainty claim must be downgraded or blocked if:

- calibration is fit or selected using final test labels;
- threshold selection uses final test labels;
- prediction score fields are missing or invalid;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- matched keys are incomplete;
- class-order or label-map mapping is ambiguous;
- low-calibration budgets are sparse or missing classes and the method is not eligible;
- high-confidence-wrong evidence is used as a policy feature;
- downstream dashboard outputs hide negative results;
- source lineage, config hash, seed, schema version, or validation status is missing.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 review for Phase 3 must verify:

- all outputs have claim-safety tags;
- clinical/deployment/rehabilitation/patient-safety language is absent;
- diagnostic-only status is preserved;
- negative-result notes are visible;
- threshold sufficiency is not hidden to make IHARQ/adaptive modules appear stronger;
- Layer 10 dashboard outputs remain derived/non-primary;
- final claim-evidence mapping is prepared but not treated as empirical evidence by itself.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 are capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels, not implementation phases, ablation IDs, or artifact owners.

| Capability tier | Phase 3 effect | Claim-maturity boundary |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Strengthened by calibration, uncertainty, and selective-prediction evidence over public EEG decoder outputs | C0 can support public-data reliability/uncertainty characterization if Phase 1–3 evidence validates |
| C1 | Prepared but not matured; Phase 3 provides calibration, uncertainty, threshold, and selective-prediction evidence that later IHARQ-lite and RegimeRisk phases consume | C1 requires Phases 4–5 outputs; Phase 3 alone must not be described as completed C1 evidence |
| C2 | Prepared through fair A2 threshold and A3 uncertainty/selective-prediction baselines for later supervised evidence-quality, Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, and simulated readiness comparisons | No adaptive-policy or simulation claim matures in Phase 3 |
| C3 | Prepared through split-safe, label-free uncertainty features and threshold lineage for later contextual-bandit/RL inputs after simulation and policy phases exist | No bandit, RL, or update-enabled policy claim matures in Phase 3 |
| C4 | Prepared only through lineage and limitation propagation for later stress/embodiment/dashboard evidence | No stress, embodiment, or final dashboard claim matures in Phase 3 |

Phase 3 can be a defensible thesis stopping point for C0 public-data reliability-spine evidence if it produces complete A1–A3 calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction records, metric dictionary linkage, matched operating points, negative-result notes, limitation tags, and reproducibility manifests. It prepares C1, C2, C3, and C4, but those tiers remain incomplete until their required later phases produce and validate their own records.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

Phase 3 must treat negative results as evidence, not failures to hide.

### 19.1 Required negative-result cases

| Negative or sufficiency condition | Required handling | Claim impact |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration does not improve ECE/Brier/NLL or worsens them | Produce `NegativeResultNote`; keep raw-vs-calibrated evidence visible | Narrow claim to reliability audit/visibility, not calibration improvement |
| No-calibration baseline is best | Record method comparison and fallback status | Blocks claim that advanced calibration is necessary |
| Thresholding is sufficient at matched coverage/cost | Produce threshold-sufficiency note | Later IHARQ/adaptive novelty claims must be narrowed or compared against threshold sufficiency |
| Selective prediction matches later proposed improvements | Preserve A3 sufficiency evidence | Later modules cannot claim added value unless matched improvement exists |
| Calibration split is sparse or missing classes | Produce `CalibrationEligibilityTable` and sparse-budget warning | Method invalid or diagnostic-only under affected budget |
| Probability/logit/score fields are missing | Mark decoder ineligible for calibrated use | Blocks A1–A3 calibrated evidence for affected decoder |
| High-confidence-wrong clusters are severe | Produce diagnostic table and limitation note | Supports need for evidence verification but not clinical safety |
| Metric dictionary missing | Attach diagnostic-only flag | Blocks thesis-ready metric claim |
| Matched operating point missing | Attach diagnostic-only flag | Blocks fair improvement/sufficiency claim |

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency principle

If A1 calibration, A2 thresholding, or A3 uncertainty and selective prediction is sufficient under declared matched coverage/cost rules, the plan must preserve that result. Later IHARQ, RegimeRisk, learning-to-defer, Adaptive-IHARQ, bandit/RL, stress, or embodiment phases must compare against this sufficiency rather than silently ignoring it.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure or missingness condition | Required Phase 3 response | Diagnostic-only or blocking result |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `PredictionRecord` | Cannot produce calibration/uncertainty for affected case | Blocking |
| Missing `ModelRegistryRecord` | Cannot validate score/class/model lineage | Blocking |
| Missing probability/logit/decision score fields | Cannot calibrate unless declared score fallback is valid | Calibration-dependent use diagnostic-only or ineligible |
| Missing `score_type` | Score interpretation invalid | Blocking for calibration |
| Missing or inconsistent `class_order` | Probability vector cannot map to labels | Blocking |
| Missing `LabelMapRecord` | Class semantics ambiguous | Blocking |
| Split overlap between calibration/threshold/test | Produce `LeakageWarningRecord`; block final claims | Blocking for final evaluation; exploratory only if retained |
| Threshold selected on test labels | Mark threshold oracle diagnostic only | Blocks fair threshold/IHARQ comparisons |
| Calibration method selected on test outcomes | Mark calibration invalid | Blocking for final use |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Metric not thesis-ready | Diagnostic-only |
| Missing matched-comparison key | Comparison not fair | Diagnostic-only |
| Sparse calibration budget | Produce eligibility/fallback warning | Method-specific invalid or diagnostic-only |
| Missing subject/session/trial/window joins | Group or matched analysis incomplete | Diagnostic-only for affected grouping |
| Artifact flags missing | Do not imply clean data | Limitation tag required |
| High-confidence-wrong uses evaluation labels | Allowed only offline | Diagnostic/evaluation-only |
| Dashboard lineage missing | Not dashboard/export ready | Dashboard warning; final export block |
| Negative result absent despite failure | Claim-safety failure | Block claim-evidence approval |
| Unsupported clinical/deployment claim | Claim-safety violation | Block and require Layer 0 review |

Phase 3 must not repair missing upstream data by editing source files. It may produce versioned derived artifacts, warnings, ineligibility entries, and diagnostic-only flags.

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

Repository paths remain subject to `MC-009` final reconciliation. The following are conceptual storage expectations, not unsupported new official paths unless already confirmed by the registry/repository architecture.

| Artifact family | Conceptual storage expectation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CalibrationRecord` | `records/calibration_records/` and/or run-local `results/layer3/calibration_records.*` | Preserve source prediction IDs, calibration ID, split, config, seed, schema |
| `UncertaintyRecord` | `records/uncertainty_records/` and/or run-local `results/layer3/uncertainty_records.*` | Label-free features must be identifiable |
| `SelectivePredictionRecord` | `records/selective_prediction_records/` and/or run-local `results/layer3/selective_prediction_records.*` | Include risk/coverage and threshold lineage |
| `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | `records/threshold_registry_records/`, `registries/`, or conceptual `threshold_registry.yaml` | Exact final home remains path-reconciliation item |
| `ReliabilityAuditReport` | reports/records conceptual location | Must include metric dictionary and source lineage |
| `SplitIntegrityReport` / `LeakageWarningRecord` | validation/warning reports conceptual location | Must be referenced by handoff manifest |
| `CalibrationEligibilityTable` | tables/reports conceptual location | `normalized_candidate`; preserve method eligibility |
| `HighConfidenceWrongTable` | evaluation table/report conceptual location | Evaluation-only labels protected |
| `CalibrationDashboardMetricRecord` | dashboard-readable source metric area / Layer 3 export area / possible `records/dashboard_metric_records/` | Candidate; source metric, not Layer 10 generated view |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` | matched operating-point table/report conceptual location | Exact path unresolved; manifest must link source |
| Calibration parameter files | run-local model/calibration artifact area | Required for reproducibility |
| ReliabilityCard source inputs | card source-bundle/export-source area | Rendered card belongs to Layer 10 |
| Phase 3 handoff manifest | manifests/run or phase handoff area | Must include paths, hashes, statuses, and limitations |

All storage entries must include validation status and must be discoverable by Phase 4, Phase 5, Phase 6, Phase 14, Phase 15, and Layer 0/Layer 10 review mechanisms.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Required handoff to Phase 4

Phase 4 may begin IHARQ-lite evidence verification only when it receives:

- validated `CalibrationRecord` outputs for eligible predictions;
- validated `UncertaintyRecord` outputs with label-free decision-time features;
- `ThresholdRegistryRecord` entries with selection split, metric, version, allowed consumers, and leakage status;
- `SelectivePredictionRecord` baselines and matched operating-point evidence;
- source `PredictionRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, model, and label-budget IDs;
- high-confidence-wrong diagnostics for offline/evaluation comparison only;
- negative-result notes and diagnostic-only flags;
- metric dictionary references;
- claim-safety tags;
- Phase 3 handoff manifest.

Phase 4 must not treat `HighConfidenceWrongTable` correctness labels as decision-time IHARQ inputs and must not tune IHARQ thresholds on final test labels.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 3 is done when all conditions below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Phase 0 schemas, configs, validators, run/hash/seed conventions, metric placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, and dashboard/export placeholders are readable.
- Phase 1 source records and manifests are readable, validated, and not overwritten.
- Phase 2 `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` outputs are readable and eligibility-validated.
- Probability vectors, logits, or decision scores are present for every decoder intended for calibration-dependent evidence, or ineligibility is explicitly recorded.
- `score_type`, `class_order`, and `LabelMapRecord` mapping are validated.
- Calibration/validation/threshold-selection/test split separation is verified.
- No calibration method, threshold rule, or operating point is selected using final test labels.
- At least a declared no-calibration baseline and one feasible declared calibration method are evaluated where data permit.
- `CalibrationRecord` outputs exist for every eligible dataset, subject/session where available, split, seed, label budget, and model family intended for downstream calibrated comparison.
- `UncertaintyRecord` outputs exist with label-free decision-time features for eligible records.
- `SelectivePredictionRecord` outputs exist for declared confidence, entropy, margin, calibrated-score, or related selective baselines.
- `ThresholdRegistryRecord` entries exist for every threshold/operating point used downstream.
- `ReliabilityAuditReport` outputs include metric dictionary linkage or diagnostic-only downgrades.
- `HighConfidenceWrongTable` outputs exist where evaluation labels permit and are marked evaluation-only.
- `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` outputs exist for A1–A3 comparisons or missing matched-key diagnostic flags are attached.
- `SplitIntegrityReport` exists, and any leakage produces `LeakageWarningRecord` and claim blocking/diagnostic handling.
- `CalibrationEligibilityTable` or equivalent eligibility reporting exists for sparse/missing-class calibration budgets.
- Negative results and threshold/selective-prediction sufficiency results are visible.
- Dashboard-readable metric records/source bundles and ReliabilityCard source inputs are exported with lineage and limitation tags.
- Phase 3 handoff manifest is created with paths, hashes, schema versions, validation status, diagnostic flags, negative-result notes, metric dictionary references, and claim-safety tags.
- Downstream consumers in Phases 4–6 and Layer 10 can read the records without manual reinterpretation.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 4 and later thesis-facing calibrated/uncertainty-derived evidence must not proceed from affected Phase 3 outputs if any of the following remain unresolved without diagnostic-only handling:

- missing or invalid `PredictionRecord`;
- missing `ModelRegistryRecord` linkage;
- missing score fields for calibration-dependent use;
- missing `score_type`;
- class-order/label-map mismatch;
- illegal preprocessing fit scope;
- calibration/threshold/test split leakage;
- test-tuned calibration method or threshold;
- missing calibration parameter lineage;
- label-leaking uncertainty features;
- missing threshold registry entries for downstream threshold use;
- missing metric dictionary linkage for thesis-facing metrics;
- missing matched-comparison keys;
- hidden failed/sparse/ineligible calibration cases;
- hidden negative results;
- missing dashboard/source lineage;
- missing claim-safety tags;
- implied clinical, deployment, real-patient, rehabilitation, medical-device, real muscle-stimulation, or real assistive-control claim.

### 26.3 Completion statement

When done, Phase 3 hands forward a validated reliability evidence set: calibrated probabilities, label-free uncertainty features, threshold registries, selective-prediction baselines, matched operating points, split-integrity reports, high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, eligibility reports, negative-result notes, dashboard-readable source bundles, and claim-safety limitations. This enables IHARQ-lite, RegimeRisk, evidence-quality estimation, learning-to-defer, adaptive policy, simulation, stress, embodiment, dashboard, and final thesis integration while preserving the boundary that Phase 3 provides reliability evidence only, not readiness decisions, clinical safety, deployment readiness, or rehabilitation efficacy.

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 4 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 4` |
| Official phase name | `IHARQ-lite evidence verification` |
| Official implementation order | After `Phase 3 — Calibration and uncertainty`; before `Phase 5 — RegimeRisk temporal trust` |
| Primary layer ownership | `Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification` |
| Direct upstream phase dependencies | `Phase 0`, `Phase 1`, `Phase 2`, `Phase 3` |
| Hard downstream phase consumers | `Phase 5`, `Phase 6`, `Phase 8`, `Phase 14`, `Phase 15` |
| Indirect downstream contexts | `Phase 7`, `Phase 9`, `Phase 10`, `Phase 11`, `Phase 12`, and `Phase 13` through later readiness, policy, simulation, stress, bandit/RL, and embodiment handoffs; Phase 4 does not produce those later records |
| Evidence role | Interpretable readiness-control gate and non-learned IHARQ-lite baseline before learned Adaptive-IHARQ or policy optimization |
| Empirical-output status | Produces derived evidence-verification and readiness-action records from validated saved upstream records |
| Source-record status | Does not overwrite Layer 1 clean records, Layer 2 prediction records, or Layer 3 calibration/uncertainty/threshold records |
| Decision-policy status | Deterministic, reason-coded, non-learned IHARQ-lite decision logic; not contextual bandit, RL, or learned Adaptive-IHARQ |
| Dashboard status | Produces dashboard-readable source records, logs, evaluation artifacts, and card source inputs; Layer 10 later renders derived views/cards/exports |
| Claim status | Supports bounded computational/proxy IHARQ-style evidence-verification and readiness-control evidence only |
| Forbidden status | Does not support clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, or real deployment readiness |

Phase 4 is the architecture-defined interpretable readiness-control gate. It creates a non-learned IHARQ-lite reference before any learned evidence-quality estimator, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer policy, contextual bandit, or reinforcement-learning policy is introduced. It consumes validated Phase 1–3 source, prediction, calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, and threshold evidence and converts that evidence into finite, reason-coded readiness actions.

Phase 4 must not be collapsed into ordinary confidence thresholding, Adaptive-IHARQ, RegimeRisk, Layer 7 simulation, StressForge-Lite, embodiment, dashboard rendering, or Layer 0 claim review. Its role is to verify whether current evidence is strong, stable, calibrated, and safe enough to support a computational readiness action now, while preserving exact lineage to the saved records and configurations that produced the decision.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 4 creates the interpretable IHARQ-lite evidence-verification baseline. Its purpose is to decide, from saved and validated evidence, whether a low-calibration neural-intent prediction should be accepted, delayed, supplemented, combined, routed to fallback, marked uncertain, or blocked as unsafe in a computational/proxy sense.

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 4 controls the bottleneck of forced acceptance under incomplete evidence. A raw or calibrated decoder can be confident but wrong, locally stable but globally fragile, spatially unstable across channels, contradictory across model families, or insufficiently trustworthy under signal-quality and risk constraints. Phase 4 prevents downstream adaptive policies and simulations from acting as if calibrated confidence alone is a readiness decision.

### 4.3 Why this phase exists

Phase 4 exists to provide a non-learned, reason-coded, ablatable reference before learned evidence-quality estimation, Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, contextual bandit, or reinforcement-learning policies are credited. Without Phase 4, later learned methods would lack an interpretable comparator and the thesis would be vulnerable to the criticism that the system jumps from classifier confidence directly to policy learning.

### 4.4 What would fail without this phase

Without Phase 4:

- Phase 5 would lack IHARQ decision histories for temporal trust analysis;
- Phase 6 would lack an interpretable IHARQ-lite comparator and rule-derived evidence-quality context;
- Phase 8 would simulate raw or threshold-only decisions without explicit readiness-action traces;
- Phase 14 would lack IHARQ timelines, reason-code distributions, fallback logs, unsafe-event views, and trace-completeness warnings;
- Phase 15 would lack claim-bounded A5 evidence and negative-result notes distinguishing useful IHARQ behavior from threshold-equivalent or over-conservative behavior.

### 4.5 Evidence role

Phase 4 produces evidence-verification records, not source data, decoder predictions, calibration parameters, temporal-trust states, learned policies, simulated transitions, stress profiles, embodiment outcomes, or final claims. Its evidence contribution is a reproducible, reason-coded record family that can be compared against simple baselines at matched coverage, matched request budget, or matched action cost.

## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

### 5.1 Layer ownership and participation

| Layer | Phase 4 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Primary producing layer | Owns IHARQ evidence-verification records and reason-coded non-learned readiness decisions |
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Claim-safety auditor | Applies limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, non-claim boundaries, and final claim review; does not produce empirical IHARQ evidence |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Read-only upstream source layer | Provides immutable dataset, window, split, preprocessing, label-map, and artifact/source lineage; Phase 4 may validate/reference but must not overwrite |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Read-only upstream evidence layer | Provides prediction/model/ordinary-control evidence and model-family context; Phase 4 does not train or repair decoders |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Immediate upstream evidence layer | Provides calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, and threshold registry records; Phase 4 does not fit calibration or retune thresholds |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Downstream consumer and later optional feedback context | Not required for initial Phase 4 because Phase 5 follows Phase 4; later regime-aware IHARQ must be versioned and matched, with `regime_aware` status visible |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Downstream consumer | Consumes IHARQ decisions, rule-derived evidence-quality context, action costs, fallback labels, and unsafe/uncertain flags; Phase 4 does not learn policies |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Downstream simulation consumer | Later consumes IHARQ actions, request/wait delays, evidence budgets, fallback routes, unsafe blocks, and action costs; Phase 4 does not produce transitions or rewards |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Downstream optional stress context | May later stress-condition IHARQ decisions; Phase 4 does not own stress profiles or schedules |
| Layer 9 — Embodiment demo/replay | Downstream optional proxy consumer | May receive gating context through later simulation/policy records; Phase 4 does not validate real embodiment or muscle control |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, cards, and reproducibility | Read/export/derived-output owner | Reads Phase 4 records and renders views/cards/exports; must not recompute IHARQ decisions or retune thresholds |

### 5.2 Active modules

| Module / submodule | Phase 4 participation | Output / evidence effect |
|---|---|---|
| Input validator | Validates canonical upstream records, IDs, split roles, schema versions, probability fields, threshold references, and decision-time/evaluation-only separation | Validation status, degraded-mode reason codes, diagnostic-only flags where needed |
| Evidence feature builder | Builds Phase 4 decision features from calibrated probabilities, uncertainty fields, threshold registry entries, stability views, model agreement, artifact flags, and optional context | Feature provenance in `IHARQTraceRecord` and `IHARQDecisionRecord` |
| Reason-code registry | Owns finite reason-code taxonomy and display mapping for stored actions | Versioned reason-code config and dashboard-readable reason labels |
| IHARQ rule engine | Applies deterministic, non-learned accept/wait/request/combine/fallback/uncertain/unsafe logic | `IHARQDecisionRecord` |
| Window stability checker | Uses past/adjacent/repeated windows only where available without future leakage | Stability features or degraded-mode flags |
| Channel-subset checker | Checks spatial robustness where channel metadata and budget allow | Channel stability scores or unavailable/degraded flags |
| Model-family agreement checker | Compares model-family agreement or disagreement where multiple families exist | Agreement features, trusted-family/disagreement reason codes |
| Evidence combiner | Combines eligible windows or sources without hiding contradiction | `CombinedEvidenceRecord` and linked decision updates |
| Fallback router | Routes to declared conservative/fallback alternatives when configured | `FallbackDecisionRecord` and fallback logs |
| Unsafe-state monitor | Blocks acceptance under severe artifacts, contradiction, invalid inputs, high-risk proxy conditions, or unavailable fallback under high risk | `UnsafeEventRecord` and unsafe-event logs |
| Decision logger | Saves decisions, traces, input lineage, configs, metric links, claim tags, and dashboard/export pointers | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord` |
| Ablation and matched-comparison exporter | Creates A5 rows and compatible A6/A7/A12/A13 context rows where applicable | `IHARQAblationRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote` |
| Dashboard and claim-evidence exporter | Packages dashboard-readable source records and Layer 0 review inputs | card source bundles, claim-evidence entries, warning inputs |

### 5.3 Excluded modules

Phase 4 must not perform raw EEG preprocessing, split creation, decoder training, calibration fitting, threshold selection on test data, RegimeRisk state estimation, learned evidence-quality estimation, Adaptive-IHARQ training, deferral policy learning, contextual-bandit updates, RL policy learning, closed-loop transition simulation, stress-profile generation, embodiment simulation, dashboard rendering, or final claim approval.

### 5.4 Conditional/stretch modules

The following modules are permitted only with explicit availability, lineage, and status tags:

- RegimeRisk-aware threshold tightening or fallback recommendations: `conditional_later_context`, normally produced after Phase 5 and not a hard prerequisite for core Phase 4.
- Stress-conditioned IHARQ analysis: downstream A12 context; Phase 8 owns stress artifacts.
- Embodiment-compatible hold/stop/fallback aliases: downstream A13 context; Layer 9 owns embodiment records.
- Conformal or advanced uncertainty proxies: allowed only if Phase 3 supplied split-safe records; otherwise omitted or marked `inferred_candidate` / `requires_confirmation`.

The unresolved gaps do not block a core A5 IHARQ-lite run, but they block or weaken thesis-ready claims when metric definitions, action-token aliases, evidence-quality producer variants, repository paths, or dashboard/claim boundaries are not traceable.

### 7.2 Phase 0 inheritance matrix

| Phase 0 foundation item | Required by Phase 4? | Status inherited from predecessor sections | Phase 4 handling |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Schema definitions | Yes | Phase 0 prepared canonical/candidate schema substrate | Validate all Phase 4 records against schema version; preserve candidate status where unresolved |
| Record/interface definitions | Yes | Phase 0 prepared registry-driven definitions | Use canonical registry names; local helper views remain local/candidate |
| Configuration families | Yes | Phase 0 prepared IHARQ, threshold, metric, dashboard, claim-safety, and evaluation configs | Require config hash for IHARQ rule engine, evidence budget, fallback routes, reason codes, action costs, and ablation/evaluation configs |
| Mock records/mockable fixtures | Yes for validator readiness only | Phase 0 prepared mock and malformed fixtures | Mock use allowed for validation development, not thesis empirical claims |
| Validation scripts | Yes | Phase 0 prepared validators | Use schema, split, leakage, action-token, reason-code, threshold, metric, matched-key, manifest, and claim-boundary validators |
| Run identifier conventions | Yes | Phase 0 established run ID conventions | Every Phase 4 output must carry `run_id` |
| Config hash conventions | Yes | Phase 0 established config hashing | Every decision/evaluation output must carry `config_hash` |
| Seed conventions | Yes where stochastic inputs or comparisons are used | Phase 0 established seed policy | Preserve upstream seed and Phase 4 seed where random sampling/subsets/bootstraps are used |
| Manifest conventions | Yes | Phase 0 established manifest discipline | Phase 4 handoff manifest required |
| Repository skeleton expectations | Yes | Phase 0 established conceptual storage homes | Use conceptual Layer 4 storage; carry `MC-009` until concrete paths are confirmed |
| Metric dictionary placeholders | Yes | Phase 0 prepared metric placeholder discipline | Convert used metrics to `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or mark diagnostic-only |
| Claim-evidence placeholders | Yes | Phase 0 prepared claim-evidence placeholders | Prepare claim-evidence entries but do not approve final claims |
| Dashboard/export-readiness placeholders | Yes | Phase 0 prepared Layer 10 ingestion/export expectations | Export dashboard-readable source bundles; Layer 10 derives later views |
| Diagnostic-only/negative-result templates | Yes | Phase 0 required negative-result visibility | Use negative-result notes for threshold-equivalent, over-conservative, incomplete, or no-improvement outcomes |
| Policy-update fixtures | Boundary only | Phase 0 prepared `PolicyUpdateTrace` and disabled-update audit fixtures | No Phase 4 policy updates occur; later adaptive phases must preserve separation |

## 8. Upstream Dependency and Continuity Check

### 8.1 Phase 0 → Phase 4 continuity

| Dependency | Status | Phase 4 continuity handling |
|---|---|---|
| Schema/config/validator inheritance | Pass with open issue caveat | Use Phase 0 substrate; carry `MC-008`, `MC-009`, and `MC-010` |
| IHARQ/action-token configuration | Conditional pass | Use canonical tokens; `combine` alias remains display-only unless final registry states otherwise |
| Metric dictionary placeholders | Conditional pass | Create or reference metric entries; missing entries make evaluation rows diagnostic-only |
| Claim-evidence placeholders | Pass with naming ambiguity | Prepare rows/pointers under `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` ambiguity |
| Dashboard/export placeholders | Pass with `MC-011` caveat | Produce source bundles; Layer 10 derives views/cards/exports later |
| Frozen/update separation fixtures | Pass as future boundary | Phase 4 is deterministic and non-updating; no `PolicyUpdateTrace` is created by core Phase 4 |

### 8.2 Phase 1 → Phase 4 continuity

| Phase 1 output | Required Phase 4 use | Continuity status |
|---|---|---|
| `DatasetRecord` | Dataset/source lineage for every IHARQ decision and evaluation row | Required and immutable |
| `WindowRecord` | Window identity, ordering, duration/stride, subject/session join keys, possible window history derivation | Required and immutable |
| `SplitRecord` / split manifest | Decision/evaluation split legality and leakage prevention | Hard gate |
| `PreprocessingRecord` | Preprocessing lineage and fit-scope legality | Required for lineage and leakage audit |
| `LabelMapRecord` | Class order and accepted-class interpretation | Hard gate |
| `ArtifactFlagRecord` where available | Signal/channel/artifact quality and unsafe/degraded-mode logic | Strongly recommended; missing flags trigger limitation |
| `Layer1Manifest` and source hashes | Reproducibility and source validation | Required for thesis-ready rows |

Phase 4 must not overwrite Phase 1 source records. If source keys are missing, split roles are ambiguous, artifact flags are missing, or label maps are invalid, Phase 4 must either block the affected decision/evaluation row or mark it diagnostic-only.

### 8.3 Phase 2 → Phase 4 continuity

| Phase 2 output | Phase 4 use | Continuity status |
|---|---|---|
| `PredictionRecord` | Primary predicted class, score/probability/logit lineage, model ID, model family, class order, source IDs | Hard required |
| `ModelRegistryRecord` | Decoder/model identity, model family, score type, seed/config lineage, run status | Hard required |
| Probability vector/logits/decision scores | Inputs later calibrated by Phase 3 and audited by Phase 4 | Required for calibrated mode; missing fields block calibrated IHARQ or force diagnostic/degraded mode |
| `BaselineMetricRecord` | A0 raw-decoder comparator context | Consumed for comparison, not rewritten |
| `EnsembleControlRecord` / A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, ordinary ensemble, and model-family control context | Strongly recommended comparator where compatible |
| `FailureCaseIndex` | Diagnostic context and negative-result visibility | Consumed without hiding failures |
| `Layer2ReadinessReport` | Eligibility and downstream-readiness check | Required for thesis-ready Phase 4 handoff |

Phase 4 must not relabel ordinary controls as IHARQ. Longer-window decisions, multi-window voting, probability averaging, and ordinary ensembles are A4 controls unless the Phase 4 rule engine emits reason-coded IHARQ decisions with trace and matched comparison.

### 8.4 Phase 3 → Phase 4 continuity

| Phase 3 output | Phase 4 use | Continuity status |
|---|---|---|
| `CalibrationRecord` | Calibrated probability and calibration metadata for decision logic | Hard required for calibrated IHARQ mode |
| `UncertaintyRecord` | Confidence, entropy, margin, variation ratio, disagreement, and label-free uncertainty features | Hard required |
| `SelectivePredictionRecord` | Selective-prediction baseline and threshold/rejection comparator | Required comparator |
| `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Registered thresholds, selection split, allowed consumers, leakage status | Hard gate for fair decisions and comparisons |
| `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable` | Matched coverage/cost operating points and downstream baseline fairness | Required for thesis-ready comparisons where applicable |
| `ReliabilityAuditReport` | Reliability context and failure visibility | Consumed for evaluation and diagnostics |
| `HighConfidenceWrongTable` | Offline/evaluation-only diagnostic of wrong high-confidence cases | Must not be decision-time input |
| Phase 3 `NegativeResultNote` / `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Carried into Phase 4 handoff and claim limitations | Required where applicable |
| Phase 3 dashboard/source bundles | Layer 10 continuity and source-to-card lineage | Consumed as source, not rendered by Phase 4 |

Phase 4 must not tune IHARQ thresholds or action rules on final test labels or use Phase 3 high-confidence-wrong correctness labels as ordinary decision-time features.

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

### 12.1 Evidence chain

Phase 4 must remain at evidence-plan level:

```text
validated upstream records
→ input validation and leakage/partition checks
→ evidence feature assembly from saved prediction/calibration/uncertainty/threshold/source records
→ deterministic reason-coded IHARQ rule evaluation
→ optional stability/agreement/combine/fallback/unsafe handling where inputs exist
→ saved Layer 4 records and traces
→ matched comparison against A0–A4 and local ablations
→ metric dictionary, negative-result, diagnostic-only, dashboard, and claim-evidence handoff
```

This section is not an operational playbook and does not define exact code, class bodies, command lines, or debugging workflows.

### 12.2 Decision-time partition discipline

The rule engine may use only decision-time-legal evidence: saved prediction outputs, calibrated probabilities, label-free uncertainty features, threshold registry entries, source/window metadata, past or adjacent-window history allowed by the protocol, channel/artifact flags, model-family agreement, and explicitly available context. It must not use true labels, future correctness, future reward, future simulation outcomes, future windows, dashboard-derived metrics, or final test-tuned thresholds to make ordinary decisions.

### 12.3 Canonical action logic

The stored action must be one of:

```text
accept
wait
request_evidence
combine_evidence
fallback
uncertain
unsafe
```

Human-readable labels may display “Accept”, “Wait”, “Request evidence”, “Combine evidence”, “Fallback”, “Uncertain”, and “Unsafe”, but the stored `IHARQDecisionRecord.action` must use the canonical token. The `combine` alias remains an alias/open issue and must not replace `combine_evidence` in stored Layer 4 records.

### 12.4 Degraded-mode handling

Phase 4 must use explicit degraded modes rather than silent assumptions:

- missing calibrated probabilities: allow uncalibrated fallback only if explicitly configured; otherwise request evidence, mark uncertain, or block calibrated claims;
- missing window history: disable stability/combine logic and record degraded-evidence reason code;
- missing channel-subset output: disable channel-subset checks and record degraded spatial evidence;
- missing model-family alternatives: run single-model IHARQ and record agreement unavailable;
- missing artifact flags: treat signal quality as unknown, not clean;
- missing RegimeRisk: set `regime_aware=false` and defer regime-aware claims;
- invalid probability vector or mismatched IDs: block acceptance and record validation error.

### 12.5 Comparison logic

Phase 4 must compare IHARQ-lite against compatible simpler baselines only under matched keys and metric definitions. Valid comparators include accept-all raw decoder, calibrated confidence rejection, entropy rejection, margin rejection, selective prediction, longer-window decoding, multi-window voting, probability averaging, ordinary ensembles, fallback-only baseline, and regime-unaware IHARQ where regime-aware comparisons are later available. Oracle-like upper bounds may appear only as clearly labeled diagnostic/headroom estimates and may not support deployable claims.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 foundation gate | Schemas, configs, validators, run IDs, hashes, seeds, manifests, metrics, claims, and dashboard placeholders are available | Block or carry `phase0_inheritance_gap` if absent |
| Source-record gate | Phase 1 source records are valid and immutable | Block affected rows or diagnostic-only |
| Prediction/model gate | `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` exist and join to source records | Block affected decisions |
| Calibration/uncertainty gate | `CalibrationRecord` and `UncertaintyRecord` exist for calibrated IHARQ mode | Degraded/uncalibrated mode only if explicitly declared; otherwise block |
| Threshold registry gate | `ThresholdRegistryRecord` entries exist and are leakage-safe | Block threshold/IHARQ claims using affected thresholds |
| Split/leakage gate | Decision/evaluation features respect split roles and decision-time legality | Reject run or diagnostic-only |
| Action-token gate | Stored action is one of canonical tokens | Block stored decision record if invalid |
| Reason-code gate | Every decision has reason code, reason text or mapped label, and rule path | Block thesis-ready row if missing |
| Feature-provenance gate | Decision records identify input feature sources and threshold identifiers | Diagnostic-only or block if missing |
| Degraded-mode gate | Missing optional evidence produces explicit degraded-mode flags | Warning/diagnostic if absent |
| Unsafe/fallback/combine gate | Active behaviors produce corresponding records and logs | Block behavior-specific claims if missing |
| Matched-comparison gate | A5 and local ablations match required keys | Diagnostic-only if unmatched |
| Metric dictionary gate | Every metric has `MetricDictionaryEntry` linkage | Diagnostic-only if missing |
| Negative-result gate | Threshold-equivalent, over-conservative, no-improvement, or incomplete results are visible | Block cherry-picked improvement claim |
| Dashboard source-bundle gate | Dashboard-readable records, warning inputs, card source bundles, and export manifest inputs have lineage | Layer 10 export warning/block if incomplete |
| Claim-safety gate | Limitation tags and forbidden-claim checks are present | Block final claim handoff if absent |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 4 exits successfully when:

- validated upstream Phase 1–3 records can be joined without split, source, label-map, model, calibration, threshold, or metric mismatch;
- `IHARQDecisionRecord` outputs exist for declared eligible decision cases;
- every decision includes canonical action token, display-label mapping, reason code, rule path, input feature provenance, threshold identifiers, config hash, seed, schema version, validation status, matched-comparison key where evaluated, and claim-safety tags;
- associated `IHARQTraceRecord`, `IHARQAblationRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, matched-comparison reports, metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, and diagnostic-only flags exist where applicable;
- `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, and `UnsafeEventRecord` exist when those behaviors are active;
- A5 comparisons against A0–A4 controls and local ablations are matched or explicitly diagnostic-only;
- dashboard-readable records and IHARQ reliability card source inputs are exported without allowing Layer 10 to recompute decisions;
- all clinical, deployment, real patient-safety, real rehabilitation, real muscle-stimulation, and real assistive-control safety claims are blocked.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

### 14.1 Required matched-comparison key envelope

Phase 4 comparisons must preserve the following keys where available and applicable:

```text
source_record_ids
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
producer_module
phase_id
global_ablation_id
local_ablation_id
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
decoder_id
model_family
label_budget_id
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
system_variant_id
iharq_config_id_or_hash
evidence_budget_config_id_or_hash
fallback_config_id_or_hash
action_cost_config_id_or_hash
matched_comparison_key
metric_dictionary_id
negative_result_note_id_if_any
dashboard_export_id_if_available
```

If public dataset metadata do not provide a field, the missing field must be explicit and must not be silently dropped from the comparison logic.

### 14.2 Required matching across evaluation contexts

| Comparison | Required matching logic | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| A5 vs A0 raw decoder | Same dataset, subject/session where available, window/trial IDs, split, preprocessing, label map, model family/seed where applicable | Missing prediction/source/calibration joins or unmatched model/split keys |
| A5 vs A1 calibrated decoder | Same calibrated outputs and calibration IDs | Missing calibration ID or calibration/test leakage |
| A5 vs A2 simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Same threshold registry, operating-point context, coverage, and cost keys | Missing threshold registry or unmatched coverage/cost keys |
| A5 vs A3 uncertainty and selective prediction | Same dataset, subject/session where available, split, preprocessing, model family where applicable, calibration/uncertainty/threshold IDs, coverage, and cost accounting | Missing uncertainty/selective record, threshold/operating-point identity, unmatched coverage/cost keys, or split leakage |
| A5 vs A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Same source window universe, aggregation rule, delay/evidence-cost accounting, class-order mapping, and model-family/control compatibility | Missing delay/cost keys, missing aggregation provenance, or incompatible control definition |
| IHARQ local submodule ablations | Same source records, same upstream predictions/calibration/uncertainty, only declared submodule changed | Multiple changed factors without variant trace |
| Request/combine/fallback/unsafe comparisons | Same evidence budget/action-cost configuration and eligible case set | Missing cost model or behavior-specific logs |
| Future A6 comparison | Same IHARQ records plus separated rule-derived vs learned evidence-quality variants | Shared-producer ambiguity or target leakage |
| Future A7 comparison | Same ordered sequence and causal RegimeRisk context where Phase 5 records exist | RegimeRisk absent, temporal leakage, or unmatched sequence |
| Future A12/A13 contexts | Matched clean/stressed or simulated/embodiment lineage with stress/embodiment IDs | Stress/embodiment lineage missing or proxy limits absent |

### 14.3 Handling missing keys

If any comparison key is missing, Phase 4 must:

1. preserve upstream records unchanged;
2. write missingness into the relevant `IHARQTraceRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, handoff manifest, or warning artifact;
3. mark affected comparisons `diagnostic_only` or `incomplete`;
4. prevent thesis-ready improvement or readiness-control claims for the affected comparison;
5. carry the issue to Layer 10 warning inputs and the Phase 15 claim-evidence package.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 A0–A13 treatment

A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata only. Phase 4 produces records used by A5 and prepares/strengthens downstream A6/A7/A12/A13 contexts. No ablation owns a canonical record.

### 15.2 Direct and downstream evaluation linkage

| Evaluation ID | Evaluation meaning | Phase 4 role | Explicit evaluation artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| A0 — raw decoder | Accept-all or raw decoder baseline | Consumed comparator from Phase 2 | Source `PredictionRecord` IDs, baseline metrics, matched keys |
| A1 — calibrated decoder | Calibrated decoder evidence | Consumed comparator from Phase 3 | `CalibrationRecord`, calibration metrics, matched keys |
| A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Registered-threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Consumed comparator from Phase 3 | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, coverage/cost rows |
| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | Uncertainty/selective-prediction comparator context | Consumed comparator context where Phase 3 uncertainty and selective-prediction outputs exist | `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `Layer3MatchedOperatingPointTable`, and matched `PredictionRecord` lineage where applicable; diagnostic-only if A3 identity is not separable from A2 threshold or A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Ordinary combination/control baseline | Consumed comparator from Phase 2 | `EnsembleControlRecord`, longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging/probability-average, and ordinary-control rows; preserve candidate/object-class caveat |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Primary Phase 4 evaluation context | Phase 4 directly produces/strengthens records used by this evaluation context | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, `IHARQAblationRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, claim-evidence entry |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Learned quality downstream context | Phase 4 produces rule-derived baseline/context; learned estimator belongs to Phase 6 | separated rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord`, variant tags or equivalent, target-leakage warnings, metric dictionary |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Regime-aware IHARQ downstream context | Prepared only; core Phase 4 is regime-unaware until Phase 5 records exist | `regime_aware=false` baseline, later matched regime-aware/unaware report after Phase 5 |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Downstream deferral policy | Provides IHARQ actions, fallback/uncertain/request labels, action costs as context | Later deferral evaluation artifacts; Phase 4 does not produce `DeferralRecord` |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Downstream supervised adaptive policy | Provides interpretable pseudo-decision/context and rule-derived comparator | Later supervised-policy evaluation; Phase 4 does not train adaptive policy |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Downstream update-enabled policy | Provides frozen context only | Later `PolicyUpdateTrace` required; Phase 4 produces no bandit updates |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Downstream RL policy | Provides frozen context only | Later RL evaluation and update traces; Phase 4 produces no RL records |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Stress-conditioned robustness | Provides Layer 4 decisions for later stress context; Layer 8 owns stress artifacts | Stress matched reports later; Phase 4 clean records must remain distinct |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Embodiment proxy/simulation demo | Provides readiness/gating context indirectly through later layers | Embodiment outcome/card artifacts later; Phase 4 does not validate real control |

### 15.3 Required explicit evaluation artifacts

Phase 4 must produce or prepare:

- `IHARQDecisionRecord` for A5;
- `IHARQTraceRecord` for rule-path and provenance reproducibility;
- `IHARQAblationRecord` for local submodule ablations and A5 variants;
- Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` for accepted accuracy, coverage, wrong-accept, request/fallback/unsafe/uncertain/action-cost metrics;
- `MatchedComparisonReport` for IHARQ versus A0–A4 and local ablations;
- `MetricDictionaryEntry` entries/references for every metric used;
- `NegativeResultNote` entries for threshold-equivalent, no-improvement, excessive-cost, over-request, over-fallback, or over-conservative results;
- `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` entries for incomplete, unmatched, missing-lineage, missing-metric, or alias-conflicted rows;
- claim-evidence entries for Phase 15 under the unresolved matrix/manifest naming issue;
- dashboard-readable source bundles and card inputs for Phase 14.

Every Phase 4 export package must preserve source-record IDs, run IDs, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, validation status, metric dictionary references, matched-comparison keys, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, claim-safety tags, and actual storage locations/hashes where available.

### 16.5 Not-dashboard inputs

The following are not allowed to be dashboard-created or dashboard-recomputed inputs:

- action-token alias repair.

Layer 10 may warn about missing or invalid records but must not silently repair them.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 4 may support bounded claims about:

- IHARQ-style evidence verification using public EEG-derived records;
- computational/proxy readiness-control decisions;
- reason-coded accept/wait/request/combine/fallback/uncertain/unsafe behavior;
- reduced wrong accepted decisions or improved accepted-decision reliability compared with matched baselines where supported;
- increased traceability of decision reasons, fallback, unsafe/proxy blocking, and uncertainty handling;
- negative results showing when IHARQ is threshold-equivalent, over-conservative, or insufficient.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 4 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- clinical unsafe-state detection;
- real fatigue or neurological-state diagnosis;
- real-world closed-loop control reliability.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 4 records and claim-evidence entries must carry the strictest applicable tags, including:

```text
public_eeg_only
proxy_readiness
computational_evidence_verification
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
evaluation_only where labels/outcomes are used
diagnostic_only where matching/lineage/metric completeness fails
simulation_only where later Layer 7 records are used
stress_conditioned where later Layer 8 stress records are used
embodiment_proxy_only where later Layer 9 records are used
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Phase 4 claims must be downgraded to diagnostic-only or blocked when:

- source lineage is incomplete;
- split leakage or test-tuned thresholds are detected;
- canonical action tokens are not used;
- reason codes or rule paths are missing;
- matched-comparison keys are missing;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- negative results are hidden;
- dashboard outputs lack source lineage;
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants are not separated for A6;
- helper views are missing but strong-stability claims are made;
- RegimeRisk is absent but regime-aware claims are attempted;
- stress/simulation/embodiment tags are missing for later contexts;
- clinical, deployment, rehabilitation, patient-safety, or real-control wording appears.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 must later review Phase 4 claim-evidence entries, limitation tags, forbidden claim wording, diagnostic-only statuses, negative-result notes, and dashboard/card captions. Layer 0 does not produce empirical IHARQ evidence and must not be cited as the source of performance improvement.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 are capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and stopping-point labels only. They are not phases, ablation IDs, artifact owners, or substitutes for Phase 0–15.

| Capability tier | Phase 4 effect | Claim maturity consequence |
|---|---|---|
| C0 — Public-data reliability spine | Consumes and depends on C0 baseline/calibration evidence from Phases 1–3 | C0 remains prerequisite; Phase 4 does not replace C0 evidence |
| C1 — IHARQ and RegimeRisk reliability control | Phase 4 matures the IHARQ portion of C1; RegimeRisk portion waits for Phase 5 | C1 becomes partially matured for IHARQ-lite only; full C1 requires Phase 5 temporal trust evidence |
| C2 — Adaptive policy layer | Phase 4 prepares interpretable comparator and policy context for Phase 6/7 | C2 not matured in Phase 4 |
| C3 — Bandit/RL simulation layer | Phase 4 prepares frozen context/actions for later simulation and policy learning | C3 not matured in Phase 4 |
| C4 — Embodiment and dashboard layer | Phase 4 prepares dashboard/card source inputs and later embodiment gating context | C4 not matured in Phase 4; dashboard cards and embodiment outputs are later/derived |

Phase 4 may be a thesis-valid stopping point for bounded IHARQ-lite evidence-verification claims if and only if matched baselines, metric definitions, negative results, diagnostic-only flags, trace completeness, and claim-safety boundaries are complete.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative results are evidence

Phase 4 must not hide negative or null findings. A negative result is required evidence when:

- confidence thresholding performs as well as IHARQ at matched coverage/cost;
- selective prediction is sufficient under the declared protocol;
- longer-window, voting, averaging, or ordinary ensemble controls matches IHARQ;
- IHARQ over-requests evidence or adds unacceptable delay;
- IHARQ over-fallbacks or becomes too conservative;
- unsafe-state blocking reduces wrong accepts only by collapsing coverage;
- combination behavior hides no additional value over ordinary aggregation;
- missing helper views prevent strong stability/agreement claims;
- RegimeRisk is unavailable and regime-aware claims must be deferred.

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency rule

If A0–A4 baselines are sufficient under matched coverage, matched request budget, or matched action cost, Phase 4 must record that sufficiency as a `NegativeResultNote` and must not overstate IHARQ as necessary. Such a result can still support a scientifically valuable claim: the evidence plan identified the point at which a simpler, cheaper, more interpretable baseline is enough.

### 19.3 Required baseline set

Where available and compatible, Phase 4 should compare against:

- accept-all raw decoder;
- calibrated confidence threshold;
- entropy rejection;
- margin rejection;
- selective prediction;
- longer-window decoder;
- multi-window voting;
- probability averaging;
- ordinary ensembles;
- fallback-only baseline;
- local IHARQ ablations with submodules removed.

Missing baselines must be explained. They must not be replaced by unsupported invented controls.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure / missingness condition | Required Phase 4 response | Diagnostic / claim consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Missing or invalid `PredictionRecord` | Block affected decision | No Phase 4 decision or A5 row |
| Missing `CalibrationRecord` in calibrated mode | Use declared uncalibrated fallback only if configured; otherwise block | Calibrated IHARQ claim blocked |
| Missing `UncertaintyRecord` | Block or degraded mode | Uncertainty-based IHARQ claim blocked |
| Missing `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Block threshold-based rule/comparison | Matched threshold claims blocked |
| Split or threshold-selection leakage | Reject run or diagnostic-only | No thesis-ready comparison |
| True label/future outcome in decision-time features | Reject run unless declared oracle diagnostic analysis | Leakage violation; no ordinary claim |
| Invalid action token | Reject record | Stored decision invalid |
| `combine` stored instead of `combine_evidence` | Alias violation | Must repair via versioned rerun or mark invalid; no silent normalization |
| Missing reason code or rule path | Mark incomplete or reject | No interpretable IHARQ claim |
| Missing matched key | Mark diagnostic-only | No comparative improvement claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Mark diagnostic-only | No metric-based claim |
| Missing negative-result note where applicable | Block claim integration | Cherry-picking risk |
| Missing trace/source lineage | Dashboard warning and diagnostic-only | No thesis-ready export |
| Missing optional helper view | Disable associated submodule | Strong/stability/agreement claim blocked |
| Missing RegimeRisk | Set `regime_aware=false` | A7/regime-aware claim deferred |
| Missing fallback/unsafe logs when behavior active | Block behavior-specific claim | Fallback/unsafe claims invalid |
| Overclaim wording detected | Layer 0 downgrade/block | No clinical/deployment/safety claim |

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Required handoff to Phase 5

Phase 5 may begin RegimeRisk temporal trust work only when it receives:

- validated `IHARQDecisionRecord` outputs;
- action distributions and reason-code histories;
- rule-derived evidence-quality histories where available;
- accepted/fallback/uncertain/unsafe labels;
- request/wait/combine/fallback counts and costs;
- decision-time ordering fields;
- source dataset/subject/session/trial/window/split lineage;
- model/calibration/threshold lineage;
- trace records and validation status;
- negative-result and diagnostic-only flags;
- explicit `regime_aware=false` status for core Phase 4 runs.

Phase 5 must not rewrite Phase 4 decisions in place. Later regime-aware IHARQ comparisons must be versioned and matched against the regime-unaware Phase 4 baseline.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phases 6–15

| Downstream phase | Phase 4 handoff content | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 6 — Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, reason codes, action costs, fallback/unsafe/uncertain labels, diagnostic-only flags | Phase 4 does not produce learned quality estimator or supervised policy |
| Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer | Request/wait/fallback/uncertain/unsafe decisions, cost/coverage context, selective-prediction comparators | Phase 4 does not produce `DeferralRecord` |
| Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness | IHARQ action decisions, request/wait delays, evidence budgets, fallback routes, downstream no-action aliases only through explicit mapping, unsafe blocks, action costs | Phase 4 does not produce transitions, rewards, sessions, or environment diagnostics |
| Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite | Clean IHARQ decision lineage for later stress-conditioning | Phase 4 does not create stress profiles, schedules, or stressed records |
| Phase 10 — Contextual bandit | Frozen IHARQ context through later simulation/policy records | Phase 4 produces no bandit policy or `PolicyUpdateTrace` |
| Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy | Frozen IHARQ context through later simulation/policy records | Phase 4 produces no RL policy, reward trace, or update trace |
| Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo | Readiness/gating context through later simulation/embodiment mapping | Phase 4 does not validate real muscle control or real safety |
| Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison | Readiness/gating context through later replay mapping | Phase 4 does not produce OpenSim evidence |
| Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards | Validated Layer 4 source records, evaluation artifacts, logs, card source bundles, warning inputs, manifests | Layer 10 renders derived outputs only |
| Phase 15 — Final thesis integration | A5 evidence, matched comparisons, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, limitation tags, claim-evidence entries | Phase 15 integrates claims; Phase 4 does not approve final claims |

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 4 is done when all conditions below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Phase 0 schemas, configs, validators, run/hash/seed conventions, metric placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, diagnostic-only templates, negative-result templates, and dashboard/export placeholders are readable.
- Phase 1 source records and manifests are readable, validated, and not overwritten.
- Phase 2 `PredictionRecord` and `ModelRegistryRecord` outputs are readable and eligibility-validated.
- Phase 3 `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, and `ThresholdRegistryRecord` outputs are readable, validated, and split-safe for Phase 4 use.
- Decision-time and evaluation-only fields are separated; true labels, future correctness, future reward, future stress outcomes, and dashboard-derived metrics are not used to make ordinary decisions.
- Canonical action vocabulary is formalized and stored records use `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, and `unsafe` only.
- Any `no_action`, hold, no-op, or downstream simulator/policy command is represented only as an explicit fallback route, adapter/display alias, or downstream mapping field, never as a stored Layer 4 action token.
- Reason-code taxonomy/config and action-token display mapping exist and are versioned.
- `IHARQDecisionRecord` outputs exist for all declared eligible Phase 4 decision cases.
- Every decision includes source IDs, run ID, config hash, seed, schema version, validation status, threshold IDs, feature provenance, action token, reason code, rule path, claim-safety tags, and diagnostic-only status where applicable.
- `IHARQTraceRecord` outputs exist and can regenerate decision lineage from saved records and configs.
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` rule-derived outputs exist where evidence-quality features are claimed, with shared-producer caveat preserved for Phase 6.
- `CombinedEvidenceRecord`, `FallbackDecisionRecord`, and `UnsafeEventRecord` exist when their corresponding behaviors are active.
- `IHARQAblationRecord`, Layer 4 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry` references, `NegativeResultNote`, and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` outputs exist for A5 and local ablations where applicable.
- IHARQ-lite is compared to available A0–A4 controls and local ablations at matched coverage, matched request budget, or matched action cost, or unmatched rows are visibly diagnostic-only.
- Negative results are visible and not hidden.
- Dashboard-readable source bundles, warning inputs, and IHARQ reliability card source inputs are exported with lineage and limitation tags.
- Phase 4 handoff manifest is created with paths, hashes, schema versions, validation status, diagnostic flags, negative-result notes, metric dictionary references, action-token mapping, reason-code registry, and claim-safety tags.
- Layer 0 claim-safety review inputs are prepared, but no final clinical/deployment/real-safety claim is made.
- Downstream consumers in Phases 5, 6, 8, 14, and 15 can read the records without manual reinterpretation.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 5 and later thesis-facing use of Phase 4 outputs must not proceed from affected records if any of the following remain unresolved without diagnostic-only handling:

- missing or invalid upstream source records;
- missing `PredictionRecord` / `ModelRegistryRecord` linkage;
- missing calibrated probability or uncertainty fields for calibrated IHARQ mode;
- missing threshold registry for threshold-based decisions;
- split leakage, threshold-selection leakage, or test-label tuning;
- evaluation-only labels/outcomes present in decision-time features;
- invalid stored action token or unresolved `combine` alias in stored records;
- missing reason code, rule path, or action-token display mapping;
- missing feature provenance or threshold identifiers;
- missing matched-comparison keys;
- missing metric dictionary entry for reported metric;
- missing negative-result note where required;
- missing diagnostic-only flag for incomplete evidence;
- missing trace records for thesis-relevant decisions;
- missing logs for active combine/fallback/unsafe behavior;
- hidden failed, skipped, unsupported, over-conservative, or threshold-equivalent variants;
- dashboard/card output lacking source lineage;
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` shared-producer ambiguity in A6 context;
- RegimeRisk-aware claim attempted before Phase 5 records exist;
- clinical, deployment, rehabilitation, patient-safety, real muscle-stimulation, or real assistive-control safety claim attempted.

### 26.3 Minimum viable Phase 4

A minimum viable Phase 4 includes validated calibrated confidence and uncertainty inputs, canonical action vocabulary, reason codes, deterministic accept/wait/request_evidence/fallback/uncertain/unsafe decisions, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `IHARQTraceRecord`, matched comparison against confidence thresholding, metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and claim-safety tags.

### 26.4 Strong Phase 4

A strong Phase 4 additionally includes window stability, channel-subset stability, model-family agreement, `combine_evidence`, fallback routing, unsafe-state logic, local submodule ablations, A0–A4 matched comparisons, source-bundle exports, IHARQ reliability card source inputs, trace-completeness reporting, claim-evidence entries, and Phase 5/6/8/14/15-ready handoff lineage.

### 26.5 Stretch C-ready Phase 4

A Stretch C-ready Phase 4 preserves policy-ready evidence-quality features, action-cost and reward-context fields for later Layer 7 simulation, simulation-ready request/wait/fallback behavior, embodiment-gating compatibility through later layers, stress-conditioned lineage placeholders without owning stress artifacts, and complete A0–A13-aware evaluation lineage while maintaining all public-data, proxy-only, simulation-only, stress-only, embodiment-proxy-only, dashboard-derived, and claim-safety limitations.

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 5 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 5` |
| Official phase name | `RegimeRisk temporal trust` |
| Primary architecture layer | Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring |
| Functional module name | Module E: Temporal regime and trust engine |
| Short module name | RegimeRisk |
| Phase type | Core C1 temporal-trust evidence phase after IHARQ-lite and before learned adaptive policy phases |
| Primary evidence role | Produce temporal trust, regime-risk, trust-allocation, and stop-loss evidence from causal rolling histories |
| Main phase-owned source records/artifacts | `RegimeStateRecord`; conditional `TrustStateRecord`; `regime_timelines.csv`; `trust_scores.csv`; `stop_loss_warnings.csv`; Layer 5 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`; Layer 5 matched-comparison and negative-control evaluation artifacts |
| Upstream prerequisite phases | Phase 0, Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, Phase 4 |
| Direct downstream consumers | Phase 6, Phase 7, Phase 8, Phase 9, Phase 12, Phase 13, Phase 14, Phase 15; Layer 4 regime-aware rerun/evaluation contexts where explicitly versioned |
| Main ablation/evaluation context | A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk |
| Secondary evaluation contexts | A5 and A6 comparison support; A12 stress-conditioned context; A13 simulation/proxy embodiment context |
| Capability-tier effect | Strengthens C1 and prepares C2/C3/C4; does not create a new capability tier |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Evidence-production logic only; not a function-level implementation playbook |
| Claim boundary | Public-data and simulation/proxy temporal-trust evidence only; no clinical fatigue diagnosis, no real patient safety, no medical-device readiness, no real rehabilitation efficacy, no real muscle stimulation control, and no deployment-readiness claim |

Phase 5 is the official implementation phase that introduces RegimeRisk temporal trust. It converts ordered prediction, calibration, uncertainty, IHARQ, artifact, and metadata histories into traceable temporal-trust records. It addresses the architecture’s temporal-reliability bottleneck: a decoder, threshold, evidence source, or IHARQ action may appear locally reliable while recent behavior shows drift-risk, fatigue-like degradation, dropout-risk, instability, evidence-source degradation, request-evidence bursts, fallback bursts, or rising wrong-accept risk.

Phase 5 does not overwrite Phase 4 IHARQ-lite records. Core Phase 4 remains the regime-unaware interpretable baseline. Any later regime-aware IHARQ comparison must be versioned, matched, and traceable to saved Phase 5 records rather than silently modifying the Phase 4 baseline.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 5 is the temporal reliability gate. It monitors changing reliability across time, subject, session, trial/window sequence, stress condition where declared, and decoder/IHARQ behavior. The phase prevents the system from assuming stationary reliability and supplies temporal context to IHARQ, adaptive policies, simulation, stress analysis, embodiment-proxy gating, dashboard views, and final thesis evidence.

The central Phase 5 question is:

> When a decoder or IHARQ decision appears locally confident or acceptable, should the system still trust that evidence under the recent temporal operating regime?

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 5 controls the temporal-trust bottleneck created by low-calibration neural-intent data. Earlier phases establish clean data, prediction evidence, calibration/uncertainty evidence, and pointwise IHARQ evidence verification. Those phases do not, by themselves, prove that a decoder, threshold, evidence source, or readiness action remains trustworthy after recent instability, drift-risk, fatigue-like degradation, dropout-risk, request-evidence bursts, fallback bursts, high-confidence wrong clusters, or agreement collapse.

### 4.3 Scientific role

Phase 5 supports the thesis argument that low-calibration BCI reliability is not only a pointwise classification, calibration, uncertainty, or IHARQ-readiness problem. It is also a temporal operating-regime problem. Phase 5 produces traceable records that test whether temporal regime context improves reliability interpretation, failure explanation, conservative decision routing, adaptive-policy context, simulation behavior, stress-conditioned analysis, and dashboard evidence.

### 4.4 What Phase 5 must not claim

Phase 5 must not claim that RegimeRisk detects true physiological fatigue, diagnoses neurological state, clinically validates BCI safety, guarantees safe assistive action, validates medical-device readiness, proves real rehabilitation efficacy, controls real muscle stimulation, or demonstrates deployment readiness. Its appropriate language is temporal trust, drift-risk, fatigue-like degradation proxy, dropout-risk, evidence instability, stop-loss warning, conservative recommendation, simulation-only proxy, stress-conditioned proxy, and diagnostic-only evidence where applicable.
