| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | Required baseline where available | Uncertainty/selective matched comparison consumed | baseline/control |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Required baseline where available | Longer-window/aggregation/ensemble matched comparison consumed | baseline/control |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Required primary baseline | Phase 4 `IHARQDecisionRecord`, traces, evaluation outcomes consumed | interpretable evidence verification baseline |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Primary Phase 6 evidence-quality evaluation | Learned `EvidenceQualityRecord`, A6 `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric entries, target-construction card, negative-result notes | proxy evidence quality only |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Upstream context/baseline | Phase 5 `RegimeStateRecord` and A7 outputs consumed | temporal-trust/proxy only |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Downstream prepared, not produced | Readiness contexts and cost/fallback configs prepared; no `DeferralRecord` output | future Phase 7 |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Primary Phase 6 supervised policy evaluation | `PolicyActionRecord`, policy artifact, pseudo-label files, cost-model card/source bundle, controller-card source bundle, A9 matched report | pseudo-label based proxy readiness |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Future downstream | Frozen policy/context/action records prepared for later simulation/bandit comparison | simulation-only later |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Future downstream | Frozen supervised baseline and context/action records prepared | simulation-only later |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Future downstream | Source policy/context lineage prepared; no stress outputs | stress-conditioned later only |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Future downstream | Simulation-compatible action/context lineage prepared; no embodiment outputs | embodiment proxy later only |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts required from Phase 6

| Evaluation artifact | Required for | Content |
|---|---|---|
| A6 `MatchedComparisonReport` | Evidence-quality evaluation | learned quality vs rule/IHARQ/uncertainty baselines, matched keys, metrics, target-construction status |
| A9 `MatchedComparisonReport` | Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ evaluation | learned policy vs IHARQ-lite, threshold/selective, aggregation/ensemble, evidence-quality threshold, RegimeRisk-aware baselines where available |
| Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | A6/A9 | evaluation metrics, split, rows, baselines, diagnostic status, metric dictionary IDs |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Every reported metric | metric definition, directionality, units, applicability, claim status |
| Target-construction card/source bundle | A6/A9 | source labels, allowed future info, cost vector, target route, split, leakage guard, limitation tags |
| Pseudo-label file | A9 | per-row target labels, action costs, source IDs, legality mask IDs, version/hash |
| Action-distribution report | A9 | action rates, class imbalance, illegal-action count, split, policy/baseline |
| Cost-sensitivity report | A9 | cost variants, label shifts, policy shifts, metric sensitivity, negative results |
| Context-ablation table | A6/A9 | contribution of calibration, uncertainty, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, history features |
| High-confidence-wrong detection table | A6 | detection of high-confidence failures and learned quality behavior |
| Reliability-vs-coverage curve/table | A6 | accepted risk/coverage as quality threshold changes |
| `NegativeResultNote` | All where applicable | weak estimator, baseline equivalence, over-conservative actions, unstable cost sensitivity, leakage failure, missing baseline |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | All where applicable | unmatched comparisons, missing metric dictionary, missing target card, shared-producer ambiguity, missing legality mask |
| Claim-evidence entry | Phase 15 | final claim/limitation trace for A6/A9 evidence |

### 15.3 Required baseline sufficiency for Phase 6

Phase 6 must compare against the following baselines where available and explicitly explain missing baselines:

- accept-all raw decoder;
- confidence threshold;
- entropy rejection;
- margin rejection;
- calibrated decoder operating point;
- registered confidence-threshold / simple threshold baseline;
- uncertainty and selective prediction;
- longer-window decoder;
- multi-window voting;
- probability averaging;
- ordinary ensemble;
- IHARQ-lite;
- RegimeRisk-aware IHARQ where Phase 5 outputs are available;
- evidence-quality threshold baseline;
- fallback-only or no-action conservative route where declared.

Learning-to-defer is a Phase 7 evaluation context and should not be claimed as a completed Phase 6 output unless a separately declared baseline-only comparator is explicitly marked as non-Phase-7 and diagnostic/supporting.

### 16.2 Dashboard-warning inputs

Layer 10 must be able to warn on:

- missing or invalid upstream Phase 1–5 records;
- missing source IDs or lineage fields;
- target leakage or decision-time visibility violation;
- missing pseudo-label/target-construction card;
- missing action-space, legality-mask, or cost-model configuration;

- weak/missing baselines;
- hidden negative results;

These are derived outputs and must remain linked to Phase 6 source records, metrics, configs, seeds, schema versions, validation status, and claim-safety tags.

### 16.5 Not-dashboard inputs

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 6 may support bounded claims such as:

- learned evidence-quality estimation can characterize proxy decoder reliability under public EEG/low-calibration constraints;
- evidence-quality scores may improve detection of high-confidence wrong or unreliable evidence under declared target-construction rules;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ can be compared against IHARQ-lite, selective prediction, and other baselines under matched cost/coverage;
- RegimeRisk and IHARQ features may improve computational readiness-policy decisions when matched and leakage-safe;
- action-space and cost-model sensitivity can characterize trade-offs among wrong accepts, waiting, requesting evidence, fallback, no-action, and unsafe blocking;
- a frozen supervised policy can serve as a baseline for later simulated closed-loop, stress, bandit, RL, and embodiment-proxy studies.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 6 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- physiological fatigue diagnosis;
- human expert readiness labeling unless such labels are actually present, licensed, and documented, which this architecture does not assume;
- online adaptive safety or real-world controller adaptation.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 6 outputs must inherit upstream tags and add applicable tags from:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based
evaluation_only
computational_policy_only
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
diagnostic_only where applicable
simulation_only where future simulation records are used
stress_conditioned where future stress records are used
embodiment_proxy_only where future embodiment records are used
```

### 17.4 Diagnostic-only cases

Affected Phase 6 outputs must be diagnostic-only if:

- target construction uses future/test-only information outside the declared target partition;
- pseudo-label files are missing, unversioned, or not split-safe;
- `ReadinessContextRecord` contains hidden targets or oracle fields;
- `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants are not producer/derivation-tagged;
- action-space or legality-mask files are missing;
- illegal actions are emitted as valid policy actions;
- cost weights are arbitrary and no sensitivity analysis is provided;
- matched comparison keys are missing;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- required baselines are missing without a reason;
- a learned policy performs similarly to simple baselines and this is hidden;
- dashboard-generated views are used as source evidence;
- forbidden clinical/deployment wording appears.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 review for Phase 6 must check:

- all claim-safety tags;
- pseudo-label and target-construction limitations;
- leakage and split status;
- baseline sufficiency;
- negative-result visibility;
- diagnostic-only flags;
- source-vs-derived dashboard separation;
- frozen/update separation;
- forbidden-claim absence;
- final claim-evidence matrix/manifest entries.

---

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

### 18.1 Capability-tier role

C0–C4 are capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and stopping-point labels, not implementation phases, ablations, artifact owners, or substitutes for Phase 6.

Phase 6 primarily strengthens the project’s Adaptive-IHARQ claim maturity after earlier phases have established:

- C0-style raw/public EEG baseline evidence;
- C1-style calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction evidence;
- IHARQ-lite evidence-verification baseline;
- RegimeRisk temporal trust context.

### 18.2 Phase 6 contribution to tiers

| Capability tier / maturity area | Phase 6 contribution | Claim maturity condition |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline/public EEG reliability | Uses A0–A4 baselines for fair comparison | Must not weaken or overwrite baseline evidence. |
| Calibration/uncertainty visibility | Uses calibrated/uncertainty features in evidence-quality and policy context | Requires Phase 3 eligibility and no threshold leakage. |
| IHARQ evidence verification | Uses IHARQ-lite as interpretable baseline | Must preserve Layer 4 action tokens and reason codes. |
| RegimeRisk temporal trust | Uses temporal-trust fields as context | Must keep RegimeRisk proxy/non-clinical limitation. |
| Adaptive-IHARQ learned readiness | Produces A6/A9 evidence | Thesis-ready only if target construction, matched comparisons, baselines, metrics, and claim tags pass. |
| Later simulation/stress/embodiment tiers | Prepares frozen policies and source records | No simulation/stress/embodiment claim until later phases produce those records. |

### 18.3 Claim-maturity downgrade rules

Phase 6 claim maturity is downgraded when:

- learned evidence-quality does not improve over confidence/uncertainty baselines;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ does not improve over IHARQ-lite or selective prediction under matched cost/coverage;
- results are sensitive to arbitrary cost weights;
- action distributions collapse to fallback/wait/no-action;
- context ablations show RegimeRisk/evidence-quality adds no value;
- evidence is unmatched, leaky, or metric-incomplete;
- negative results are present but hidden.

A downgraded Phase 6 can still be thesis-valid as a negative or baseline-sufficiency result if limitations, diagnostics, and handoff records are complete.

---

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative-result categories

Phase 6 must preserve negative results for:

- evidence-quality estimator fails to predict reliability better than confidence/entropy/margin baselines;
- quality score is poorly calibrated;
- high-confidence wrong detection is weak;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ performs similarly to IHARQ-lite or selective prediction;
- learned policy improves only by lowering coverage unfairly;
- learned policy overuses fallback, wait, request-evidence, no-action, or unsafe;
- learned policy over-accepts wrong predictions;
- pseudo-labels are unstable under cost changes;
- action classes are too imbalanced for reliable learning;
- RegimeRisk context adds no benefit;
- context ablations show simple calibration/threshold baselines are sufficient;
- held-out performance is unstable across seeds, subjects, sessions, datasets, or splits;
- leakage checks fail;
- required baselines or metric dictionary entries are missing.

### 19.2 Baseline-sufficiency rule

If simpler baselines match or exceed Phase 6 learned outputs under matched cost and coverage, the correct thesis handling is:

1. save the learned-policy records and evaluation artifacts;
2. create a `NegativeResultNote`;
3. mark Adaptive-IHARQ superiority claims as unsupported or diagnostic-only;
4. state that simpler threshold/selective/IHARQ-lite/RegimeRisk-aware policies were sufficient for the tested public-EEG/proxy setting;
5. preserve the frozen policy as a downstream baseline only if validation and lineage are complete.

### 19.3 Negative-result visibility obligations

Negative results must be visible in:

- Layer 6 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`;
- A6/A9 `MatchedComparisonReport`;
- action-distribution and cost-sensitivity reports;
- controller-card/evidence-quality-card source bundles;
- dashboard warning inputs;
- claim-evidence matrix/manifest rows;
- Phase 6 handoff manifest;
- Phase 15 final integration notes.

---

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

### 20.1 Failure modes and required response

| Failure mode | Risk | Required response |
|---|---|---|
| Missing upstream records | Context/policy cannot be joined | Block affected rows or diagnostic-only. |
| Split leakage | Inflated evidence-quality/policy results | Block thesis-facing claim. |
| Target leakage | Correctness/future information enters decision-time features | Block policy evaluation; create diagnostic flag. |
| Unversioned pseudo-labels | Policy labels not reproducible | A9 diagnostic-only. |
| Missing target-construction card | Proxy-label basis hidden | A6/A9 diagnostic-only. |
| Shared `EvidenceQualityRecord` not producer-tagged | Layer 4 and Layer 6 evidence-quality semantics confused | A6 diagnostic-only until variant metadata fixed. |
| Invalid action-space map | Policy actions not interpretable | Block `PolicyActionRecord` export. |
| Missing legality mask | Unsafe/illegal actions may be learned | Block or diagnostic-only. |
| Illegal action output | Policy violates constraints | Mark row invalid; log failure; do not claim improvement. |
| Cost-model instability | Results depend on arbitrary costs | Require sensitivity; downgrade if unstable. |
| Action imbalance | Policy may collapse to dominant route | Report action distribution and imbalance handling; downgrade if unresolved. |
| Missing baseline | Learned policy not fairly evaluated | No superiority claim. |
| Missing metric dictionary | Metric not reproducible | Metric diagnostic-only. |
| Unmatched comparison | Apparent improvement may be due to different cases | Diagnostic-only. |
| Hidden negative results | Thesis overclaiming risk | Block final handoff until notes added. |
| Dashboard repair | Layer 10 becomes hidden evidence producer | Block dashboard export/claim. |
| Frozen/update contamination | Training/adaptation curves mixed with evaluation | Block policy-learning claim. |

### 20.2 Missingness rules

- Missing optional features must be explicitly encoded as missing, not imputed silently into source records.
- If RegimeRisk fields are missing, produce regime-unaware Phase 6 rows and mark RegimeRisk-aware rows diagnostic-only.
- If rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord` is absent, learned evidence-quality may still run from calibration/uncertainty/target construction, but comparisons to rule-derived quality are not claimed.
- If trust timelines are absent but compact `RegimeStateRecord` trust fields exist, use only the compact fields and mark independent trust timeline unavailable.
- If fallback source definitions are absent, fallback/defer-related actions must be illegal or diagnostic-only.
- If no future window exists in offline replay, `request_evidence` pseudo-labels depending on future windows must be illegal or target-only with explicit constraints.

### 20.3 Diagnostic-only downgrade table

| Condition | Downgrade scope |
|---|---|
| Upstream source leakage | Entire affected run/split |
| Policy-visible hidden target | Entire policy/context artifact |
| Missing pseudo-label provenance | A9 learned-policy claim |
| Missing evidence-quality target provenance | A6 evidence-quality claim |
| Missing matched keys | Affected comparison rows |
| Missing metric dictionary | Affected metric and claim row |
| Missing legality mask | Affected `PolicyActionRecord` and policy artifact |
| Invalid action alias | Affected action rows and action-distribution report |
| Missing cost sensitivity | Cost-superiority claim |
| Baseline-equivalent learned policy | Superiority claim only; negative result remains valid |
| Dashboard-only evidence | Dashboard/thesis claim using that evidence |

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

### 21.1 Repository expectation status

The exact repository homes for some Layer 6 artifacts remain partly unresolved by the merged registry. Phase 6 may use architecture/registry-supported conceptual storage expectations, but final concrete paths must remain manifest-mapped until `MC-009` and `L6L7-OI-006` are resolved.

### 21.2 Conceptual storage expectations

| Storage area | Expected Phase 6 content | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `configs/policies/` | action-space maps, legality masks, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ configs, cost-model configs, pseudo-label construction configs, policy selection configs | architecture-supported conceptual area |
| `records/readiness_context_records/` | validated `ReadinessContextRecord` exports | registry-supported conceptual/canonical area |
| `records/evidence_quality_records/` | learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants and source metadata | registry-supported conceptual area; variant governance required |
| `records/policy_records/` | `PolicyActionRecord`, policy metadata, supervised policy outputs | registry-supported conceptual/canonical area |
| evaluation artifact area | `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry` references, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags | exact path governed by registry/repository conventions |
| card/source-bundle area | target-construction, cost-model, evidence-quality, and controller-card source bundles | exact canonical names/paths unresolved; Layer 10 renders later |
| manifests/handoff area | Phase 6 handoff manifest, hashes, validation status, open issues, claim tags | required for downstream phases and reproducibility |

### 21.3 Storage prohibitions

Phase 6 storage must not:

- overwrite upstream clean/source records;
- store dashboard-generated cards/views as primary evidence;
- store pseudo-labels as ground-truth readiness labels;
- store hidden targets as context features;
- store update-enabled training curves in the same artifact as held-out frozen evaluation results;
- hide failed/negative results;
- omit open issues from manifests;
- use unregistered action aliases as canonical action tokens.

### 21.4 Manifest requirements

Every Phase 6 output package must include:

```text
stress_profile_id where applicable later/downstream only
embodiment_mode_id where applicable later/downstream only

legality_mask_id where applicable
cost_config_id where applicable
target_construction_id where applicable
metric_dictionary_ids where applicable
matched_comparison_report_ids where applicable
negative_result_note_ids where applicable

```

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Required handoff to Phase 7 — Learning-to-defer

Phase 7 may consume Phase 6 outputs only through validated policy context/action/cost/fallback lineage. The Phase 7 handoff must include:

- `ReadinessContextRecord` IDs;
- learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` IDs where used;
- `PolicyActionRecord` IDs and policy family;
- action-space version and legality-mask ID;
- fallback-source definitions where available;
- cost-model config and cost sensitivity status;
- pseudo-label/target-construction IDs and leakage status;
- A9 baseline results and diagnostic flags;
- claim tags and open issue IDs.

Phase 7 owns `DeferralRecord`; Phase 6 must not pre-create it as if learning-to-defer has already been implemented.

### 23.2 Required handoff to Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness

Phase 8 may consume Phase 6 frozen policies, readiness contexts, policy actions, legality masks, and cost/reward configuration references for replay. Phase 6 does not produce transitions, sessions, reward traces, policy rollouts, or environment diagnostics.

Required Phase 8 handoff fields:

```text

EvidenceQualityRecord pointers where used

run_id
config_hash
seed
validation_status
claim_safety_tags
diagnostic_only status
```

### 23.3 Required handoff to Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite

Phase 9 may use Phase 6 records as clean-policy/context baselines for later stress-conditioned comparisons. Phase 6 does not produce `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifests, or stressed variants.

Stress-conditioned use must later create new derived/stress records while preserving the clean Phase 6 source IDs and adding `stress_conditioned` / `stress_conditioned_proxy_only` tags as applicable.

### 23.4 Required handoff to Phase 10 — Contextual bandit

Phase 10 may use Phase 6 as the frozen supervised baseline and context/action source for immediate-reward adaptation. Phase 10 must not treat Phase 6 supervised training logs as online adaptation evidence. Any Phase 10 update-enabled run requires `PolicyUpdateTrace`, simulation-training/adaptation separation, and held-out frozen evaluation.

### 23.5 Required handoff to Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy

Phase 11 may use Phase 6 supervised policy/context/action records as baselines and initial policy families, but delayed-consequence reward and transition evidence must come from Layer 7/Phase 8 onward. Phase 6 does not create RL reward traces, transition logs, or update curves.

### 23.6 Required handoff to Phases 12–13

Phase 12 and Phase 13 may consume only simulation-compatible policy/action/context lineage after intervening simulation/stress phases have validated the records. Phase 6 does not support real muscle stimulation, real assistive control, real rehabilitation, or clinical embodiment evidence.

### 23.7 Required handoff to Phase 14 and Phase 15

Phase 14 receives Phase 6 dashboard-readable source records, validation reports, evaluation artifacts, card source bundles, metrics, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, limitation tags, and handoff manifest. Layer 10 renders derived cards/views/exports only.

Phase 15 receives Phase 6 claim-evidence pointers, matched comparison reports, metric dictionary references, limitation tags, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, and final open issue list. Phase 15 may integrate only bounded proxy-readiness and evidence-quality claims that survive Phase 6 validation.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 6 is done when all required criteria below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest/metric/claim/dashboard foundations are available or gaps are logged.
- Phase 1 source records are readable, immutable, split-safe, temporally ordered, and lineage-complete.
- Phase 2 prediction/model records are readable, valid, and joinable.
- Phase 3 calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, and threshold records are valid and split-safe.
- Phase 4 IHARQ decisions, traces, action tokens, reason codes, fallback/unsafe records, and rule-derived evidence-quality variants where used are valid.
- Phase 5 RegimeRisk records, conditional trust records, stop-loss warnings, temporal cutoffs, and proxy limitation tags are valid where used.
- `ReadinessContextRecord` outputs exist for all eligible rows and include source IDs, run/config/seed/schema/version/validation fields, split IDs, action-space version, observable-field-set ID, and claim tags.
- No target, true label, decoder correctness, future reward, future window, future stress outcome, future embodiment outcome, oracle cost, or dashboard-derived metric appears as an ordinary decision-time feature.
- Learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` outputs exist where A6 is claimed and include producer/variant metadata, target-construction ID/version, split, source IDs, schema version, config hash, seed, and proxy-target status.
- Pseudo-label files are generated, versioned, split-safe, and leakage-audited.
- Target-construction card/source bundle records source labels, allowed future information, cost vector, leakage guard, split, target route, and claim boundary.
- Action-space file, action alias map, and legality-mask file exist, validate, and preserve canonical Layer 4 token identities.
- Cost-model config and cost-model card/source bundle exist, are hashed, and include sensitivity variants or a limitation note.
- Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ policy artifacts are trained on training data, selected on validation data, and evaluated frozen on held-out data.
- `PolicyActionRecord` outputs exist and include policy ID, policy family, action, source context ID, action-space version, legality-mask ID, cost config ID, `source_iharq_action` where applicable, action probability/expected cost where applicable, frozen/update mode, source IDs, and claim tags.
- A6 evaluation artifacts include learned evidence-quality metrics, reliability-vs-coverage, high-confidence-wrong detection, matched report, metric dictionary references, and negative-result notes where applicable.
- A9 evaluation artifacts include action-distribution, matched-cost/coverage comparison, context ablation, cost sensitivity, metric dictionary references, and negative-result notes where applicable.
- Required baselines are present or explicitly recorded as missing with downgrade handling.
- Matched comparison keys are present for thesis-facing results, or affected rows are diagnostic-only.
- Every reported metric has a `MetricDictionaryEntry` reference, or it is diagnostic-only.
- Negative results and baseline-equivalent outcomes are visible and not hidden.
- Dashboard-readable source bundles and Layer 10 warning inputs are exported with lineage.
- Controller-card and evidence-quality-card source bundles are prepared without treating rendered cards as source evidence.
- Layer 0 claim-safety tags and forbidden-claim checks are complete.
- Phase 6 handoff manifest is complete and usable by Phases 7–15.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 7 or thesis-facing use of Phase 6 outputs must not proceed from affected records if any of the following remain unresolved without diagnostic-only handling:

- missing or invalid upstream Phase 1–5 records;
- missing split, source ID, config hash, seed, or schema version;
- source-record mutation or overwritten upstream evidence;
- split leakage or target leakage;
- hidden labels, future evidence, future reward, oracle cost, or dashboard-generated metric in decision-time context;
- missing or invalid `ReadinessContextRecord`;
- learned/rule `EvidenceQualityRecord` variants not distinguishable;
- missing target-construction/pseudo-label provenance;
- missing action-space or legality-mask file;
- illegal actions emitted as valid policy output;
- unversioned cost model;
- policy selected on test data;
- training/update curves merged with held-out frozen evaluation;
- missing matched-comparison keys;
- missing metric dictionary entries;
- missing negative-result notes where learned policy fails, is unstable, or is baseline-equivalent;
- dashboard/card output lacking source lineage;
- clinical, deployment, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real muscle-stimulation, or real assistive-control safety claim attempted.

### 26.3 Minimum viable Phase 6

A minimum viable Phase 6 includes validated upstream inputs, `ReadinessContextRecord` assembly, a learned evidence-quality estimator with learned `EvidenceQualityRecord` outputs, leakage-safe target construction, reliability-vs-coverage and high-confidence-wrong diagnostics, a declared action space and legality mask, a versioned cost model, pseudo-label files, a supervised Adaptive-IHARQ policy evaluated frozen against IHARQ-lite and simple threshold/selective baselines, `PolicyActionRecord` outputs, A6/A9 evaluation artifacts, metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, claim tags, card source bundles, and a handoff manifest.

### 26.4 Strong / thesis-ready Phase 6

A strong Phase 6 additionally includes robust subject/session/dataset generalization, context ablations, cost sensitivity, action imbalance analysis, multiple seed stability, high-confidence wrong detection, comparison against longer-window/voting/averaging/ensemble baselines, RegimeRisk-aware and regime-unaware policy comparisons, complete target-construction cards, complete controller/evidence-quality source bundles, complete dashboard warning inputs, complete claim-evidence rows, and explicit negative-result/baseline-sufficiency discussion.

### 26.5 Phase 6 final self-check

Before Phase 6 is considered complete, verify that:

- official Phase 0–15 identities are preserved;
- A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata only;
- C0–C4 remain claim-maturity summaries only;
- Layer 6 owns policy context/action records but does not overwrite Layer 4 or Layer 5 records;
- IHARQ-lite remains Phase 4 / Layer 4-owned and appears in Phase 6 only as an upstream baseline/reference context;
- learned and rule-derived evidence-quality variants remain distinguishable;
- pseudo-labels are not treated as clinical/human readiness labels;
- matched-comparison keys and metric dictionary entries are present;
- frozen evaluation is separated from training/update-enabled adaptation;
- Layer 10 source-vs-derived boundaries are preserved;
- Layer 0 claim-safety boundaries are preserved;
- negative results are visible;
- all unresolved issues are listed rather than hidden;
- the downstream handoff enables Phase 7 without requiring unsupported reinterpretation.

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 7 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 7` |
| Official phase name | `Learning-to-defer` |
| Primary architecture layer | Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer |
| Primary Layer 6 submodule | 6.3 Learning-to-defer |
| Official implementation role | Routing and fallback baseline gate after Phase 6 and before Phase 8 simulated closed-loop readiness |
| Primary evidence role | Evaluate whether uncertain or risky cases should be routed away from direct prediction toward fallback, safer model, request-more-evidence, no-action/safe-hold, or explicitly labeled supervisor-proxy routes under matched cost/coverage constraints |
| Primary record produced | `DeferralRecord` |
| Conditional record produced | Deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows where the deferral router emits policy actions rather than only annotations; these must preserve action-space version, legality-mask ID, `source_iharq_action` where applicable, and Phase 7 lineage |
| Main artifacts produced/prepared | deferral target definition files, fallback-source logs, direct-versus-defer expected-cost tables, deferral burden curves, matched-cost and matched-coverage reports, learning-to-defer card source bundle, Phase 7 evaluation records, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and handoff manifest |
| Main upstream inputs | `ReadinessContextRecord`, learned or rule-derived `EvidenceQualityRecord` where valid, `PolicyActionRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord`, conditional `TrustStateRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, cost configs, action-space/legality-mask files, fallback-source definitions, and split-safe evaluation labels |
| Main downstream consumers | Phase 8 simulated closed-loop readiness; Phase 9 StressForge-Lite; Phase 10 contextual bandit; Phase 11 reinforcement-learning policy; Phase 12 MyoSuite embodiment demo; Phase 13 OpenSim replay or optional comparison; Phase 14 dashboard/cards; Phase 15 final thesis integration; Layer 0 claim-safety review |
| Main ablation/evaluation linkage | A8 — learning-to-defer; strengthens comparisons with A3, A5, A6, A7, and A9; prepares deferral-route context for A10/A11 and later A12/A13 contexts |
| Evidence boundary | Computational/proxy deferral evaluation on public EEG and derived readiness records; no clinical routing, no real expert triage, no real patient safety, and no real deployment readiness |
| Claim-safety tags | `public_eeg_only`, `low_calibration_protocol`, `proxy_readiness`, `pseudo_label_based` where pseudo-labels train targets, `evaluation_only`, `computational_policy_only`, `diagnostic_only` where applicable, `simulation_only` only when a supervisor proxy or later simulation route is used, and all non-clinical/non-deployment prohibition tags |

Phase 7 implements the learning-to-defer evidence gate. It asks whether a model should act directly, request or wait for more evidence, route to a fallback or safer decision source, choose a no-action/safe-hold route, or use a simulation-only supervisor proxy. It is not a generic abstention phase: abstention only says “do not predict,” while deferral must identify a target route, cost, burden, reason, and downstream consequence.

Phase 7 also acts as a criticism-resistant comparator for Phase 6 supervised Adaptive-IHARQ. If learning-to-defer performs similarly to or better than Adaptive-IHARQ under matched cost and matched coverage, the thesis must preserve that result and narrow any claim that the more complex adaptive policy is necessary. If Adaptive-IHARQ outperforms learning-to-defer under fair matching, Phase 7 provides the baseline needed to justify the added complexity.

Phase 7 does not own Layer 7 simulation records, StressForge profiles, contextual-bandit updates, RL updates, embodiment outcomes, dashboard cards, or final thesis claims. It produces deferral/routing evidence that later phases may consume.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 7 is the routing and fallback baseline gate. It evaluates whether uncertain or high-risk cases should be routed away from direct prediction rather than simply rejected or accepted. It makes deferral explicit by requiring a declared target, cost, reason, fallback availability, burden, and outcome-scoring route.

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 7 controls the bottleneck between selective prediction and adaptive readiness policy. Selective prediction can abstain, but it does not say what happens next. Phase 7 tests whether the system can make a better bounded routing decision among:

- direct acceptance;
- waiting or requesting more evidence;
- fallback to a conservative decoder or safer model family;
- no-action/safe-hold routing;
- unsafe blocking;
- simulation-only supervisor proxy or oracle-for-analysis-only route.

### 4.3 Scientific role

Phase 7 is both a policy component and a baseline challenge to supervised Adaptive-IHARQ. It asks whether a simpler learned deferral router explains most of the benefit that might otherwise be attributed to a more complex adaptive policy. This is necessary for a criticism-resistant thesis because a learned readiness policy is only meaningfully justified if it improves over strong routing baselines under matched comparison rules.

### 4.4 Evidence role

Phase 7 produces evidence about:

1. deferral rate;
2. deferral target distribution;
3. fallback burden;
4. direct-versus-defer expected cost;
5. accepted accuracy after deferral;
6. deferred-case accuracy or deferred-case scored outcome where available;
7. wrong-accept reduction;
8. matched-cost and matched-coverage performance;
9. benefit under high uncertainty or high RegimeRisk;
10. over-deferral and unrealistic fallback failure modes.

### 4.5 What Phase 7 must not do

Phase 7 must not:

- treat rejection as deferral unless a target route exists;
- imply a real expert fallback unless real expert labels, licensing, and availability are documented;
- use oracle labels or future outcomes as decision-time features;
- hide fallback burden or defer-rate inflation;
- overwrite Phase 6 policy actions or Phase 4 IHARQ decisions;
- produce simulation transitions, reward traces, StressForge profiles, embodiment outcomes, dashboard cards, or final thesis claims as primary source evidence;
- claim clinical safety, medical-device readiness, real patient safety, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real deployment readiness, or real assistive-control safety.

## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

| Layer | Phase 7 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews deferral/fallback wording, proxy/oracle labels, diagnostic-only downgrades, negative results, and limitation tags | Layer 0 audits claims; it does not produce empirical deferral evidence. |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Supplies immutable dataset/window/split/preprocessing/label-map/artifact-flag lineage and matched keys | Layer 1 records remain clean sources and must not be overwritten. |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Supplies predictions, model registry, baseline metrics, subject profiles where available, failure cases, and possible conservative/safer fallback model evidence | Phase 7 may use Layer 2 outputs as fallback candidates only through declared fallback-source definitions. |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Supplies calibrated confidence, entropy, margin, uncertainty, selective-prediction baselines, threshold registry, and matched operating points | Phase 7 may compare against selective prediction and thresholds but must not retune thresholds on test data. |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Supplies IHARQ action tokens, reason codes, fallback/unsafe/request evidence traces, rule-derived evidence-quality variants where available, and A5 baseline | Phase 7 preserves Layer 4 tokens in `source_iharq_action` or references; it must not rename Layer 4 `uncertain` as `defer`. |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Supplies temporal trust, risk, stop-loss, and conditional trust-state context for deferral decisions where split-safe and decision-time legal | RegimeRisk remains temporal trust/proxy context, not physiological diagnosis or safety proof. |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Primary owner of learning-to-defer, `DeferralRecord`, and conditional deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows | Layer 6 owns deferral/routing records; it does not own upstream prediction/calibration/IHARQ/regime records. |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Downstream consumer in Phase 8; applies deferral routes in simulation later | Phase 7 does not create `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, or simulation episodes. |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Later consumer of deferral policies under stress profiles | Phase 7 does not produce stress profiles/schedules/manifests. |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite / OpenSim / Static-Replay Embodiment | Later optional consumer of hold/no-action/fallback-compatible routes through simulation-compatible policy records | Phase 7 does not produce embodiment state/outcome/demo records. |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Later read-only renderer of deferral page, learning-to-defer card, curves, fallback burden tables, warnings, and exports | Layer 10 outputs are derived and must not be treated as primary deferral evidence. |

## 6. Registry Issue Intake and Impact Assessment

| Registry / continuity issue | Affected Phase 7 entity | Impact on Phase 7 | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/7 boundary | `ReadinessContextRecord` inputs and later simulation-visible context | Phase 7 consumes canonical Layer 6 context; later Phase 8 may use run-specific simulation-compatible instances | Preserve Layer 6 ownership; do not create a Layer 7-owned context in Phase 7. |
| `DeferralRecord` target/reason vocabulary incomplete | `DeferralRecord.deferral_target`, `deferral_reason` | Implementations may invent incompatible target/reason values | Use declared local controlled vocabulary with manifest mapping; mark final enum as unresolved until registry confirmation. |
| Target-construction artifact names/paths unresolved | Learning-to-defer labels and target/source bundles | Leakage and reproducibility risk | Mark exact artifact name/path as `inferred_candidate`, `requires_confirmation: true`; require manifest mapping and split/leakage validation. |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema/path unresolved | Deferral rate, fallback burden, matched cost, wrong-accept reduction, accepted accuracy | Missing metric definitions weaken thesis-readiness | Require metric dictionary references; downgrade metrics without entries to diagnostic-only. |
| `PolicyActionRecord` action aliases | `defer`, `no_action`, `fallback`, `unsafe`, `uncertain`, `combine_evidence` | Action semantics may be overwritten or confused | Preserve `defer`/`no_action` as Layer 6 policy-only routes; preserve Layer 4 tokens in `source_iharq_action`; enforce action-space version and alias map. |
| Real expert/proxy fallback ambiguity | fallback-source logs and supervisor-proxy routes | Unsupported expert-routing or clinical fallback claims | Require source type: conservative decoder, safer model, request path, no-action/safe hold, simulated supervisor proxy, oracle-for-analysis-only; forbid unverified real expert claims. |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` lifecycle | Later update-enabled use of deferral policy | Phase 7 default frozen evaluation could be contaminated by update hooks | Mark update disabled; require disabled-update audit if an update-capable environment is present; require `PolicyUpdateTrace` only for later authorized update-enabled phases. |
| Dashboard metric/source boundary | deferral curves, burden tables, card source bundle, dashboard metrics | Layer 10 outputs could be mistaken for primary evidence | Mark Phase 7 records as dashboard-readable source; Layer 10 card/figures/views as generated later. |
| Repository storage homes partially unresolved | card source bundles, target-construction artifacts, evaluation reports | Loader/export fragmentation | Use canonical supported `records/deferral_records/` for `DeferralRecord`; use manifest-mapped run-local paths for unresolved artifacts. |
| Layer 0 claim artifact schemas/path incomplete | claim-evidence entries and limitation tags | Final claim approval may be blocked | Preserve claim-evidence rows and limitation tags; keep final claim wording pending Layer 0 review. |
| Phase 5 simulated-trajectory wording issue | Phase 7 vs Phase 8 boundary | Possible confusion that Phase 7 owns simulated trajectories | Treat Phase 7 as deferral/routing only; Phase 8 owns simulated closed-loop readiness records. |

### 6.1 Impact assessment summary

No registry issue blocks Phase 7 from producing bounded learning-to-defer evidence if all unresolved items are handled through explicit manifest mapping, controlled local vocabularies, diagnostic-only downgrades, and claim-safety tags. However, thesis-ready A8 evidence is weakened or blocked if deferral targets, metric dictionary entries, matched keys, or fallback-source assumptions are missing or unversioned.

### 7.2 Phase 0 inheritance verdict

```yaml
phase0_inheritance_gap: true
gap_scope:
  - exact canonical name/path for learning-to-defer target-construction artifacts
  - final controlled vocabulary for deferral_target and deferral_reason
  - fully instantiated MetricDictionaryEntry rows for all deferral metrics
  - final claim-evidence artifact schema/path for Layer 0 approval
gap_effect:
  blocks_phase_execution: false
  weakens_thesis_readiness: true
  requires_diagnostic_only_if_unresolved: true
  requires_manifest_mapping: true
```

Phase 7 may proceed if these gaps are explicitly tracked and if affected comparisons are marked diagnostic-only until the missing definitions are repaired. Phase 7 must not present A8 results as thesis-ready when required metric dictionary entries, deferral target definitions, fallback-source declarations, matched keys, or claim-evidence rows are missing.

### 9.2 Forbidden or restricted inputs

| Restricted input | Rule |
|---|---|
| True labels or decoder correctness | May be used for training target construction or evaluation scoring only under split rules; must not be ordinary decision-time features. |
| Oracle fallback actions | May be analysis-only or simulation-only; must not be treated as available real fallback during production-style evaluation. |
| Future windows or post-deferral outcomes | May score a deferral strategy only after the decision point; must not be used as observable context before the decision. |
| Dashboard-derived metrics/cards | May not be used as policy features or evidence-generation inputs. |
| Real expert labels | Not assumed. If absent, expert/supervisor channels must be tagged `proxy`, `oracle_for_analysis_only`, or `simulation_only`. |
| Phase 8 transition/reward feedback | Not required and not policy-visible in Phase 7; later simulation-only use must be separated. |

### 9.3 Input validation states

Every Phase 7 computational input must be classified as one of:

```text
valid_source_input
valid_derived_input
valid_proxy_target_input
valid_scoring_only_input
valid_dashboard_readiness_input
missing_but_optional
missing_blocks_claim
invalid_diagnostic_only
invalid_blocked
```

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 7 evidence production follows this evidence-level chain:

```text
validated upstream context/action/calibration/IHARQ/regime records
→ deferral target and fallback-source declaration
→ cost/action/legal target validation
→ split-safe deferral target construction and/or router training
→ frozen held-out deferral evaluation
→ DeferralRecord production
→ matched comparison against direct prediction, selective prediction, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality threshold, and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ
→ negative-result and diagnostic-only tagging
→ dashboard-readable source bundle and handoff manifest
→ later Layer 10 derived views/cards/exports
→ Layer 0 claim-safety review and Phase 15 thesis integration
```

### 12.1 Deferral semantics

Phase 7 must explicitly distinguish:

| Route | Meaning | Phase 7 rule |
|---|---|---|
| `accept` | Use current predicted intent | Allowed only when action is legal and cost/risk supports direct action. |
| `wait` | Delay without selecting another decision source | Distinct from deferral; must have wait budget and reason. |
| `request_evidence` | Acquire/reveal/evaluate another evidence window | Distinct from deferral target unless declared as the target route. |
| `defer` | Route to another decision source | Policy-only Layer 6 route requiring target, fallback/source, and cost. |
| `fallback` | Use conservative baseline or safe route | Must declare fallback source and availability. |
| `no_action` | Safe hold/no-op/no-action route | Policy-only route; not a clinical safety proof. |
| `unsafe` | Block action / safety warning | Must preserve upstream unsafe or stop-loss lineage where relevant. |
| `reject` | Generic refusal to predict | Not sufficient as a deferral record unless mapped to a target route and reason. |

### 12.2 Deferral target construction

Target construction may use split-safe scoring information to learn when deferral would reduce cost relative to direct prediction. However:

- target labels must be versioned and tied to a target-construction config;
- correctness, future outcomes, oracle labels, or supervisor-proxy outcomes are scoring/target fields, not policy-visible decision-time features;
- proxy/oracle/simulated fallback must be labeled as such;
- cost weights must be sensitivity-analyzed or limitation-tagged;
- if target construction is arbitrary or unversioned, A8 results are diagnostic-only.

### 12.3 Evidence outputs by logical stage

| Stage | Evidence action | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Input readiness | validate upstream records, splits, contexts, and actions | input validation report, diagnostic-only flags where required |
| Target declaration | define fallback/deferral targets and reason vocabulary | deferral target-definition file, fallback-source log |
| Cost declaration | define direct/defer/fallback/request/no-action costs | cost config reference, direct-versus-defer cost table |
| Router evaluation | train/select/evaluate learning-to-defer model or baseline under split-safe protocol | `DeferralRecord`, conditional deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord`, Phase 7 evaluation records |
| Comparison | compare against accept-all, confidence/entropy/margin thresholds, selective prediction, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality threshold, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, and available longer-window/voting/ensemble controls | A8 matched reports, burden curves, baseline-sufficiency table |
| Limitation handling | preserve negative results, proxy limitations, over-deferral, unrealistic fallback, missing metrics | `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, claim tags |
| Handoff | package source records and config/evaluation lineage | Phase 7 handoff manifest, card source bundle |

---

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream input gate | Phase 1–6 source records exist, validate, and join on matched keys | Block affected rows or mark diagnostic-only. |
| Deferral target gate | Each deferral route has declared target, source type, availability rule, proxy/oracle/simulation status, and legality relation | `DeferralRecord` blocked for targetless rows; rejection-only results not A8. |
| Fallback-source gate | Fallback or safer model source is versioned, split-safe, and not hidden oracle unless tagged analysis-only | Fallback claims diagnostic-only. |
| Action-space/alias gate | `defer` and `no_action` are policy-only; Layer 4 source tokens preserved; aliases mapped | Invalid action rows diagnostic-only or blocked. |
| Cost-model gate | Direct/defer/fallback/request/no-action costs are versioned and sensitivity status is reported | Matched-cost claims blocked if missing. |
| Leakage gate | No true label, decoder correctness, future window, future reward/outcome, or oracle cost is visible as ordinary policy input | Leakage blocks thesis-ready A8. |
| Split gate | Training/validation/test and subject/session boundaries are preserved | Leakage or unmatched splits make results diagnostic-only. |
| Frozen-evaluation gate | Final A8 comparison uses frozen policy/router on held-out data | Mixed training/evaluation curves blocked. |
| Baseline sufficiency gate | Required baselines are present or missingness is disclosed | Adaptive/deferral claims narrowed if baselines are missing. |
| Matched-comparison gate | Cost, coverage, request budget, fallback burden, and matched lineage are preserved | Unmatched comparisons diagnostic-only. |
| Metric dictionary gate | Deferral metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Missing metrics diagnostic-only. |
| Negative-result gate | Over-deferral, no benefit, underperformance, fallback failure, or baseline equivalence is recorded | Missing note blocks claim-safety approval. |
| Dashboard boundary gate | Phase 7 source records separated from Layer 10 generated cards/plots | Dashboard-derived evidence misuse invalid. |
| Claim-safety gate | Forbidden claims blocked; proxy labels and limitations attached | Forbidden claims invalid. |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 7 exits successfully when:

1. valid `DeferralRecord` outputs exist for eligible rows;
2. deferral targets, fallback sources, reason codes, costs, legality masks, and proxy/oracle/simulation labels are declared and versioned;
3. learning-to-defer is fairly compared against direct prediction, selective prediction, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality threshold, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, and available baseline/fallback alternatives under matched cost or matched coverage;
4. all A8 evaluation artifacts, matched reports, metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, diagnostic flags, and claim tags are present;
5. Phase 7 produces a handoff package that Phase 8 can consume without interpreting deferral as simulation, reward, or embodiment evidence.

Exact local field names for fallback prediction and cost components must be schema-bound or manifest-mapped if the final registry schema does not yet fix them.

| Missing key type | Consequence |

| Source identity keys missing | Block affected rows. |

| Matched group missing | Comparison cannot be used as matched A8 evidence. |
| Claim tag missing | Layer 0 review blocks claim use. |
| Stress/embodiment keys missing | Not blocking Phase 7 unless Phase 7 claims stress/embodiment linkage; later phases must add them. |

### 15.1 A0–A13 linkage

| A0 — raw decoder | Baseline comparator | Use accept-all/direct prediction reference where available; no A0 ownership. |
| A1 — calibrated decoder | Upstream calibration reference | Consume calibrated probabilities indirectly through context; no A1 ownership. |
| A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Baseline comparator | Compare against confidence/threshold rejection under matched coverage/cost. |
| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | Upstream/supporting comparator where available | Use entropy, margin, calibrated uncertainty, and selective-prediction/risk-coverage baselines according to available Phase 3 records; do not rename ablation IDs. |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Fallback/baseline comparator where available | May serve as safer model/fallback source only if declared and matched; corrected document keeps these ordinary-control contexts under A4. |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Required baseline comparator | Compare deferral against rule-based IHARQ-lite and reason-coded actions. |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Upstream context/comparator | Use evidence-quality thresholds or learned score context where available. |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Optional/conditional context | Compare deferral with/without RegimeRisk context where available. |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Primary Phase 7 evaluation context | Produce `DeferralRecord`, matched reports, burden curves, fallback-source logs, and A8 evaluation artifacts. |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Required comparator | Compare learning-to-defer against Phase 6 supervised Adaptive-IHARQ under matched cost/coverage. |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Downstream prepared only | Provide deferral route/action lineage for later bandit simulation; no updates. |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Downstream prepared only | Provide deferral route/action lineage for later RL simulation; no updates. |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Downstream prepared only | Prepare stress-compatible IDs/tags if needed later; no stress records. |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Downstream optional prepared only | Provide no-action/fallback-compatible route lineage where later embodiment consumes it; no embodiment records. |

Note: A0–A13 remain evaluation-use metadata only. Phase 7 produces records used by A8; A8 does not produce or own `DeferralRecord`.

### 16.2 Required Layer 10 learning-to-defer page behavior

The Phase 14 learning-to-defer page must show, but not recompute hidden evidence logic:

- deferral rate;

### 16.3 Layer 10 prohibitions

Layer 10 must not:

- train or select the deferral router;
- retune thresholds or costs;
- create hidden fallback definitions;
- repair missing `DeferralRecord` rows;
- hide over-deferral or negative results;
- erase proxy/oracle/simulation-only labels;
- promote rendered card/curve/table as primary evidence;
- convert diagnostic-only A8 results into thesis-ready claims.

### 16.4 Not-dashboard inputs and dashboard-export manifest inputs

The following Phase 7 materials are not ordinary dashboard inputs and must not be exposed as if they were user-facing evidence unless converted into validated, traceable summaries with the required limitation tags:

| Material | Dashboard handling | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Training-only target construction rows | `not_dashboard_input`; may be summarized only through validated evaluation artifacts | Prevents pseudo-label or target-construction internals from being mistaken for observed readiness labels. |
| Scoring-only true labels, correctness flags, post-deferral outcome fields, oracle labels, and oracle costs | `not_dashboard_input`; allowed only as evaluation-source lineage behind aggregate reports | Prevents decision-time leakage and prevents oracle/proxy information from being treated as deployable context. |
| Cost-sensitivity sweeps used only for model selection | `not_dashboard_input` until final selected/frozen cost config and sensitivity report are saved | Prevents hidden retuning or cherry-picked dashboard curves. |
| Intermediate router checkpoints not selected under the declared validation protocol | `not_dashboard_input`; record only in reproducibility manifests if retained | Prevents dashboard promotion of training artifacts. |
| Raw unsupported fallback assumptions | `dashboard_warning_input` only after versioned fallback-source logging | Prevents unsupported expert/fallback claims. |
| Phase 7 source-record/export manifest entries | `dashboard_export_manifest_input` | Allows Layer 10 to package traceable exports without becoming the owner of Phase 7 evidence. |

Dashboard export packages prepared from Phase 7 must include source-record IDs, run IDs, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, metric dictionary IDs, matched-comparison IDs, diagnostic-only flags, negative-result-note IDs, claim-safety tags, and unresolved-issue references.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 7 may support bounded claims such as:

- learning-to-defer can be evaluated as a routing comparator for uncertain public-EEG evidence;
- deferral/fallback routing can reduce wrong accepts under declared cost and proxy-fallback assumptions;
- deferral burden, fallback availability, and accepted/deferred-case outcomes are necessary to interpret readiness policies;
- learning-to-defer is a strong baseline for supervised Adaptive-IHARQ under matched cost/coverage;
- in some regimes, a simpler deferral route may be sufficient or may narrow the need for more complex adaptive policies;
- deferral evaluation improves traceability of accept/reject/request/fallback/no-action behavior.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 7 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- validated human expert triage unless real expert labels/source are actually present and documented;
- clinical fallback availability;
- real physiological safety from no-action/safe-hold routes;
- deployed online learning or adaptive intervention.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 7 outputs must carry the strictest applicable tags:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based where pseudo labels construct targets
evaluation_only
computational_policy_only
fallback_proxy_limited where fallback is not a real validated route
oracle_for_analysis_only where oracle labels are used for analysis/scoring
simulation_only where a supervisor proxy or later simulation route is used
diagnostic_only where validation or matching is incomplete
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_real_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Claims must be downgraded to diagnostic-only or non-thesis-ready if:

- fallback source is undefined;
- deferral target vocabulary is absent;
- true labels/oracle costs leak into decision-time inputs;
- cost weights are unversioned or unreported;
- matched cost/coverage is absent;
- required baselines are missing and not disclosed;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- over-deferral hides low coverage;
- supervisor proxy is presented as a real expert;
- Phase 7 results are mixed with later simulation/update-enabled results;
- dashboard-generated outputs are treated as primary evidence.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 must review:

- A8 claim-evidence rows;
- all limitation tags;
- diagnostic-only flags;
- negative-result notes;
- fallback/proxy/oracle wording;
- matched comparison status;
- forbidden claim scan;
- final thesis phrasing before any Phase 15 claim uses Phase 7 evidence.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 remain capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels. They are not phases, ablation IDs, layers, artifact owners, or substitutes for official Phase 7.

| Capability tier relationship | Phase 7 effect | Claim-maturity handling |
|---|---|---|
| Earlier decoder/calibration/IHARQ/RegimeRisk maturity | Preserved | Phase 7 consumes earlier evidence; it does not weaken prior valid claims unless it reveals baseline-sufficiency/negative-result limitations. |
| C2-style adaptive policy maturity | Strengthened conditionally | Phase 7 strengthens adaptive-policy maturity by adding learning-to-defer as a strong comparator and routing mechanism. |
| C3/C4 simulation/stress/embodiment maturity | Prepared only | Phase 7 provides deferral routes for later simulation/stress/embodiment contexts but does not claim those tiers. |
| Stopping-point governance | Strengthened | If Phase 7 is strong and later phases fail, the thesis can still report a deferral/routing comparator under proxy limits. |
| Claim narrowing | Required when applicable | If learning-to-defer matches or beats Adaptive-IHARQ, Adaptive-IHARQ superiority claims must be narrowed. |

Phase 7 can improve claim maturity only when A8 records, matched comparisons, metric definitions, fallback-source assumptions, negative-result notes, and Layer 0 claim-safety tags are complete. Otherwise, Phase 7 remains diagnostic/supporting evidence.

---

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Required negative-result cases

Phase 7 must explicitly preserve negative results including:

- learning-to-defer does not improve wrong-accept reduction;
- learning-to-defer reduces wrong accepts but at unacceptable fallback/request/no-action burden;
- deferral performs similarly to supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- deferral beats supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- deferral overuses fallback or no-action routes;
- fallback source is unrealistic or unavailable for many cases;
- deferral helps only under high RegimeRisk or certain subjects/sessions;
- cost sensitivity reverses conclusions;
- deferral model is unstable across seeds or splits;
- required baselines are missing;
- metric dictionary or matched-comparison gaps make results diagnostic-only.

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency requirements

Phase 7 must compare against the strongest feasible baselines:

| Baseline | Required status | Missingness handling |
|---|---|---|
| Accept-all / direct decoder | Required | A8 incomplete if absent. |
| Confidence threshold | Required | Must disclose if unavailable. |
| Entropy rejection | Required where uncertainty exists | Diagnostic if omitted without reason. |
| Margin rejection | Required where margin exists | Diagnostic if omitted without reason. |
| Selective prediction / risk-coverage | Required where Phase 3 produced it | A8 weakened if absent. |
| IHARQ-lite | Required | A8 claim blocked if absent without justified upstream failure. |
| Evidence-quality threshold | Required where Phase 6 produced score | A6/A8 comparison weakened if absent. |
| Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Required comparator | The central Phase 6/Phase 7 comparison is missing if absent. |
| Longer-window/voting/averaging/ensemble controls | Required where available and relevant as fallback/safer model | Missingness must be disclosed. |
| Regime-aware vs regime-unaware deferral | Conditional | Required only if RegimeRisk features are used. |

### 19.3 Handling if learning-to-defer matches Adaptive-IHARQ

If Phase 7 A8 matches Phase 6 A9 at matched cost/coverage, the correct thesis interpretation is not to hide the result. It should be reported as evidence that a simpler routing policy may be sufficient under the tested conditions. Adaptive-IHARQ novelty or superiority claims must be narrowed or made conditional.

### 19.4 Handling if learning-to-defer fails

If learning-to-defer fails, the phase still contributes evidence by identifying routing limits, fallback assumptions, deferral burden, and cases where richer readiness policies may be necessary. Negative results must be attached to `NegativeResultNote` entries and surfaced to Layer 10 and Layer 0.

---

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure / missingness condition | Consequence | Required record/tag |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `ReadinessContextRecord` | Block affected rows | validation failure |
| Missing fallback-source definition | `DeferralRecord` blocked or diagnostic-only | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` |
| Deferral target absent or targetless rejection | Not valid A8 deferral evidence | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` |
| Real expert implied without evidence | Claim blocked | forbidden-claim flag / limitation tag |
| Oracle label used as decision-time feature | Leakage; block thesis-ready use | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`; Layer 0 warning |
| Future windows/outcomes visible before decision | Leakage; block affected comparison | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` |
| Unversioned cost model | Matched-cost claims blocked | negative/diagnostic note |
| No cost sensitivity or limitation | Claim weakened | limitation tag |
| Missing action-space/legality mask | Deferral action invalid | diagnostic-only/block |
| `uncertain` treated as `defer` without alias map | Invalid action mapping | diagnostic-only/block |
| Over-deferral hides low coverage | Negative result; claim narrowed | `NegativeResultNote` |
| Baselines missing | Claim narrowed or diagnostic-only | baseline-sufficiency note |
| Metric dictionary entries missing | Affected metrics diagnostic-only | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` |
| Matched comparison keys missing | Comparison diagnostic-only | `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` |
| Mixed Phase 7 frozen results with later update-enabled simulation | Block adaptive-policy claim | Layer 0 warning |
| Dashboard outputs used as primary evidence | Invalid | Layer 10/Layer 0 warning |
| Clinical/deployment/safety claim attempted | Forbidden | invalid-claim flag / limitation tag |

### 20.1 Diagnostic-only rules

A Phase 7 result must be marked diagnostic-only if any of the following apply and cannot be repaired:

```text
leakage_detected
fallback_source_missing
fallback_source_oracle_only_without_label
unmatched_cost_or_coverage
metric_dictionary_missing
required_baseline_missing
split_boundary_invalid
action_alias_unresolved
deferral_target_vocabulary_missing
cost_model_unversioned
negative_result_hidden
proxy_limitation_missing
dashboard_generated_output_used_as_source
```

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

### 21.1 Supported storage expectations

| Record/artifact | Repository/storage expectation | Path status |
|---|---|---|
| `DeferralRecord` | `records/deferral_records/` | Architecture-supported canonical record path. |
| `ReadinessContextRecord` input | `records/readiness_context_records/` | Upstream input path; Phase 7 does not overwrite. |
| `PolicyActionRecord` input/output where emitted | `records/policy_records/` | Architecture-supported canonical record path. |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` | `records/policy_update_traces/` or later run-local Layer 7 update paths | Not a default Phase 7 output; reserved/audited later if update hooks exist. |
| Deferral target-definition file | run-local config/manifest-mapped location | Exact canonical name/path unresolved; manifest mapping required. |
| Fallback-source log/table | run-local evaluation/trace artifact, manifest-mapped | Exact canonical name/path unresolved; do not invent authoritative path. |
| Direct-versus-defer expected-cost table | run-local evaluation artifact, manifest-mapped | Exact canonical path unresolved. |
| A8 `MatchedComparisonReport` | evaluation artifact with manifest entry | Canonical record name supported; exact path governed by repository issue. |
| Metric dictionary references | metric dictionary/entry registry | Schema/path unresolved; must still reference IDs. |
| Learning-to-defer card source bundle | card source bundle for later Layer 10 rendering | Exact path unresolved; rendered card generated later. |
| Phase 7 handoff manifest | run-local manifest / reproducibility manifest input | Manifest mapping required. |

### 21.2 Storage rules

- Phase 7 must write new outputs rather than mutating Phase 6 or upstream records.
- All records must include `run_id`, `config_hash`, `seed`, `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `phase_id`, `source_record_ids`, `validation_status`, and claim tags where applicable.
- Candidate or unresolved paths must be resolved through manifests, not silent ad hoc assumptions.
- Clean upstream records must remain immutable.
- Rendered dashboard/card outputs are Phase 14 derived artifacts and must point back to Phase 7 source records.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Required handoff to Phase 8 — Simulated closed-loop readiness

Phase 8 may consume Phase 7 outputs only through validated deferral route/action/context/cost lineage. The handoff must include:

```text
DeferralRecord IDs
ReadinessContextRecord IDs
PolicyActionRecord IDs where emitted or referenced
policy_id / deferral_policy_id
action_space_version
legality_mask_id
deferral_target_config_id
fallback_source_id
fallback_cost_config_id
cost_config_id
matched_group_id
frozen_or_update_mode = frozen for Phase 7 thesis-facing evaluation
proxy/oracle/simulation tags
DiagnosticOnlyFlag IDs
NegativeResultNote IDs
MetricDictionaryEntry IDs
ClaimEvidenceMatrix / ClaimEvidenceManifest pointer where available
source_record_ids
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
validation_status
```

Phase 8 owns transition, session, reward, rollout, diagnostic, and safety-event records. Phase 7 must not create those records or imply that A8 deferral results are closed-loop outcomes.

### 23.2 Required handoff to Phase 9 — StressForge-Lite

Phase 9 may stress-test deferral routes only after Phase 7 source records are validated. The handoff must include deferral policy/context/action lineage and clean matched comparison keys. Phase 7 does not produce `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, or stress-run manifests.

### 23.3 Required handoff to Phase 10 — Contextual bandit

Phase 10 may use Phase 7 deferral routes as candidate bandit arms or comparison baselines only in declared simulation-authorized contexts. Phase 7 provides frozen deferral-router outputs and cost/fallback assumptions. It does not produce bandit rewards, regret curves, exploration traces, or update-enabled `PolicyUpdateTrace` outputs.

### 23.4 Required handoff to Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy

Phase 11 may use deferral routes as part of the sequential action set after Phase 8 simulation records exist. Phase 7 provides route definitions and validated deferral records only. It does not produce RL state transitions, delayed rewards, or policy-update evidence.

### 23.5 Required handoff to Phase 12 and Phase 13 — Embodiment demo/replay contexts

Phase 12/13 may consume only simulation-compatible fallback/no-action/hold route lineage through Phase 8/Layer 7 or validated policy records. Phase 7 does not directly map deferral to muscle stimulation, real device control, clinical action, or embodiment outcomes.

### 23.6 Required handoff to Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

Phase 14 must receive:

- `DeferralRecord` files;
- deferral-aware `PolicyActionRecord` rows where emitted;
- fallback-source logs;
- target-definition files;
- direct-versus-defer cost tables;
- burden curve source data;
- matched reports;
- metric dictionary references;
- negative-result notes;
- diagnostic-only flags;
- learning-to-defer card source bundle;
- handoff/reproducibility manifest entries;
- claim-safety limitation tags.

Phase 14 must render derived views/cards/exports only from these saved source artifacts.

### 23.7 Required handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 15 may use Phase 7 only if A8 records are validated and claim-safety reviewed. It must include deferral evidence in the thesis as bounded proxy/computational readiness routing evidence, not clinical safety or deployment evidence.
