## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

### 5.1 Layer participation

| Layer | Phase 9 role | Ownership and boundary rule |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews stress-conditioned wording, limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, non-claim boundaries, and claim-evidence entries | Layer 0 does not produce stress evidence; it may downgrade or reject claims if stress lineage, metrics, or limitations are missing |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Supplies immutable clean dataset/window/split/label/preprocessing/artifact records and matched keys | Layer 1 records are never overwritten by stress; stressed derivatives must preserve source IDs and split roles |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Supplies immutable prediction/model/baseline records that may be stress-targeted through derived views or stress-conditioned replay | Layer 2 owns decoder evidence; stress cannot change canonical clean predictions or model provenance |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Supplies calibration, uncertainty, threshold, reliability, and leakage-warning records that may be stress-evaluated or stress-targeted only through declared derived records | Layer 3 owns calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction evidence; stress does not retune thresholds on final stress results |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Supplies IHARQ decisions, reason codes, evidence-quality variants, fallback/unsafe/request/combine traces for stress-conditioned evaluation | Layer 4 owns IHARQ semantics; stress may test behavior but not redefine IHARQ actions |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Supplies regime/trust/stop-loss context for stress-conditioned temporal analysis | Layer 5 owns RegimeRisk semantics; stress may stratify or condition analyses but not redefine regime labels |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Supplies readiness contexts, policy actions, deferrals, policy IDs, legality masks, reward/cost config references, and conditional update-trace metadata | Layer 6 owns policy-action records; Phase 9 may evaluate stress-conditioned policy behavior but must not mutate learned policies except through separately declared update-enabled phases with traces |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Supplies transition/session/reward/episode/rollout/diagnostic records and stress-coupling hooks for simulation-side stress evaluation | Layer 7 owns simulation records; Phase 9 may trigger new stress-conditioned runs but must label them Layer 8 stress-conditioned / Layer 7 simulation-derived outputs rather than clean simulation baselines |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite Stress Generator | Primary phase owner; defines stress families, profiles, schedules, injection targets, stressed pointers/views, run manifests, metrics, stress cards/source bundles, and failure taxonomy | Layer 8 owns stress profiles, schedules, stress manifests, stress validity reports, source stress metrics/evaluation artifacts, and stress failure-taxonomy updates; Layer 10 owns dashboard-derived metric/view records |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment | Optional downstream consumer of stress profiles/schedules for later stress-conditioned embodiment demonstration | Phase 9 does not produce embodiment state/outcome records; stress-conditioned embodiment remains Phase 12/13 responsibility |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Later reads saved stress records, metrics, reports, cards/source bundles, warnings, and manifests to render StressForge views/exports | Layer 10 may summarize, visualize, validate, warn, card, export, and package; it must not generate stress profiles, mutate stress schedules, repair missing lineage, or hide negative stress results |

### 5.2 Layer 8 module participation

| Layer 8 module / responsibility | Phase 9 evidence role | Inputs | Outputs | Failure/claim notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stress registry | Defines legal stress families, legal target records/fields, legal intensity ranges, and schedule families | Stress configs, target record family list, claim boundaries | Stress registry config; `StressProfileRecord` candidates | Unsupported stress family or ambiguous target blocks stress claim or makes it diagnostic-only |
| Scenario builder | Composes clean/stressed matched scenarios | Clean source records, split/session keys, stress registry, seeds | `StressProfileRecord`; scenario definitions | Missing clean run or unmatched keys blocks confirmatory comparison |
| Schedule engine | Creates reproducible timing/intensity schedules | Stress profile, window/session/episode timing, seed | `StressScheduleRecord` | Unseeded or post-hoc schedule makes run diagnostic-only |
| Injection adapter | Produces derived stressed views/pointers without mutating clean records | Clean records, target record family, stress profile, stress schedule | `StressedRecordPointer` / `StressedRecordView` candidate objects or equivalent manifest-mapped derived pointers | Clean-source overwrite invalidates stress evidence |
| Consistency guard | Validates stress legality, source/target compatibility, clean/stressed pairing, split safety, and leakage protection | Profiles, schedules, source records, stressed pointers, split manifests | `stress_validity_report.json`; warning inputs | Failed guard produces diagnostic-only or blocked stress run |
| Run orchestrator | Executes or coordinates declared stress runs and preserves reproducibility manifests | Profiles, schedules, clean/stressed pointers, configs, seeds, selected policy/simulation outputs | `stress_run_manifest.csv`; stress run records | Partial or config-drifted runs require negative-result or diagnostic-only status |
| Metric collector | Computes stress degradation, stress sensitivity, stress-conditioned reliability/policy/action/failure metrics | Clean/stressed outcomes, metric dictionary, matched reports | `stress_metrics.parquet`; stress-conditioned metric outputs | Missing metric dictionary or unmatched comparison blocks thesis-ready metric use |
| Stress-card and failure-taxonomy writer | Prepares stress card/source bundle and failure-taxonomy updates | Stress metrics, validity report, negative-result notes, limitation tags | `StressCard` / stress-card source bundle; `stress_failure_taxonomy.csv`; stress limitation notes | Cards are not primary evidence unless linked to records, metrics, configs, seeds, warnings, and claim-evidence entries |

### 5.3 Module-family preservation rule

Phase 9 preserves the following boundaries:

- StressForge-Lite is not Layer 7 simulation, even when stress-conditioned transitions are produced by Layer 7 modules.
- StressForge-Lite is not Layer 6 policy learning, even when policy actions are evaluated under stress.
- StressForge-Lite is not RegimeRisk, even when stress changes regime-aware summaries.
- StressForge-Lite is not IHARQ, even when IHARQ decisions are tested under stress.
- StressForge-Lite is not Layer 9 embodiment, even when stress profiles later condition simulated embodiment.
- Stress cards, dashboard views, and exported stress figures are derived reporting outputs, not hidden primary stress evidence.

## 6. Registry Issue Intake and Impact Assessment

| Issue / unresolved item | Source / status | Phase 9 impact | Required handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Final canonical name for stressed pointer/view | `StressedRecordPointer` / `StressedRecordView` remains `unresolved_requires_confirmation` | Stress injection needs a traceable derived record or pointer family but final export name is not fully confirmed | Use candidate names with `requires_confirmation: true`; preserve `source_record_ids`, `target_record_family`, `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `clean_run_id`, `stressed_run_id`, `seed`, and `config_hash` |
| Metric dictionary path/schema | Inherited unresolved metric dictionary governance | Stress metrics cannot be thesis-ready without `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Export or manifest-map stress metric dictionary entries; mark metrics diagnostic-only if undefined |
| `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` layer-specific filenames | Resolved as global family with layer-specific contexts but requires implementation consistency | Layer 8 stress outcomes must not be presented as records owned by `A12` | Use global `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` with Layer 8 stress context carrying `A12` evaluation-use metadata; preserve explicit artifact filenames where used |
| `ClaimEvidenceManifest` / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` alias governance | Inherited unresolved naming | Stress claims need claim-evidence lineage but final naming may differ | Preserve both terms as alias-governed claim-evidence artifacts until final Phase 15 resolution |
| Dashboard artifact/export IDs | Layer 10 finalization deferred to Phase 14 | Stress dashboards cannot become thesis-ready without export manifests and source links | Prepare manifest-ready IDs and hand off to Phase 14; do not treat ad hoc dashboard plots as evidence |
| Repository path finalization | Some Layer 8 paths are architecture-supported examples or conceptual | Path drift could break reproducibility | Use manifest-mapped Layer 8 locations and preserve path status as supported/recommended or unresolved where registry says so |
| Safety-event naming when stress conditions produce safety events | `SafetyEventRecord` versus logs remains partly unresolved | Stress-induced safety-event summaries could be inconsistently treated | Use producer-owned `SafetyEventRecord` where available; otherwise manifest-map safety logs and mark alias unresolved |
| Stress selected based on final outcomes | Forbidden by architecture | Invalidates robustness evidence | Stress profiles, schedules, intensity levels, and seeds must be declared before final stress evaluation or marked exploratory/diagnostic-only |
| Stress leakage into training or threshold tuning | Forbidden for confirmatory stress claims | Could falsely improve stress robustness | Freeze selected stress evaluation protocol; any update-enabled adaptation must be trace-bound and separated from held-out frozen evaluation |
| Synthetic weakness/fatigue-like stress interpretation | Claim-safety risk | Could be misread as real physiological fatigue/weakness | Use proxy/stress-only wording and limitation tags; no clinical or physiological diagnosis claim |

### 6.1 Registry issue disposition

No unresolved registry issue is silently normalized in Phase 9. Where a missing or unresolved item affects stress evidence, the affected result is handled as one of:

- `blocked_for_confirmatory_use`;
- `diagnostic_only`;
- `inferred_candidate` with `requires_confirmation: true`;
- `manifest_mapped_pending_final_path`;
- `negative_result_preserved`;
- `claim_blocked_until_layer0_review`.

### 7.1 Required Phase 0 foundations

| Phase 0 foundation item | Required by Phase 9? | Expected Phase 9 use | Status / gap handling |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Schema definitions | Yes | Validate `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifests, stressed pointer/view candidates, stress metrics, stress evaluation artifacts, and claim tags | Core schemas expected from Phase 0; stressed pointer/view final naming remains unresolved |
| Record/interface definitions | Yes | Preserve canonical record names and producer-consumer ownership | `StressProfileRecord` and `StressScheduleRecord` supported; pointer/view candidate requires confirmation |
| Configuration families | Yes | Stress registry, stress family configs, intensity configs, matched-comparison configs, injection target configs, guardrails, dashboard/export configs | Required; missing config family blocks or downgrades stress run |
| Mock records / mockable fixtures | Yes | Stress validators should be testable on mock clean/stressed records and malformed stress profiles | Required before stress claims; if absent, validation confidence is weakened |
| Validation scripts | Yes | Validate stress legality, seed/schedule determinism, clean/stressed pairing, split safety, source preservation, metrics, dashboards, claim tags | Missing validators block thesis-ready A12 evidence |
| Run identifier conventions | Yes | Link clean run, stressed run, stress profile, stress schedule, policy, session, and evaluation artifacts | Missing run IDs make results diagnostic-only |
| Config hash conventions | Yes | Hash stress configs, target families, injection rules, reward configs, policy configs, and evaluation configs | Missing hashes block reproducibility claims |
| Seed conventions | Yes | Reproduce stress schedules and stochastic stress variants | Missing seed downgrades stress to diagnostic-only |
| Manifest conventions | Yes | Link stress-run manifest, artifact manifest, claim-evidence manifest/matrix, export manifest, reproducibility manifest | Missing manifests block dashboard/thesis export readiness |
| Repository skeleton expectations | Yes | Store Layer 8 configs, records, reports, metrics, cards/source bundles, and manifests in manifest-mapped locations | Exact path finalization may remain unresolved but must be recorded |
| Metric dictionary placeholders | Yes | Define every stress metric and interpretation direction | Missing entries make metrics non-thesis-ready |
| Claim-evidence placeholders | Yes | Link A12 stress evidence to limitation tags and allowed claim wording | Claim-evidence alias issue persists; must be carried |
| Dashboard/export-readiness placeholders | Yes | Prepare Layer 10-readable stress records, warnings, cards, and export inputs | Phase 14 renders/exports; Phase 9 prepares inputs only |

### 7.2 Phase 0 inheritance result

```text
phase0_inheritance_gap: true
```

The gap is not a failure of the Phase 9 concept, but a carried implementation/registry gap for the exact canonical stressed pointer/view export name, some metric dictionary path/schema details, and claim-evidence manifest/matrix alias governance. This gap does not block a minimum viable StressForge-Lite run if Phase 9 manifest-maps the candidate stressed pointer/view family and labels unresolved outputs correctly. It does weaken or block thesis-ready A12 stress robustness claims for any result missing stress profile, schedule, seed, clean/stressed pairing, metric dictionary, validation, or claim-evidence lineage.

### 7.3 Phase 0 inheritance repair rule

If a required Phase 0 item is missing at Phase 9 execution time, Phase 9 must not invent a local silent replacement. It must either:

1. reuse the Phase 0 placeholder and mark the item `unresolved_requires_confirmation`;
2. create a versioned, manifest-mapped candidate artifact with `inferred_candidate` and `requires_confirmation: true`;
3. downgrade the affected stress result to `diagnostic_only`; or
4. block the affected stress claim until the foundation item is repaired.

| Stress claim-evidence manifest/matrix entry | claim-evidence artifact | Layer 8 exporter / Layer 0 review path | Source records, metric entries, matched reports, negative notes, limitation tags, claim wording status | Layer 0, Layer 10, Phase 15 | Claim-evidence view input | Final claim approval deferred to Layer 0 / Phase 15 |
| `StressCard` / stress-card source bundle | card/source artifact | Layer 8 or later Layer 10 from Layer 8 records | Stress purpose, family, intensity, schedule, injection point, affected modules, expected/observed failure signatures, metrics, sensitivity curves, comparison tables, limitations, reproducibility paths | Layer 10, thesis appendix | Layer 10 may render derived `CardRecord`; Phase 9 may prepare source card bundle | Not primary evidence without record/metric/manifest lineage |
| Stress failure taxonomy update | report/table artifact | Layer 8 stress-card/failure writer | Stress-induced failure categories, affected modules, severity, reason codes, downstream warning status | Layer 10, Layer 0, Phase 15 | Dashboard warning/table input | Failure taxonomy is limitation evidence; not clinical safety validation |

### 10.2 Outputs explicitly not owned by Phase 9

| Not owned by Phase 9 | Owner / phase | Phase 9 handling |

| Clean `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord` | Layer 1 / Phase 1 | Read immutably; preserve lineage |
| Clean `PredictionRecord` / `ModelRegistryRecord` | Layer 2 / Phase 2 | Read or target through stress-derived pointers only |
| Clean `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord` | Layer 3 / Phase 3 | Read or stress-condition through derived views; no retuning |

| `PolicyActionRecord`, `DeferralRecord`, learned policy artifacts | Layer 6 / Phases 6–7/10–11 | Consume for stress evaluation; no policy-learning ownership |
| Core `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord` semantics | Layer 7 / Phase 8 and later runs | Stress-conditioned runs may create new derived simulation records with Layer 7 semantics and Layer 8 stress lineage |
| `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` | Layer 9 / Phases 12–13 | Optional downstream consumption; not produced by Phase 9 |

| Final claim approval | Layer 0 / Phase 15 | Phase 9 prepares claim-evidence entries and limitation tags; final wording remains review-bound |

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

### 12.1 Evidence-level transformation chain

Phase 9 follows the evidence-level chain below:

```text
validated clean source/evidence records
→ declared stress family, intensity, target, injection point, seed, schedule, and guardrail
→ source-preserving stressed pointer/view or stress-conditioned run
→ matched clean/stressed evaluation under fixed split/session/policy/reward/config keys
→ stress metrics, sensitivity curves, failure taxonomy, negative-result notes, and diagnostic-only flags
→ Layer 10-readable source records and warning/export inputs
→ Layer 0 claim-safety and Phase 15 thesis-evidence handoff
```

This chain is intentionally record-first. It does not require the Execution and Evidence Plan to specify exact function implementations, command-line invocations, low-level adapter code, or debugging procedure. Those belong to a future detailed design or implementation build book.

### 12.2 Stress-family evidence logic

Phase 9 may define stress families including:

| Stress family | Evidence role | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Delay | Tests sensitivity to delayed evidence/action/replay timing | Synthetic delay/proxy; not real device latency validation |
| Dropout | Tests behavior under missing channels, windows, evidence requests, or signal availability where declared | Synthetic dropout/proxy; not hardware reliability proof |
| Noisy intent | Tests sensitivity to degraded prediction/evidence quality or noisy input evidence where declared | Proxy/noise stress; not real neural-intent validation |
| Weakness proxy | Tests downstream readiness/command consequences under declared reduced action effectiveness if later used by simulation/embodiment | Proxy only; no physiological weakness diagnosis |
| Drift | Tests temporal distribution or evidence degradation under declared drift schedules | Synthetic drift; not real longitudinal patient adaptation evidence |
| Fatigue-like degradation | Tests robustness under a declared degradation pattern resembling fatigue in computational form | Fatigue-like proxy only; no clinical fatigue claim |
| Curated combined stress | Tests interactions among stressors under predeclared combinations | Combined synthetic stress only; not deployment safety evidence |

If a stress family is not explicitly defined, bounded, seeded, and target-compatible, it may be retained as an exploratory or negative/configuration result but must not support confirmatory stress robustness claims.

### 12.3 Clean/stressed comparison logic

For any stress metric or thesis-facing stress statement, Phase 9 must preserve:

- a clean baseline record or run;
- the stressed counterpart record or run;
- matched dataset, subject, session, split, trial/window/episode, model/policy, reward/cost, config, and seed keys where applicable;
- stress profile and schedule IDs;
- stress intensity and family;
- validation status;
- negative-result and diagnostic-only status;
- metric dictionary ID;
- claim-safety tags.

### 12.4 Frozen versus update-enabled governance

Phase 9 is not a policy-learning phase. Therefore:

- held-out frozen stress evaluation must not mutate policies, calibrators, thresholds, IHARQ rules, RegimeRisk rules, or stress schedules;
- any update-enabled adaptation under stress must be explicitly declared as training/adaptation, must be separated from held-out frozen evaluation, and must include a valid `PolicyUpdateTrace`;
- stress profiles used for final held-out evaluation must not be chosen because they make an adaptive policy look better after inspecting final outcomes;
- stress-conditioned training/adaptation curves must not be merged with stress-conditioned frozen-policy evaluation curves;
- missing update traces or frozen no-mutation failures downgrade affected adaptive stress results to diagnostic-only.

### 12.5 Negative-result logic

Stress failures are expected scientific outputs. A policy, decoder, IHARQ rule, RegimeRisk setting, or simulation branch that degrades under stress is not an implementation failure if it is recorded with valid lineage. It becomes a failure only if the result is hidden, unmatched, unseeded, unvalidated, overwritten, or overclaimed.

---

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Blocking / downgrade condition |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream validity gate | All selected Phase 1–8 source records are schema-valid, split-safe, lineage-complete, and not diagnostic-only for the intended stress use | Missing or invalid upstream source blocks stress claim for affected target |
| Stress config gate | Stress family, intensity, target record/field, injection point, guardrail, seed, and schedule generator are declared before final stress evaluation | Undeclared or post-hoc stress makes result exploratory/diagnostic-only |
| Target compatibility gate | Stress target is legal for the record family and does not inject hidden labels, future outcomes, future rewards, or dashboard-generated metrics into decision-visible state | Leakage or illegal target invalidates affected run |
| Clean-source immutability gate | Stress creates derived records/pointers/runs and never overwrites clean source records | Overwrite invalidates stress result and triggers failure/negative-result note |
| Clean/stressed pairing gate | Every thesis-facing stress comparison has clean and stressed paired keys, including split/session/model/policy/reward/config/seed where applicable | Unmatched comparison is diagnostic-only |
| Schedule reproducibility gate | `StressScheduleRecord` is seed-linked and deterministic/reproducible where required | Missing seed or irreproducible schedule blocks confirmatory evidence |
| Split/leakage gate | Stress does not change split membership, tune on final test outcomes, or expose evaluation-only variables to policy-visible state | Leakage invalidates run |
| Frozen no-mutation gate | Held-out frozen stress evaluation does not mutate policy/model/threshold/calibration/IHARQ/RegimeRisk/stress schedule | Mutation downgrades/invalidates frozen stress claims |
| Update-trace gate | Any declared stress adaptation/update run has valid `PolicyUpdateTrace` and remains separate from held-out frozen evaluation | Missing trace or mixed curves produce diagnostic-only status |
| Metric dictionary gate | Every reported stress metric has a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or equivalent manifest-mapped dictionary entry | Undefined metrics are not thesis-ready |
| Matched report gate | `MatchedComparisonReport` records clean/stressed pair completeness and failures | Missing matched report blocks comparison claim |
| Negative-result gate | Failed, degraded, flat, infeasible, or partial stress results have `NegativeResultNote` entries | Hidden negative results block thesis-ready status |
| Dashboard-source gate | Layer 10-facing inputs include source IDs, config hashes, metric dictionary IDs, limitation tags, warnings, and manifest entries | Dashboard view/export later blocked or downgraded |
| Claim-safety gate | Layer 0 limitation tags and forbidden-claim checks are present | Any clinical/deployment/real-safety claim is rejected |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 9 exits successfully when it produces a minimal but defensible stress suite with documented clean and degraded comparisons, including validated `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifests, stress validity reports, stress-conditioned metrics with metric dictionary references, matched comparison reports, negative-result notes where applicable, diagnostic-only flags where needed, claim-evidence entries, and Layer 10-readable handoff bundles.

### 13.3 Minimum viable exit

A minimum viable Phase 9 may use a small declared stress suite, such as delay, dropout, and noisy-intent/noise, if it satisfies:

- predeclared family/intensity/target/schedule/seed configuration;
- clean/stressed matched comparisons;
- no clean-record mutation;
- split safety;
- metric dictionary references or diagnostic-only labels;
- negative-result preservation;
- limitation tags.

### 13.4 Strong thesis-ready exit

A stronger Phase 9 includes mild/moderate/severe intensity sweeps, curated combined stress, stress-family stratification, stress-conditioned comparisons across multiple available policy and baseline families, reward/action/fallback/deferral/safety-event sensitivity, stress-induced failure taxonomy, multiple seeds where stochasticity exists, stress robustness reports, complete Layer 8 stress evaluation artifacts carrying `A12` context, dashboard-ready source bundles, and Layer 0 claim-evidence entries.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

### 14.1 Required stress-matching keys

Every stress comparison intended for thesis-facing use must preserve the following keys where applicable:

```text

policy_family

reward_config_id
cost_config_id
readiness_context_id
deferral_config_id
regime_state_id
trust_state_id where applicable
closed_loop_session_id

reward_trace_id
policy_rollout_id

matched_comparison_report_id
negative_result_note_id where applicable
claim_evidence_manifest_id or claim_evidence_matrix_id where applicable
```

### 14.2 Matched comparison rules

| Comparison type | Required match rule | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Clean vs stressed decoder evidence | Same dataset/subject/session/split/model/label/preprocessing keys, with stress profile/schedule IDs added | Different clean/stressed source keys, missing source IDs, or overwritten clean record |
| Clean vs stressed calibration/uncertainty evidence | Same model/calibration/threshold fit-scope and split policy; no stress-retuned threshold for final evaluation | Threshold/calibration chosen after final stress outcomes |
| Clean vs stressed IHARQ decisions | Same upstream evidence and IHARQ config, with stress-derived evidence pointers and stress profile/schedule lineage | IHARQ rules altered without new config/version or selected by stress outcome |
| Clean vs stressed RegimeRisk summaries | Same temporal cutoff and past-only visibility rules, with stress state declared | Future stress outcome leaks into temporal state or regime semantics changed |
| Clean vs stressed policy rollouts | Same policy family/version/action space/reward config/session/split/seed, with stress profile/schedule added | Policy mutation during frozen evaluation or unmatched sessions/seeds |
| Stress intensity sweep | Same clean baseline and target keys across mild/moderate/severe/combined intensity variants | Intensity-specific hand-picked runs or missing severity schedule links |
| Stress-conditioned embodiment linkage | Same upstream readiness/action/transition context plus stress profile/schedule and embodiment mode IDs | Missing embodiment manifest/command mapping; Phase 9 alone cannot support A13 |

### 14.3 Missing key handling

If a required matched key is missing, Phase 9 must not infer it silently. It must mark the affected comparison as `diagnostic_only`, attach a `NegativeResultNote` or validation warning where appropriate, and preserve the failure in the stress validity report and downstream handoff.

### 15.1 Ablation identity handling

| A1 — calibrated decoder | Upstream comparison context where calibration is stress-evaluated | A1 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |
| A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Upstream comparison context where registered-threshold behavior is stress-evaluated | A2 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |
| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | Upstream comparison context where uncertainty/selective behavior is stress-evaluated | A3 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Upstream baseline context for stress comparison | A4 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Upstream behavior tested under stress | A5 does not own stress artifacts |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Upstream evidence-quality context tested under stress | A6 does not own stress artifacts |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Upstream regime-aware context tested under stress | A7 does not own stress artifacts |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Upstream deferral context tested under stress | A8 does not own stress artifacts |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Upstream supervised policy context tested under stress | A9 does not own stress artifacts |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Downstream Phase 10 may consume Phase 9 stress profiles; Phase 9 does not produce bandit policy learning evidence | A10 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Downstream Phase 11 may consume Phase 9 stress profiles; Phase 9 does not produce RL evidence | A11 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Primary Phase 9 evaluation-use identity | Layer 8 / Phase 9 produce and validate stress records; A12 is metadata/evaluation context only |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Optional downstream stress-conditioned embodiment context | Layer 9 owns embodiment records; A13 does not own Phase 9 artifacts |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts for Phase 9

| Artifact | Required status | Purpose | Diagnostic-only condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `records/evaluation_outcomes/layer8_stress_evaluation_outcomes.parquet` or manifest-mapped `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` export | Required when A12 is used | Stores Layer 8 stress evaluation outcomes with A12 context | Missing matched keys, metrics, lineage, or limitation tags |
| `reports/matched_comparisons/layer8_matched_stress_comparisons.csv` or manifest-mapped `MatchedComparisonReport` | Required | Confirms clean/stressed pairing and comparison validity | Missing or failed clean/stressed pairings |
| `metrics/metric_dictionary_layer8_stress.yaml` or manifest-mapped stress `MetricDictionaryEntry` entries | Required for thesis metrics | Defines stress metrics, direction, aggregation, interpretation, and limitations | Undefined metric or informal dashboard-only metric |
| `notes/negative_results/layer8_stress_negative_results.md` or equivalent `NegativeResultNote` set | Required where negative, flat, failed, infeasible, partial, or diagnostic-only results occur | Preserves stress failures and robustness limitations | Hidden or omitted negative results |
| `manifests/claim_evidence/layer8_stress_claim_evidence.json` or alias-governed claim-evidence matrix/manifest entry | Required for final claim linkage | Links stress claims to source records, metrics, comparisons, warnings, and limitations | Missing claim-evidence or unresolved unsupported wording |
| Stress validity report | Required | Confirms stress legality, source preservation, and leakage checks | Failed guardrail or missing validation |
| Stress failure taxonomy update | Required where failure categories are analyzed | Preserves failure signatures and stress-induced limitation evidence | Hand-picked or untraceable failure category |
| Stress card/source bundle | Required for dashboard/thesis card readiness where cards are used | Summarizes profiles, schedules, stress metrics, failures, limitations, and lineage | Missing source IDs, metrics, warnings, or limitation tags |

### 15.3 Evaluation conclusion rules

Phase 9 may support statements such as:

- the architecture was evaluated under declared synthetic stress profiles;
- specific modules showed robustness or fragility under those profiles;
- certain stress families caused more fallback, deferral, unsafe/proxy warning, request, or reward degradation;
- stress-conditioned evidence is diagnostic-only where matched comparisons, metric definitions, or lineage are incomplete.

Phase 9 may not support statements that synthetic stress validates real patient fatigue, real hardware safety, clinical BCI-FES robustness, medical-device readiness, real assistive control, or deployment safety.

These are derived reporting artifacts only. They must point back to Phase 9 source records, configs, metric dictionaries, matched reports, negative-result notes, warnings, claim-evidence entries, seeds, and manifests.

### 16.4 Dashboard-export manifest inputs

Phase 9 must prepare export-ready lineage for:

- StressForge card/source bundle;

### 16.5 Not-dashboard inputs

Layer 10 must not:

- create hidden matched groups from dashboard filters;
- remove stress/proxy/simulation limitation tags.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

If Phase 9 validation gates pass, Phase 9 may support bounded claims about:

- stress-conditioned robustness testing under declared synthetic degradation profiles;
- clean versus stressed behavior of decoders, calibration/uncertainty, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, readiness policies, learning-to-defer, and simulated closed-loop outcomes;
- failure signatures and sensitivity curves under delay, dropout, noisy intent, weakness proxy, drift, fatigue-like, or combined stress;
- the value of testing readiness architectures under controlled degradation rather than clean conditions only;
- reproducibility of stress profiles, schedules, run manifests, and stress-conditioned comparisons;
- diagnostic stress fragility where results degrade or fail.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 9 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real deployment readiness;
- real physiological fatigue or weakness diagnosis;
- hardware reliability validation;
- real user adaptation under stress;
- real closed-loop treatment safety.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 9 outputs must inherit or attach limitation tags such as:

```text
public_eeg_only
not_clinical_validation
stress_conditioned
synthetic_stress_only
simulation_only where Layer 7 outcomes are used
proxy_only where weakness/fatigue-like/noisy-intent/embodiment proxies are used
evaluation_only for metrics and matched comparisons
diagnostic_only where lineage/matching/metrics/validation are incomplete
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_patient_safety
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
```

The exact tag vocabulary must remain aligned with the registry and Phase 0 claim-safety schema. If a tag is not finalized, it must be manifest-mapped or marked `requires_confirmation: true` rather than silently replaced.

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Stress claims must be downgraded or blocked when:

- stress profile or schedule is missing;
- stress family or intensity is unsupported;
- stress target is incompatible with the source record;
- stress is selected after seeing final outcomes;
- clean source records are overwritten;
- clean/stressed pairs are unmatched;
- split leakage or decision-time leakage occurs;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- matched comparison reports are missing;
- negative results are hidden;
- update-enabled and frozen curves are merged;
- Layer 10 output lacks source-record/export lineage;
- limitation tags are absent;
- clinical/deployment wording appears.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 must review Phase 9 claim-evidence entries before final thesis integration. The review must verify source-record lineage, matched comparison status, metric dictionary completeness, negative-result visibility, diagnostic-only labels, stress/proxy/simulation limitations, and absence of forbidden clinical/deployment/medical-device claims.

---

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

### 18.1 C0–C4 boundary

C0–C4 are claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels. They are not implementation phases, ablation IDs, artifact owners, dashboard pages, or substitutes for Phase 9.

### 18.2 Phase 9 contribution to capability maturity

| Capability-tier concept | Phase 9 contribution | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Lower-tier clean/offline evidence | Phase 9 does not replace clean decoder, calibration, IHARQ, RegimeRisk, policy, or simulation evidence from earlier phases | If stress fails, lower-tier clean evidence remains valid only within its original clean-condition claim boundary |
| Stress-conditioned robustness maturity | Phase 9 can strengthen stress-conditioned evidence where A12 artifacts are complete | Stress evidence is condition-specific and cannot become deployment safety evidence |
| Optional/stretch branches | Stress-conditioned embodiment or downstream adaptive-policy stress use may support later stretch discussion | Phase 9 alone does not complete A10, A11, A13, dashboard, or final thesis packaging |
| Final thesis claim maturity | Phase 9 prepares evidence that Phase 14/15 can render and integrate | Layer 0 review and Layer 10 export lineage remain required |

### 18.3 Stopping-point governance

If Phase 9 is incomplete, the thesis may still stop at a lower validated capability tier, provided stress-conditioned claims are omitted or labeled future work/diagnostic-only. If Phase 9 is complete but Phase 10–13 are not, Phase 9 may still support A12 stress robustness/fragility evidence for the already-validated policy/simulation contexts, but it must not claim bandit/RL/embodiment robustness.

---

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative results to preserve

Phase 9 must preserve, not hide, the following negative or weak outcomes:

- a stress family cannot be validated or reproduced;
- a stress target is incompatible with a record family;
- stress schedules are too unstable or unseeded;
- stress causes decoder confidence collapse or high-confidence wrong behavior;
- calibration/threshold behavior degrades under stress;
- IHARQ over-accepts, over-waits, over-requests, or falls back too often under stress;
- RegimeRisk does not detect stress-related temporal degradation;
- policy actions become brittle under stress;
- learning-to-defer over-defers or under-defers under stress;
- closed-loop reward/cost worsens under stress;
- safety-event or unsafe/proxy warning rates increase under stress;
- combined stress reveals failure not seen in single-stressor runs;
- stress comparisons are unmatched or only diagnostic;
- stress results are flat or fail to distinguish systems.

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency

A stress result is not sufficient for a thesis-facing comparison unless it compares against appropriate available clean baselines and relevant previous-phase variants. Depending on availability, this may include raw decoder, calibrated decoder, selective/thresholded baseline, ordinary ensemble/longer-window controls, IHARQ-lite, evidence-quality/RegimeRisk variants, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, and Phase 8 simulated policies.

If simpler baselines are missing, Phase 9 must mark the stress comparison as baseline-incomplete or diagnostic-only rather than claiming superiority. Negative or flat comparisons must be included in stress negative-result notes and failure taxonomy entries.

### 19.3 Stress-suite sufficiency

A minimal stress suite may be acceptable if it is honest and reproducible. However, claims must match scope:

- delay/dropout/noise-only suite supports only delay/dropout/noise stress evidence;
- single-intensity stress supports only single-intensity conclusions;
- no combined stress means no combined-stress robustness claim;
- no held-out stress suite means no held-out stress generalization claim;
- no stress-conditioned policy comparison means no policy robustness claim.

---

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure / missingness case | Consequence | Required repair or downgrade |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `StressProfileRecord` | A12 stress condition undefined | Block stress run/claim or create versioned profile before evaluation |
| Missing `StressScheduleRecord` | Stress timing unreproducible | Downgrade run to diagnostic-only or regenerate seeded schedule |
| Missing seed | Stress cannot be reproduced | Diagnostic-only for affected schedule/run |
| Unsupported stress family | Stress definition invalid or exploratory | Preserve as negative/config failure; no confirmatory claim |
| Unsupported target record/field | Injection invalid | Block affected stress profile and record validation failure |
| Source record overwritten | Clean-source immutability violated | Invalidate affected stress evidence; preserve failure note; rebuild from clean source |
| Missing `source_record_ids` | Lineage gap | Diagnostic-only until repaired |
| Missing clean run or stressed run ID | Pairing impossible | No confirmatory clean/stressed comparison |
| Unmatched split/session/policy/reward/config keys | Unfair comparison | Matched report failure and diagnostic-only comparison |
| Stress selected after final outcome inspection | Protocol bias | Exploratory only; cannot support final stress claim |
| Split leakage or future correctness in policy-visible state | Evaluation invalid | Invalidate affected run |
| Threshold/calibration/policy retuned on final stress outcomes | Stress leakage/tuning | Diagnostic-only or invalid unless declared as separate training/adaptation with held-out evaluation |
| Policy mutation during frozen stress replay | Frozen-evaluation violation | Invalidate frozen stress evaluation for that run |
| Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for update-enabled stress adaptation | Update lineage gap | Diagnostic-only adaptive stress result |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Metric not interpretable | Diagnostic-only metric and dashboard warning |
| Missing matched comparison report | Comparison not confirmatory | Diagnostic-only result |
| Missing negative-result note | Evidence-honesty gap | Block thesis-ready export until note is added |
| Missing claim-evidence entry | Claim lineage gap | Claim blocked until Layer 0/Phase 15 review |
| Missing stress limitation tag | Claim-safety gap | Claim blocked; dashboard/card warning required |
| Missing dashboard/export manifest | Dashboard output not thesis-ready | Phase 14 export blocked or downgraded |
| Missing safety-event schema/log where safety burden is reported | Safety summary unsupported | Warning-only or diagnostic-only summary |
| Missing embodiment manifest for stress-conditioned embodiment | A13 stress linkage incomplete | Phase 9 remains valid for A12 only; A13 diagnostic-only |

---

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

### 21.1 Repository principle

Phase 9 may use architecture-supported or registry-recommended Layer 8 locations, but it must not invent unresolved final paths as if they were fully canonical. Every artifact path must be manifest-mapped with run IDs, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, source-record IDs, validation status, and limitation tags.

### 21.2 Expected Phase 9 storage families

| Family | Supported / recommended conceptual location | Path status | Required lineage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stress configs | `configs/stressforge/` including stress registry, delay, dropout, noisy intent, weakness, drift, fatigue-like, combined stress, and matched comparison config files where implemented | architecture-supported / final exact file set may vary | config hash, stress registry version, intensity bounds, target families, guardrails |
| Layer 8 source/module code | `src/stressforge/` | architecture-supported | producer module, version, config hash |
| Stress profile/schedule records | `records/stress_records/stress_profile_records.parquet`, `records/stress_records/stress_schedule.parquet` or manifest-mapped equivalents | explicit/recommended | stress IDs, seed, target family, source IDs, split/session/run IDs |
| Stressed pointer/view records | `records/stress_records/stressed_record_pointers.parquet` or manifest-mapped candidate equivalent | explicit/recommended but canonical name unresolved | `requires_confirmation: true`, source IDs, clean/stressed IDs, profile/schedule IDs |
| Stress-run manifest | `records/stress_records/stress_run_manifest.csv` or manifest-mapped equivalent | architecture-supported | run IDs, profile/schedule IDs, output locations, config hashes, seeds, validation status |
| Stress validity report | `records/stress_records/stress_validity_report.json` or manifest-mapped equivalent | architecture-supported | legality, pairing, leakage, source-preservation, diagnostics |
| Stress metrics | `metrics/stress_metrics.parquet` or equivalent stress metric export | explicit/recommended | metric dictionary IDs, matched comparison IDs, source records |
| Matched-stress reports | `reports/matched_comparisons/layer8_matched_stress_comparisons.csv` or equivalent `MatchedComparisonReport` export | explicit/recommended | matched keys, failure rows, diagnostic labels |
| Layer 8 evaluation outcomes | `records/evaluation_outcomes/layer8_stress_evaluation_outcomes.parquet` or manifest-mapped global `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` context | architecture-supported | A12 context, metric IDs, matched report IDs, negative-result IDs |
| Negative-result notes | `notes/negative_results/layer8_stress_negative_results.md` or equivalent | architecture-supported | affected run/metric/claim, interpretation, limitation tags |
| Stress cards/source bundles | `cards/stress_cards/` or Layer 8 card source bundle consumed by Phase 14 | explicit/recommended | source IDs, metric IDs, limitations, warnings, export readiness |
| Stress sensitivity figures/tables | `figures/stress_sensitivity/` or manifest-mapped source tables | explicit/recommended | source metrics, run IDs, matched keys, export IDs later |
| Claim-evidence manifests | `manifests/claim_evidence/layer8_stress_claim_evidence.json` or alias-governed claim-evidence entry | architecture-supported | claim wording status, source IDs, metrics, matched reports, negative notes, limitations |

### 21.3 Storage anti-patterns

Phase 9 must not store:

- stressed variants by overwriting clean source records;
- unseeded stress schedules as canonical schedules;
- dashboard-only stress edits as source configurations;
- hand-picked stress curves without matched report rows;
- stress metrics without metric dictionary entries;
- stress cards without source-record and limitation links;
- exploratory stress runs in confirmatory output locations without diagnostic-only status.

## 22. Phase Summary and Handoff Record

### 22.1 Narrative summary

Phase 9 implements the StressForge-Lite evidence gate. It consumes validated Phase 1–8 clean records, policy/simulation outputs, and Phase 0 schema/config/validator infrastructure; defines declared stress families, profiles, schedules, injection targets, guardrails, and seeds; produces source-preserving stressed pointers/views and stress-conditioned runs; evaluates clean versus stressed behavior through matched comparisons; and exports stress metrics, stress sensitivity curves, A12 evaluation artifacts, negative-result notes, stress-card/source bundles, failure taxonomy updates, and claim-evidence inputs. It preserves all stress-only, proxy-only, simulation-only, diagnostic-only, and non-clinical limitations.

Official phase name: StressForge-Lite
Produced records/artifacts: StressProfileRecord; StressScheduleRecord; StressedRecordPointer / StressedRecordView candidate or manifest-mapped stressed pointer/view; stress-run manifest; stress validity report; stress-conditioned metrics; stress sensitivity curve source tables; Layer 8 stress EvaluationOutcomeRecord exports carrying A12 context; matched-stress comparison reports; stress MetricDictionaryEntry exports; stress NegativeResultNote entries; DiagnosticOnlyFlag entries where needed; stress claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries; StressCard or stress-card source bundle; stress failure taxonomy updates.

Validated records/artifacts: Stress profiles; stress schedules; stress target/injection compatibility; clean/stressed pairing; split safety; source-record immutability; stress-run manifests; metric dictionary linkage; matched comparison reports; negative-result notes; diagnostic-only flags; claim-safety tags.
Consumed upstream records/artifacts: Phase 0 schemas/configs/validators/manifests/metric and claim placeholders; Phase 1 DatasetRecord, WindowRecord, SplitRecord and protocol lineage; Phase 2 PredictionRecord and ModelRegistryRecord; Phase 3 CalibrationRecord, UncertaintyRecord, ThresholdRegistryRecord, SelectivePredictionRecord and reliability/leakage records; Phase 4 IHARQDecisionRecord, IHARQTraceRecord, reason-code/action-token and fallback/unsafe/request/combine records; Phase 5 RegimeStateRecord and conditional TrustStateRecord; Phase 6 ReadinessContextRecord, EvidenceQualityRecord, PolicyActionRecord, learned policy lineage, cost/reward configs and legality masks; Phase 7 DeferralRecord and fallback/deferral metadata; Phase 8 TransitionRecord, ClosedLoopSessionRecord, RewardTraceRecord, EpisodeSummaryRecord, PolicyRolloutRecord, EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord, and SafetyEventRecord where materialized.

Capability tiers affected: Strengthens stress-conditioned robustness maturity, especially C3-style stress evaluation where complete; lower tiers remain valid only within their original non-stress claim boundaries; C0-C4 remain claim-maturity summaries, not phases or artifact owners.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Handoff to Phase 10 — Contextual bandit

Phase 9 hands Phase 10:

- validated `StressProfileRecord` and `StressScheduleRecord` files;
- stress family/intensity/target definitions;
- stress-run manifests and stress validity reports;
- clean/stressed matched keys;
- stress-conditioned reward/action/failure metrics where Phase 8 simulation outputs are used;
- stress limitation tags;
- no-mutation/frozen-evaluation rules;
- required `PolicyUpdateTrace` rule for any stress-conditioned bandit adaptation.

Phase 10 may use stress profiles for contextual-bandit evaluation, but it must not treat Phase 9 stress outputs as bandit policy-learning artifacts.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy

Phase 9 hands Phase 11:

- stress profiles and schedules for delayed-consequence stress evaluation;
- matched stress-run keys;
- stress-conditioned transition/reward/safety-event lineage where available;
- stress failure taxonomy entries;
- stress metric dictionary entries;
- update/frozen separation rules;
- diagnostic-only triggers for missing stress lineage.

Phase 11 may evaluate RL policies under stress only if update-enabled training and held-out frozen evaluation remain separated and trace-bound.

### 23.3 Handoff to Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo

Phase 9 hands Phase 12:

- stress profile/schedule IDs and stress-family definitions;
- stress-conditioned policy/simulation context where available;
- stressed pointer/view source lineage;
- stress-conditioned safety/fallback/deferral/failure categories;
- limitation tags for synthetic stress and proxy-only weakness/fatigue-like conditions;
- diagnostic-only status for stress runs lacking clean/stressed pairing.

Phase 12 must create and own embodiment state/outcome/demo records if stress-conditioned embodiment is demonstrated. Phase 9 does not produce A13 evidence.

### 23.4 Handoff to Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison

Phase 9 hands Phase 13 stress profiles, schedules, manifests, and stress-conditioned lineage only if optional OpenSim replay uses stress-conditioned inputs. Phase 13 remains optional and must not convert synthetic stress into real biomechanical or clinical validation.

### 23.5 Handoff to Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

Phase 9 hands Phase 14:

- dashboard-readable stress records and artifacts;
- StressForge warning inputs;
- metric dictionary references;
- matched stress reports;
- stress negative-result notes;
- stress diagnostic-only flags;
- stress card/source bundles;
- failure taxonomy updates;
- claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries;
- export manifest inputs;
- reproducibility manifest inputs.

Layer 10 must render StressForge pages and cards from saved Phase 9 records only and must not recompute stress logic, modify stress schedules, hide negative results, or erase diagnostic-only labels.

### 23.6 Handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 9 hands Phase 15:

- stress-conditioned robustness/fragility evidence;
- A12 evaluation artifacts;
- stress metric dictionary entries;
- matched comparison reports;
- negative-result and diagnostic-only records;
- stress failure taxonomy;
- stress cards/source bundles and dashboard export references;
- claim-evidence entries and limitation tags;
- open issues that constrain final wording.

Phase 15 must phrase stress results as controlled synthetic stress evidence under public-data/simulation/proxy boundaries and must preserve all limitations.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 9 is done when all criteria below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Phase 0 schemas, validators, config conventions, run IDs, config hashes, seed conventions, manifests, metric placeholders, claim placeholders, and dashboard/export placeholders are available or gaps are logged.
- Phase 1 clean source records and split/protocol lineage are valid and immutable.
- Phase 2 prediction/model/baseline records are valid for selected stress targets.
- Phase 3 calibration/uncertainty/threshold/selective-prediction records are valid and not retuned on final stress outcomes.
- Phase 4 IHARQ decision/action/reason/fallback/unsafe/request/combine lineage is valid where IHARQ behavior is stress-tested.
- Phase 5 RegimeRisk/trust/stop-loss lineage is valid where regime-aware stress analysis is reported.
- Phase 6 policy/action/readiness/evidence-quality/cost/reward/legality lineage is valid where policy behavior is stress-tested.
- Phase 7 deferral/fallback/cost/proxy-supervisor lineage is valid where deferral behavior is stress-tested.
- Phase 8 transition/session/reward/rollout/episode/diagnostic records are valid where stress-conditioned closed-loop behavior is tested.
- Stress families, intensity levels, target record families, injection points, guardrails, seeds, and schedules are declared before final stress evaluation.
- `StressProfileRecord` exists for every stress condition used in a thesis-facing result.
- `StressScheduleRecord` exists for every scheduled stress run.
- Candidate `StressedRecordPointer` / `StressedRecordView` or equivalent manifest-mapped stressed pointer/view artifacts preserve source IDs and clean/stressed lineage.
- Stress-run manifests exist with run IDs, config hashes, seeds, output paths, validation status, and diagnostic-only flags.
- Stress validity reports confirm legality, source preservation, pairing, leakage status, and guardrail status.
- Clean/stressed matched comparison reports exist for thesis-facing comparisons.
- Stress metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or are marked diagnostic-only.
- Stress sensitivity curves and stress-conditioned tables are linked to source metrics and matched reports.
- Negative-result notes exist for degraded, flat, failed, infeasible, partial, or diagnostic-only stress outcomes.
- Diagnostic-only flags exist for any incomplete, unmatched, unseeded, unresolved, or exploratory result.
- Frozen stress evaluation passes no-mutation checks.
- Any update-enabled stress adaptation has valid `PolicyUpdateTrace` and is separated from held-out frozen evaluation.
- Dashboard-readable source bundles and warning inputs are prepared for Phase 14.
- Stress card/source bundles include source records, metrics, warnings, limitations, and reproducibility paths.
- Claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries are prepared for Layer 0 and Phase 15 review.
- Stress-only, proxy-only, simulation-only, public-data-only, evaluation-only, diagnostic-only, and non-clinical limitation tags are preserved.
- No clinical, medical-device, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation-control, real assistive-control safety, or deployment-readiness claim is supported.
- Phase 9 handoff package is complete for Phases 10, 11, 12, 14, and 15.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 9 outputs must not be used for thesis-facing stress claims if any of the following remain unresolved without diagnostic-only handling:

- missing or invalid upstream Phase 1–8 source records;
- missing Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundation;
- missing stress profile;
- missing stress schedule;
- missing seed;
- unsupported or unbounded stress family;
- illegal or incompatible target record/field;
- missing source IDs;
- clean source record overwrite;
- missing clean/stressed pair;
- unmatched split/session/model/policy/reward/config keys;
- post-hoc stress selection based on final results;
- split leakage or decision-time leakage;
- retuning calibrators, thresholds, IHARQ rules, RegimeRisk rules, policies, reward weights, or stress schedules on final stress outcomes without new separated training/evaluation status;
- mutation during frozen stress evaluation;
- missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for update-enabled stress adaptation;
- missing metric dictionary entries;
- missing matched comparison reports;
- missing negative-result notes;
- missing diagnostic-only labels for incomplete results;
- missing claim-evidence entries or limitation tags;
- dashboard/card/export output without source lineage;
- unsupported clinical, deployment, real safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation, or real control wording.

### 26.3 Minimum viable Phase 9

A minimum viable Phase 9 includes:

- a declared small stress suite, such as delay, dropout, and noise/noisy-intent;
- versioned stress configs, seeds, profiles, and schedules;
- valid clean source records from earlier phases;
- source-preserving stressed pointers/views or stress-conditioned runs;
- clean/stressed matched comparison reports;
- stress validity report;
- stress metrics with metric dictionary references or diagnostic-only status;
- negative-result notes;
- stress limitation tags;
- stress card/source bundle;
- downstream handoff manifest.

### 26.4 Strong / thesis-ready Phase 9

A strong Phase 9 additionally includes:

- multiple stress families including delay, dropout, noisy intent, weakness proxy, drift, fatigue-like degradation, and curated combined stress where justified;
- mild/moderate/severe intensity sweeps;
- multiple seeds for stochastic stress families;
- stress-conditioned evaluation across relevant available baseline and policy families;
- stress-conditioned closed-loop transition/reward/action/fallback/deferral/safety-event analysis;
- stress sensitivity curves and stress-conditioned ablation tables;
- stress failure taxonomy with source-record links;
- complete Layer 8 stress `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` exports carrying `A12` context;
- complete metric dictionary entries;
- complete matched reports;
- complete negative-result and diagnostic-only records;
- complete dashboard warning/export inputs;
- complete claim-evidence entries and limitation tags;
- Layer 0-ready claim wording constraints.

### 26.5 Phase 9 final self-check

Before Phase 9 is considered complete, verify that:

- official Phase 0–15 identities are preserved;
- Phase 9 is not renamed as a wave, tier, scenario, or ablation;
- Layer 8 owns stress records and stress evaluation artifacts;
- A12 is evaluation-use metadata only;
- C0–C4 remain claim-maturity summaries only;
- upstream clean source records remain immutable;
- stress profiles, schedules, seeds, target families, injection points, and guardrails are declared;
- stressed pointers/views preserve source IDs and are marked candidate if canonical naming remains unresolved;
- clean/stressed comparisons are matched or diagnostic-only;
- all stress metrics have dictionary entries or diagnostic-only labels;
- negative results are preserved;
- frozen stress evaluation has no mutation;
- update-enabled adaptation, if any, has `PolicyUpdateTrace` and is separated from frozen evaluation;
- Layer 10 source-vs-derived boundaries are preserved;
- Layer 0 claim-safety boundaries are preserved;
- stress results are not described as clinical, deployment, medical-device, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation, or real control evidence;
- all unresolved issues are listed rather than hidden;
- the downstream handoff enables Phase 10, Phase 11, Phase 12, Phase 14, and Phase 15 without unsupported reinterpretation.

| Supporting layers | Layers 1–5 as immutable upstream source/evidence providers; Layer 8 as optional stress-context provider for stress-conditioned A10; Layer 9 as downstream/optional embodiment compatibility only, not a required Phase 10 input in the official sequence; Layer 10 as later dashboard/card/export/reproducibility reader; Layer 0 as claim-safety and limitation-governance reviewer |
| Primary ablation/evaluation linkage | `A10 — contextual bandit` as evaluation-use metadata only, not an artifact owner |
| Related evaluation contexts | `A8` and `A9` as non-bandit policy baselines; `A12` where Phase 9 stress profiles are used; `A11` as the downstream RL comparison that consumes A10 as a simpler adaptive baseline; `A13` is not produced or required by Phase 10 and may only later reuse Phase 10 policy outputs if Layer 9 records are created in Phase 12/13 |
| Capability-tier relevance | Strengthens simulation-bounded C3-style policy-learning evidence if validation gates pass; does not replace C0–C4 claim-maturity summaries and does not make contextual bandit mandatory for lower-tier thesis validity |
| Phase type | Stretch C simulation-only adaptive-policy evidence phase for immediate-reward adaptation, reward/regret curves, exploration logs, action-probability traces, safety-override logs, controller cards/source bundles, matched comparison reports, and policy-update governance |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Describes evidence-production contracts and validation gates; not a function-level bandit algorithm playbook, command-run guide, or implementation build book |
| Required upstream continuity | Depends on Phase 0 schema/config/validator substrate; validated Phase 1–7 source/policy/simulation records; Phase 8 stable transition/reward/session environment; and Phase 9 stress profiles only for stress-conditioned bandit claims |
| Frozen/update separation | Required. Update-enabled bandit training/adaptation must be separated from held-out frozen-policy evaluation, and every simulation-authorized mutation must have `PolicyUpdateTrace` lineage or a diagnostic-only downgrade |
| Claim boundary | Supports only public-data, proxy-readiness, simulation-only, evaluation-only, and where applicable stress-conditioned evidence about immediate-reward adaptation in a declared simulated environment. It does not support clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, or real deployment readiness. |

Phase 10 tests whether a lightweight contextual bandit can adapt readiness actions, threshold modes, decoder-trust choices, or deferral routes under immediate or near-immediate simulated reward. Its scientific purpose is deliberately narrower than Phase 11 RL: it asks whether online adaptation is useful before introducing high-variance sequential policy learning. A successful Phase 10 produces traceable reward/regret and matched comparison evidence; an unsuccessful Phase 10 is still valid thesis evidence when recorded as a negative result showing that simpler fixed policies, IHARQ-lite, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, or learning-to-defer are sufficient under the declared simulation and reward assumptions.

It treats Layer 6 as policy owner, Layer 7 as simulation/environment record owner, Layer 8 as stress owner, Layer 10 as dashboard/card/export owner, and Layer 0 as claim-safety owner. Where the documents imply a bandit-specific artifact without a confirmed canonical name, this section uses a descriptive non-canonical label such as “bandit policy artifact,” “exploration log,” or “bandit controller card/source bundle” and preserves its status as phase-local, dashboard-derived, or manifest-mapped unless the registry confirms a canonical record name.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 10 is the first update-enabled adaptive-policy phase in the official implementation pipeline. It evaluates whether immediate-reward online adaptation can improve readiness decisions in the declared Layer 7 simulated environment. It is intentionally placed before Phase 11 because contextual bandits provide a lighter test of adaptation than full sequential reinforcement learning.

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 10 controls the following bottleneck:

```text
fixed thresholds / fixed IHARQ-lite / fixed supervised policies
→ may not remain best across subject, session, regime, stress, history, and simulated consequence contexts
→ contextual bandit tests whether limited immediate-reward adaptation helps
→ without introducing full delayed-consequence RL complexity
```

The phase asks whether the best threshold mode, readiness action, decoder-trust choice, or deferral route changes across calibrated uncertainty, evidence quality, IHARQ state, RegimeRisk state, previous action summaries, and stress state where declared. In the official Phase 0–15 sequence, Phase 10 does not require Layer 9 embodiment records; embodiment-proxy context is only a declared optional compatibility path if such records are separately available or if later Phase 12/13 work reuses Phase 10 policy outputs.

### 4.3 Scientific role

Phase 10 supports a bounded thesis claim that lightweight online adaptation can be evaluated under declared simulated consequences. It does not need to prove that bandits always outperform simpler methods. It can produce any of the following valid outcomes:

- contextual bandit improves cumulative reward or regret relative to best fixed policies under held-out frozen evaluation;
- contextual bandit helps only under declared regime shift or stress profiles;
- contextual bandit does not outperform learning-to-defer or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, supporting baseline sufficiency;
- contextual bandit over-explores, overfits reward noise, or becomes reward-sensitive, creating useful limitation evidence;
- contextual bandit results are diagnostic-only because trace, matching, reward, legality, or held-out evaluation requirements are incomplete.

### 4.4 What Phase 10 must not become

Phase 10 must not become:

- a full RL phase;
- a deployment-oriented online controller;
- a claim that simulated reward is clinical utility;
- a proof of real patient-safe adaptation;
- a mechanism that tunes thresholds, reward weights, or policies on final held-out outcomes without new run IDs and separated training/evaluation status;
- a dashboard-generated reinterpretation of policy behavior;
- an A10-owned artifact family.

## 6. Registry Issue Intake and Impact Assessment

| Registry issue or ambiguity | Phase 10 impact | Required handling in this phase | Blocking status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/7 boundary | Bandit context must be policy-visible, decision-time safe, and source-traceable; Layer 7 may consume context for simulation state but must not redefine it | Preserve Layer 6 policy-context ownership; mark any environment-only context extension as simulation/evaluation context with source IDs | Blocks thesis-ready A10 if context includes hidden labels, future rewards, or future outcomes |
| `PolicyActionRecord` action alias governance | Bandit arms may include threshold modes, deferral routes, or policy-only actions not identical to Layer 4 IHARQ tokens | Preserve `source_iharq_action` separately from `action`; require `action_alias_map_id` or equivalent manifest mapping | Blocks comparability if source tokens are overwritten |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` shared/update governance | Every update-enabled bandit mutation must be traceable; frozen evaluation must prove no mutation | Require trace completeness for update mode and disabled-update/no-mutation audit for frozen evaluation | Blocking for A10 adaptive-policy claims; missing trace makes run diagnostic-only |
| `RewardTraceRecord` and reward-config lineage | Reward/regret curves can be misleading if reward formula or cost weights are unversioned | Require reward model/config ID, reward decomposition, sensitivity notes, and metric dictionary linkage | Blocking for thesis-ready reward/regret claims if unresolved |
| `SafetyEventRecord` alias/path conflict | Bandit may trigger unsafe/blocked action or safety override logs; canonical schema/path may be unresolved | Use canonical `SafetyEventRecord` where materialized; otherwise manifest-map safety logs and mark alias uncertainty | Warning/diagnostic-only if safety-event lineage is incomplete |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` schema/path uncertainty | Reward, regret, wrong-accept-over-time, exploration burden, policy stability, and safety metrics need definitions | Require metric dictionary references or mark metric outputs diagnostic-only | Weakens but does not block internal debugging |
| `ClaimEvidenceManifest` / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` alias governance | Phase 10 claim lineage must be exported for Layer 0/Phase 15 | Preserve both terms where needed and map them explicitly; do not silently choose unsupported canonical status | Weakens final thesis integration if unresolved |
| Dashboard-readable versus dashboard-generated separation | Bandit dashboards can be mistaken as primary evidence | Classify source records separately from Layer 10 views/cards/exports | Blocking for dashboard-derived thesis use if lineage absent |
| Repository path finalization | Registry notes unresolved final path status for some outputs | Use manifest-mapped conceptual locations and architecture-supported path only where specified | Non-blocking if manifests are complete; blocking if outputs become untraceable |
| Phase 9 stressed pointer/view naming | Stress-conditioned bandit uses Phase 9 stress lineage but stressed pointer/view canonical name may remain candidate | Consume stress profiles/schedules and manifest-mapped stressed lineage; do not claim final canonical stressed pointer name if unresolved | Diagnostic-only for unmatched stress-conditioned A10 claims |
| `EvidenceQualityRecord` shared-producer nuance | Phase 10 may consume Layer 4 or Layer 6 evidence-quality variants | Preserve producer module and target-construction route; do not merge rule-based and learned variants silently | Blocks evidence-quality-context ablations if producer ambiguity affects matching |
| Controller card/card ownership | Phase 10 may prepare controller-card source bundles; Layer 10 may generate final rendered card | Distinguish `CardRecord` or card source bundle from dashboard-generated card/export | Non-blocking if status is explicit |

No registry issue prevents writing the Phase 10 plan. Several issues can block thesis-ready A10 claims if unresolved during execution.

phase0_inheritance_gap: true

| `DeferralRecord` | Layer 6 / Phase 7 | Deferral routes, fallback availability, deferral costs, direct-versus-defer references | Required only if deferral route is a bandit arm or baseline |
| `TransitionRecord` | Layer 7 / Phase 8 | State-action-next-state-reward lineage, source policy action, simulator ID, session/episode/window IDs, reward/cost linkage, update/frozen status where applicable | Mandatory for immediate reward adaptation and held-out evaluation |
| `RewardTraceRecord` | Layer 7 / Phase 8 onward | Reward version, reward terms, cost components, source transition IDs, regret fields where available, seed, config hash, simulation warning | Mandatory where reward/regret curves are claimed |
| `ClosedLoopSessionRecord` | Layer 7 / Phase 8 | Dataset/subject/session IDs, replay mode, reward/action/evidence hashes, update/frozen mode, claim boundary | Required for held-out simulated session separation |
| `PolicyRolloutRecord` / `EpisodeSummaryRecord` | Layer 7 / Phase 8 onward | Policy identity, frozen/update mode, action sequences, reward summaries, matched keys, metric dictionary IDs, diagnostic flags | Required for policy-family comparison and dashboard handoff |
| `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` | Layer 7 / Phase 8 onward | Reward/action/transition validation warnings, illegal actions, no-mutation status, missing records, unmatched comparisons | Must be checked before using results as evidence |
| Action legality masks | Layer 6 / Layer 7 validators | Legal actions per decision point, unsafe override, stop-loss state, fallback availability, request budget, stress/embodiment constraints, simulation-only restrictions | Mandatory; illegal selected actions block thesis-ready results |
| Reward definitions / reward config | Layer 6 cost/reward manager and Layer 7 RewardEngine | Reward formula, cost weights, penalty hierarchy, stress multipliers, optional embodiment terms, config hash, sensitivity grid | Mandatory; reward changes require new config hash and separated evidence status |
| Bandit policy configs | Layer 6 | Policy family, exploration schedule, algorithm family, action space, seeds, update mode, frozen-evaluation plan, reward model ID | Mandatory for reproducibility |
| Held-out subject/session definitions | Layer 1 / Phase 8 evaluation protocol | Subject/session/split partitions for adaptation/training versus frozen evaluation | Mandatory for generalization claims |
| Baseline policy outputs | Phases 2–7 / Layer 6 | Accept-all, static thresholds, IHARQ-lite, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, and any best-fixed policy references available | Required for fair comparison; missing baseline narrows claims |

### 9.2 Conditional inputs

| Conditional input | Required when | Producer / owner | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `StressProfileRecord` and `StressScheduleRecord` | Bandit claims mention stress, robustness, drift, dropout, delay, noisy intent, weakness proxy, fatigue-like degradation, or combined stress | Layer 8 / Phase 9 | Consume as stress context/evaluation condition; preserve stress-only/proxy-only tags |
| Candidate `StressedRecordPointer` / `StressedRecordView` or manifest-mapped stressed lineage | Stress-conditioned bandit uses stressed source records or stress-conditioned runs | Layer 8 / Phase 9 | Preserve candidate status if canonical naming unresolved |
| `SafetyEventRecord` or safety-event logs | Unsafe, blocked, wrong-accept, stop-loss, or unsupported-command events are materialized during Phase 10 simulation; over-assist or embodiment-specific events only apply in later optional Layer 9 use | Layer 7 for Phase 10 simulation events; Layer 9 only for later embodiment branches | Preserve alias/path uncertainty; dashboard-warning input |
| Embodiment pre-action state or outcome-derived reward term | Not required for ordinary Phase 10; only applicable if separately available from a declared optional branch or if later Phase 12/13 reuses Phase 10 outputs for embodiment-aware replay | Layer 9 / Phase 12+ if available | `not_applicable_with_reason` for core Phase 10; Phase 10 alone must not claim A13; optional terms remain simulation/proxy-only |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` schema/path | Any update-enabled bandit run mutates policy parameters or action-selection parameters | Layer 6/7 update-governance path | Mandatory trace per update; missing trace blocks A10 adaptive claims |
| Disabled-update audit entries | A bandit policy artifact is evaluated without mutation | Layer 7 environment / update-governance path | Mandatory for frozen evaluation evidence |

### 9.3 Forbidden inputs

Phase 10 policies must not use the following as decision-time inputs:

- true labels;
- decoder correctness;
- future reward;
- next state before action;
- endpoint error after the action;
- future-window evidence unless revealed through a declared replay transition;
- oracle best action as a production action;
- dashboard filters or manual inspection notes that alter completed outputs;
- stress or reward settings selected post-hoc from final held-out results.

### 10.2 Outputs not produced by Phase 10

Phase 10 must not produce or claim ownership of:

- `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PredictionRecord`, `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord`, or `StressProfileRecord` semantics;
- Phase 11 RL policy artifacts or A11 results;
- Phase 12 MyoSuite embodiment records or A13 results;
- Phase 13 OpenSim replay records;
- Phase 14 dashboard-generated final views, cards, export manifests, or reproducibility packages;
- Phase 15 final thesis claim approvals.

Layer 7 may emit new `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, or `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` during Phase 10 evaluation runs, but their semantic owner remains Layer 7. Phase 10 consumes and links them as contextual-bandit evaluation evidence.
