## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

### 12.1 Evidence chain

Phase 10 evidence production follows this chain:

```text
validated upstream source records
→ split-safe ReadinessContextRecord and baseline policy outputs
→ declared action space, legality mask, reward config, exploration schedule, and held-out session plan
→ update-enabled contextual-bandit training/adaptation runs with PolicyUpdateTrace per mutation
→ frozen bandit artifact or fixed update schedule for held-out evaluation
→ Layer 7 transition/reward/session/rollout logging
→ reward/regret, wrong-accept, exploration, action-distribution, and safety analyses
→ matched comparison against non-bandit policies
→ negative-result and diagnostic-only records where applicable
→ dashboard-readable source bundle and Layer 0 claim-safety handoff
```

### 12.2 Context-action-reward definition

The Phase 10 context-action-reward tuple must be declared before evaluation:

| Tuple element | Allowed content | Forbidden content |
|---|---|---|
| Context | Calibrated uncertainty, evidence quality, IHARQ state, RegimeRisk state, previous action summary, and stress state where declared; no Layer 9 context is required in the official Phase 10 path | True label, future reward, future next state, future endpoint outcome, hidden correctness target, post-hoc dashboard note, or later embodiment outcome leaked into policy-visible context |
| Action | Readiness action, threshold mode, decoder-trust action, deferral route, conservative/balanced/aggressive threshold selection, no-action/fallback route where declared | Undefined action, illegal action, unsupported simulator command, or oracle action as production output |
| Reward | Correct-action reward minus wrong-accept, delay, request, fallback, unsafe, and optional embodiment proxy penalties under a versioned reward model | Clinical utility, real patient safety utility, unversioned post-hoc reward, or hidden outcome-selected reward |

### 12.3 Training/adaptation versus frozen evaluation

Phase 10 must maintain two separate evidence families:

1. `update_enabled_training_or_adaptation`: bandit action-selection parameters may update after actions using immediate reward in declared simulation mode. Every update requires `PolicyUpdateTrace` and cannot be merged with held-out evaluation curves.
2. `held_out_frozen_evaluation`: a frozen bandit policy/artifact is evaluated without mutation on held-out simulated sessions, subjects, seeds, and stress profiles where available. This requires disabled-update audit or no-mutation proof.

A result that improves only during ongoing adaptation may support a narrow claim about online-adaptation behavior under simulation, but it must not be described as frozen-policy superiority.

### 12.4 Baseline comparison logic

Phase 10 must compare bandit behavior against the strongest available non-bandit baselines from earlier phases:

- accept-all decoder / raw decoder baseline;
- calibrated decoder baseline;
- registered confidence-threshold / simple threshold baseline;
- uncertainty and selective prediction;
- IHARQ-lite;
- IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator where available;
- IHARQ + RegimeRisk where available;
- learning-to-defer;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- best fixed threshold/action/deferral policy under the same reward definition.

If one or more baselines are unavailable, the comparison must state the missing baseline and narrow the claim accordingly.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Pass condition | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schema and lineage gate | All Phase 10 records and consumed source records validate against schemas and preserve source IDs | No critical schema/source-lineage failure | Block or diagnostic-only |
| Phase 0 inheritance gate | Required configs, validators, run/hash/seed/manifest conventions, metric and claim placeholders exist | No blocking Phase 0 foundation gap | Log limited gaps; thesis claims blocked if metric/claim/export lineage missing |
| Context leakage gate | `ReadinessContextRecord` contains only decision-time-visible fields | No labels, correctness, future rewards, future outcomes, or oracle costs in policy-visible context | Block A10 claim; rerun or diagnostic-only |
| Action legality gate | Selected actions obey legality mask, unsafe overrides, stop-loss, fallback availability, request budgets, stress/embodiment constraints | No illegal selected action in thesis-facing evaluation | Block or safety diagnostic-only |
| Reward config gate | Reward formula, weights, penalty hierarchy, optional stress/embodiment terms, and config hash are declared before evaluation | Reward is versioned and sensitivity-ready | Diagnostic-only for unversioned/post-hoc reward |
| Update trace gate | Every update-enabled mutation has `PolicyUpdateTrace` | Complete trace coverage | Update-enabled claim blocked if missing |
| Frozen evaluation gate | Held-out frozen evaluation has disabled-update/no-mutation proof | No mutation during held-out frozen evaluation | Mark as adaptation-only or diagnostic-only |
| Held-out session gate | Training/adaptation and held-out evaluation subjects/sessions/seeds/stress profiles are separated where claims require generalization | Held-out plan and split lineage valid | Downgrade to in-sample adaptation diagnostic |
| Baseline sufficiency gate | Fair non-bandit baselines are present and matched | Required baselines validated or missingness disclosed | Narrow or diagnostic-only claim |
| Matched comparison gate | Required matched keys are complete | `MatchedComparisonReport` passes validation | Diagnostic-only for unmatched comparisons |
| Stress gate | Stress profiles/schedules are validated if stress-conditioned A10 is claimed | Clean/stressed matched lineage valid | No stress-conditioned claim |
| Metric dictionary gate | Metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | All thesis-facing metrics defined | Diagnostic-only metric output |
| Negative-result gate | Failed, flat, unsafe, overfit, or reward-sensitive results have notes | `NegativeResultNote` linked to run/matched key | Incomplete evidence package |
| Dashboard/export gate | Layer 10 source inputs have lineage, warning, limitation, metric, and manifest references | Dashboard/export input package complete | Dashboard views not thesis-ready |
| Claim-safety gate | Layer 0 limitation tags and forbidden-claim checks pass | No unsupported clinical/deployment/safety wording | Claim blocked/downgraded |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 10 exits successfully when the project has a traceable contextual-bandit evaluation result that either improves or fails transparently relative to simpler policies under declared reward, legal actions, held-out evaluation, matched comparisons, and limitation tags. The exit condition is not “bandit wins.” The exit condition is that A10 evidence is complete, interpretable, reproducible, and claim-safe.

### 13.3 Minimum exit package

A minimum valid Phase 10 includes:

- declared small action space, such as threshold-mode or deferral-route selection;
- versioned reward config;
- validated action legality masks;
- update-enabled training/adaptation logs with complete `PolicyUpdateTrace`, or frozen-only evaluation with disabled-update proof;
- held-out frozen evaluation on validated simulated sessions;
- comparison against at least accept-all, static threshold/selective, IHARQ-lite, and one stronger available policy baseline;
- reward/regret curves with metric dictionary references;
- matched comparison report;
- negative-result notes where applicable;
- controller card/source bundle;
- simulation-only and non-clinical limitation tags.

### 13.4 Fallback exit condition

If a full contextual bandit is unstable or unsupported, Phase 10 may fall back to bandit-based threshold-mode selection only. This fallback remains valid if it preserves reward/config/trace/matching/frozen-evaluation controls. If even threshold-mode bandit evidence is incomplete, Phase 10 can be closed as diagnostic-only or future work without blocking lower-tier thesis validity.

### 14.2 Matching dimensions

### 14.3 Diagnostic-only rule

Any Phase 10 result that lacks required matched keys must be marked diagnostic-only. Missing keys must not be repaired silently by dashboard filtering or post-hoc grouping. The `MatchedComparisonReport` must explicitly list excluded records, missing keys, unmatched baselines, and the claim consequence.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 A0–A13 linkage

| Evaluation ID | Phase 10 relationship | Ownership rule |
|---|---|---|
| `A0 — raw decoder` | Baseline reference for accept-all/no-policy behavior | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A1 — calibrated decoder` | Upstream calibrated reference where used | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline` | Required non-bandit registered-threshold baseline | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction` | Optional uncertainty/selective-prediction baseline where previous Phase 3 outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls` | Optional ordinary aggregation control where previous outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A5 — IHARQ-lite` | Required interpretable non-bandit baseline where Phase 4 outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator` | Context/baseline relation where Phase 6 evidence-quality outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk` | Regime-aware baseline/context relation where Phase 5/6 outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A8 — learning-to-defer` | Required strong non-bandit comparison where Phase 7 outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ` | Strong supervised policy comparison where Phase 6 outputs exist | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A10 — contextual bandit` | Primary Phase 10 evaluation context | Evaluation metadata only; Phase 10/Layer 6 produces records used for A10 |
| `A11 — reinforcement-learning policy` | Downstream Phase 11 comparison; Phase 10 becomes simpler adaptive baseline | Evaluation metadata only |
| `A12 — StressForge stress tests` | Conditional stress-conditioned A10 evaluation if Phase 9 stress profiles are used | Evaluation metadata only; Layer 8 owns stress artifacts |
| `A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo` | Not produced by Phase 10; optional future embodiment-aware reward/context relation only after Layer 9 records exist | Evaluation metadata only |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts

Phase 10 must produce or prepare the following evaluation artifacts:

| Evaluation artifact | Required status | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| A10 policy comparison table | `created/validated` | Compares contextual bandit against non-bandit baselines |
| Reward/regret metric definitions | `created_or_referenced` | Defines cumulative reward, regret, reward decomposition, exploration burden, wrong-accept-over-time, and policy stability metrics |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | `created/validated` | Proves comparisons are matched or diagnostic-only |
| Reward sensitivity note/table | `created_where_applicable` | Shows whether policy ranking depends on reward weights |
| Seed sensitivity note/table | `created_where_applicable` | Shows policy stability across exploration seeds |
| Safety override / illegal-action summary | `created/validated` | Documents unsafe/blocked action handling |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` completeness report | `created_for_update_enabled_runs` | Proves update lineage completeness |
| Disabled-update/no-mutation report | `created_for_frozen_evaluation` | Proves frozen evaluation separation |
| Negative-result note index | `created_where_applicable` | Preserves failed/flat/unsafe/reward-sensitive results |
| Diagnostic-only flag table | `created_where_applicable` | Prevents unsupported claims from incomplete runs |
| Controller card/source bundle | `prepared` | Supports Phase 14 cards and Phase 15 appendix |
| Claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries | `prepared` | Supports Layer 0 and Phase 15 review |

### 15.3 Evaluation questions answered

Phase 10 answers:

1. Does immediate-reward adaptation improve simulated readiness-policy outcomes beyond the best fixed policy?
2. Is the improvement stable under held-out simulated sessions rather than only during adaptation?
3. Does contextual bandit reduce wrong accepts without excessive delay, request, fallback, or exploration burden?
4. Does contextual bandit remain legal and safe under action masks and unsafe overrides?
5. Does stress context change the value of adaptation when Phase 9 stress profiles are available?
6. Are conclusions robust to reward-weight and seed sensitivity?
7. Is Phase 11 RL justified, or are simpler policies sufficient?

### 16.2 Dashboard-warning inputs

Layer 10 warning views must surface:

These are Layer 10-derived outputs, not hidden primary evidence. They must link back to source records, config hashes, seeds, metric dictionaries, matched comparison reports, claim-evidence entries, and limitation tags.

- context IDs and source-record IDs;
- transition/reward/session/rollout IDs;
- update/frozen mode and trace/no-mutation status;
- metric dictionary IDs;
- matched comparison IDs;
- negative-result and diagnostic-only IDs;
- claim-safety tags;
- stress and embodiment IDs where applicable;
- repository/manifest-mapped output locations.

### 16.5 Not-dashboard inputs

The following remain outside Layer 10 authority:

- bandit policy training/adaptation logic;
- exploration strategy selection;
- reward function tuning;
- action legality decisions;
- threshold retuning;
- simulator transition generation;
- stress profile generation;
- claim approval.

Layer 10 may expose and validate saved records but must not recompute or repair them silently.

---

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

If validation gates pass, Phase 10 may support bounded claims about:

- simulation-only contextual-bandit readiness-policy evaluation;
- immediate-reward adaptation under declared Layer 7 simulated consequences;
- reward/regret behavior relative to matched non-bandit baselines;
- exploration burden and action-distribution behavior;
- wrong-accept, delay, fallback, request, and unsafe-event proxy trade-offs;
- stress-conditioned contextual-bandit behavior where Phase 9 lineage is valid;
- reward/seed sensitivity as limitation evidence;
- dashboard/reproducibility traceability of adaptive-policy evidence.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 10 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real deployment readiness;
- real online patient adaptation;
- clinical utility of the reward function;
- validated physiological fatigue/weakness state;
- validated real embodiment or biomechanical safety.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 10 outputs must carry the strictest applicable combination of:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based
evaluation_only
simulation_only
stress_conditioned
embodiment_proxy_only where optional embodiment terms are active
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
diagnostic_only where applicable
future_work_only where applicable
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Phase 10 claims must be downgraded when:

- update traces are missing;
- frozen evaluation mutated policy state;
- reward weights are unversioned or post-hoc selected;
- policy ranking changes materially under reasonable reward sensitivity;
- baselines are incomplete or weak;
- comparisons are unmatched;
- stress lineage is missing for stress-conditioned claims;
- safety overrides or illegal actions are unresolved;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- dashboard lineage is incomplete;
- negative-result or diagnostic-only labels are absent.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Layer 0 must review Phase 10 outputs before thesis-facing use for:

- simulation-only and proxy-readiness wording;
- non-clinical/non-deployment warnings;
- adaptive-policy and online-adaptation overclaim risk;
- reward-sensitivity limitations;
- update/frozen separation;
- negative-result visibility;
- diagnostic-only flags;
- controller-card limitation completeness;
- final claim-evidence manifest/matrix linkage.

---

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

| Capability tier | Phase 10 relationship | Governance rule |
|---|---|---|
| `C0` | Not required | Core public EEG reliability evidence can remain valid without Phase 10 |
| `C1` | Not required | Calibration/uncertainty/IHARQ evidence can remain valid without bandit adaptation |
| `C2` | Not required | RegimeRisk/adaptive supervised policy/learning-to-defer/simulation readiness can remain valid without A10 if claims are narrowed |
| `C3` | Strengthened by Phase 10 | Phase 10 contributes simulation-bounded policy-learning evidence where A10 validation passes; C3 remains a claim-maturity summary, not an implementation phase |
| `C4` | Not established by Phase 10 alone | Embodiment/demo/final integration claims require later phases and remain simulation/proxy-only |

Phase 10 is a stretch evidence phase. If it fails or remains diagnostic-only, the thesis may still stop at a lower validated capability tier with explicit limitation language. If Phase 10 succeeds but Phase 11 fails, contextual-bandit results may still serve as the strongest online-adaptation evidence, provided the claim remains simulation-only and immediate-reward bounded.

---

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Valid negative outcomes

The following are valid Phase 10 outcomes, not automatic failures:

- contextual bandit does not outperform the best fixed threshold/action policy;
- contextual bandit matches but does not exceed learning-to-defer or supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- contextual bandit improves reward but increases wrong-accept or unsafe-proxy events;
- contextual bandit helps only under stress or regime-shift conditions;
- contextual bandit is highly reward-sensitive;
- contextual bandit is unstable across seeds;
- contextual bandit over-explores or collapses to fallback/no-action;
- contextual bandit improves during adaptation but not under held-out frozen evaluation;
- contextual bandit results are diagnostic-only because trace/matching/metric requirements are incomplete.

### 19.2 Required negative-result handling

Each negative or mixed result must produce a `NegativeResultNote` or equivalent registered note that includes:

- run ID;
- policy ID;
- A10 linkage;
- matched comparison key;
- reward config ID;
- relevant seed(s);
- stress profile ID where applicable;
- affected metric dictionary IDs;
- baseline comparison result;
- diagnostic-only status if applicable;
- claim consequence;
- dashboard warning linkage.

### 19.3 Baseline sufficiency rule

If simpler policies perform as well as or better than the contextual bandit under matched conditions, Phase 10 must say so. Such a result strengthens the thesis by showing that the system evaluated adaptation honestly rather than assuming adaptation is necessary. Baseline sufficiency can support a claim that fixed IHARQ-lite, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, or learning-to-defer may be preferable under the declared reward and simulation assumptions.

---

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure or missingness case | Risk | Required handling | Diagnostic-only consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Missing `ReadinessContextRecord` lineage | Policy context cannot be audited | Block or rerun context assembly | Diagnostic-only if used |
| Hidden label/future reward in context | Leakage and invalid adaptation evidence | Block A10 claim | Required diagnostic/failure flag |
| Missing action legality mask | Unsafe or undefined actions may be selected | Block bandit run or restrict to safe fallback action space | Diagnostic-only |
| Illegal action selected | Policy violates legality constraints | Block thesis-facing result; log safety/illegal-action event | Diagnostic-only or failed run |
| Missing reward config hash | Reward/regret cannot be interpreted | Block reward/regret claims | Diagnostic-only metrics |
| Post-hoc reward tuning on held-out outcomes | Overfitting/claim inflation | Create new run/config and mark old result diagnostic | Diagnostic-only |
| Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for mutation | Update evidence untraceable | Block update-enabled claim | Diagnostic-only adaptation curve |
| Mutation during frozen evaluation | Frozen-policy superiority invalid | Reclassify as online-adaptation behavior or rerun frozen | Diagnostic-only for frozen claim |
| Mixed training/adaptation and evaluation curves | Inflated evidence | Separate curves or downgrade | Diagnostic-only comparison |
| Missing held-out sessions | No generalization evidence | Limit to in-sample adaptation | Diagnostic-only for generalization |
| Missing strong baselines | Weak comparison | Narrow claim and create missing-baseline note | Diagnostic-only for superiority claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Metric ambiguity | Add dictionary entry or downgrade | Diagnostic-only metric |
| Missing matched comparison report | Unfair comparison risk | Create report or downgrade | Diagnostic-only comparison |
| Stress profile missing for stress claim | Unsupported stress conclusion | Remove stress claim | Diagnostic-only stress result |
| Safety-event alias unresolved | Warning not comparable | Manifest-map event/log and preserve open issue | Warning-only / diagnostic-only if material |
| Reward-sensitive ranking | Claim instability | Add reward sensitivity note and downgrade | Reward-sensitive limitation |
| Seed-sensitive ranking | Policy instability | Add seed sensitivity note and downgrade | Diagnostic or limitation claim |
| Dashboard lineage missing | Export cannot support thesis | Block dashboard-derived thesis use | Dashboard-only diagnostic |

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

### 21.1 Storage principles

Phase 10 storage must follow the repository and manifest conventions inherited from Phase 0 and prior phases. Because the registry preserves unresolved path-status issues, this section does not invent final paths. Outputs must be manifest-mapped with run IDs, config hashes, seeds, schema versions, source-record IDs, phase IDs, A10 linkage, claim tags, and validation status.

### 21.2 Architecture-supported locations and conceptual homes

| Output family | Storage expectation | Path-status note |
|---|---|---|
| Bandit policy config and action-space/reward configs | Store under the existing policy/config family and manifest-map each file | `configs/policies/` is architecture-supported; exact subpath naming should follow repository manifest |
| Bandit `PolicyActionRecord` rows | Store with Layer 6 policy-action outputs and/or run-local policy results | Use canonical record name; final path must be manifest-mapped |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` files | Store under the architecture-specified update-trace area when update mode is enabled | Architecture explicitly names `runs/<run_id>/results/layer7_closed_loop/policy_updates/`; use manifest mapping for exact files |
| Disabled-update/no-mutation audit entries | Store with Layer 7 closed-loop diagnostics or update-governance audit outputs | Exact path may remain manifest-mapped; must be discoverable by Phase 14 |
| Layer 7 transition/reward/session/rollout records emitted during Phase 10 evaluation | Store with Layer 7 closed-loop result families | Preserve Layer 7 semantic ownership and run-local lineage |
| Reward/regret curves and evaluation tables | Store as evaluation artifacts with metric dictionary and matched-report references | Do not treat rendered plots as primary evidence |
| Exploration logs/action-probability traces | Store as policy logs/source tables linked to policy IDs and contexts | Must include seed/config/action legality lineage |
| Safety override/illegal-action logs | Store with environment diagnostics or safety-event records/logs | Preserve `SafetyEventRecord` alias uncertainty if unresolved |
| Stress-conditioned A10 outputs | Link to Layer 8 stress profiles/schedules and clean/stressed matched keys | Do not overwrite stress or clean records |
| Controller card source bundle | Store as card source data or `CardRecord` where supported; rendered card generated later by Layer 10 | Distinguish source bundle from dashboard-generated card |
| Claim-evidence entries | Store in claim-evidence manifest/matrix family with alias mapping preserved | Exact `ClaimEvidenceManifest`/`ClaimEvidenceMatrix` resolution deferred |
| Reproducibility manifest inputs | Store run/config/seed/source-output references for Phase 14/15 | Layer 10 final package generated later |

### 21.3 Required validation/test families

Phase 10 must be covered by validators for:

- schema validity;
- policy-context leakage;
- action legality;
- reward config and reward decomposition;
- update trace completeness;
- disabled-update/no-mutation;
- held-out partition separation;
- matched comparison completeness;
- metric dictionary completeness;
- stress lineage where stress is active;
- dashboard read/export input lineage;
- limitation and claim-safety tags.

## 22. Phase Summary and Handoff Record

### 22.1 Narrative summary

Phase 10 adds a lightweight online-adaptation simulation test to the Stretch C evidence stack. It consumes validated readiness context, policy baselines, transition/reward environment records, action legality masks, reward configs, and optional stress profiles. It produces contextual-bandit policy actions, update traces when mutation is enabled, frozen-evaluation no-mutation evidence, reward/regret and exploration analyses, matched comparison reports, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and controller-card source bundles. Its output is simulation-only adaptive-policy evidence, not deployment or clinical control evidence.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Handoff to Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy

Phase 10 hands Phase 11:

- validated contextual-bandit policy artifacts;
- A10 reward/regret and comparison evidence;
- action-space and legality-mask versions;
- reward/cost config versions and sensitivity notes;
- exploration logs/action-probability traces;
- `PolicyUpdateTrace` completeness evidence for update-enabled runs;
- disabled-update/no-mutation evidence for frozen evaluation;
- held-out session plan and evaluation partitions;
- matched comparison reports;
- negative-result and diagnostic-only records;
- limitations on immediate-reward versus delayed-consequence evidence.

Phase 11 may use Phase 10 as the simpler adaptive-policy baseline. Phase 11 must not reinterpret Phase 10 immediate-reward bandit success as evidence of sequential delayed-consequence learning.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo

Phase 10 hands Phase 12 only the validated policy actions, action legality status, reward/config lineage, and limitation tags that may be used for readiness-gated embodiment demonstration. Phase 10 does not produce `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, `Layer9RewardTrace`, or `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`. Phase 12 must create and own embodiment records if embodiment is implemented.

### 23.3 Handoff to Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison

Phase 10 hands Phase 13 policy-action and evaluation context only if optional OpenSim replay uses contextual-bandit outputs. Phase 13 remains optional and must preserve simulation/proxy-only limitations. Phase 10 does not make OpenSim comparison claims.

### 23.4 Handoff to Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

Phase 10 hands Phase 14:

- dashboard-readable bandit `PolicyActionRecord` rows;
- policy artifacts and config manifests;
- exploration logs/action-probability traces;
- reward/regret source tables;
- wrong-accept and action-distribution source tables;
- `PolicyUpdateTrace` and update-trace completeness reports;
- disabled-update/no-mutation audit entries;
- `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, and `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` links;
- safety override and illegal-action logs;
- stress profile/schedule links where stress-conditioned A10 is active;
- metric dictionary references;
- matched comparison reports;
- negative-result notes;
- diagnostic-only flags;
- controller card/source bundles;
- claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries;
- limitation tags and warning requirements.

Layer 10 must render these from saved records only and must not rerun bandit updates, retune rewards, hide negative results, erase diagnostic-only labels, or treat dashboard plots as primary evidence.

### 23.5 Handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 10 hands Phase 15:

- A10 simulation-only contextual-bandit evidence;
- reward/regret and comparison artifacts;
- baseline sufficiency or negative-result notes;
- matched comparison reports;
- reward/seed sensitivity limitations;
- update/frozen separation evidence;
- metric dictionary references;
- controller card/export references;
- claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries;
- open issues that constrain final claim wording.

Phase 15 must phrase Phase 10 results as simulation-only immediate-reward adaptation evidence under public-data/proxy constraints. It must not convert Phase 10 into clinical, real safety, medical-device, rehabilitation, real stimulation, or deployment evidence.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 10 is done when all criteria below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundations are available or gaps are logged.
- Phase 1–7 upstream records used for context and baselines are valid, immutable, and source-traceable.
- Phase 8 closed-loop environment, transition, reward, session, rollout, and diagnostic records are valid for the selected evaluation scope.
- Phase 9 stress profiles/schedules are valid if and only if stress-conditioned A10 claims are made.
- `ReadinessContextRecord` inputs pass decision-time leakage validation.
- Bandit action space is declared and small enough for the evidence scope.
- Action legality masks are validated for every decision point.
- Reward formula, cost weights, penalty hierarchy, optional stress/embodiment terms, and reward config hashes are declared before evaluation.
- Bandit policy configuration, algorithm family, exploration schedule, seeds, and update/frozen mode are versioned.
- Update-enabled training/adaptation runs produce complete `PolicyUpdateTrace` coverage.
- Held-out frozen evaluation has disabled-update/no-mutation evidence.
- Adaptation curves and held-out frozen-evaluation curves are exported separately.
- Held-out subject/session/seed/stress partitions are defined where generalization or stress claims are made.
- `TransitionRecord` and `RewardTraceRecord` lineage is complete for reward/regret evidence.
- Baseline comparisons include the strongest validated non-bandit policies available and disclose missing baselines.
- Matched comparison reports exist for thesis-facing comparisons.
- Reward/regret, wrong-accept, exploration, action-distribution, policy-stability, safety-override, and reward-sensitivity metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or diagnostic-only labels.
- Negative-result notes exist for failed, flat, unsafe, overfit, reward-sensitive, seed-sensitive, or diagnostic-only outcomes.
- Diagnostic-only flags exist for incomplete, unmatched, untraced, unversioned, or leakage-risk outputs.
- Controller card/source bundle includes policy identity, inputs, action space, reward design, update/frozen status, metrics, failures, limitations, and source links.
- Layer 10 dashboard/card/export source inputs are complete and read-only.
- Layer 0 claim-safety tags and limitation language are attached.
- No clinical, medical-device, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation-control, real assistive-control safety, or deployment-readiness claim is supported.
- Phase 10 handoff package is complete for Phase 11, Phase 14, Phase 15, and optional Phase 12/13 use.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 10 outputs must not be used for thesis-facing A10 claims if any of the following remain unresolved without diagnostic-only handling:

- missing or invalid upstream source records;
- missing Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundation;
- invalid Phase 8 environment or reward records;
- hidden labels, correctness, future reward, future next state, or future embodiment outcomes in policy context;
- missing action legality mask;
- illegal selected action in thesis-facing evaluation;
- unversioned reward/cost model;
- post-hoc reward tuning on held-out outcomes;
- missing policy config, seed, or config hash;
- missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for any update-enabled mutation;
- mutation during held-out frozen evaluation;
- mixed adaptation and frozen-evaluation curves;
- missing held-out session/subject/seed separation for generalization claims;
- missing strong baselines without claim narrowing;
- missing `MatchedComparisonReport`;
- missing metric dictionary entries;
- missing stress profile/schedule/matched keys for stress-conditioned A10;
- unresolved safety-event linkage where safety claims or warnings are material;
- missing negative-result notes;
- missing diagnostic-only flags;
- missing dashboard/export source lineage;
- missing claim-evidence entries or limitation tags;
- unsupported clinical, deployment, real safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation, real control, or medical-device wording.

### 26.3 Minimum viable Phase 10

A minimum viable Phase 10 includes:

- a small declared action space, preferably threshold-mode selection or deferral-route selection;
- versioned reward config and legality mask;
- validated `ReadinessContextRecord` inputs;
- update-enabled training/adaptation with complete `PolicyUpdateTrace` or a clearly frozen-only evaluation mode;
- held-out frozen evaluation with no-mutation evidence;
- Layer 7 transition/reward/session linkage;
- reward and regret curves against a declared best-fixed or baseline policy;
- comparison against accept-all, static threshold/selective, IHARQ-lite, and at least one validated stronger policy baseline where available;
- matched comparison report;
- metric dictionary references or diagnostic-only labels;
- negative-result notes where applicable;
- controller card/source bundle;
- simulation-only and non-clinical limitation tags.

### 26.4 Strong / thesis-ready Phase 10

A strong Phase 10 additionally includes:

- multiple bandit modes such as threshold selection, action selection, decoder-family trust selection, and deferral-route selection where justified;
- reward sensitivity and seed sensitivity analysis;
- stress-conditioned evaluation across validated Phase 9 profiles;
- matched comparisons against all available validated policy families through A9;
- complete reward/regret, wrong-accept-over-time, exploration-burden, action-distribution, policy-stability, and safety-override metrics;
- complete `PolicyUpdateTrace` and disabled-update/no-mutation audit artifacts;
- complete Layer 7 rollout/session/transition/reward records for Phase 10 runs;
- complete metric dictionary coverage;
- complete matched comparison reports;
- complete negative-result and diagnostic-only records;
- complete controller card/source bundle;
- complete dashboard/export/reproducibility inputs for Phase 14;
- complete claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries and Layer 0-ready limitation language.

### 26.5 Phase 10 final self-check

Before Phase 10 is considered complete, verify that:

- official Phase 0–15 identities are preserved;
- Phase 10 is not renamed as a wave, tier, scenario, or ablation;
- Layer 6 owns contextual-bandit policy outputs;
- Layer 7 owns transition/reward/session/rollout/environment records;
- Layer 8 owns stress profiles/schedules;
- Layer 10 owns dashboard/card/export outputs only;
- Layer 0 owns claim-safety review only;
- `A10` is evaluation-use metadata only;
- C0–C4 remain claim-maturity summaries only;
- clean upstream source records remain immutable;
- context leakage checks pass;
- action legality masks pass;
- reward configs are frozen and versioned before held-out evaluation;
- update-enabled traces are complete;
- frozen evaluation has no mutation;
- adaptation curves and frozen-evaluation curves are separated;
- matched comparison keys are complete or diagnostic-only labels are attached;
- missing baselines are disclosed;
- negative results are preserved;
- reward/seed sensitivity is reported;
- dashboard source-vs-derived boundaries are preserved;
- claim-safety boundaries are preserved;
- no clinical, deployment, medical-device, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real muscle-stimulation, or real assistive-control safety claim is supported;
- all unresolved issues are listed rather than hidden;
- downstream handoff enables Phase 11, Phase 14, and Phase 15 without unsupported reinterpretation.

# Phase 11 — Reinforcement-learning policy

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 11 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 11` |
| Official phase name | `Reinforcement-learning policy` |
| Phase status | Stretch C sequential policy-learning gate |
| Phase type | Simulation-only adaptive-policy evidence phase |
| Primary layer ownership | Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer, especially the `6.5 Reinforcement-learning readiness policy` module |
| Direct simulation layer participation | Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment |
| Supporting layer participation | Layers 0–5, Layer 8, optional downstream Layer 9, Layer 10 |
| Official ablation/evaluation linkage | `A11 — reinforcement-learning policy`; may also participate in `A12` stress-conditioned evaluation when Phase 9 stress inputs are valid |
| Primary predecessor phases | Phase 0 through Phase 10 |
| Primary downstream phases | Phase 12, Phase 13 where optional replay consumes policy outputs, Phase 14, Phase 15 |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Evidence-production logic only; not a function-level RL implementation playbook, algorithm tutorial, training recipe, or command-run guide |
| Claim boundary | Public-data/proxy/simulation-only sequential policy-learning evidence; no clinical, medical-device, real patient-safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation-control, deployment-readiness, or real assistive-control safety claim |

Phase 11 is the official Stretch C phase that evaluates whether a reinforcement-learning policy can add transparent, bounded value beyond simpler policy families under the already-declared simulated closed-loop readiness environment. It is not a mandatory condition for lower capability-tier thesis validity. It is valid only after Phase 8 has produced a stable simulation environment, Phase 9 has produced validated stress inputs for any stress-conditioned claim, and Phase 10 has produced contextual-bandit evidence that can serve as a simpler online-adaptation baseline where available.

Phase 11 must not be renamed as a policy-learning wave, online-control epic, advanced controller tier, or RL ablation owner. `A11` is evaluation-use metadata only. Layer 6 owns RL policy artifacts and `PolicyActionRecord` policy outputs. Layer 7 owns transitions, rewards, sessions, rollouts, diagnostics, and the update/frozen-evaluation environment evidence. Layer 10 may later render records and cards; it does not train, retune, repair, or recompute RL evidence. Layer 0 audits claims and limitation language; it does not produce empirical policy evidence.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 11 is the sequential policy-learning stretch phase. Its purpose is to evaluate whether reinforcement learning adds value over threshold rules, IHARQ-lite, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, contextual bandit, and other validated non-RL baselines in the Layer 7 simulated closed-loop readiness environment.

The Phase 11 evidence question is not “Can this project deploy an RL controller?” The valid question is:

```text
Under declared public-data, proxy-readiness, simulation-only assumptions, does a frozen RL policy trained/adapted in a declared simulation mode improve delayed-consequence reward, safety-proxy behavior, waiting/fallback burden, or stress-conditioned robustness compared with simpler validated policies, and when does it fail?
```

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 11 controls the following bottlenecks:

1. delayed-consequence policy learning beyond immediate-reward contextual bandits;
2. action-space explosion and unsafe exploration;
3. reward hacking and unversioned reward tuning;
4. simulator overfitting;
5. unstable seed-sensitive training;
6. policy opacity and weak interpretability;
7. missing policy-update traces;
8. mutation during held-out frozen evaluation;
9. mixed training/adaptation and frozen-evaluation curves;
10. unfair comparisons against weaker or unmatched baselines;
11. stress-conditioned claims without matched stress profiles;
12. optional embodiment-aware reward terms before embodiment records exist;
13. exaggerated clinical, deployment, safety, or real-control claims.

### 4.3 Evidence role

Phase 11 produces simulation-only A11 evidence for the advanced policy-learning stretch section of the thesis. It may strengthen the thesis by showing:

- transparent reward-learning and reward-sensitivity behavior;
- whether delayed-consequence policy learning improves over simpler policies;
- whether RL is unstable, reward-sensitive, overfit, unsafe, or unnecessary;
- how frozen evaluation differs from update-enabled training/adaptation;
- how stress profiles affect sequential policy behavior if Phase 9 stress evidence is valid.

Phase 11 remains thesis-useful even when RL fails. A well-documented negative RL result can support the project’s defensive design argument that more complex adaptive policies should not be overclaimed and may be unnecessary when simpler policies are sufficient.

### 4.4 What Phase 11 is not

Phase 11 is not:

- a real-time clinical controller;
- a deployed online adaptation system;
- a medical-device readiness demonstration;
- a real assistive-control safety validation;
- a real BCI-FES or muscle-stimulation controller;
- an embodiment-demonstration phase by itself;
- a dashboard evidence producer;
- an ablation owner;
- a replacement for Phase 10 contextual bandit or earlier baselines;
- proof that RL is superior unless matched, held-out, frozen, trace-complete evidence supports the narrower claim.

## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

### 5.1 Layer participation

| Layer | Phase 11 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Audits A11 claim language, limitation tags, diagnostic-only downgrades, frozen/update separation, and non-clinical boundaries | Does not produce empirical RL evidence or repair records |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Supplies immutable dataset, window, split, label, preprocessing, source lineage, and matched-comparison keys inherited through downstream records | Clean source records must not be overwritten by RL training, stress, simulation, or dashboard use |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Supplies prediction evidence, model identity, baseline decoder outputs, and baseline metric context used in readiness states and comparisons | Decoder predictions are upstream evidence, not RL outputs |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Supplies calibrated probabilities, uncertainty features, thresholds, selective-prediction status, and reliability warnings used by readiness contexts and policy baselines | Calibration/threshold records must remain frozen according to split rules |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Supplies `IHARQDecisionRecord`, evidence-verification status, rule-based action tokens, fallback/unsafe decisions, and evidence-quality inputs where applicable | IHARQ is not collapsed into Adaptive-IHARQ or RL |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Supplies regime/trust state features and temporal warnings when enabled | RegimeRisk is not redefined as RL state ownership |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Primary owner of RL policy artifacts, RL `PolicyActionRecord` rows, action-space declarations, reward/cost policy settings, policy-family identity, and controller-card source content | Layer 6 owns readiness-policy outputs; it must preserve simulation-only/update-mode limitations |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Runs matched simulated sessions, produces transitions, rewards, rollouts, diagnostics, update traces where mutation occurs, and disabled-update audit evidence | Layer 7 owns simulation transition/session/reward evidence; frozen evaluation cannot mutate policies |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Supplies `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifests, stress validity reports, and clean/stressed matching where stress-conditioned A11 is claimed | StressForge-Lite remains Layer 8-owned and must not overwrite clean source records |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite / OpenSim / Static-Replay Embodiment | Optional downstream/future source of embodiment state/outcome/reward records for later embodiment-aware analysis | Phase 11 does not require Layer 9 records; embodiment-aware claims are `not_applicable_with_reason` until Phase 12/13 produce them |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, Export, and Reproducibility | Later reads Phase 11 records, renders controller/reward/update/stress cards and views, surfaces warnings, and creates export/reproducibility manifests | Must not train RL, retune rewards, recompute hidden logic, hide negative results, or erase diagnostic-only labels |

### 5.2 Module participation

| Module / module family | Participation in Phase 11 | Inputs | Outputs / obligations |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layer 6 `6.5 Reinforcement-learning readiness policy` | Primary Phase 11 policy module | Transition/reward logs, readiness context, action history, stress state, reward config, legality masks, optional embodiment state only if legitimately available | RL policy artifact, RL `PolicyActionRecord`, reward/stability curves, controller-card source content, optional `PolicyUpdateTrace` through update hook |
| Layer 7 `StateAssembler` | Builds observable simulation state | Prediction, calibration, uncertainty, IHARQ, evidence quality, RegimeRisk, stress, history, allowed optional embodiment fields | Simulation-visible context; no hidden labels/future outcomes |
| Layer 7 `PolicyAdapter` | Normalizes RL and baseline policy outputs | `PolicyActionRecord`, action map, policy config | Normalized policy action for validation |
| Layer 7 `ActionValidator` | Enforces legality masks and safety/proxy constraints | Normalized action, budgets, fallback rules, stress/embodiment mode | Valid action or safe substitute; invalid action warning fields |
| Layer 7 `RewardEngine` | Computes declared reward/cost decomposition | State, action, consequence, reward config, stress/regime/optional embodiment terms | `RewardTraceRecord` and reward components |
| Layer 7 `PolicyUpdateHook` | Applies update-enabled training/adaptation feedback and writes traces | Update config, context, action, reward, next state | `PolicyUpdateTrace`, updated simulation-policy pointer, disabled-update audit where applicable |
| Layer 7 `PolicyComparisonHarness` | Runs matched RL and non-RL baselines over identical conditions | Policies, sessions, stress profiles, seeds, reward configs | `PolicyRolloutRecord`, comparison tables, matched reports |
| Layer 7 `EnvironmentValidator` | Checks invariants, leakage, reward consistency, matching, and no-mutation status | Records/configs/run outputs | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, warnings, diagnostic-only triggers |
| Layer 8 `StressCoupler` | Applies stress only for validated stress-conditioned evaluation | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifest | Stress-conditioned transition/reward/evaluation lineage |
| Layer 10 card/export components | Later consume saved Phase 11 source records | RL records, metrics, traces, diagnostics, limitations | Dashboard-derived views/cards/exports with source lineage |
| Layer 0 policy-learning safety guard | Audits claims and downgrade conditions | Update/frozen evidence, reward configs, matched reports, metric entries, limitations | Claim-safety tags, downgrade requirements, invalid-claim warnings |

| `SafetyEventRecord` versus safety logs/path alias | `unresolved_requires_confirmation` | Unsafe action, invalid action, safe-hold, and safety-proxy counts may become incomparable if event schema is unclear | Use manifest mapping; mark safety-event summaries warning-only/diagnostic-only if linkage is incomplete |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` schema/path finalization | `requires_confirmation` | Reward, stability, safety, waiting, fallback, stress, and sensitivity metrics are diagnostic-only without metric definitions | Require metric dictionary references or diagnostic-only labels |
| `ClaimEvidenceManifest` versus `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` alias governance | `unresolved_alias_governance` | Final A11 claim trace may use both names unless resolved | Preserve both names and map explicitly in handoff |
| Dashboard/export ID conventions | `deferred_to_phase14` | Phase 11 can prepare dashboard-readable source bundles but final export IDs wait for Phase 14 | Provide source lineage and placeholders; do not assert final dashboard export IDs |
| Repository path status for policy/RL outputs | `unresolved_path_status` | Some paths are registry-supported or conceptual but not final | Use manifest-mapped storage expectations, not unsupported fixed paths |
| Reward sensitivity downgrade criteria | `requires_confirmation` | RL rankings may change under reward weights; claim strength depends on declared criteria | Require reward ablation plan and downgrade rule before thesis-facing claim |
| Seed sensitivity criteria | `requires_confirmation` | Unstable RL results may be overclaimed | Require multiple-seed summary and downgrade rule before thesis-facing claim |
| Stress pointer/view canonical naming from Phase 9 | `unresolved_from_phase9` | Stress-conditioned A11 needs valid stress profile/schedule lineage and clean/stressed matched keys | Use Phase 9 validated stress records and manifest mapping; otherwise no A12-conditioned A11 claim |
| Optional embodiment reward terms | `not_available_until_phase12_or_external_supply` | Phase 11 cannot include embodiment-aware reward/context claims before Layer 9 records exist | Treat as downstream compatibility only; `not_applicable_with_reason` for core Phase 11 |
| Controller card / `CardRecord` ownership | `layer10_rendering_boundary` | Phase 11 prepares source content; Layer 10 renders dashboard/card artifacts later | Label Phase 11 card material as source bundle unless registry supports direct `CardRecord` production |

### 6.2 Impact assessment

None of the open registry issues prevents writing Phase 11 as an evidence plan. They do constrain thesis-ready A11 claims. The most important blocking issues for evidence use are:

1. missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for any update-enabled RL mutation;
2. missing disabled-update/no-mutation audit for held-out frozen evaluation;
3. unversioned or post-hoc reward/cost configuration;
4. missing metric dictionary entries for RL-facing metrics;
5. unmatched comparison keys;
6. stress lineage gaps for stress-conditioned claims;
7. unresolved safety-event linkage where safety-proxy behavior is material;
8. unsupported dashboard or claim-evidence alias resolution.

Where unresolved issues cannot be repaired inside Phase 11 without inventing schema details, this section preserves them as open issues and downgrades affected outputs to diagnostic-only until resolved.

```yaml
phase0_inheritance_gap: conditional
blocking_status: mixed
blocks_phase_execution: false_if_manifest_mapped_and_diagnostic_labels_are_used
blocks_thesis_ready_A11_claims: true_where_trace_audit_metric_claim_or_export_foundations_are_missing

```

Phase 11 may proceed as a plan and may produce diagnostic simulation evidence when Phase 0 foundations are incomplete. ### 9.2 Forbidden inputs

Phase 11 must not use the following as ordinary policy-visible inputs:

- true labels before the simulated action consequence is scored;
- future correctness;
- future reward;
- future next state;
- future stress outcome;
- future embodiment outcome;
- hidden simulator diagnostics;
- dashboard-generated metrics;
- claim-safety downgrades as policy optimization targets;
- post-hoc threshold or reward values tuned on held-out outcomes;
- Layer 10 views as source evidence;
- Layer 0 claim-audit labels as empirical evidence.

### 9.3 Required lineage fields

All Phase 11-derived records must preserve applicable lineage fields:

```text
source_record_ids
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
producer_module
phase_id
ablation_id where applicable
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
policy_id
stress_profile_id where applicable
embodiment_mode_id where applicable
policy_update_trace_id where applicable
reward_config_id
action_space_version
legality_mask_id
environment_config_id
```

If any required key is missing, the affected comparison must be marked diagnostic-only or incomplete.

| `MatchedComparisonReport` | `created`; `validated`; `dashboarded_later`; `used_for_thesis_later` | Required for fair comparison to non-RL and bandit baselines | Missing or incomplete report makes comparisons diagnostic-only |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` references/updates | `prepared`; `validated`; `used_for_thesis_later` | Metrics must be defined before dashboard/thesis use | Undefined metrics cannot support thesis-facing claims |
| `NegativeResultNote` and `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | `created` where applicable; `validated`; `dashboarded_later`; `used_for_thesis_later` | Negative and incomplete outcomes are evidence, not disposable failures | Hidden negative or diagnostic labels block claim-safety approval |
| Controller-card source bundle | `prepared`; `validated`; `dashboarded_later`; `used_for_thesis_later` | Phase 11 prepares source content; Layer 10 renders final controller card | Card cannot be claim-facing without source links and limitation tags |
| Dashboard views/cards/exports | `not_applicable` as Phase 11-created outputs; `enabled`; `dashboarded_later` | Layer 10 owns generated dashboard/card/export outputs in Phase 14 | Phase 11 must not treat dashboard-derived outputs as primary evidence |

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

### 12.1 Evidence chain

Phase 11 follows this evidence chain:

```text
validated public-data and split lineage
→ valid decoder/calibration/IHARQ/RegimeRisk/readiness context
→ stable Layer 7 simulation environment and reward definitions
→ declared action space, legality masks, reward/cost config, seeds, and held-out sessions
→ update-enabled RL training/adaptation with complete PolicyUpdateTrace
→ frozen trained/adapted policy artifact
→ held-out frozen evaluation with disabled-update/no-mutation audit
→ matched comparison against non-RL policies and contextual bandit
→ stress-conditioned evaluation only where Phase 9 stress lineage is valid
→ reward/seed sensitivity and stability analysis
→ evaluation records, metric dictionary references, negative notes, diagnostic flags
→ Layer 10-ready source bundles and Layer 0-ready limitation tags
```

### 12.2 Required evidence-production behavior

Phase 11 must:

1. start with simple RL policies and a small declared action space;
2. freeze reward/cost configuration before claim-facing evaluation;
3. declare all reward terms, including accuracy, accepted-trial correctness, unsafe events, evidence requests, waiting, fallback, delay, and optional embodiment-relevant penalties where actually supported;
4. enforce action legality masks before actions are applied;
5. block exploration of unsafe or undefined actions;
6. write `PolicyUpdateTrace` for every simulation-authorized RL update;
7. preserve `TransitionRecord.policy_update_trace_id` linkage where applicable;
8. keep update-enabled training/adaptation curves separate from held-out frozen-evaluation curves;
9. freeze trained/adapted policy artifacts before held-out evaluation;
10. write disabled-update/no-mutation audit evidence for frozen evaluation;
11. compare RL against IHARQ-lite, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, contextual bandit, static thresholds, and accept-all policies where validated;
12. run reward ablations and seed sensitivity checks;
13. report policy stability and failure modes;
14. evaluate under stress profiles only when Phase 9 stress records are valid and matched;
15. preserve negative results and diagnostic-only downgrades;
16. prepare controller-card source bundles with reward design, action space, safety constraints, training instability, and simulation-only limitations.

### 12.3 Evidence-production boundaries

Phase 11 must not:

- use future labels, rewards, next states, or embodiment outcomes as ordinary policy inputs;
- tune rewards on held-out frozen-evaluation outcomes;
- mutate policy during held-out frozen evaluation;
- merge adaptation curves with frozen-evaluation curves;
- compare policies under different sessions, seeds, reward configs, stress profiles, or splits without diagnostic-only labeling;
- treat stress inputs as measured physiological state;
- treat embodiment-relevant reward terms as valid before Layer 9 records exist;
- let Layer 10 recompute RL logic;
- let Layer 0 claim-safety review count as empirical evidence;
- use A11 as an artifact owner;
- claim real safety, deployment, clinical validation, rehabilitation efficacy, or real stimulation/control readiness.

### 12.4 Fallback logic

If Phase 11 fails or is not strong enough for thesis-facing evidence:

- report RL as optional Stretch C or future work;
- retain reward/seed sensitivity and failure analysis;
- use contextual bandit, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, IHARQ-lite, RegimeRisk, and static/selective baselines as the sufficient evidence path where their gates pass;
- mark A11 outputs diagnostic-only where trace, metric, matching, stability, or claim-evidence gates fail.

---

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Required validation gates

| Gate | Requirement | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 inheritance gate | Required schemas/configs/validators/run/hash/seed/manifest/metric/claim foundations exist or are gap-logged | Blocks or downgrades A11 |
| Source lineage gate | All consumed upstream records preserve source IDs and split lineage | Blocks thesis-facing use |
| Clean-source immutability gate | No upstream clean record is overwritten by RL, simulation, stress, dashboard, or manual repair | Blocks evidence if violated |
| Readiness context leakage gate | No hidden label, future correctness, future reward, future next state, or future embodiment outcome is policy-visible | Invalidates run |
| Phase 8 environment stability gate | Stable environment API, transition/reward/session/rollout/diagnostic records exist and pass invariants | Blocks Phase 11 thesis-facing evidence |
| Action-space gate | RL action space is declared, versioned, small enough for the evidence scope, and mapped to canonical actions | Diagnostic-only or blocked if unclear |
| Legality-mask gate | Every action is legality-checked before application | Invalid/unsafe action blocks or downgrades |
| Reward/cost config gate | Reward weights and costs are declared, versioned, hashed, and frozen before evaluation | Diagnostic-only if unversioned or post-hoc |
| Update-trace gate | Every update-enabled mutation emits `PolicyUpdateTrace` | Update-enabled A11 invalid if missing |
| Transition-update linkage gate | Transitions link to update traces where applicable | Update evidence diagnostic-only if missing |
| Frozen evaluation/no-mutation gate | Held-out evaluation uses frozen policy and disabled-update/no-mutation audit | Held-out A11 invalid if mutation occurs |
| Curve-separation gate | Training/adaptation curves are stored/exported separately from frozen evaluation curves | Dashboard/thesis use blocked if mixed |
| Held-out session gate | Held-out subjects/sessions/seeds/stress profiles exist where generalization/stress claims are made | Claims narrowed or blocked |
| Baseline sufficiency gate | Compare against strongest validated non-RL and bandit baselines available; disclose missing baselines | Superiority claims blocked/narrowed |
| Matched comparison gate | Policies share matched sessions, splits, seeds, reward configs, stress profiles, and evaluation settings | Unmatched comparisons diagnostic-only |
| Stress lineage gate | Stress-conditioned claims use valid Phase 9 `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifest, and matched clean/stressed keys | No stress-conditioned claim if missing |
| Reward sensitivity gate | Reward ablations test whether rankings are stable under declared weight changes | Reward-sensitive claims downgraded |
| Seed sensitivity/stability gate | Multiple seeds or declared stability checks support policy stability claims | Unstable or under-sampled results diagnostic-only |
| Simple-RL escalation gate | Phase 11 starts from simple RL policies and a small declared action space before broader stretch variants | Complex or opaque variants without a simple baseline remain diagnostic-only/future-work |
| Controller-card source-bundle gate | Controller-card source content captures reward design, action space, safety constraints, training instability, update/frozen status, simulation-only limitations, and source links | Card/dashboard use blocked or diagnostic-only if missing |
| Safety-event linkage gate | Safety/unsafe/invalid-action summaries link to canonical or manifest-mapped safety event records/logs | Safety claims/warnings diagnostic-only |
| Metric dictionary gate | All thesis-facing metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Metrics diagnostic-only if undefined |
| Negative-result gate | Negative/flat/unstable/unsafe/overfit outcomes are preserved | Final claim use blocked if hidden |
| Dashboard/export gate | Layer 10 receives source records, configs, metrics, warnings, limitations, and manifests only | Dashboard use blocked if lineage missing |
| Claim-safety gate | Layer 0 limitations and non-claim boundaries attached | Claims blocked or downgraded if missing |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 11 exits successfully when it produces a transparent, trace-complete, matched, held-out, frozen-evaluation comparison showing whether RL adds value or fails under declared constraints. RL superiority is not required. A valid negative result is an acceptable Phase 11 exit if it is fully documented, matched where required, metric-defined, limitation-tagged, and preserved for Layer 10/Phase 15.

### 13.3 Hard failure conditions

Phase 11 fails for thesis-facing A11 evidence if any of the following occur without diagnostic-only downgrade:

- update-enabled run lacks `PolicyUpdateTrace`;
- held-out frozen evaluation mutates policy;
- disabled-update/no-mutation audit is missing where configured;
- dashboard exports mix training/adaptation curves with frozen-evaluation curves;
- reward/cost configuration is unversioned or tuned post-hoc on held-out outcomes;
- hidden labels, future reward, future next state, or future embodiment outcomes leak into policy context;
- action legality masks are missing or ignored;
- matched comparisons are missing;
- stress-conditioned claims lack validated Phase 9 stress lineage;
- required metric dictionary entries are missing;
- negative results are hidden;
- claim-safety tags or limitation language are absent.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

### 14.1 Required matched keys

Phase 11 comparisons must preserve these keys where applicable:

```text
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
policy_id
policy_family
policy_version
action_space_version
legality_mask_id
reward_config_id
environment_config_id
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
phase_id
ablation_id
matched_comparison_id
stress_profile_id where applicable
stress_schedule_id where applicable
stress_run_manifest_id where applicable
policy_update_trace_id where applicable
frozen_evaluation_flag
update_mode
embodiment_mode_id where applicable
```

### 14.2 Matched-comparison obligations

| Comparison | Required matching | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|
| RL vs contextual bandit | Same sessions, splits, seeds where applicable, reward config, action-space mapping or declared action-map equivalence, evaluation mode, stress profile if used | Missing A10 baseline, unmatched reward/stress/session setup, or different action semantics without caveat |
| RL vs supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Same source records, split, context fields, action legality, reward/cost evaluation, held-out partitions | Missing supervised baseline or incompatible context/action map |
| RL vs learning-to-defer | Same replay sessions, fallback/request budgets, reward/cost terms, held-out partitions | Different fallback availability or request budget |
| RL vs IHARQ-lite | Same source IHARQ token lineage, sessions, splits, reward/cost scoring, stress profile if used | Overwriting IHARQ token or unmatched sessions |
| RL vs static threshold/selective baseline | Same thresholds as frozen registry entries, same evaluation sessions, same reward scoring | Post-hoc threshold tuning |
| RL stress vs RL clean | Same policy artifact where frozen evaluation is claimed, matched clean/stressed source IDs, stress profile/schedule lineage | Stress creates incomparable or unpaired source records |
| RL training vs RL held-out evaluation | Must be separated, not directly interpreted as same evidence family | Any merged curve or mutation in held-out evaluation |

### 14.3 Missing key handling

If any matched-comparison key is missing:

```yaml
comparison_status: diagnostic_only
claim_effect: no superiority_or_robustness_claim
required_record: DiagnosticOnlyFlag
required_note: NegativeResultNote if result is failed, unstable, flat, unsafe, or unreplicable
dashboard_behavior: surface warning; do not hide missingness
phase15_behavior: claim must be narrowed or omitted
```

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 Ablation linkage

| Evaluation ID | Relationship to Phase 11 | Artifact ownership rule |
|---|---|---|
| `A0 — raw decoder` | Baseline context only through previous phases | A0 does not own records |
| `A1 — calibrated decoder` | Baseline/calibration context only | A1 does not own records |
| `A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline` | Static registered-threshold baseline for policy comparison | A2 does not own records |
| `A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction` | Optional uncertainty/selective-prediction baseline context if produced upstream | A3 does not own records |
| `A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls` | Optional non-RL baseline context if produced upstream | A4 does not own records |
| `A5 — IHARQ-lite` | Required reference baseline where available | A5 does not own `IHARQDecisionRecord` |
| `A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator` | Evidence-quality-aware baseline/context | A6 does not own `EvidenceQualityRecord` |
| `A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk` | Regime-aware baseline/context if Phase 5 active | A7 does not own RegimeRisk records |
| `A8 — learning-to-defer` | Non-RL deferral baseline | A8 does not own `DeferralRecord` |
| `A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ` | Non-RL learned-policy baseline | A9 does not own policy records |
| `A10 — contextual bandit` | Simpler online-adaptation baseline for Phase 11 | A10 does not own bandit artifacts |
| `A11 — reinforcement-learning policy` | Primary evaluation-use metadata for Phase 11 | A11 does not own RL artifacts; Layer 6/7 own records |
| `A12 — StressForge stress tests` | Optional stress-conditioned evaluation context for A11 if Phase 9 records are valid | A12 does not own stress records; Layer 8 does |
| `A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo` | Not produced in Phase 11; may be future optional context after Phase 12/13 | A13 does not own embodiment records; Layer 9 does |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts

Phase 11 must produce or prepare the following explicit evaluation artifacts:

| Evaluation artifact | Required status | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` for A11 | Required | Summarize RL evaluation status, metrics, limitations, and diagnostic flags |
| A11 policy comparison table | Required | Compare RL against validated baselines |
| Held-out frozen-evaluation table | Required for thesis-facing A11 | Separate claim-facing evidence from training/adaptation |
| Training/adaptation curve table | Required if updates/training are shown | Show learning behavior without claiming held-out performance |
| `PolicyUpdateTrace` completeness report | Required for update-enabled runs | Prove updates are traceable |
| Disabled-update/no-mutation report | Required for frozen evaluation | Prove held-out policy did not mutate |
| Reward sensitivity table / note | Required | Detect reward hacking and ranking instability |
| Seed sensitivity / policy stability table | Required | Detect training instability |
| Stress-conditioned evaluation table | Required only for stress-conditioned claims | Link A11 with A12 where Phase 9 valid |
| Safety/invalid-action summary | Required where safety events or invalid actions occur | Surface unsafe or blocked actions |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | Required for thesis-facing comparisons | Preserve matched comparison keys |
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` references | Required | Define metrics used in tables/figures |
| `NegativeResultNote` index | Required where applicable | Preserve failures and non-improvements |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` table | Required where applicable | Downgrade incomplete/unmatched/untraced evidence |
| Controller-card source bundle | Required | Prepare Layer 10 card and thesis appendix |
| Claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries | Prepared | Enable Phase 15 claim audit |
| Reproducibility manifest inputs | Prepared | Enable Phase 14/15 export packaging |

### 15.3 Evaluation result interpretation

Phase 11 may support only bounded statements such as:

- “In simulation-only replay, the RL policy was evaluated against simpler baselines under declared reward and held-out conditions.”
- “RL did/did not improve delayed-consequence reward under the declared simulator and reward weights.”
- “RL performance was sensitive to reward weights or seeds and is therefore diagnostic-only or limited.”
- “Stress-conditioned A11 behavior was evaluated only under validated StressForge-Lite profiles.”

Phase 11 may not support claims that RL is ready for clinical use, safe for patients, suitable for deployment, or validated for real assistive control.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

If validation gates pass, Phase 11 may support bounded claims about:

- public EEG/proxy readiness policy evaluation;
- simulation-only sequential policy-learning behavior;
- delayed-consequence reward under declared reward weights;
- comparison of RL against validated simpler policies in matched simulated replay;
- frozen-policy held-out simulated evaluation;
- reward sensitivity and seed sensitivity of RL behavior;
- stress-conditioned RL robustness only under validated Phase 9 stress profiles;
- update-trace and reproducibility discipline for simulation-authorized policy updates;
- negative/diagnostic findings showing RL is unstable, unnecessary, unsafe under proxy constraints, or inferior to simpler baselines.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 11 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- safe real-world online adaptation;
- actual physiological fatigue or recovery control;
- real embodiment control unless Phase 12/13 later supply bounded simulation-only embodiment records;
- superiority of RL when matched comparison, metric, trace, and frozen-evaluation gates fail.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 11 outputs must carry relevant tags:

```text
public_eeg_only
proxy_readiness
simulation_only
evaluation_only
policy_learning_stretch
delayed_consequence_simulation
update_enabled_training_only where applicable
frozen_policy_evaluation where applicable
stress_conditioned where applicable
pseudo_label_based where applicable
embodiment_proxy_only where optional later embodiment terms are used
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
diagnostic_only where applicable
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Phase 11 claims must be downgraded when:

- RL is evaluated only on training/adaptation curves;
- held-out frozen evaluation is missing;
- updates occur during frozen evaluation;
- `PolicyUpdateTrace` is missing for update-enabled mutation;
- disabled-update/no-mutation audit is missing;
- reward/cost config is unversioned or tuned post-hoc;
- reward sensitivity changes conclusions materially;
- seed sensitivity or policy instability is high;
- baseline comparisons are missing, weak, or unmatched;
- stress-conditioned evidence lacks valid Phase 9 lineage;
- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- safety-event linkage is unresolved for safety-related summaries;
- diagnostic-only flags or negative-result notes are present;
- claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries are incomplete.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Before Phase 11 evidence can enter final thesis claims, Layer 0 must verify:

- all claim wording is simulation-only and proxy-bounded;
- forbidden claim classes are absent;
- limitations are visible in cards, dashboards, exports, and thesis text;
- negative results are not hidden;
- diagnostic-only labels are preserved;
- `A11` is treated as evaluation-use metadata, not artifact ownership;
- reward/frozen/update/matched-comparison gates are satisfied;
- optional stress or embodiment language is properly limited.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

### 18.1 Capability-tier relationship

| Capability tier | Phase 11 relationship |
|---|---|
| C0 | Not required. Phase 11 does not affect baseline repository/data/decoder evidence validity. |
| C1 | Not required. Phase 11 does not affect calibration, uncertainty, or selective-prediction claim maturity. |
| C2 | Not required. Phase 11 does not affect IHARQ/RegimeRisk/adaptive supervised policy sufficiency if those gates pass. |
| C3 | Phase 11 can strengthen C3-style simulation-bounded closed-loop/adaptive policy-learning evidence if all gates pass. |
| C4 | Phase 11 does not establish C4. C4 requires Layer 9 embodiment demonstration evidence from Phase 12/13. |

C0–C4 are claim-maturity summaries and stopping-point labels only. They are not phases, not ablation IDs, not artifact owners, and not substitutes for Phase 11 validation gates.

### 18.2 Claim-maturity outcomes for Phase 11

| Phase 11 result | Capability-tier effect | Claim handling |
|---|---|---|
| Valid held-out frozen RL evaluation with matched baselines and trace-complete training | Strengthens C3-style stretch evidence | Bounded simulation-only A11 claim may be used |
| RL inferior to contextual bandit or simpler baselines but fully documented | Still supports C3 defensive evaluation maturity | Negative result may be thesis-useful |
| RL unstable across seeds or reward weights | Weakens A11 | Diagnostic-only or limited sensitivity claim |
| RL lacks held-out frozen evaluation | Does not strengthen C3 claim maturity | Training/adaptation-only diagnostic evidence |
| RL lacks trace/audit evidence | Does not support update-enabled A11 | Downgrade or omit adaptive claim |
| RL stress-conditioned evidence valid | May strengthen C3 stress-conditioned discussion with A12 context | Still simulation/stress-only |
| Embodiment-aware RL before Phase 12/13 | No C4 contribution | Not applicable / unsupported |

---

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative-result handling

Phase 11 must preserve negative or weak results including:

- RL fails to beat contextual bandit;
- RL fails to beat supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- RL fails to beat learning-to-defer;
- RL fails to beat IHARQ-lite or static thresholds;
- RL reward improves while safety-proxy, wrong-accept, waiting, fallback, or request burden worsens;
- RL is seed-sensitive or unstable;
- RL is reward-weight-sensitive;
- RL overfits training/adaptation sessions;
- RL exploits reward loopholes;
- RL selects illegal or blocked actions frequently;
- RL degrades under stress;
- RL requires complexity that simpler policies avoid;
- RL evidence is diagnostic-only due to trace, metric, matching, stress, or claim-evidence gaps.

Each material negative result requires a `NegativeResultNote` and, where applicable, a `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`.

### 19.2 Baseline sufficiency

Phase 11 must compare RL against the strongest validated baselines available from earlier phases:

- accept-all baseline;
- static threshold/selective prediction baseline;
- IHARQ-lite baseline;
- IHARQ + evidence-quality where available;
- IHARQ + RegimeRisk where available;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ;
- learning-to-defer;
- contextual bandit from Phase 10;
- stress-conditioned versions of the above only when Phase 9 stress lineage is valid.

If a baseline is missing, Phase 11 must state why it is missing and narrow any claim. Missing baselines do not necessarily block Phase 11, but they block broad RL superiority claims.

### 19.3 Baseline-sufficiency outcomes

| Baseline state | Phase 11 claim effect |
|---|---|
| All validated baselines available and matched | RL comparison can be thesis-facing if all other gates pass |
| Contextual bandit missing or diagnostic-only | RL may still be evaluated, but “beyond bandit” claims are blocked |
| Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ missing | RL comparison narrowed; no claim against supervised adaptive policy |
| Learning-to-defer missing | Deferral-burden comparison narrowed |
| IHARQ-lite missing | Phase 11 baseline sufficiency substantially weakened |
| Static/selective baseline missing | Threshold/selective improvement claims blocked |
| Baselines unmatched | Comparison diagnostic-only |
| Baselines negative but documented | RL comparison may proceed with proper limitations |
