## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

### 20.1 Failure and diagnostic-only table

| Failure / missingness case | Required label | Phase 11 consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Missing Phase 8 stable environment records | `diagnostic_only` or `blocked` | No thesis-facing A11 |
| Missing `TransitionRecord` or `RewardTraceRecord` | `blocked` | RL training/evaluation invalid |
| Missing `ReadinessContextRecord` or leakage-checked context | `blocked` | Policy state invalid |
| Hidden label/future reward/future next-state leakage | `invalid_run` | Run excluded from claims |
| Missing action legality mask | `diagnostic_only` / `blocked` | No policy safety/proxy claim |
| Illegal or undefined actions not blocked/logged | `invalid_or_diagnostic_only` | Claims downgraded or blocked |
| Unversioned reward/cost config | `diagnostic_only` | No reward-based claim |
| Post-hoc reward tuning on held-out evaluation | `invalid_run` | Exclude from claim-facing evaluation |
| Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for mutation | `invalid_update_evidence` | No update-enabled A11 claim |
| Missing transition-to-update trace linkage | `diagnostic_only` | Update evidence cannot be fully audited |
| Mutation during held-out frozen evaluation | `invalid_frozen_evaluation` | Held-out A11 claim blocked |
| Missing disabled-update/no-mutation audit | `diagnostic_only` / `blocked` | Frozen evaluation not thesis-ready |
| Mixed training/adaptation and frozen-evaluation curves | `invalid_export` | Dashboard/thesis use blocked until separated |
| Missing held-out sessions | `training_only` / `diagnostic_only` | No held-out performance claim |
| Missing contextual-bandit baseline | `baseline_gap` | No “better than bandit” claim |
| Missing stronger non-RL baselines | `baseline_gap` | Superiority claim narrowed |
| Missing `MatchedComparisonReport` | `diagnostic_only` | No comparison claim |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | `diagnostic_only` | Metric/figure cannot support claim |
| Reward sensitivity changes conclusion | `diagnostic_only_or_limited` | Claim narrowed to sensitivity finding |
| Seed instability | `diagnostic_only_or_limited` | Stability claim blocked |
| Missing Phase 9 stress lineage for stress claim | `stress_conditioned_claim_blocked` | Clean-only A11 possible |
| Safety-event alias/path unresolved | `warning_only_or_diagnostic_only` | Safety summaries limited |
| Missing negative-result note | `claim_blocked_until_repaired` | Cannot hide failure |
| Missing limitation tags | `claim_blocked` | Layer 0 blocks final claim |
| Clinical/deployment wording | `invalid_claim` | Must be removed or rewritten |

### 20.2 Diagnostic-only rule

Diagnostic-only Phase 11 outputs may be kept for engineering, thesis limitations, failure analysis, and future-work discussion. They must be visibly marked and cannot be used to support stronger A11 claims.

### 20.3 Missingness reporting

All missingness must be recorded with:

- affected record/artifact/interface;
- affected comparison;
- missing key or schema;
- risk;
- diagnostic-only status;
- required repair;
- downstream effect on Phase 14/15.

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

### 21.1 Storage principle

Phase 11 storage must be record-driven, manifest-mapped, and lineage-preserving. Because the registry retains unresolved path-status issues, this section treats listed paths as registry-supported, architecture-supported, or conceptual expectations rather than inventing new final paths.

### 21.2 Expected storage families

| Storage family | Expected content | Path/status note |
|---|---|---|
| Policy records | RL `PolicyActionRecord` rows and policy-output summaries | Use `records/policy_records/` and run-local policy output manifests where supported |
| Policy models | RL policy artifacts, model/preprocessor/action-space files | Use `models/policy_models/` and run-local model manifests where supported |
| Policy update traces | `PolicyUpdateTrace`, update-step logs, update metadata | Registry supports `records/policy_update_traces/`; architecture supports run-local `runs/<run_id>/results/layer7_closed_loop/policy_updates/`; final path must be manifest-mapped |
| Disabled-update audit | No-mutation/frozen evaluation audit entries | `update_disabled_audit.csv` or manifest-mapped equivalent; schema/name unresolved |
| Transitions | Phase 11 `TransitionRecord` rows | `records/transition_records/` and run-local Layer 7 transition storage where supported |
| Rewards | Phase 11 `RewardTraceRecord` rows and reward decomposition | `records/reward_trace_records/` and run-local reward storage where supported |
| Sessions | `ClosedLoopSessionRecord` and held-out session manifests | `records/closed_loop_session_records/` and run-local session storage where supported |
| Rollouts | `PolicyRolloutRecord` for RL and baselines | `records/policy_rollout_records/` and run-local evaluation storage where supported |
| Episode summaries | `EpisodeSummaryRecord` | `records/episode_summary_records/` and run-local summary storage where supported |
| Diagnostics | `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord`, leakage/reward/mutation/matching warnings | `records/environment_diagnostic_records/` and run-local diagnostic storage where supported |
| Safety events | `SafetyEventRecord` or manifest-mapped safety logs | Canonical path/log alias unresolved; must be mapped in manifest |
| Stress linkage | Stress profile/schedule/run-manifest pointers | Use Phase 9 records; Phase 11 must not create Layer 8 source records |
| Evaluation artifacts | A11 comparison tables, held-out evaluation, reward/seed sensitivity, `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Use evaluation artifact storage with metric and matched-report references; exact path governed by manifest |
| Matched comparisons | `MatchedComparisonReport` | Store/report with complete keys and diagnostic labels |
| Metric dictionary | `MetricDictionaryEntry` references/updates | Final path/schema unresolved; manifest mapping required |
| Negative and diagnostic artifacts | `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Must be visible to dashboard/export/final claims |
| Controller-card source bundle | Reward design, action space, update/frozen status, limitations, source links | Phase 11 prepares source bundle; Layer 10 renders cards |
| Claim evidence | `ClaimEvidenceManifest` / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` entries | Alias governance unresolved; preserve mapping |
| Reproducibility | Record lists, configs, hashes, seeds, schemas, manifests | Phase 11 prepares inputs for Phase 14/15 |

### 21.3 Repository rules

Phase 11 must:

- preserve clean-source records unchanged;
- write derived records with lineage fields;
- version every reward/config/policy/action-space/legality-mask object;
- store seeds and config hashes for every run;
- separate training/adaptation and frozen-evaluation output families;
- keep update traces adjacent to or manifest-linked with runs;
- manifest-map unresolved paths instead of inventing final names;
- ensure dashboard exports can trace back to source records;
- preserve negative-result and diagnostic-only records.

## 22. Phase Summary and Handoff Record

### 22.1 Narrative summary

Phase 11 evaluates reinforcement-learning readiness policies as a simulation-only Stretch C extension. It consumes the validated Phase 8 closed-loop environment, Phase 9 stress records where stress-conditioned claims are made, and Phase 10 contextual-bandit evidence as a simpler adaptive baseline. It produces RL policy artifacts, RL `PolicyActionRecord` rows, update traces for update-enabled training/adaptation, disabled-update/no-mutation evidence for frozen evaluation, held-out evaluation tables, reward/seed sensitivity analyses, stress-conditioned comparisons where valid, matched comparison reports, metric dictionary references, negative-result notes, diagnostic-only flags, and controller-card source bundles. Its evidence role is to show whether delayed-consequence policy learning adds value or fails under declared public-data, proxy-readiness, simulation-only constraints. RL superiority is not required.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Handoff to Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo

Phase 11 hands Phase 12:

- validated RL `PolicyActionRecord` outputs where selected for embodiment demonstration;
- action-space and legality-mask lineage;
- reward/cost configuration and limitation tags;
- frozen/update mode metadata;
- policy identity, config hash, and seed lineage;
- safety/invalid-action warning summaries where materialized;
- diagnostic-only labels and negative-result notes.

Phase 12 must create and own Layer 9 embodiment records if embodiment is implemented. Phase 11 does not produce `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, `Layer9RewardTrace`, or `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`. Phase 12 must not treat RL policy output as real motor-control safety or real stimulation-control evidence.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison

Phase 11 hands Phase 13 only policy-action and evaluation context if optional OpenSim replay or comparison consumes RL outputs. Phase 13 remains optional and must preserve proxy/simulation-only limitations. Phase 11 does not make OpenSim claims.

### 23.3 Handoff to Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

Phase 11 hands Phase 14:

- RL `PolicyActionRecord` rows;
- RL policy artifact metadata and manifests;
- `TransitionRecord`, `RewardTraceRecord`, `PolicyRolloutRecord`, `ClosedLoopSessionRecord`, `EpisodeSummaryRecord`, and `EnvironmentDiagnosticRecord` links;
- `PolicyUpdateTrace` files and completeness reports;
- disabled-update/no-mutation audit entries;
- reward learning/adaptation curves;
- held-out frozen-evaluation tables;
- reward sensitivity tables;
- seed sensitivity/stability tables;
- stress-conditioned comparison tables and Phase 9 stress lineage where applicable;
- safety/invalid-action summaries;
- A11 comparison tables;
- `MatchedComparisonReport`;
- `MetricDictionaryEntry` references;
- `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`;
- `NegativeResultNote`;
- `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`;
- controller-card source bundle;
- claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries;
- limitation tags and warning requirements;
- reproducibility manifest inputs.

Layer 10 must read these records only. It must not rerun RL, mutate policy artifacts, retune reward weights, recompute hidden policy logic, merge training and evaluation curves, hide negative results, erase diagnostic-only labels, or promote optional stretch evidence into core claims.

### 23.4 Handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 11 hands Phase 15:

- A11 simulation-only reinforcement-learning evidence;
- matched comparison reports against validated baselines;
- held-out frozen-evaluation results;
- training/adaptation evidence kept separate;
- update-trace completeness evidence;
- disabled-update/no-mutation evidence;
- reward and seed sensitivity analyses;
- stress-conditioned results only where Phase 9 lineage is valid;
- negative-result notes;
- diagnostic-only labels;
- metric dictionary references;
- controller-card/export references;
- claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries;
- open issues constraining final claim wording.

Phase 15 must frame Phase 11 as simulation-only delayed-consequence policy-learning evidence. It must not convert Phase 11 into clinical, real safety, medical-device, rehabilitation, real stimulation, real assistive-control safety, or deployment evidence.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 11 is done when all criteria below are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with diagnostic-only handling.

### 26.1 Required completion criteria

- Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundations are available or gaps are logged.
- Phase 1–7 upstream records used for context and baselines are valid, immutable, and source-traceable.
- Phase 8 closed-loop environment, transition, reward, session, rollout, and diagnostic records are valid for the selected evaluation scope.
- Phase 9 stress profiles/schedules/manifests are valid if and only if stress-conditioned A11 claims are made.
- Phase 10 contextual-bandit evidence is used as the simpler online-adaptation baseline where validated, or its absence/diagnostic status is disclosed.
- `ReadinessContextRecord` inputs pass decision-time leakage validation.
- RL action space is declared, versioned, small, and mapped to canonical actions.
- Action legality masks are validated for every decision point.
- Reward formula, cost weights, penalty hierarchy, optional stress terms, and any optional later embodiment-relevant terms are declared and hashed before evaluation.
- RL policy configuration, algorithm family, seeds, exploration/update mode, and model/policy artifact version are recorded.
- Update-enabled training/adaptation runs produce complete `PolicyUpdateTrace` coverage.
- `TransitionRecord.policy_update_trace_id` or equivalent trace linkage exists where applicable.
- Held-out frozen evaluation has disabled-update/no-mutation evidence.
- Training/adaptation curves and held-out frozen-evaluation curves are exported separately.
- Held-out subject/session/seed/stress partitions are defined where generalization or stress claims are made.
- `TransitionRecord` and `RewardTraceRecord` lineage is complete for reward and delayed-consequence evidence.
- Baseline comparisons include the strongest validated non-RL and bandit policies available and disclose missing baselines.
- Matched comparison reports exist for thesis-facing comparisons.
- Reward, safety-proxy, waiting/fallback/request burden, policy-stability, reward-sensitivity, seed-sensitivity, stress, and comparison metrics have `MetricDictionaryEntry` references or diagnostic-only labels.
- Reward sensitivity and seed sensitivity are evaluated or explicitly marked as not claim-ready.
- Negative-result notes exist for failed, flat, unstable, unsafe, overfit, reward-sensitive, seed-sensitive, or diagnostic-only outcomes.
- Diagnostic-only flags exist for incomplete, unmatched, untraced, unversioned, leakage-risk, metric-undefined, or stress-lineage-incomplete outputs.
- Controller card/source bundle follows the declared controller-card template/source-bundle schema and includes policy identity, inputs, action space, reward design, safety constraints, update/frozen status, training instability, metrics, failures, simulation-only limitations, and source links.
- Layer 10 dashboard/card/export source inputs are complete and read-only.
- Layer 0 claim-safety tags and limitation language are attached.
- No clinical, medical-device, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation-control, real assistive-control safety, or deployment-readiness claim is supported.
- Phase 11 handoff package is complete for Phase 12, Phase 13 where optional, Phase 14, Phase 15, and Layer 0 review.

### 26.2 Blocking conditions

Phase 11 outputs must not be used for thesis-facing A11 claims if any of the following remain unresolved without diagnostic-only handling:

- missing or invalid upstream source records;
- missing Phase 0 schema/config/validator/run/hash/seed/manifest foundation;
- invalid Phase 8 environment or reward records;
- hidden labels, correctness, future reward, future next state, future stress outcome, or future embodiment outcome in policy context;
- missing action legality mask;
- illegal selected action in thesis-facing evaluation;
- unversioned reward/cost model;
- post-hoc reward tuning on held-out outcomes;
- missing policy config, seed, or config hash;
- missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for any update-enabled mutation;
- missing transition-update trace linkage where applicable;
- mutation during held-out frozen evaluation;
- missing disabled-update/no-mutation audit;
- mixed adaptation/training and frozen-evaluation curves;
- missing held-out session/subject/seed separation for generalization claims;
- missing contextual-bandit or other strong baselines without claim narrowing;
- missing `MatchedComparisonReport`;
- missing metric dictionary entries;
- missing stress profile/schedule/matched keys for stress-conditioned A11;
- unresolved safety-event linkage where safety-proxy claims or warnings are material;
- reward sensitivity or seed instability without limitation tag;
- missing negative-result notes;
- missing diagnostic-only flags;
- missing dashboard/export source lineage;
- missing claim-evidence entries or limitation tags;
- unsupported clinical, deployment, real safety, rehabilitation, real stimulation, real control, or medical-device wording.

### 26.3 Minimum viable Phase 11

A minimum viable Phase 11 includes:

- one simple RL policy family with a small declared action space;
- versioned reward/cost config and action legality mask;
- validated `ReadinessContextRecord` inputs;
- stable Phase 8 transition/reward/session/diagnostic records;
- update-enabled training/adaptation with complete `PolicyUpdateTrace` or clearly declared frozen-only/offline evaluation mode;
- frozen policy artifact before held-out evaluation;
- held-out frozen evaluation with no-mutation evidence;
- comparison against accept-all, static threshold/selective, IHARQ-lite, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, and contextual bandit where validated;
- matched comparison report;
- metric dictionary references or diagnostic-only labels;
- negative-result notes where applicable;
- controller-card source bundle;
- simulation-only and non-clinical limitation tags.

### 26.4 Strong / thesis-ready Phase 11

A strong Phase 11 additionally includes:

- reward ablations across declared reward-weight alternatives;
- seed sensitivity and policy-stability analysis;
- stress-conditioned evaluation across validated Phase 9 profiles;
- matched comparisons against all available validated policy families through A10;
- complete reward, wrong-accept/safety-proxy, waiting, fallback, request burden, action-distribution, policy-stability, and sensitivity metrics;
- complete `PolicyUpdateTrace` and disabled-update/no-mutation audit artifacts;
- complete Layer 7 rollout/session/transition/reward records for Phase 11 runs;
- complete metric dictionary coverage;
- complete matched comparison reports;
- complete negative-result and diagnostic-only records;
- complete controller-card source bundle;
- complete dashboard/export/reproducibility inputs for Phase 14;
- complete claim-evidence manifest/matrix entries and Layer 0-ready limitation language.

### 26.5 Phase 11 final self-check

Before Phase 11 is considered complete, verify that:

- official Phase 0–15 identities are preserved;
- Phase 11 is not renamed as a wave, tier, scenario, or ablation;
- Layer 6 owns RL policy outputs;
- Layer 7 owns transition/reward/session/rollout/environment/update-hook records;
- Layer 8 owns stress profiles/schedules;
- Layer 9 embodiment outputs are not claimed before Phase 12/13;
- Layer 10 owns dashboard/card/export outputs only;
- Layer 0 owns claim-safety review only;
- `A11` is evaluation-use metadata only;
- C0–C4 remain claim-maturity summaries only;
- clean upstream source records remain immutable;
- context leakage checks pass;
- action legality masks pass;
- reward configs are frozen and versioned before held-out evaluation;
- update-enabled traces are complete;
- frozen evaluation has no mutation;
- adaptation/training curves and frozen-evaluation curves are separated;
- matched comparison keys are complete or diagnostic-only labels are attached;
- missing baselines are disclosed;
- negative results are preserved;
- reward/seed sensitivity is reported or claim-downgraded;
- dashboard source-vs-derived boundaries are preserved;
- claim-safety boundaries are preserved;
- no clinical, deployment, medical-device, real-patient-safety, rehabilitation, real muscle-stimulation, or real assistive-control safety claim is supported;
- all unresolved issues are listed rather than hidden;
- downstream handoff enables Phase 12, Phase 13 where optional, Phase 14, and Phase 15 without unsupported reinterpretation.

# Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 12 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 12` |
| Official phase name | `MyoSuite embodiment demo` |
| Primary architecture layer | Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim Embodiment Demo |
| Primary module family | Module H — Embodiment adapter engine |
| Implementation-order role | Stretch C simulated embodiment proof-of-concept after Phase 11 RL policy and before Phase 13 optional OpenSim replay/comparison |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Evidence-production plan only; not a function-level simulator implementation guide, not a MyoSuite/OpenSim installation playbook, and not a biomechanics validation protocol |
| Core evidence role | Convert readiness-gated policy/IHARQ decisions into declared proxy simulated command consequences, record the simulated state/outcome/safety evidence, and prepare A13 embodiment-demo evaluation artifacts |
| Required claim boundary | Simulation-only, proxy-mapped, non-clinical embodiment demonstration; no real assistive-control, rehabilitation, stimulation, patient-safety, or medical-device claim |
| Optionality | Stretch C / C4-oriented. E0/E1 fallback preserves thesis validity if MyoSuite physics is infeasible. |
| Previous phases retained in this file | Phase 0 through Phase 11 are preserved above without deletion or replacement. |

Phase 12 is the official implementation phase that materializes the Layer 9 embodiment branch. It is not a new policy phase, not a dashboard phase, not a clinical validation phase, and not a replacement for Phase 7 closed-loop simulation. Its purpose is to show, under strict proxy and simulation-only limitations, how readiness decisions from IHARQ, RegimeRisk, supervised policy, contextual bandit, or RL policy outputs can gate simulated assistive-action commands and produce traceable action-level outcomes.

Phase 12 may be thesis-strengthening if it reaches E2 or higher, but the core thesis can remain defensible through earlier phases if the embodiment branch is limited to E0/E1 or downgraded to diagnostic-only.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

Phase 12 controls the bottleneck between abstract readiness decisions and simulated action-level consequences. Earlier phases can show decoder accuracy, calibration, uncertainty, IHARQ decision quality, temporal trust, supervised policy behavior, closed-loop simulated rewards, stress robustness, contextual-bandit learning, and RL policy behavior. Those phases do not by themselves show how a readiness-gated decision would affect an action-facing assistive interface. Phase 12 adds that consequence layer by mapping accepted proxy intent into simulated commands while logging holds, no-actions, fallback behavior, blocked commands, endpoint error, command success/failure, safety events, delay cost, and reward terms where enabled.

The purpose is deliberately bounded:

1. demonstrate readiness-gated simulated action consequences through declared proxy mappings;
2. preserve upstream source lineage and canonical action tokens;
3. enforce a readiness safety gate before any static replay or MyoSuite step;
4. produce Layer 9-owned `EmbodimentStateRecord` and `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord` outputs;
5. produce A13-ready evaluation artifacts only when matched comparisons and metric dictionaries are complete;
6. prepare read-only dashboard/card/reproducibility inputs for Phase 14;
7. maintain Layer 0 non-clinical, simulation-only, embodiment-proxy limitations.

Phase 12 is not responsible for proving real biomechanics, clinical rehabilitation value, real muscle stimulation control, or real assistive-control safety. Its thesis value is a reproducible demonstration that reliability-aware readiness decisions can be connected to simulated assistive-action consequences under declared proxy and simulation limits.

| Registry issue / ambiguity | Phase 12 impact | Required handling | Claim consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SafetyEventRecord` versus `safety_event_log.csv` storage alias remains unresolved | Phase 12 may produce either a canonical record table or a safety-event log depending on implemented storage | Use `SafetyEventRecord` canonically where schema exists; preserve `safety_event_log.csv` as storage alias; document mapping in manifest | Missing or unmapped safety event evidence downgrades A13 to diagnostic-only |
| `Layer9RewardTrace` is a normalized candidate | Reward-enabled embodiment may need a reward-trace artifact that is not fully globally reconciled | Use `Layer9RewardTrace` only where enabled and mark candidate status; otherwise disable reward feedback and state no-reward mode | Reward-based policy/embodiment claims blocked if trace is absent or candidate status is hidden |
| Exact command-mapping vocabulary is not globally finalized | Unsupported or ambiguous EEG-label-to-command mappings could become invented commands | Require versioned `command_mapping.yaml`, mapping ID, mapping rationale, known limitation, and unsupported/no-action behavior | Unsupported mapping blocks command execution or makes result diagnostic-only |
| Exact safety severity/reason-code scale remains partly unresolved | Unsafe/safety summaries may be incomparable | Use architecture-supported L9 reason codes and preserve unresolved severity scale as open issue | No real patient-safety claim; safety summaries remain simulation/proxy-only |
| Dashboard metric/view/card/export ID conventions remain partially unresolved | Phase 14 may not be able to render thesis-ready embodiment views if Phase 12 exports lack expected IDs | Include dashboard-compatible export IDs, source-record IDs, metric dictionary IDs, matched comparison IDs, and manifest IDs where available; carry ID convention gap forward | Export is incomplete until Layer 10 validates IDs |
| Metric dictionary formulas for Layer 9 embodiment may require implementation confirmation | A13 comparisons need metric definitions, directionality, aggregation, and claim boundaries | Produce `metrics/metric_dictionary_layer9_embodiment.yaml` or mark metric as diagnostic-only | Thesis-ready A13 blocked without metric dictionary |
| `ClaimEvidenceManifest` naming and claim-evidence path linkage must remain explicit | Phase 12 can otherwise cite a path without preserving the canonical claim-evidence artifact identity | Use `ClaimEvidenceManifest` for the canonical artifact and `manifests/claim_evidence/layer9_embodiment_claim_evidence.json` as its expected path/form | Phase 15 embodiment wording cannot cite A13 if this linkage is absent |
| Repository path status has architecture-supported examples but some final paths may remain merge-pending | Storage ambiguity can break Phase 14/15 reproducibility | Use architecture-listed paths while marking them as expected repository expectations unless final registry confirms exact paths | Missing path manifest downgrades reproducibility readiness |
| A13 is evaluation-use metadata, not artifact owner | Risk of saying A13 produces records | State that Phase 12 / Layer 9 produces records used by A13 | Ownership confusion blocks claim-safety approval |
| Layer 9 embodiment feedback into policy is conditional | Risk of hidden update-enabled training from embodiment reward | Require declared simulation-only feedback mode, `PolicyUpdateTrace` where updates occur, and held-out frozen evaluation separation | Missing update trace blocks adaptive/embodiment-feedback claims |

### 7.2 Phase 0 inheritance decision

```text
phase0_inheritance_gap: true
severity: weakens_or_blocks_specific_claims_not_core_execution
```

Phase 0 established the general substrate required for Phase 12, but several Layer 9 details remain registry-candidate or merge-pending: `SafetyEventRecord` versus safety-event log storage, `Layer9RewardTrace` canonical status, exact Layer 9 metric formulas, final dashboard/export ID conventions, and some exact repository path confirmations. These gaps do not block E0/E1 fallback, and they do not block producing a diagnostic Layer 9 embodiment demo. They do block thesis-ready A13, reward-enabled policy-feedback, or Phase 14 dashboard export claims unless Phase 12 explicitly fills, validates, or carries them as open issues.

Temporary handling: run Phase 12 with conservative status labels. Use `diagnostic_only` for unmatched or candidate-schema outputs, `optional_stretch` for E2+ MyoSuite / E3 stress / E4 OpenSim-related outputs, and `blocked` for any reward-enabled or thesis-ready claim missing required lineage, metric dictionary, safety log, or manifest.

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 12 evidence production follows a record-first chain:

```text
Phase 0 schemas/configs/validators
→ Phase 1–11 upstream records and limitation tags
→ Layer 9 record-intake validation
→ readiness-context assembly
→ readiness safety gate
→ proxy command mapping
→ optional stress embedding
→ static replay or MyoSuite adapter branch
→ simulator/replay step only after safety gate
→ outcome and reward computation where enabled
→ EmbodimentStateRecord / EmbodimentOutcomeRecord / safety log / transition linkage
→ command timeline and endpoint-error curve
→ Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest
→ A13 evaluation artifacts
→ Layer 10 read-only dashboard/card/export package
→ Phase 15 bounded thesis evidence
```

### 12.1 Mode-specific evidence logic

| Mode | Evidence-production status | Required outputs | Thesis interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| E0 — No embodiment | Accepted absence / fallback | E0 `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` explaining absence and limitation | Core thesis can remain valid; no action-level embodiment claim |
| E1 — Static replay | Minimum command-timeline bridge | Command timeline, safety-event log, replay manifest, mapping manifest, preliminary card source | Shows readiness-to-command/no-command behavior without physics |
| E2 — MyoSuite simple task | Preferred Phase 12 physical-simulation branch | `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, endpoint-error curve, command success/failure, transition linkage, manifest | Supports bounded simulated action-consequence claim |
| E3 — MyoSuite with stress | Conditional stress embodiment | E2 outputs plus stress profile/schedule lineage, paired clean/stress outcomes, stress-conditioned negative-result notes where needed | Strengthens A12/A13 intersection under declared stress proxies |
| E4 — OpenSim replay/visualization | Optional / Phase 13-facing branch | Replay assets, screenshots/video manifest if generated, limitations statement | Phase 12 may prepare E4-compatible trajectories only if configured; official OpenSim replay/comparison remains Phase 13 and is not required for Phase 12 completion |
| E5 — Comparative embodiment report | Synthesis mode | Matched comparison report, A13 tables, cards/source bundles, `ClaimEvidenceManifest`, limitations | Thesis-ready only if matched keys, metrics, warnings, and manifests validate |

### 12.2 Safety gate invariant

The Phase 12 safety invariant is:

```text
unsafe, uncertain, unsupported, fallback, wait, request_evidence, unresolved combine_evidence, simulator_error, stop_loss, or high-risk states must not execute aggressive assistive commands.
```

They may produce safe hold, no-action, conservative fallback, blocked command, request-more-evidence behavior, or run termination with a recorded reason. The safety gate must occur before static replay stepping, MyoSuite stepping, OpenSim replay export, outcome computation, and reward computation.

### 12.3 Evidence-production boundaries

- Decoder predictions, calibrated confidence, IHARQ actions, RegimeRisk states, policy actions, and stress schedules are inputs to Layer 9; they are not rewritten by Layer 9.
- Layer 9 adapter statuses are not exported as canonical IHARQ actions.
- Ground-truth labels are evaluation-only and may be attached only after the policy action and safety result are fixed.
- Embodiment outcomes may provide simulation-only reward feedback only if the experiment configuration explicitly enables that path.
- Dashboard exports read saved records only.
- Visual screenshots or videos are not substitutes for `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, safety logs, command timelines, metric dictionaries, matched comparisons, or manifests.

---

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Core validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Pass condition | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Record-intake gate | Required upstream records, schema versions, IDs, split/protocol lineage, config hashes, seeds, limitation tags | All required records validate or accepted missingness is declared | Execution blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Clean-source immutability gate | Embodiment does not overwrite Layer 1–8 records | All derived records preserve `source_record_ids` and lineage | Phase 12 invalid if source records are modified |
| Readiness-token gate | IHARQ/policy/readiness actions use allowed canonical tokens or declared action maps | `accept`, `wait`, `request_evidence`, `combine_evidence`, `fallback`, `uncertain`, `unsafe` preserved; unresolved aliases mapped | Unsupported token forces hold/no-action and warning |
| Command-mapping gate | Mapping file is versioned, branch-compatible, limited, and rationale-bearing | Mapping ID, branch compatibility, fallback behavior, limitation field, and config hash present | Unsupported mapping blocks command or downgrades run |
| Safety-gate call-order gate | Safety result occurs before command mapping step execution | No decoder/policy output directly calls simulator step | Run invalid; claim blocked |
| Simulator/static replay gate | Branch reset/step/state/outcome values finite and logged | E1/E2/E3 branch runs reproducibly or fails closed | E0/E1 fallback or diagnostic-only |
| Branch progression gate | E1 static replay is attempted or explicitly waived before E2 stepped MyoSuite is treated as thesis-ready | Static replay mapping/safety timeline validates, or accepted missingness explains why E2 is used directly | E2 may remain diagnostic-only until mapping/safety bridge is justified |
| Stress-conditioning gate | E3 stress uses valid `StressProfileRecord` and `StressScheduleRecord` with matched clean baseline | Stress ID, schedule, injection point, seed, and clean/stress pairing validate | E3 diagnostic-only or not applicable |
| Reward gate | Reward terms are declared, versioned, decomposed, ablated, and traceable where enabled | `reward_config.yaml`, `Layer9RewardTrace`, reward decomposition, feedback flag present | Reward claim blocked; no policy feedback |
| Safety-event gate | Safety/block/error/fallback events are logged or empty log is validated | `SafetyEventRecord` or mapped storage alias present with reason codes | Safety/blocked-command analysis blocked |
| Evaluation gate | A13 outputs have metric dictionary, matched report, evaluation outcome record, negative-result note where needed | All explicit evaluation artifacts exist and validate | A13 diagnostic-only |
| Dashboard/export gate | Layer 10 source bundle has IDs, hashes, warnings, card source, and demo manifest | Dashboard-compatible export and manifest validate | Phase 14 cannot mark embodiment page thesis-ready |
| Claim-safety gate | Non-clinical, simulation-only, embodiment-proxy warnings are visible in records/cards/manifests | Strictest limitation tags present | Layer 0 downgrade or claim block |

### 13.2 Exit conditions

Phase 12 is complete at the minimum acceptable level when:

1. E0 accepted-missingness or E1 static replay is explicitly declared and manifested, or E2+ MyoSuite branch produces validated state/outcome evidence;
2. command mappings are versioned, branch-compatible, and limitation-labeled;
3. readiness safety gate cannot be bypassed;
4. all commands, holds, no-actions, fallbacks, blocks, unsupported mappings, simulator errors, and stop-loss blocks are logged;
5. all generated outputs preserve upstream lineage, run ID, config hash, seed, schema version, producer module, phase ID, and limitation tags;
6. A13 claims are made only if `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `NegativeResultNote` where applicable, and `ClaimEvidenceManifest` are complete;
7. `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` is complete for every run/mode;
8. Layer 10 can consume saved outputs without recomputing hidden simulator logic;
9. Layer 0 claim-safety review can identify allowed claims, forbidden claims, diagnostic-only cases, and limitation tags.

Phase 12 does not require MyoSuite superiority or policy superiority. A negative, null, static-only, or failed simulator result is valid evidence if it is preserved with correct diagnostic-only or limitation labeling.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

A13 embodiment comparisons are valid only if matched-comparison keys are preserved from public-data source records through readiness decisions, policy actions, embodiment runs, and evaluation exports.

| Key family | Required Phase 12 keys |
|---|---|
| Source/protocol identity | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `split_role`, `preprocessing_id`, `label_map_id`, `source_record_ids`, `artifact_flag_ids` |
| Decoder/calibration/readiness identity | `model_id`, `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, `evidence_quality_record_id`, `iharq_decision_record_id`, `readiness_context_record_id` |
| Policy identity | `policy_id`, `policy_family`, `policy_action_record_id`, `deferral_record_id`, `policy_update_mode`, `policy_update_trace_id` where applicable, `frozen_evaluation_flag` |
| Simulation/transition identity | `closed_loop_session_id`, `episode_id`, `transition_record_id`, `reward_trace_id`, `environment_diagnostic_id`, `safety_event_id` where applicable |
| Stress identity | `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, `stress_family`, `stress_intensity`, `stress_seed`, clean/stress pairing ID where active |
| Embodiment identity | `embodiment_session_id`, `embodiment_mode_id`, `simulator_branch`, `simulator_id`, `simulator_version`, `command_mapping_id`, `safety_rules_id`, `logging_schema_id`, `embodiment_record_id`, `outcome_record_id`, `command_timeline_id`, `endpoint_curve_id`, `demo_manifest_id` |
| Evaluation identity | `ablation_id` = `A13` where applicable, matched comparison ID, metric dictionary ID, negative result note ID, evaluation outcome ID, `ClaimEvidenceManifest` / claim-evidence ID, dashboard export ID |
| Reproducibility identity | `run_id`, `config_hash`, `seed`, `schema_version`, `producer_module`, `phase_id`, artifact hashes, repository path, validation status, claim-safety tags |

### 14.1 Matched-comparison failure rules

| Missing key or mismatch | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Dataset/split/window mismatch | A13 comparison blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Different command mapping versions across variants without declared comparison purpose | Matched embodiment comparison invalid |
| Different simulator config, task, horizon, seed, or safety rules without explicit stratification | Comparison diagnostic-only |
| Stress-conditioned run without matched clean baseline | E3 result diagnostic-only |
| Policy update mode mixed with frozen evaluation | Adaptive/embodiment feedback claim blocked |
| Missing metric dictionary or negative-result note for null/failure result | Thesis-ready A13 blocked |
| Missing `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` | Reproducibility and dashboard export blocked |

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 Evaluation-use boundary

A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo — is evaluation-use metadata only. Phase 12 / Layer 9 creates records and artifacts used by A13. A13 does not create, own, validate, or store records.

### 15.2 A13 variants and evaluation obligations

| A13 variant / comparison family | Evidence role | Required Phase 12 artifacts | Diagnostic-only trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accept-all embodiment | Baseline showing what happens if proxy commands execute without readiness gating | command timeline, outcome records where executed, safety log, metric entries | Missing source matching or unsafe unsupported mapping |
| Confidence-only embodiment | Baseline tied to calibrated confidence/thresholds | upstream threshold/calibration lineage, command mapping, outcome records | Threshold leakage or missing threshold registry |
| IHARQ-gated embodiment | Tests Layer 4 readiness gate effect | `IHARQDecisionRecord` lineage, safety gate, outcome records | Canonical action-token mismatch |
| RegimeRisk-aware embodiment | Tests temporal trust gating | `RegimeStateRecord`/trust/stop-loss lineage, safety gate, outcome records | Temporal leakage or missing risk context |
| Supervised Adaptive-IHARQ / learning-to-defer embodiment | Tests supervised policy/deferral action consequences | `PolicyActionRecord`, `DeferralRecord`, action-legality status, outcome records | Deferral/policy fields missing or unsupported |
| Contextual-bandit embodiment | Optional policy comparison using Phase 10 outputs | bandit policy ID/action records, update/frozen status, outcome/reward records where enabled | Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for update-enabled run |
| RL policy embodiment | Optional policy comparison using Phase 11 outputs | RL policy ID/action records, held-out frozen status, outcome/reward records where enabled | Frozen/update mixing or missing disabled-update audit |
| Stress-conditioned embodiment | A12/A13 intersection | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, paired clean/stress records, outcome records | Unmatched clean/stress pair or invalid injection point |
| Static replay E1 | Fallback evidence when MyoSuite unavailable | command timeline, safety log, E1 manifest | Presented as physics-based result |
| MyoSuite E2/E3 | Preferred simulated embodiment evidence | state/outcome records, endpoint curves, safety logs, demo manifest | Simulator non-finite/unlogged or metric dictionary missing |
| Optional OpenSim replay E4 | Phase 13-facing visualization/comparison | selected command trajectories, replay manifest, limitation statement | Presented as biomechanics/clinical validation |

### 15.3 Explicit evaluation artifacts

Phase 12 must produce or explicitly mark absent the following evaluation artifacts:

| Evaluation artifact | Required when | Required content |
|---|---|---|
| `records/evaluation_outcomes/layer9_embodiment_evaluation_outcomes.parquet` / Layer 9 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` | Any A13 result is reported | metric outputs, A13 ID, matched comparison ID, metric dictionary ID, diagnostic-only flag, claim-evidence pointer, embodiment mode, stress ID where active |
| `reports/matched_comparisons/layer9_matched_embodiment_comparisons.csv` / `MatchedComparisonReport` | Any comparison claim is made | matched keys, compared variants, source records, mapping/simulator/stress/reward config equality or declared stratification, diagnostic-only flags |
| `metrics/metric_dictionary_layer9_embodiment.yaml` / `MetricDictionaryEntry` set | Any metric appears in a table, card, dashboard, or thesis figure | metric name, definition, directionality, aggregation unit, required fields, valid range, limitation tags, ablation ID, warning rules |
| `notes/negative_results/layer9_embodiment_negative_results.md` / `NegativeResultNote` | Any branch fails, result is null, comparison is unmatched, reward dominates, simulator unstable, E0/E1 fallback is used, or only diagnostic evidence exists | negative result statement, affected variants, root cause, claim downgrade, limitation tags, downstream handling |
| `manifests/claim_evidence/layer9_embodiment_claim_evidence.json` / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` | Any Phase 15 claim cites A13 | claim text, allowed claim type, source records, metric dictionary IDs, matched reports, negative-result notes, limitation tags, dashboard/export IDs |
| `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` | Every Phase 12 mode/run | configs, hashes, seeds, simulator branch/version, command mapping ID, safety rules ID, output paths, file hashes, missingness, warnings, reproduction command |

### 15.4 Frozen/update evidence separation where applicable

Phase 12 normally evaluates saved policies or readiness decisions in evaluation-only embodiment mode. If embodiment outcomes or rewards are fed back into contextual-bandit, RL, or other adaptive policy learning, the run becomes a simulation-only policy-feedback embodiment mode and must satisfy:

- update-enabled policy changes are separated from held-out frozen evaluation;
- every mutation has `PolicyUpdateTrace` where applicable;
- disabled-update audits are available for frozen evaluation;
- training/adaptation curves are not merged with frozen-policy embodiment evaluation curves;
- reward terms are decomposed and ablated;
- dashboard/card/export bundles visibly display feedback-enabled status;
- all such evidence is labeled simulation-only and cannot support real deployment or patient-facing control claims.

## 16. Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Obligations

### 16.1 Layer 10 source-vs-derived separation

| Category | Phase 12 content | Layer 10 permission | Layer 10 prohibition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard-readable source records | `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, embodiment-linked transition pointers, safety-event logs, command timelines, endpoint-error source curves, `Layer9RewardTrace` where enabled, `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`, evaluation artifacts | Read, validate, summarize, filter, visualize, warn, export, card, and package | Must not recompute hidden simulator outcomes or alter Layer 9 records |
| Dashboard-warning inputs | missing source IDs, unsupported mapping, simulator error, safety gate bypass, manifest missing, metric dictionary missing, unmatched comparison, reward trace missing, stress lineage missing, clinical-overclaim wording | Display warnings and downgrade status | Must not hide warnings or replace them with styling |
| Dashboard-generated derived outputs | `DashboardMetricRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, `CardRecord`, final dashboard embodiment page, endpoint-error panel, safety-event table, command-timeline view, export logs, reproducibility package entries | Generate traceable derived views with source pointers | Must not be treated as primary evidence |
| Dashboard-export manifest inputs | file paths, hashes, run IDs, config hashes, command mapping IDs, simulator metadata, matched report IDs, metric dictionary IDs, negative result IDs, claim evidence IDs | Include in artifact/reproducibility manifests | Must not export untraceable figures as thesis-ready |
| Not-dashboard inputs | live simulator state, raw MyoSuite environment instance, optional OpenSim runtime internals, local debug logs not saved as artifacts | May be referenced only through saved records/manifests | Must not use live runtime state to recompute results during dashboarding |

### 16.2 Required Phase 12 dashboard/card inputs

Phase 12 must prepare the following Layer 10-readable sources:

- embodiment mode and branch summary;
- command mapping table and limitation statement;
- readiness action to safety-gate timeline;
- command/no-action/fallback/blocked timeline;
- `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord` table;
- endpoint-error curve source;
- command-success/failure table;
- unsafe-event / blocked-command / unsupported-mapping summary;
- no-action/fallback burden table;
- stress-conditioned outcome table where E3 is active;
- reward decomposition and `Layer9RewardTrace` where reward is enabled;
- screenshot/video manifest where generated;
- `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`;
- metric dictionary, matched comparison, negative-result, and `ClaimEvidenceManifest` references;
- simulation-only and non-clinical warning text.

### 16.3 Embodiment card content boundary

Phase 12 prepares embodiment-card source content. Phase 14 may render it as Layer 10 `CardRecord` / dashboard card output. The card source must include identity, source records, command mapping, simulator setup, stress profile/schedule where active, metrics, metric dictionary IDs, matched-comparison status, failures, negative-result notes where applicable, limitations, claim-evidence ID, reproduction command, and file hashes.

A polished card without source-record lineage, warning flags, metric dictionary entries, matched comparison status, or claim-evidence linkage is not thesis-ready.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 12 may support only bounded claims such as:

1. the architecture can connect readiness-gated neural-intent decisions to simulated assistive-action consequences through declared proxy mappings;
2. static replay or MyoSuite execution can expose command/no-action/fallback/blocked-command timelines under simulation-only assumptions;
3. readiness gating can be compared with accept-all, confidence-only, IHARQ-gated, RegimeRisk-aware, supervised/adaptive-policy, contextual-bandit, or RL policy variants when matched keys are preserved;
4. stress-conditioned embodiment can expose failure modes under declared simulated stress profiles;
5. embodiment outcomes can provide simulation-only reward/cost terms for policy comparison when reward feedback is explicitly enabled and traced;
6. Layer 10 can inspect and reproduce saved Layer 9 outputs using records, cards/source bundles, figures, logs, metric dictionaries, matched reports, and manifests.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 12 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real exoskeleton or assistive-control safety;
- direct EEG-to-muscle actuation;
- subject-specific biomechanics validation;
- real deployment readiness;
- patient-facing adaptive control;
- OpenSim or MyoSuite evidence as proof of real-world therapeutic effect.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

At minimum, Phase 12 records, cards/source bundles, evaluation artifacts, dashboards, manifests, and thesis-ready exports must carry the strictest applicable subset of:

```text
public_eeg_only
proxy_readiness
proxy_label_based
evaluation_only
simulation_only
stress_conditioned
embodiment_proxy_only
MyoSuite_OpenSim_demo_only
diagnostic_only
future_work_only
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

| Condition | Claim downgrade |
|---|---|
| E0/no embodiment only | No action-level embodiment claim; core reliability claims unaffected |
| E1/static replay only | Command-timeline demonstration only; no physics/movement-outcome claim |
| E2 MyoSuite records exist but no matched report | Diagnostic action-outcome demonstration only |
| Missing metric dictionary | No thesis-ready metric claim |
| Missing safety-event log | No safety-event or blocked-command analysis claim |
| Missing `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` | No reproducible embodiment claim |
| Reward feedback enabled without trace/ablation | Reward or adaptive embodiment-feedback claim blocked |
| Clinical wording present | Layer 0 must reject or rewrite claim; affected artifact cannot be thesis-ready |

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

Capability tiers C0–C4 are claim-maturity summaries and stopping-point labels, not implementation phases, ablation owners, or artifact owners.

| Capability tier | Phase 12 relationship | Claim-maturity effect |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Earlier baseline/public-data reliability remains valid without Phase 12 | Unchanged by Phase 12 |
| C1 | Calibration/uncertainty visibility remains upstream | Unchanged except as inherited readiness context |
| C2 | IHARQ/RegimeRisk/adaptive-readiness evidence can feed embodiment, but remains upstream | Phase 12 may strengthen action-consequence interpretation, not upstream validity |
| C3 | Simulation/stress/policy evidence from Phases 8–11 remains valid without embodiment | Phase 12 can connect C3 policies/stress to action-level proxy outcomes |
| C4 | Phase 12 is one possible contributor to C4 embodiment/dashboard maturity | C4 requires validated Layer 9 outputs plus Phase 14 dashboard/card/export and Phase 15 claim audit; Phase 12 alone is not C4 |

Phase 12 reaches a strong C4-supporting status only if E2+ or E3/E5 outputs are validated, A13 evaluation artifacts exist, Layer 10 can read/export them, and Layer 0 confirms bounded non-clinical claims. If Phase 12 stops at E0 or E1, the project may still be thesis-valid at earlier tiers; the embodiment contribution remains optional/stretch or diagnostic.

---

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative-result obligations

Phase 12 must produce a `NegativeResultNote` or equivalent negative-result entry when:

- MyoSuite is unavailable or unstable and the branch falls back to E0/E1;
- command mapping coverage is incomplete or unsupported;
- the safety gate blocks most commands and no action-level improvement is observed;
- accept-all or confidence-only baselines perform similarly to readiness-gated variants;
- RegimeRisk-aware or policy-based variants are overly conservative or produce excessive no-action/fallback burden;
- stress-conditioned embodiment degrades performance or exposes failure modes;
- reward terms dominate or create reward-hacking behavior;
- OpenSim replay is unavailable or visualization-only;
- matched comparison keys are incomplete;
- metric dictionary, safety-event logs, or manifest linkage is incomplete;
- results are only diagnostic, optional, or non-thesis-ready.

Negative results are not failures to be hidden. They are evidence about simulator fragility, mapping limitations, policy conservatism, stress sensitivity, reward design, or claim boundaries.

### 19.2 Baseline-sufficiency requirements

Phase 12 should compare readiness-gated embodiment against the simplest valid baselines before claiming added value:

| Baseline / comparator | Required purpose | Sufficiency condition |
|---|---|---|
| No embodiment E0 | Shows thesis without embodiment branch | Manifested accepted absence |
| Static replay E1 | Shows command/no-command behavior without physics | Command timeline and safety log complete |
| Accept-all embodiment | Shows unfiltered action execution burden | Matched to same records/mapping/simulator/horizon |
| Confidence-only embodiment | Shows threshold-only action gating | Matched threshold/calibration lineage |
| IHARQ-gated embodiment | Shows evidence-verification contribution | Canonical IHARQ tokens preserved |
| RegimeRisk-aware embodiment | Shows temporal trust contribution | Regime/trust context validated |
| Adaptive / bandit / RL policy embodiment | Shows policy-learning contribution | Frozen/update separation and action legality validated |
| Clean versus stress-conditioned embodiment | Shows stress sensitivity | Paired clean/stress keys validated |

If these baselines are unavailable, the corresponding comparison must be marked `diagnostic_only`, `not_applicable`, or `optional_stretch`, rather than being presented as a positive A13 claim.

---

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure / missingness condition | Detection | Required handling | Diagnostic-only / blocked result |
|---|---|---|---|
| MyoSuite installation or task instability | Branch smoke test, reset/step failure, non-finite state | Fall back to E0/E1, write manifest and negative-result note | E2/E3 blocked; E1 may remain valid |
| Command mapping unsupported | Mapping validator | No-action/hold or blocked command; log mapping warning | Unsupported variant diagnostic-only |
| Safety gate bypass | Adapter call-order test | Invalidate run; no command accepted | Phase 12 run blocked |
| Simulator error unlogged | Exception/log completeness check | Write simulator-error event/manifest; fail closed | Outcome claim blocked |
| Safety-event log missing | Safety log validator | Block safety-event rate and blocked-command claims | A13 diagnostic-only or blocked |
| `Layer9RewardTrace` missing in reward-enabled run | Reward trace completeness check | Disable reward feedback or block reward claim | Reward analysis blocked |
| Frozen/update mode mixed | Policy update/frozen audit | Separate training/adaptation/frozen results; require `PolicyUpdateTrace` | Adaptive embodiment-feedback claim blocked |
| Stress schedule missing for E3 | Stress lineage validator | Mark stress-conditioned embodiment not applicable | E3 diagnostic-only |
| Metric dictionary missing | Metric dictionary validator | Do not export thesis-ready metrics | A13 blocked |
| Matched comparison missing | Matched report validator | Mark comparison diagnostic-only | No comparative claim |
| `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` missing | Manifest completeness check | Block Phase 14/15 reuse | No reproducible embodiment claim |
| Clinical or real-control wording | Layer 0 claim audit | Rewrite/downgrade; add limitation tags | Claim blocked |
| Dashboard recomputes outcomes | Source-table hash check | Invalidate dashboard export | Dashboard non-thesis-ready |

Accepted missingness is allowed only when the mode explicitly justifies it. For example, E0 may have no `EmbodimentStateRecord` and no `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord` if the manifest states no embodiment was executed. E1 may lack physics-state records if it provides command timeline and safety logs. E2/E3 cannot claim physical-simulation outcomes without state/outcome records.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Handoff to Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison

Phase 12 hands Phase 13:

- selected command timelines;
- movement profiles or exported trajectories where generated;
- endpoint-error curves and outcome summaries;
- simulator branch/version metadata;
- command mapping manifest and limitations;
- safety-event logs and blocked-command summaries;
- `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`;
- accepted missingness / diagnostic-only labels;
- explicit warning that OpenSim replay is optional and non-clinical.

Phase 13 may not reinterpret Phase 12 outputs as patient-specific biomechanics, rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle activation, or medical-device safety.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

Phase 12 hands Phase 14:

- dashboard-readable Layer 9 source records;
- safety-event logs;
- command timelines;
- endpoint-error curves;
- reward traces where enabled;
- metric dictionary entries;
- matched comparison reports;
- negative-result notes;
- claim-evidence manifest;
- card source bundle;
- `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`;
- validation logs, missingness logs, and limitation tags.

Phase 14 must read and render these sources without recomputing simulator outcomes, changing command mappings, mutating source records, hiding failed runs, or promoting optional/stretch outputs into core claims.

### 23.3 Handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 12 hands Phase 15 only bounded evidence:

- simulated action-consequence figures;
- A13 tables if matched and validated;
- endpoint-error and command-timeline evidence;
- safety-event and blocked-command summaries;
- stress-conditioned embodiment comparisons where E3 is valid;
- reward-decomposition summaries where enabled and traced;
- negative-result notes;
- claim-evidence manifest;
- explicit limitations and non-claim statements.

Phase 15 must cite Phase 12 as optional/stretch, simulation-only, embodiment-proxy evidence. If Phase 12 remains E0/E1 or diagnostic-only, Phase 15 must state that the core thesis is supported by earlier phases and that embodiment is absent, static-replay-only, or future work.

### 23.4 Handoff to Layer 0 claim-safety review

Layer 0 receives:

- allowed claim text and forbidden claim text;
- limitation tags;
- diagnostic-only labels;
- negative-result notes;
- overclaiming risks;
- final A13 evidence linkage;
- safety-event summaries with explicit non-real-patient-safety warnings;
- OpenSim/MyoSuite optionality statements.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 12 is definition-of-done complete when all of the following conditions are satisfied or explicitly downgraded with accepted missingness:

1. The combined Markdown file preserves Phase 0–11 predecessor content above the Phase 12 section.
2. Phase 12 uses the official identity `Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo` and Layer 9 ownership.
3. Phase 0 inheritance is checked and any schema/path/candidate gaps are marked with consequences.
4. All Phase 1–11 upstream dependencies are consumed only through validated source lineage and not overwritten.
5. E0, E1, E2, E3, E4, or E5 mode is explicitly declared per run.
6. Record intake validates source IDs, schema versions, config hashes, seeds, limitation tags, action tokens, policy-update modes, stress lineage where applicable, and dashboard/export IDs where available.
7. Versioned command mapping exists with mapping ID, mapping type, branch compatibility, fallback behavior, rationale, and known limitation.
8. Readiness safety gate occurs before any simulator/static replay step.
9. E1 static replay mapping/safety timeline is validated before E2 MyoSuite evidence is promoted to thesis-ready status, unless accepted missingness explicitly justifies direct E2 use.
10. Unsupported, unsafe, uncertain, fallback, wait, request-evidence, unresolved combine-evidence, simulator-error, stop-loss, or high-risk states cannot issue aggressive commands.
11. `EmbodimentStateRecord` and `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord` are produced for E2+ executed modes, or accepted missingness is documented for E0/E1.
12. Safety events are logged as `SafetyEventRecord` or a mapped safety-event log storage alias.
13. `Layer9RewardTrace` is produced and validated when reward-enabled embodiment is claimed; otherwise reward feedback is explicitly disabled.
14. Command timelines and endpoint-error curves are produced where required by mode.
15. `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` is complete for every Phase 12 run/mode.
16. A13 evaluation artifacts are produced when A13 is evaluated: Layer 9 `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `MetricDictionaryEntry` set, `NegativeResultNote` where applicable, and `ClaimEvidenceManifest`.
17. Matched-comparison keys preserve dataset, subject, session, trial/window, split, preprocessing, model, calibration, threshold, IHARQ, regime, policy, transition, stress, embodiment mode, command mapping, simulator config, reward config, seed, run ID, metric dictionary, and claim-evidence lineage.
18. Frozen/update evidence separation is enforced for any feedback-enabled embodiment run.
19. Dashboard-readable source records, dashboard-warning inputs, dashboard-generated derived outputs, dashboard-export manifest inputs, and not-dashboard inputs are explicitly separated.
20. Negative results, failed simulator branches, E0/E1 fallback, unsupported mappings, reward imbalance, and unmatched comparisons are preserved rather than hidden.
21. Layer 0 limitation tags are present on all relevant records, manifests, cards/source bundles, evaluation artifacts, `ClaimEvidenceManifest`, and thesis/export packages.
22. Phase 13, Phase 14, Phase 15, and Layer 0 handoff packages are complete.
23. Open issues remain visible and do not support overclaiming.

If any required item fails without accepted missingness, Phase 12 may still be retained as diagnostic-only or optional/stretch evidence, but A13 and C4 embodiment claims must be downgraded or blocked.

# Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 13 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 13` |
| Official phase name | `OpenSim replay or optional comparison` |
| Phase status | `optional_stretch_phase`; non-blocking biomechanical visualization / optional comparison gate |
| Phase type | Stretch / optional / diagnostic-only unless fully traced and bounded |
| Primary layer ownership | Layer 9 — MyoSuite / OpenSim / Static-Replay Embodiment |
| Supporting layers | Layer 0 claim-safety governance; Layer 10 dashboard/card/export/reproducibility; Layer 8 stress lineage where stress-conditioned trajectories are replayed; Layer 7 simulation lineage where transitions/rewards are consumed; Layer 6 policy lineage where policy actions are replayed; Layers 1–5 inherited source and readiness lineage |
| Implementation-order role | After `Phase 12 — MyoSuite embodiment demo`; before `Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards`; feeds optional appendix/demo material to `Phase 15 — Final thesis integration` |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Evidence-production logic only; not an OpenSim installation manual, simulator build guide, musculoskeletal model tutorial, or operational runbook |
| Blocking status | Non-blocking by architecture: thesis validity must remain intact if OpenSim is skipped, infeasible, future-work-only, or diagnostic-only |
| Scientific-output status | Optional visualization, replay manifest, replay logs, screenshots/plots, mapping-limitation source bundle / card input, optional comparison report, and explicit branch-status declaration; not primary validation evidence |
| Thesis role | Supports optional qualitative visualization, bounded comparison, appendix material, and future-work discussion; may strengthen C4 only if lineage, limitations, and Layer 0 claim-safety gates pass |

Phase 13 exists to keep OpenSim useful but controlled. It may replay selected Phase 12 command trajectories, movement profiles, or replay assets and may compare implemented embodiment modes where mapping and matched-comparison validity are explicit. It must not become a hidden core dependency, a policy-training environment, a clinical validation path, a patient-specific biomechanical model, or a source of real rehabilitation or real muscle-control claims.

Phase 13 is not responsible for:

- generating clean public EEG records;
- training decoders;
- fitting calibration models;
- producing IHARQ, RegimeRisk, policy, stress, or MyoSuite source evidence;
- modifying Phase 12 `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, command timelines, endpoint-error curves, safety-event logs, reward traces, or `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` source records;
- recomputing dashboard results;
- turning optional OpenSim visualization into clinical, biomechanical efficacy, patient-safety, medical-device, deployment, rehabilitation, real assistive-control, or real muscle-stimulation evidence.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

Phase 13 is the optional biomechanical visualization and comparison gate for the Layer 9 embodiment branch. Its purpose is to let the project replay selected command trajectories, movement profiles, or exported assets through an OpenSim-style replay/visualization pathway when doing so is feasible and clearly bounded. It also allows a comparative embodiment report when implemented E0–E4 branches can be compared under matched conditions.

The bottleneck controlled by Phase 13 is not classifier accuracy, policy learning, simulator control, or rehabilitation effect. The bottleneck is **optional dependency containment**. OpenSim can add persuasive visuals and useful qualitative inspection, but it can also create false authority if a reader mistakes a replay for subject-specific biomechanical validation. Phase 13 therefore controls:

1. OpenSim installation/runtime burden;
2. model and replay-asset provenance;
3. units and movement-profile assumptions;
4. mapping limitations from proxy EEG intent to replay movement;
5. optional comparison validity;
6. screenshot/plot/replay-log traceability;
7. non-clinical limitation visibility;
8. non-blocking thesis fallback when OpenSim is absent or infeasible.

The architecture-defined exit condition is intentionally two-branched:

- **implemented branch:** a documented optional replay artifact, manifest, logs, plots/screenshots, limitations, and optional comparison report exist and are traceable;
- **skipped branch:** an explicit decision to skip OpenSim is recorded without weakening thesis validity.

Both branches are valid Phase 13 completions if they preserve Layer 0 limitations and downstream handoff clarity.

### 5.3 Explicit boundary rules

Phase 13 must preserve all of the following boundaries:

- OpenSim replay is not the first training environment and not a required policy-training environment.
- Decoder predictions cannot directly call simulator steps.
- Readiness decisions and command mappings from Phase 12 must remain the source of replay behavior.
- Phase 13 may not overwrite Phase 12 `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, command timelines, endpoint-error curves, safety-event logs, reward traces, or `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` source artifacts.
- Optional OpenSim outputs are Layer 9 optional artifacts; Layer 10 displays them only as read-only derived views/cards/exports.
- OpenSim visuals cannot support clinical BCI-FES validation, patient-specific biomechanics, real rehabilitation efficacy, medical-device readiness, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, or deployment readiness.

Because Phase 13 is optional, missing Phase 0 items usually weaken or downgrade the OpenSim branch rather than block the whole thesis. If the branch is skipped, Phase 0 still must support a traceable skip/negative-result/future-work note.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema definitions | Needed for source-record IDs, manifest entries, optional comparison reports, negative-result notes, claim tags, dashboard/export pointers | Partly inherited; OpenSim-specific schema remains partly unresolved | `true` for OpenSim-specific output schema | Implemented branch becomes diagnostic-only if output schema cannot be validated | Use architecture-supported output families; preserve schema gap as open issue |
| Record/interface definitions | Needed for inherited `PolicyActionRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `ReadinessContextRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, `SafetyEventRecord`, `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord` | Inherited from Phase 0/registry/predecessors | `false` for inherited records; `true` for OpenSim-specific replay logs if canonical schema expected | Missing inherited record lineage blocks comparison and may force skip | Consume only validated predecessor artifacts; do not create new canonical records |
| Configuration families | Needed for OpenSim configuration, movement profile config, mapping limitations, simulator branch metadata | Partly inherited under Layer 9 embodiment configs | `true` for exact OpenSim config schema/path | Missing config weakens reproducibility and forces skip or diagnostic-only | Record OpenSim config as branch-specific optional config with manifest hash |
| Mock records / mockable fixtures | Needed for skip branch, malformed manifest, missing limitation text, invalid mapping, missing screenshot/log cases | Inherited conceptually; exact OpenSim mocks not confirmed | `true` for OpenSim-specific mock fixtures | Validator coverage weaker | Add as open issue; require manual validation status in manifest |
| Validation scripts | Needed for lineage, claim tags, dashboard boundary, manifest completeness, metric dictionary, optional comparison matching | Inherited generally | `true` if no OpenSim manifest validator exists | Weakens replay branch; does not block skip branch | Use generic Layer 9 / Layer 10 / Layer 0 validators and mark OpenSim-specific validator gap |
| Run identifier conventions | Needed for replay run, selected input run links, export package | Inherited | `false` | Missing run ID blocks downstream reproducibility | Replay must be skipped or diagnostic-only |
| Config hash conventions | Needed for OpenSim config, movement profile config, mapping config, export config | Inherited | `false` if generic hashing applies; `true` if OpenSim config lacks hash support | Missing hash blocks reproducibility claim | Treat output as diagnostic-only |
| Seed conventions | Needed for deterministic replay settings where applicable | Inherited | `false` for seed convention; `true` if replay is deterministic without seed and lacks a deterministic setting note | Missing seed/determinism note weakens reproducibility | Record deterministic replay setting or accepted not-applicable reason |
| Manifest conventions | Needed for OpenSim output manifest, screenshot/plot manifest, skip manifest, claim-evidence linkage | Inherited generally | `true` for exact OpenSim output manifest schema | Missing manifest blocks Phase 14/15 use | Produce minimal manifest or explicit skip note |
| Repository skeleton expectations | Needed for configs, records, figures, reports, manifests, cards/source bundles | Inherited conceptually | `true` for OpenSim-specific subpath | Storage may be inconsistent | Use existing Layer 9 homes and manifest links; retain path issue |
| Metric dictionary placeholders | Needed only if optional quantitative comparison is attempted | Inherited from framework and prior phases | `false` for placeholder; `true` if Phase 13 metrics lack entries | Quantitative comparison is diagnostic-only | Replay-only qualitative output may mark metrics not applicable |
| Claim-evidence placeholders | Needed for optional claim handoff, skip/future-work note, limitation tags | Inherited with matrix/manifest alias issue | `true` due naming ambiguity | Claim handoff may fragment | Preserve `ClaimEvidenceManifest` with alias caveat |
| Dashboard/export-readiness placeholders | Needed for Phase 14 read-only display | Inherited generally | `true` for OpenSim-specific export IDs | Dashboard display diagnostic-only or skipped | Phase 14 finalizes derived IDs after reading saved manifest |

Phase 13 may proceed only as one of four status modes:

1. `implemented_validated_optional`: OpenSim replay/comparison artifacts exist and pass lineage, limitation, and reproducibility checks;
2. `implemented_diagnostic_only`: artifacts exist but missing schema/path/metric/tool-anchor/matched-comparison elements prevent claim use;
3. `skipped_non_blocking`: OpenSim is omitted with an explicit skip reason, limitation note, and downstream handoff;
4. `future_work_only`: OpenSim is not implemented in the current evidence package and is preserved only as a clearly labeled future-work branch.

| Phase 1 | Dataset/window/split/preprocessing/label-map/source lineage through inherited command trajectories | Must remain immutable and matched | Missing clean lineage makes replay/comparison diagnostic-only |
| Phase 2 | Prediction/model lineage through Phase 12 action context | Must remain source-linked; no recomputation | Missing prediction lineage blocks readiness comparison interpretation |
| Phase 3 | Calibration/uncertainty/selective-threshold lineage where used | Must preserve selected thresholds and split roles | Missing calibration lineage downgrades comparison |
| Phase 4 | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, evidence-quality/decision/fallback/unsafe-event lineage where used | Must preserve canonical action-token semantics and alias caveats | Missing or invalid IHARQ lineage blocks IHARQ-gated variant comparison |
| Phase 5 | `RegimeStateRecord`, `TrustStateRecord`, regime warnings where used | Must preserve temporal ordering and trust-state lineage | Missing regime lineage blocks RegimeRisk-aware comparison |
| Phase 6 | `ReadinessContextRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, deferral/policy/cost context where used | Must preserve decision-time-visible feature boundary | Missing policy context blocks policy-action replay interpretation |
| Phase 7 | `TransitionRecord`, session/episode/rollout/reward/safety lineage where used | Must preserve frozen/update mode and disabled-update audit where applicable | Missing transition/session lineage downgrades sequence-level comparison |
| Phase 8 | `StressProfileRecord`, stress schedules/manifests where stress-conditioned replay is attempted | Must preserve stress IDs, schedules, seeds, and paired clean/stress keys | Missing stress lineage blocks stress-conditioned comparison |
| Phase 9 | StressForge-Lite outputs consumed by Phase 12/13 only as declared stress lineage | Must not collapse stress generation into OpenSim replay | Missing stress branch simply makes stress-conditioned OpenSim not applicable |
| Phase 10 | Contextual-bandit outputs only if optional replay consumes them | Must preserve frozen-policy evaluation vs update-enabled training separation | Missing bandit outputs does not block OpenSim; only removes that variant |
| Phase 11 | RL outputs only if optional replay consumes them | Must preserve held-out/frozen evaluation boundaries and policy update traces | Missing RL outputs does not block OpenSim; only removes that variant |
| Phase 12 | Selected command timelines, movement profiles/exported trajectories, endpoint-error curves, outcome summaries, simulator metadata, command mapping manifest, safety logs, limitations, `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`, missingness/diagnostic labels | Primary hard predecessor for attempted OpenSim replay/comparison | If Phase 12 has no compatible assets, Phase 13 completes as skipped or future-work-only |

### 8.2 Cross-phase issue entries

**Cross-phase issue:** Phase 13 consumes Phase 12 assets that may not exist if Phase 12 completed at E0/E1 or skipped physical simulation.  
**Affected prior phase:** Phase 12.  
**Affected current phase:** Phase 13.  
**Affected artifact/record/interface:** selected command timelines, movement profiles/exported trajectories, `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest`, simulator metadata.  
**Risk:** OpenSim replay could be attempted without valid source assets.  
**Required repair:** Confirm asset existence, accepted missingness, or skip decision.  
**Temporary handling:** Mark Phase 13 `skipped_non_blocking` or `future_work_only` if assets are unavailable.

**Cross-phase issue:** Optional comparison may require metric dictionary and matched-comparison keys not finalized for OpenSim-specific outputs.  
**Affected prior phase:** Phase 0, Phase 12, and evaluation framework artifacts.  
**Affected current phase:** Phase 13.  
**Affected artifact/record/interface:** `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, optional comparison report, claim-evidence entry.  
**Risk:** Quantitative comparison could appear stronger than supported.  
**Required repair:** Validate metric definitions and matched keys before claim use.  
**Temporary handling:** Mark comparison diagnostic-only; replay-only visualization can remain qualitative.

**Cross-phase issue:** Policy outputs from Phases 10–11 may have update-enabled traces that must not be mixed with frozen evaluation.  
**Affected prior phase:** Phase 10 / Phase 11.  
**Affected current phase:** Phase 13.  
**Affected artifact/record/interface:** `PolicyActionRecord`, `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit, reward/config lineage.  
**Risk:** Optional replay could merge training/adaptation curves with held-out evaluation.  
**Required repair:** Separate update-enabled and frozen-policy replay outputs.  
**Temporary handling:** Use only frozen-policy actions for claim-facing replay; update-enabled replay remains diagnostic-only.
