### 9.2 Optional input contract for comparison branch

Optional comparison may consume matched outputs from implemented E0–E4 modes. It must declare which modes are present and which are absent:

- E0 no embodiment;
- E1 static replay;
- E2 MyoSuite simple task;
- E3 stress-conditioned MyoSuite;
- E4 OpenSim replay/visualization;
- E5 comparative embodiment report.

If E4 is the only branch attempted, Phase 13 may produce qualitative replay evidence without E5 quantitative comparison. If E5 is attempted, missing E0–E3/E4 branch outputs must be represented as accepted missingness rather than silently dropped.

### 9.3 Inputs explicitly not allowed

Phase 13 must not use:

- test-set correctness or future reward fields to choose replay actions;
- unvalidated or manually edited trajectories with no source record IDs;
- OpenSim visuals as a substitute for Phase 12 embodiment outcomes;
- dashboard-filtered subsets as source evidence;
- simulator outputs to change EEG labels, decoder predictions, calibration thresholds, IHARQ decisions, RegimeRisk labels, policy training data, or StressForge profiles;
- patient-specific anatomical parameters unless explicitly documented as future-work-only and outside thesis claims.

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 13 evidence production follows this bounded logic chain:

```text
validated Phase 12 command trajectory / movement profile / replay asset
→ intake validation against source IDs, mapping ID, safety-gate status, manifest, and limitation tags
→ OpenSim branch decision: attempt replay, attempt comparison, skip, or future-work-only
→ if attempted: validate OpenSim config, model/replay asset, units, deterministic setting/seed, and tool/version/license note where available
→ replay selected command timelines or simplified movement profiles
→ export output manifest, screenshots/plots, replay logs, and mapping limitation source bundle
→ if comparison is valid: compare only matched implemented E0–E4 modes with metric dictionary entries and missingness notes
→ attach Layer 0 limitation tags and diagnostic-only labels
→ hand saved outputs to Phase 14 as read-only dashboard/card/export inputs and to Phase 15 only as optional appendix/demo/future-work material
```

This is not an operational procedure. It intentionally avoids exact OpenSim commands, code-level adapter implementations, environment setup steps, and simulator debugging workflows. Those belong to a future implementation build book or execution playbook.

### 12.1 Branch logic

| Branch | Evidence action | Required output | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt_replay_validated` | Replay selected command trajectories or movement profiles and log results | OpenSim output manifest, replay logs, screenshots/plots, limitation source bundle | Optional visualization evidence only |
| `attempt_replay_diagnostic` | Replay exists but missing schema/path/metric/tool-anchor/matched lineage | Same artifacts plus diagnostic-only note | Diagnostic-only / appendix only |
| `attempt_comparison_validated` | Compare implemented E0–E4 modes where matched keys and metrics validate | Optional comparison report, `MatchedComparisonReport`, metric entries, negative-result notes as needed | Optional bounded comparison |
| `attempt_comparison_diagnostic` | Comparison attempted with incomplete matching or metrics | Diagnostic comparison report and downgrade note | Diagnostic-only |
| `skip_opensim_non_blocking` | OpenSim omitted because dependency unavailable, unnecessary, or future-work-only | Skip/future-work note, limitation statement, handoff entry | Thesis remains valid without Phase 13 empirical artifacts |

### 12.2 Clean-source immutability

OpenSim replay cannot repair upstream evidence. If a trajectory looks implausible, Phase 13 records a limitation or negative result. It must not edit the original command timeline, safety-event log, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, policy action, stress schedule, threshold, prediction, label, or dashboard source package. Any transformed trajectory or replay asset must be a derived replay artifact with a source pointer, not a replacement source.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Gate A — Optional-branch declaration

Before any Phase 13 output is interpreted, the branch status must be declared as one of:

- `implemented_validated_optional`;
- `implemented_diagnostic_only`;
- `skipped_non_blocking`;
- `future_work_only`.

Failure to declare branch status blocks Phase 14/15 use.

The branch-status declaration must also state whether OpenSim is actively used, documentation-only/contextual, omitted, or attempted but failed. This avoids treating an OpenSim citation, future-work note, or screenshot as if it were a validated replay artifact.

### 13.2 Gate B — Input lineage and Phase 12 handoff validation

The gate passes only if selected command timelines, movement profiles/replay assets, command mapping manifest, safety-gate status, simulator metadata, limitation text, and `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` links are present or explicitly marked not applicable with accepted missingness. Missing or invalid lineage downgrades the branch to diagnostic-only or skipped.

### 13.3 Gate C — OpenSim configuration and reproducibility validation

If OpenSim is attempted, the output manifest must record OpenSim configuration, model/replay asset pointer, units or movement-profile assumptions, seed or deterministic replay setting where applicable, config hash, simulator/tool version or unresolved tool-anchor note, and license/access boundary where available. Missing core reproducibility fields prevents thesis-ready optional replay use.

### 13.4 Gate D — Claim-safety validation

Every output must include non-clinical and non-biomechanical-efficacy limitation language. Layer 0 blocks any output or thesis wording that implies:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- patient-specific biomechanical validation;
- real assistive-control safety;
- deployment readiness.

### 13.5 Gate E — Optional comparison validity

If an optional comparison report is produced, it must preserve matched-comparison keys, metric dictionary entries, accepted missingness notes, and negative-result notes. It must identify which E0–E4 modes are implemented, skipped, diagnostic-only, or absent. Unmatched comparison remains diagnostic-only.

### 13.6 Exit condition

Phase 13 exits successfully when either:

1. a documented optional replay/comparison package exists with manifest, replay logs, screenshots/plots if generated, limitations, validation status, claim-safety tags, dashboard/export pointers, and handoff entries; or
2. an explicit skip/future-work note states why OpenSim was not used and confirms that thesis validity is preserved through prior phases and Phase 12 static replay/MyoSuite outcomes where available.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

Matched comparison is required only if Phase 13 produces an optional comparison report or A13 E5 comparative entries. Qualitative replay-only visualization may mark comparison fields not applicable with reason, but it still must preserve source lineage.

| Key family | Required keys where applicable | Phase 13 rule | Missing-key consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public-data/source lineage | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `split_role`, `preprocessing_id`, `label_map_id`, artifact flags | Must be inherited from Phase 1 through Phase 12 source links | Comparison diagnostic-only |
| Decoder/calibration lineage | `model_id`, prediction run ID, calibration ID, threshold registry ID, uncertainty/selective decision status | Must remain read-only | Variant comparison incomplete |
| IHARQ/RegimeRisk lineage | IHARQ decision ID, evidence-quality/fallback/unsafe-event links, regime/trust state IDs, warning status | Required for IHARQ-gated and RegimeRisk-aware variants | That variant excluded or diagnostic-only |
| Policy lineage | `policy_id`, `PolicyActionRecord` ID, cost/reward config ID, deferral route, visible-feature list | Required for adaptive/bandit/RL replay variants | Policy variant diagnostic-only |
| Frozen/update lineage | `PolicyUpdateTrace` ID where update-enabled; disabled-update audit for frozen evaluation | Required if replay consumes Phase 10/11 outputs | Update-enabled and frozen curves separated; missing trace blocks claim use |
| Simulation lineage | transition/session/episode/rollout IDs, environment diagnostic status, reward trace ID where used | Required for sequence-level comparison | Replay may remain qualitative only |
| Stress lineage | `stress_profile_id`, stress schedule ID, stress seed, clean/stress pairing key | Required for stress-conditioned OpenSim comparison | Stress comparison diagnostic-only |
| Embodiment lineage | `embodiment_mode_id`, E0–E5 mode, command mapping ID/hash, safety-rule ID, simulator branch, simulator config hash, endpoint/outcome IDs | Required for all replay/comparison outputs | A13/E5 incomplete |
| OpenSim lineage | OpenSim config ID/hash, model/replay asset ID, movement-profile config, units, deterministic setting/seed, tool/version/license note where available | Required for implemented OpenSim branch | Implemented branch diagnostic-only if absent |
| Evaluation lineage | metric dictionary entry IDs, matched comparison report ID, negative-result note ID, claim-evidence entry ID, dashboard/export ID | Required for thesis-facing comparison | Claim/evaluation handoff blocked |

Phase 13 must report matched-cost, matched-delay, matched-stress, matched-reward, and matched-mode comparisons separately where those metrics are attempted. A replay that looks persuasive in a screenshot but lacks matched lineage is visualization-only, not quantitative evidence.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

A0–A13 remain evaluation-use metadata only. Phase 13 may strengthen A13 by providing optional E4 OpenSim replay and E5 comparative embodiment material, but A13 does not own Phase 13 artifacts.

| Evaluation / ablation context | Phase 13 relationship | Explicit evaluation artifacts | Claim status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A13 — Layer 9 MyoSuite/OpenSim/static-replay embodiment demo | Phase 13 may add optional OpenSim E4 replay and E5 comparative report | OpenSim output manifest, replay logs, screenshots/plots, optional comparison report, matched comparison report, metric dictionary entries, negative-result notes, claim-evidence entry | Optional / bounded / simulation-proxy-only |
| E4 OpenSim replay/visualization | Direct Phase 13 branch | Replay artifact package and mapping limitation source bundle | Visualization / plausibility only |
| E5 comparative embodiment report | Conditional Phase 13 branch | Matched outputs from implemented E0–E4 modes, A13 table, limitations, reproducibility package | Diagnostic-only unless fully matched/validated |
| A12 stress tests | Only relevant if stress-conditioned trajectories from Phase 8/9/12 are replayed | Stress profile/schedule IDs, paired clean/stress keys, stress-conditioned comparison notes | Stress-conditioned, simulation-only; not pathology evidence |
| A10/A11 policy variants | Only relevant if contextual-bandit/RL policy outputs are replayed | Frozen/update separated replay outputs and policy-update/disabled-update audit lineage | Diagnostic-only if update/frozen separation missing |

### 15.1 Explicit evaluation artifacts required when comparison is attempted

If Phase 13 produces a quantitative or semi-quantitative comparison, it must include or prepare:

- `MetricDictionaryEntry` entries for each comparison metric;
- `MatchedComparisonReport` or equivalent matched comparison table linked to implemented E0–E4 modes;
- `NegativeResultNote` entries for failed, unstable, missing, unmatched, or diagnostic branches;
- claim-evidence entry / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` linkage with matrix/manifest alias caveat preserved;
- dashboard/export source bundle for Phase 14;
- Layer 0 limitation and diagnostic-only tags.

If these artifacts are absent, the comparison may remain an exploratory appendix item only.

## 16. Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Obligations

### 16.1 Dashboard-readable source records and artifacts

Layer 10 may read the following saved Phase 13 materials:

- OpenSim output manifest;
- replay logs;
- screenshots or plots with manifest pointers;
- optional comparison report;
- mapping limitation card/source bundle;
- skip/future-work note;
- negative-result notes;
- metric dictionary entries where comparison is attempted;
- claim-evidence entry / manifest link;
- `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` linkage;
- inherited Phase 12 command timelines, movement profiles, endpoint-error curves, simulator metadata, and limitation tags.

### 16.2 Dashboard-warning inputs

Layer 10 must surface warnings for:

- OpenSim optional / non-blocking status;
- `future_work_only` or `skipped_non_blocking` branch status;
- diagnostic-only replay or comparison;
- missing OpenSim tool/version/license/access anchor;
- missing manifest/config hash/seed/deterministic setting;
- incomplete matched-comparison keys;
- missing metric dictionary entries;
- missing or ambiguous claim-evidence matrix/manifest link;
- strict non-clinical/non-biomechanical-efficacy limitations.

### 16.3 Dashboard-generated derived outputs

Layer 10 may generate derived views, cards, warning panels, export manifests, and reproducibility packages from saved Phase 13 artifacts. It must not recompute replay, retune mappings, repair missing source lineage, edit screenshots/plots to hide failures, remove diagnostic-only labels, hide skip notes, or promote optional OpenSim outputs into core thesis claims.

### 16.4 Dashboard-export manifest inputs

The Phase 13 handoff to Phase 14 must include:

- source artifact IDs and file pointers;
- `run_id`, `config_hash`, `schema_version`, `phase_id`, `producer_module`, validation status;
- source Phase 12 manifest and command mapping ID;
- OpenSim config/tool-anchor notes where attempted;
- limitation tags and Layer 0 review status;
- metric dictionary and matched-comparison IDs where applicable;
- negative-result and skip/future-work note IDs where applicable.

### 16.5 Not-dashboard inputs

OpenSim installation logs, local environment debugging, raw simulator cache files, manually generated intermediate visualizations, and unvalidated model assets are not dashboard inputs unless they are explicitly included in a manifest with source IDs, configuration hashes, validation status, and limitation tags. Otherwise, they remain implementation-local material outside thesis evidence.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 13 may support only bounded statements such as:

- selected readiness-gated command trajectories can be replayed or visualized through an OpenSim-style optional branch;
- OpenSim replay provides qualitative or plausibility-oriented visualization under declared proxy mappings;
- optional comparison across implemented embodiment modes is possible when matched lineage and metric definitions are present;
- OpenSim was skipped or left as future work without invalidating the core thesis;
- Layer 10 can display optional replay artifacts with traceable manifests and visible limitations.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 13 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- patient-specific OpenSim biomechanical validation;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real deployment readiness;
- direct EEG-to-muscle activation;
- proof that a replayed trajectory is clinically safe or therapeutically effective.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

All implemented or skipped Phase 13 outputs must carry the strictest applicable subset of:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based
evaluation_only
simulation_only
embodiment_proxy_only
MyoSuite_OpenSim_demo_only
diagnostic_only
future_work_only
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
```

If stress-conditioned trajectories are replayed, add `stress_conditioned`. If the output is a skipped/future-work branch, add `future_work_only`. If matched comparison or reproducibility is incomplete, add `diagnostic_only`.

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

Layer 0 must downgrade or block Phase 13 if:

- any figure, card, report, or thesis paragraph implies clinical or biomechanical efficacy;
- mapping limitations are absent;
- screenshots/plots lack source manifest links;
- OpenSim version/config/replay asset provenance is missing;
- optional comparison lacks matched-comparison keys or metric dictionary entries;
- skipped OpenSim is hidden rather than documented;
- dashboard or final thesis text treats Phase 13 as required evidence rather than optional/stretch evidence.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 remain claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels, not implementation phases, ablation IDs, artifact owners, or section substitutes.

| Capability tier | Phase 13 effect | Governance rule |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | No direct dependency | Phase 13 absence cannot weaken core public-data/repository/schema readiness |
| C1 | No direct dependency | OpenSim replay cannot compensate for missing decoder/calibration/IHARQ evidence |
| C2 | No direct dependency | OpenSim replay cannot compensate for missing RegimeRisk/adaptive-policy evidence |
| C3 | No direct dependency | OpenSim replay cannot compensate for missing simulation/stress/bandit/RL evidence |
| C4 | Optional strengthening only | Implemented and validated Phase 13 can add optional OpenSim appendix/demo material; skipped Phase 13 keeps C4 bounded to available Phase 12/static/MyoSuite/stress embodiment evidence where valid |

Phase 13 must never become the reason a lower-tier thesis-valid result is delayed. If Phase 13 is skipped, the final thesis should say OpenSim replay was non-blocking and future-work-only, not that the thesis failed.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

Phase 13 treats negative results as evidence-management outputs, not as hidden failures.

| Condition | Required handling | Claim effect |
|---|---|---|
| OpenSim not installed or unavailable | Produce skip/future-work note with non-blocking status | No impact on core thesis; optional branch absent |
| OpenSim model/replay asset unavailable | Record accepted missingness or future-work note | Replay branch skipped or diagnostic-only |
| Mapping from proxy intent to replay movement invalid | Block replay or label qualitative diagnostic-only; preserve mapping limitation | No OpenSim comparison claim |
| Replay produces poor, unstable, or visually unhelpful output | Keep replay logs/screenshots if useful, add `NegativeResultNote` | Negative result / appendix only |
| Screenshots/plots require manual edits to look presentable | Do not use as evidence unless raw manifest-linked version is preserved | Edited visual cannot be source evidence |
| Quantitative comparison lacks matched keys | Produce diagnostic-only comparison note | No thesis-ready comparison |
| Metric dictionary missing | Mark comparison diagnostic-only | Quantitative claim blocked |
| OpenSim skipped because Phase 12 E0/E1 is sufficient | Record skip note | Thesis remains valid with lower-mode embodiment/future-work boundary |

Baseline sufficiency is inherited from prior phases. Phase 13 cannot make earlier baseline evidence sufficient if Phase 0–12 validation failed. Conversely, failure or absence of OpenSim cannot invalidate earlier thesis-ready evidence because Phase 13 is optional.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

### 20.1 Failure taxonomy

Phase 13 failure modes include:

- OpenSim installation/runtime failure;
- missing model/replay asset;
- missing or inconsistent units;
- missing deterministic setting or seed where needed;
- invalid movement profile;
- invalid command mapping for replay branch;
- missing Phase 12 trajectory or manifest;
- missing safety-event lineage;
- unstable or non-reproducible replay;
- missing screenshot/plot/replay-log manifest;
- incomplete metric dictionary;
- unmatched comparison keys;
- dashboard/card overclaiming;
- unsupported clinical or biomechanical wording.

### 20.2 Missingness rules

| Missing item | Phase 13 handling |
|---|---|
| No Phase 12 compatible command trajectory | Complete Phase 13 as `skipped_non_blocking` or `future_work_only` |
| No OpenSim config or installation | Complete Phase 13 as skipped/future-work-only; preserve reason |
| No mapping limitation text | Block export/thesis use until repaired |
| No output manifest | Implemented branch diagnostic-only and not dashboard-ready |
| No screenshot/plot | Replay logs/manifest may still be valid if visualization was not generated; note accepted missingness |
| No metric dictionary | Comparison diagnostic-only; replay-only visualization may continue |
| No matched comparison | E5 unavailable; E4 replay may remain qualitative |
| No Layer 0 review | No thesis-facing output allowed |
| No Layer 10 export linkage | Output may exist but is not dashboard/export ready |

### 20.3 Diagnostic-only rules

Phase 13 must mark outputs diagnostic-only when:

- source IDs or config hashes are missing;
- OpenSim version/tool/license/access anchors are missing and reproducibility is claimed;
- mapping assumptions are unresolved;
- comparison is unmatched;
- metric dictionary entries are incomplete;
- frozen/update evidence is mixed;
- stress-conditioned replay lacks paired clean/stress lineage;
- visual outputs are manually curated without raw manifest linkage;
- claim-safety tags or limitation warnings are absent.

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

Phase 13 should use the existing Layer 9 embodiment, figures, reports, cards/source-bundle, metrics, negative-result, claim-evidence, and manifest homes established by the architecture and predecessor phases. Exact OpenSim-specific concrete subpaths remain a registry/path confirmation issue and must not be invented as canonical.

| Storage family | Phase 13 expectation | Path status |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 9 embodiment configs | Store or link OpenSim replay config, movement profile config, branch settings, mapping references, safety/limitation references | Existing Layer 9 config home is architecture-supported; OpenSim-specific file name/path remains confirmable |
| Records / logs | Store replay logs and source manifest links without overwriting Phase 12 source records | Existing embodiment record/log concept supported; OpenSim log schema/path requires confirmation |
| Figures / screenshots / plots | Store manifest-linked screenshots/plots if generated | Architecture supports embodiment figures; exact OpenSim subpath requires confirmation |
| Reports / optional comparison | Store optional comparison report and matched-comparison artifacts where attempted | Supported as report family; exact path confirmable |
| Cards/source bundles | Store mapping limitation card/source bundle for Layer 10 rendering | Layer 10 renders final card; Phase 13 stores source bundle |
| Metrics | Store metric dictionary entries if quantitative comparison attempted | Metric dictionary schema/path remains open under registry issue |
| Negative results | Store skip/future-work/negative-result notes | Supported by framework; exact path follows predecessor convention |
| Claim evidence | Store claim-evidence entry/manifest link with matrix/manifest alias caveat | Naming issue preserved |
| Reproducibility manifest | Store OpenSim output manifest and export package pointers | Required for Phase 14/15 use |

Every stored Phase 13 output must include, where applicable:

```text
source_record_ids
run_id
config_hash
seed or deterministic_replay_setting
schema_version
producer_module
phase_id
ablation_id where applicable
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id

policy_id

opensim_config_id or equivalent optional branch identifier
```

If any field is not applicable, the manifest must state the reason. If any required field is missing, the output must be downgraded or skipped.

Its safety value is preventing OpenSim from becoming a hidden dependency or unsupported biomechanical/clinical claim.

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Handoff to Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

Phase 13 hands Phase 14 either an implemented optional replay/comparison source bundle or a skip/future-work note.

If implemented, the handoff includes:

- OpenSim output manifest;
- screenshots/plots with source manifest pointers;
- replay logs;
- optional comparison report where produced;
- metric dictionary entries and matched-comparison report where comparison is attempted;
- mapping limitation card/source bundle;
- Layer 0 limitation tags and review status;
- negative-result notes;
- `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` link;
- dashboard warning requirements.

If skipped, the handoff includes:

- skip/future-work note;
- reason for non-use;
- confirmation that Phase 13 is non-blocking;
- limitation tags;
- statement that no OpenSim dashboard evidence should be displayed except the skip/future-work status.

Phase 14 must not recompute OpenSim replay, fix missing artifacts silently, hide failed/skipped status, erase diagnostic-only labels, or present optional OpenSim material as core thesis evidence.

### 23.2 Handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 13 hands Phase 15 only bounded material:

- optional visualization or screenshots/plots;
- optional replay logs or manifest tables;
- optional comparison report if matched and validated;
- negative-result or skip/future-work notes;
- limitation text for every figure/table/paragraph;
- claim-evidence entry with matrix/manifest alias caveat preserved.

Phase 15 may use Phase 13 as appendix/demo/future-work material. It must not use Phase 13 to claim biomechanical efficacy, clinical validation, patient safety, rehabilitation effect, medical-device readiness, real muscle stimulation control, or deployment readiness.

### 23.3 Handoff to Layer 0 claim-safety review

Layer 0 receives:

- all intended Phase 13 claim wording;
- mapping limitations;
- OpenSim optionality statement;
- diagnostic-only labels;
- future-work labels;
- negative-result notes;
- forbidden-claim audit checklist;
- figure/card/report/export warning coverage.

Layer 0 must block any unsupported wording before Phase 14 export or Phase 15 thesis integration.

### 23.4 Handoff to repository/reproducibility package

The reproducibility package receives:

- source artifact IDs;
- OpenSim config hash and tool-anchor note where attempted;
- manifest pointers;
- replay log hashes where available;
- screenshot/plot manifest entries;
- skip/future-work reason where skipped;
- validation reports;
- limitation and claim-safety tags.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 13 is definition-of-done complete when all of the following are satisfied or explicitly marked not applicable with accepted missingness:

1. The combined Markdown file preserves Phase 0–12 predecessor content above the Phase 13 section.
2. The section uses the official identity `Phase 13 — OpenSim replay or optional comparison`.
3. Phase 13 is explicitly marked optional and non-blocking.
4. Phase 0 inheritance is checked, including schemas, configs, validators, run IDs, config hashes, seeds/deterministic replay settings, manifests, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, and dashboard/export placeholders.
5. Phase 12 handoff assets are validated or an explicit skip/future-work note is produced.
6. Branch status is declared as `implemented_validated_optional`, `implemented_diagnostic_only`, `skipped_non_blocking`, or `future_work_only`.
7. If OpenSim is attempted, the output manifest records source command timeline IDs, replay asset/profile IDs, OpenSim config hash, model/replay asset pointer, units/assumptions, seed or deterministic setting, tool/version/license note where available, validation status, and limitation tags.
8. If screenshots or plots are generated, they are linked to the output manifest and carry non-clinical/non-biomechanical-efficacy warnings.
9. Replay logs are saved and linked to source inputs when replay is attempted.
10. Mapping limitation text is attached to every replay output, card/source bundle, figure, and thesis/export handoff.
11. Optional comparison reports are produced only when implemented E0–E4 mode outputs are matched or missingness is explicitly accepted.
12. `MetricDictionaryEntry` entries exist for every quantitative comparison metric, or the comparison is diagnostic-only.
13. `MatchedComparisonReport` or equivalent matched table exists for E5 comparison, or E5 is marked not applicable / diagnostic-only.
14. `NegativeResultNote` entries exist for failed replay, unstable output, missing OpenSim dependency, missing metrics, unmatched comparison, or skipped OpenSim where relevant.
15. Claim-evidence entry / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` linkage exists for any Phase 13 thesis-facing output, with matrix/manifest alias caveat preserved.
16. Layer 10 dashboard-readable source artifacts, dashboard-warning inputs, dashboard-generated derived outputs, dashboard-export manifest inputs, and not-dashboard inputs are separated.
17. Layer 10 receives only saved artifacts and may not recompute, retune, repair, hide, or promote optional outputs.
18. Layer 0 limitation tags are present and strictest-boundary inheritance is enforced.
19. All clinical, patient-safety, medical-device, rehabilitation, real muscle-control, real assistive-control, patient-specific biomechanical validation, and deployment claims are blocked.
20. Frozen-policy and update-enabled policy outputs are separated if Phase 10/11 policy actions are replayed.
21. Stress-conditioned replay uses valid stress profile/schedule lineage and paired clean/stress keys where comparison is claimed.
22. Repository/storage expectations are manifest-linked, and unresolved OpenSim-specific paths remain open rather than invented.
23. Phase 14, Phase 15, and Layer 0 handoff packages are complete.
24. Open issues remain visible and do not support overclaiming.

If OpenSim is not implemented, Phase 13 is still complete when a non-blocking skip/future-work note, limitation tags, and downstream handoff are present. If OpenSim is implemented but any required lineage, limitation, metric, manifest, or claim-safety gate fails, Phase 13 remains `implemented_diagnostic_only` and may not support thesis-facing optional comparison claims.

# Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 14 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 14` |
| Official phase name | `Dashboard and cards` |
| Phase status | Layer 10 read/export/dashboard/card/reproducibility phase; thesis-facing derived-output phase |
| Primary layer ownership | Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer |
| Supporting layers | Layers 0–9 as source-record, warning, limitation, and evidence producers; Layer 0 as claim-safety reviewer |
| Implementation-order role | Final observability and reproducibility gate before `Phase 15 — Final thesis integration` |
| Evidence-plan boundary | Describes record-only dashboard/card/export evidence-production logic; not an implementation playbook, UI ticket list, exact function design, or command-run guide |
| Scientific-output status | Produces derived dashboard metrics, dashboard views, cards, figures, tables, export indexes, manifests, warning surfaces, and reproducibility packages from saved records only |
| Upstream dependency mode | Reads validated outputs from Phases 0–13; missing upstream branches remain visible as incomplete, diagnostic-only, skipped, or future-work-only rather than hidden |
| Downstream consumer | `Phase 15 — Final thesis integration`; Layer 0 claim-safety review; thesis figures/tables/cards appendix; reproducibility appendix; examiner/supervisor defense demo |
| Optionality | The fully interactive dashboard is optional; static record-derived cards, figures, tables, and manifests are sufficient fallback if complete and traceable |
| Claim boundary | Supports inspectability, traceability, reproducibility, and warning visibility only; does not create new empirical evidence or stronger scientific/clinical claims |

Phase 14 is the official dashboard/card/export phase. Its job is to convert already-produced, validated records into inspectable thesis artifacts without becoming a hidden second experiment engine. It may read, validate, summarize, visualize, warn, card, export, and package saved records. It must not silently recompute upstream logic, retune thresholds, repair missing records, mutate policies, re-run stress/embodiment/simulation logic, erase diagnostic-only labels, hide negative results, or promote optional Stretch C outputs into core claims.

The previous Phase 0–13 sections are preserved above this section in the combined Markdown file. Phase 14 appends the Layer 10 observability and reproducibility gate without modifying the semantic ownership or evidence outputs of those predecessor phases.

| Phase 2 | Baseline decoders | Reads prediction records, model registry records, baseline metrics, low-calibration curves, subject profiles, ensemble-control records, model/benchmark cards, and readiness reports |
| Phase 3 | Calibration and uncertainty | Reads calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, threshold registry, reliability audit, leakage/split-integrity, high-confidence-wrong, matched-operating-point, reliability-card, and negative-result outputs |
| Phase 4 | IHARQ-lite evidence verification | Reads evidence-quality, IHARQ decision, combined evidence, fallback, unsafe-event, IHARQ trace, IHARQ ablation, and evaluation outputs |
| Phase 5 | RegimeRisk temporal trust | Reads regime/trust/timeline/temporal-warning records, RegimeRisk evaluation outputs, cards/source bundles, and limitation labels |
| Phase 6 | Evidence-quality estimator and supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Reads learned evidence-quality variants, readiness-context records, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ policy/action records, pseudo-label limitation notes, and evaluation artifacts |
| Phase 7 | Learning-to-defer | Reads deferral records, deferral-policy actions, cost/coverage outputs, target-construction caveats, and diagnostic-only conditions |
| Phase 8 | Simulated closed-loop readiness | Reads transition, closed-loop session, episode summary, policy rollout, reward trace, environment diagnostic, safety-event, disabled-update audit, and simulation-only outputs |
| Phase 9 | StressForge-Lite | Reads stress profiles, stress schedules, stress-run manifests, stress validity reports, stress metrics, stress cards/source bundles, and matched stress lineage |
| Phase 10 | Contextual bandit | Reads contextual-bandit policy artifacts, policy-update traces, disabled-update audits, training/adaptation curves, frozen-evaluation outputs, reward/regret metrics, and diagnostic labels |
| Phase 11 | Reinforcement-learning policy | Reads RL policy/update/rollout/evaluation artifacts, safety/illegal-action warnings, trace completeness outputs, and frozen/update separation artifacts |
| Phase 12 | MyoSuite embodiment demo | Reads Layer 9 embodiment state/outcome, command timelines, endpoint-error curves, safety-event logs, reward traces where enabled, demo manifests, embodiment-card source bundles, and embodiment limitation tags |
| Phase 13 | OpenSim replay or optional comparison | Reads OpenSim output manifests, replay logs, screenshots/plots, optional comparison reports, mapping-limitation source bundles, skip/future-work notes, and optional branch-status declarations |

### 2.5 Source-grounding and anti-invention notes

No new official phase, layer, ablation ID, capability tier, canonical record, canonical interface, repository path, metric, dashboard output category, or claim class is introduced by this section. Where a term is unresolved in the registry, Phase 14 preserves the issue as an open issue and uses diagnostic-only or not-thesis-ready handling rather than silently resolving it. A0–A13 remain evaluation-use metadata only. C0–C4 remain claim-maturity summaries and thesis-valid stopping-point labels only. Layer 10 owns dashboard/card/export/reproducibility-derived artifacts, not upstream empirical source records. Layer 0 owns claim-safety review, not empirical evidence.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 14 is the observability, cards, export, and reproducibility gate. It turns the validated records produced by Phases 0–13 into traceable dashboard views, static figures, thesis tables, cards, warning surfaces, manifests, and export packages. Its purpose is not to improve model performance or create new scientific evidence; its purpose is to make existing evidence inspectable, reproducible, claim-safe, and ready for Phase 15 thesis integration.

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 14 controls the risk that the Stretch C system becomes an impressive but untraceable set of outputs. It prevents:

- cosmetic dashboards with no source-record lineage;
- dashboard pages that recompute hidden experimental logic;
- figures that disagree with saved records or thesis tables;
- cards that omit limitations, warnings, or reproduction fields;
- policy-update traces hidden behind summary curves;
- stress or embodiment outputs shown without proxy/simulation-only warnings;
- optional Phase 13 OpenSim outputs treated as required core evidence;
- negative results, missing records, diagnostic-only labels, or unresolved registry issues being hidden;
- A0–A13 ablation views being displayed without matched-comparison and metric-dictionary lineage;
- final thesis claims being presented without claim-evidence and limitation linkage.

### 4.3 Evidence role

Phase 14 produces derived thesis-facing artifacts. Those artifacts are valid only because they are linked to upstream source records, configurations, seeds, schema versions, validation reports, metric dictionary entries, matched-comparison reports, negative-result notes, claim-evidence entries, limitation tags, warning flags, and artifact manifests. Dashboard views, cards, figures, and tables are not primary empirical evidence by themselves.

### 4.4 Minimum successful Phase 14

The minimum successful Phase 14 can be static rather than interactive. A full web dashboard is not required if Phase 14 produces a complete static export package with:

- record-derived dashboard metrics;
- dashboard view metadata;
- required cards and limitation cards;
- thesis figures/tables with source lineage;
- manifest-linked exports;
- warning and missingness visibility;
- reproducibility manifest;
- claim-evidence links;
- diagnostic-only and negative-result indexes.

## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

### 5.1 Layer participation

| Layer | Phase 14 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Provides claim-safety labels, limitation tags, forbidden-claim rules, diagnostic-only labels, claim-evidence checks, warning requirements, and final dashboard/card/export review | Layer 0 audits claim wording and limitation coverage; it does not produce empirical source evidence or dashboard metrics |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Provides dataset/protocol/window/split/preprocessing/label/artifact records, validation reports, manifests, source cards, and ablation-readiness fixture | Layer 1 source records remain immutable clean records; Phase 14 reads and displays them |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Provides prediction/model/baseline/low-calibration/subject-profile/ordinary-ensemble/baseline-sufficiency evidence | Layer 2 owns decoder evidence; Phase 14 renders and exports it |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Provides calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, threshold registry, reliability, high-confidence-wrong, leakage, and matched-operating-point evidence | Layer 3 owns calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction evidence; Phase 14 displays and warns |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Provides IHARQ decision, evidence-quality, combined evidence, fallback, unsafe-event, trace, ablation, and local evaluation records | Layer 4 owns IHARQ evidence-verification records; Phase 14 exposes decision flow and warning lineage |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Provides regime/trust/timeline/temporal-warning records and RegimeRisk evaluation outputs | Layer 5 owns temporal-trust records; Phase 14 displays timelines and diagnostic warnings |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Provides readiness contexts, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ outputs, evidence-quality variants, policy actions, learned policies, and policy/claim limitation outputs | Layer 6 owns readiness-policy and policy-action evidence; Phase 14 displays without updating policies |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Provides transition, session, episode, rollout, reward, environment diagnostic, safety-event, and disabled-update audit records | Layer 7 owns simulation records; Phase 14 displays simulation-only outputs and warnings |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Provides stress profiles, schedules, stress-run manifests, stress validity reports, stress metrics, and stress-card source bundles | Layer 8 owns stress records; Phase 14 displays stress-conditioned robustness without redefining stress logic |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite/OpenSim/Static-Replay Embodiment | Provides embodiment states/outcomes, endpoint-error curves, command timelines, safety-event logs, reward traces where enabled, demo manifests, Phase 13 optional outputs or skip notes | Layer 9 owns embodiment/demo records; Phase 14 renders proxy-only cards, figures, and limitation warnings |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Produces dashboard-derived records, cards, views, figures, tables, manifests, export logs, warning panels, and reproducibility package | Layer 10 owns derived dashboard/card/export/reproducibility artifacts only |

### 5.2 Layer 10 module participation

| Layer 10 module | Phase 14 participation | Output / validation responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Module 10.1 — Record Loader and Canonical Artifact Reader | Loads saved records, manifests, cards/source bundles, metric dictionaries, matched reports, negative-result notes, and claim-evidence entries | Must read saved artifacts only and preserve source IDs |
| Module 10.2 — Schema Validator and Completeness Auditor | Validates record schemas, required fields, warning flags, metric dictionary references, matched-comparison keys, and missingness | Emits completeness and validation status used by views/cards/exports |
| Module 10.3 — Record Indexer and Lineage Resolver | Builds joins across dataset, subject, session, trial, window, split, model, calibration, threshold, policy, stress, embodiment, and export IDs | Emits unresolved-link reports and diagnostic-only flags when joins fail |
| Module 10.4 — Metric Summarizer and `DashboardMetricRecord` Builder | Produces dashboard-ready metric records from saved upstream metrics and declared metric definitions | Must not compute hidden experimental logic or retune thresholds/rewards/policies |
| Module 10.5 — View Model Builder, Renderer, and Scientific Observability Pages | Builds page/panel metadata and renders views | Produces `DashboardViewRecord` outputs with filters, warnings, completeness state, and export references |
| Module 10.6 — Card Generator and Card Completeness Checker | Produces or validates card records/files from saved records and templates | Ensures limitations, source lineage, reproduction fields, and warning flags are present |
| Module 10.7 — Export Manager for Thesis Figures and Tables | Produces static figures, tables, screenshots, CSV/Parquet exports, and export logs | Ensures export determinism, checksums, artifact IDs, and thesis usage references |
| Module 10.8 — Reproducibility Manifest Builder | Packages source records, configs, seeds, tool versions, scripts, hashes, cards, figures, tables, and environment notes | Produces `ReproducibilityManifest` and package index |
| Module 10.9 — Warning Engine and Claim-Safety Gate | Applies Layer 0 claim-safety, diagnostic-only, limitation, simulation/proxy/stress/embodiment warnings | Blocks unsafe or incomplete thesis-facing exports |
| Module 10.10 — Audit Logger and Artifact Registry | Records dashboard/export runs, generated artifact IDs, checksums, source links, warning states, and reviewer-visible audit logs | Prevents silent overwrite and supports Phase 15 traceability |

### 5.3 Excluded responsibilities

Phase 14 must not:

- ingest new public data;
- train decoders;
- fit calibration models;
- select thresholds from evaluation data;
- produce IHARQ decisions;
- infer RegimeRisk states;
- train or mutate policies;
- run simulated closed-loop sessions;
- generate stress perturbations;
- run contextual-bandit or RL updates;
- run MyoSuite/OpenSim/static replay;
- edit upstream source records;
- hide missingness, negative results, or diagnostic-only labels;
- author stronger claims than Layer 0 allows.

## 6. Registry Issue Intake and Impact Assessment

Phase 14 is especially sensitive to registry unresolved issues because dashboards and cards can accidentally make unresolved entities look final. The following issues are carried forward explicitly.

| Registry issue | Affected Phase 14 artifact / interface | Risk | Temporary Phase 14 handling | Blocks Phase 14? | Claim/export effect | Required repair |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MC-001` — standalone `TrialRecord` ambiguity | Join keys for trial/window-level views, figures, cards, matched comparisons, embodiment/stress views | Dashboard joins may imply a canonical standalone trial record that the registry has not confirmed | Use `WindowRecord` trial fields and manifest/source IDs as supported baseline; mark standalone `TrialRecord` as `inferred_candidate` if surfaced | No | Missing or ambiguous trial/window joins become diagnostic-only | Confirm whether trial identity remains embedded in `WindowRecord` or becomes canonical `TrialRecord` |
| `MC-002` — `EvidenceQualityRecord` shared-producer nuance | IHARQ and learned evidence-quality pages/cards | Rule-derived and learned variants may blur Layer 4 and Layer 6 ownership | Require `producer_module`, `phase_id`, source IDs, and variant tags in view filters/cards | No | Missing variant lineage blocks thesis-ready A6/evidence-quality claims | Confirm unified variant schema or split record families |
| `MC-003` — `combine` / `combine_evidence` alias | IHARQ action-token displays, policy action pages, cards | Action aliases may be displayed as different actions | Export canonical token where available; display aliases only with alias-map reference | No | Unmapped aliases remain diagnostic-only | Finalize action-token alias map |
| `MC-004` — `ReadinessContextRecord` Layer 6/Layer 7 boundary | Adaptive policy and simulation pages | Dashboard may imply Layer 7 owns readiness context semantics | Treat Layer 6 as semantic owner; Layer 7 materializations are run-specific/adapters unless confirmed | No | Missing owner/adapter metadata blocks thesis-ready policy/simulation cards | Confirm Layer 7 materialization status |
| `MC-005` — `PolicyUpdateTrace` lifecycle | Bandit/RL/update-trace cards, disabled-update audits, frozen/update filters | Training/adaptation curves may mix with frozen evaluation | Require `DashboardMetricRecord.policy_update_filter`, trace completeness views, and disabled-update audit tables | Yes for policy-update thesis exports | Missing traces or filters force diagnostic-only for update-enabled claims | Finalize trace schema/path and disabled-update audit fields |
| `MC-006` — `SafetyEventRecord` / safety-event log alias | Safety-event summaries across simulation, stress, embodiment, OpenSim | Safety warnings may point to incompatible artifacts | Preserve canonical/candidate status and map CSV/log aliases in manifest | No | Unmapped safety-event artifacts remain diagnostic-only | Resolve canonical name/path and log alias mapping |
| `MC-007` — `DashboardMetricRecord` ownership/boundary | Core Phase 14 output | Dashboard metrics may be mistaken for primary evidence | Label `DashboardMetricRecord` as Layer 10 dashboard-derived, with source records and metric dictionary references | Yes for dashboard metric export | Missing source lineage blocks thesis-ready metrics | Confirm source metric to dashboard metric mapping |
| `MC-008` — `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary` schema/path | All metric views, figures, tables, cards | Metrics may be undefined or irreproducible | Require metric dictionary ID/snapshot/path for thesis-facing metrics; otherwise diagnostic-only | Yes for metric-based thesis exports | Undefined metrics cannot support claims | Finalize schema/path/ownership |
| `MC-009` — repository paths/storage homes | All export paths, manifests, cards, figures, logs | Artifacts may be unlocatable or path-incompatible | Use architecture-supported conceptual homes and manifest mapping; preserve concrete path issue | No if manifests are complete | Missing manifest path blocks reproducibility claim | Finalize concrete storage homes |
| `MC-010` — lifecycle/schema maturity/branch status | Dashboard completeness states, optional pages, cards | Candidate/diagnostic artifacts may appear final | Preserve lifecycle and branch-status labels in views/cards/exports | No | Non-final artifacts cannot be thesis-ready | Reconcile lifecycle/status vocabulary |
| `MC-011` — Layer 10 evidence boundary | All dashboard-generated outputs | Dashboard may become hidden evidence producer | Enforce read-only source record boundary; recomputation requires new run/config/output record | Yes for Phase 14 validity | Boundary violation blocks export and Phase 15 handoff | Preserve source-vs-derived separation |
| `MC-012` — Layer 0 evidence boundary | Claim-safety pages, limitation cards, claim-evidence views | Claim audit artifacts may be treated as empirical evidence | Layer 0 pages/cards remain audit/limitation/claim-mapping outputs only | Yes for claim-facing exports | Missing Layer 0 review blocks thesis-facing export | Preserve Layer 0 audit-only boundary |
| `CL-L01-002` — `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` vs `ClaimEvidenceManifest` | Claim-evidence views and export package | Final claim trace may fragment | Preserve matrix/manifest alias caveat and include both references when predecessor artifacts use both | No | Missing claim-evidence link blocks claim-ready output | Confirm canonical name or alias relationship |
| OpenSim branch status / manifest issue from Phase 13 | Optional OpenSim views/cards | Optional output may be promoted to core evidence | Display branch status: implemented, diagnostic-only, skipped, or future-work-only | No | Optional/skipped branch must remain non-blocking and labelled | Confirm exact OpenSim manifest/config/tool-anchor schema if implemented |

No registry issue permits a stronger claim than the architecture allows. Unresolved issues become warnings, diagnostic-only states, blocked exports, or open issue rows rather than hidden assumptions.

## 7. Phase 0 Inheritance Check

Phase 14 depends heavily on Phase 0. The inherited foundation is usable if Phase 0’s schemas, fixtures, conventions, and placeholders are present and if unresolved registry schema/path issues are carried forward visibly.

| Phase 0 foundation item | Phase 14 dependency | Inheritance status | Gap effect if missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Schema definitions | Required for all source records, `DashboardMetricRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, `CardRecord`, manifest, warning, validation, metric, and claim-evidence artifacts | `inherited_required` | Blocks valid dashboard/export package |
| Record/interface definitions | Required to distinguish upstream records from Layer 10 derived outputs | `inherited_required` | Boundary violation; diagnostic-only or blocked export |
| Configuration families | Required for dashboard page config, export config, card templates, view filters, rendering choices, and manifest config hashes | `inherited_required` | Weakens reproducibility; may block thesis exports |
| Mock records / mockable fixtures | Required for Layer 10 schema, missingness, warning, card, export, and snapshot tests | `inherited_required` | Weakens QA; not necessarily a scientific blocker if real records validate |
| Validation scripts | Required for source record validation, completeness audit, card completeness, warning coverage, export determinism, and manifest integrity | `inherited_required` | Blocks Phase 14 exit |
| Run identifier conventions | Required for source runs, dashboard/export runs, cards, figures, tables, logs, and manifests | `inherited_required` | Blocks reproducibility package |
| Config hash conventions | Required for source configs, dashboard configs, card/export configs, policy/stress/embodiment filters | `inherited_required` | Blocks thesis-ready exports if missing |
| Seed conventions | Required where source records, stress profiles, policy training/adaptation, simulations, or exported figures depend on seeds | `inherited_required_if_applicable` | Missing seed or deterministic-replay reason becomes warning/diagnostic-only |
| Manifest conventions | Required for artifact manifest, dashboard export manifest, reproducibility manifest, package index, and source bundle links | `inherited_required` | Blocks Phase 15 handoff |
| Repository skeleton expectations | Required for stable storage of records, cards, figures, tables, logs, dashboard app/static exports, manifests | `inherited_required_with_MC-009_open` | Does not block if manifest maps conceptual paths; concrete path issue remains open |
| Metric dictionary placeholders | Required for all metric-bearing dashboard outputs | `inherited_required_with_MC-008_open` | Missing dictionary entries make metrics diagnostic-only |
| Claim-evidence placeholders | Required for claim-facing dashboard/card/export artifacts | `inherited_required_with_CL-L01-002_open` | Missing claim-evidence entry blocks claim-ready export |
| Dashboard/export-readiness placeholders | Required for Layer 10 outputs and Phase 15 package | `inherited_required` | Blocks Phase 14 exit if absent |
| Policy-update trace fixtures and disabled-update audit fixtures | Required for bandit/RL/update-enabled dashboard pages | `inherited_required_if_policy_pages_enabled` | Missing trace/audit support blocks policy-update thesis views |
| Negative-result and diagnostic-only fixtures | Required for missingness and failure visibility | `inherited_required` | Hidden negative results invalidate Phase 14 export |

```yaml
phase0_inheritance_gap: true_for_unresolved_metric_dictionary_claim_evidence_repository_path_and_schema_status_foundations
blocks_core_phase14: false_if_Phase0_schemas_validators_manifests_and_dashboard_export_placeholders_are_present
blocks_thesis_ready_exports: true_where_metric_dictionary_claim_evidence_policy_update_trace_or_manifest_foundations_are_missing
weakens_phase14: true_if_repository_paths_or_schema_statuses_remain_unresolved_without_manifest_mapping
required_temporary_handling: preserve MC-008, MC-009, MC-010, MC-011, MC-012, and CL-L01-002 as visible open issues; apply diagnostic-only or blocked-export status when needed
```

## 8. Upstream Dependency and Continuity Check

### 8.1 Dependency chain

Phase 14 is downstream of all prior phases. It does not require every optional upstream branch to be successfully implemented, but it requires every consumed artifact to be saved, validated, lineage-bearing, and correctly status-labelled.

| Upstream phase | Required Phase 14 continuity check |
|---|---|
| Phase 0 | Schemas, validators, configs, IDs, seeds, manifests, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, and repository skeleton expectations must be available |
| Phase 1 | Clean public-data/protocol records and split/readiness outputs must remain immutable; dashboard may not repair or overwrite them |
| Phase 2 | Decoder/baseline outputs must be shown with model/run/split/label-budget lineage and baseline-sufficiency limitations |
| Phase 3 | Calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction views must preserve threshold selection split, calibration ID, matched operating point, leakage warnings, and negative-result notes |
| Phase 4 | IHARQ views must preserve Layer 4 action tokens, evidence-quality variant lineage, fallback/unsafe states, reason codes, and A5/A6 evaluation lineage |
| Phase 5 | RegimeRisk timelines must preserve causal temporal order, trust-state availability, warning semantics, and temporal-trust proxy limitations |
| Phase 6 | Adaptive-IHARQ/evidence-quality estimator views must preserve pseudo-label limitations, policy IDs, feature/source lineage, and learned-vs-rule-derived evidence-quality variants |
| Phase 7 | Learning-to-defer views must preserve deferral target/reason vocabulary, cost/coverage metrics, target-construction caveats, and diagnostic-only downgrade rules |
| Phase 8 | Simulation views must preserve transition/session/episode/reward/action/safety lineage and frozen-policy no-mutation status |
| Phase 9 | Stress views must preserve clean/stressed pairing, stress profile/schedule/run manifest IDs, stress validity, and stress-only/proxy-only limitations |
| Phase 10 | Bandit views must separate simulation-training/adaptation curves from frozen-policy evaluation and show trace/audit completeness |
| Phase 11 | RL views must preserve update traces, disabled-update audits, reward/config lineage, safety/illegal-action warnings, and simulation-only status |
| Phase 12 | Embodiment views/cards must preserve embodiment mode, command mapping, endpoint-error, safety-event, reward-trace, demo-manifest, and proxy-only limitations |
| Phase 13 | OpenSim views/cards must preserve optional branch status, mapping limitations, output manifests, comparison reports where attempted, skip/future-work notes, and non-blocking status |

### 8.2 Continuity findings

| Check | Phase 14 finding | Temporary handling |
|---|---|---|
| Target phase consumes artifacts previous phases produced | Passed: Phase 0–13 handoff records identify dashboard/export/card consumers | Consume by manifest/source IDs only |
| Target phase relies on artifacts previous phases did not produce | Conditional: optional pages may lack upstream records if optional branches were skipped or diagnostic-only | Mark page/card incomplete, skipped, future-work-only, or diagnostic-only |
| Target phase renames previous artifacts | Not allowed | Use canonical names; display aliases require alias-map references |
| Target phase changes semantic owner of any record | Not allowed | Source records remain owned by Layers 1–9; Layer 10 owns derived outputs only |
| Target phase relies on a validation gate not previously established | Mostly inherited from Phase 0; additional Layer 10 gates are architecture-defined | Missing validators block Phase 14 exit or make exports diagnostic-only |
| Metric dictionary entries prepared | Conditional due `MC-008` | Metric-bearing outputs require dictionary ID/snapshot; otherwise diagnostic-only |
| Dashboard/export conventions established | Phase 0 and architecture establish placeholders; concrete storage homes remain partly open | Use manifests and preserve `MC-009` |
| Policy-update traces, stress profiles, embodiment mappings, simulation records exist before display | Conditional by upstream phase success | Display only if present and validated; otherwise show missingness/skip |
| Diagnostic-only labels and limitation labels preserved | Required | Layer 10 must expose them, not erase them |

### 8.3 Cross-phase issues carried into Phase 14

Cross-phase issue:

- Affected prior phase: Phase 0 and all metric-producing/evaluation-producing phases.
- Affected current phase: Phase 14.
- Affected artifact/record/interface: `MetricDictionaryEntry` / `MetricDictionary`.
- Risk: Dashboard metrics, figures, and tables become claim-facing without stable definitions.
- Required repair: Finalize metric dictionary schema/path and require dictionary IDs or snapshots in all `DashboardMetricRecord` outputs.
- Temporary handling: Metric-bearing exports without dictionary linkage are diagnostic-only and cannot support Phase 15 claims.

Cross-phase issue:

- Affected prior phase: Phases 4, 6, 8, 10, 11.
- Affected current phase: Phase 14.
- Affected artifact/record/interface: `EvidenceQualityRecord`, `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audits, `DashboardMetricRecord.policy_update_filter`.
- Risk: Rule-derived evidence quality, learned evidence quality, training/adaptation curves, and frozen-policy evaluation curves may be mixed.
- Required repair: Preserve producer/variant tags and policy-update filters in all dashboard pages, cards, figures, tables, and manifests.
- Temporary handling: Missing variant/filter lineage blocks thesis-ready A6/A10/A11 views and forces diagnostic-only status.

Cross-phase issue:

- Affected prior phase: Phases 8, 12, 13.
- Affected current phase: Phase 14.
- Affected artifact/record/interface: `SafetyEventRecord` / `safety_event_log.csv`, Layer 9 demo manifest, OpenSim optional branch manifest.
- Risk: Safety-event and embodiment warnings may be untraceable or overclaimed.
- Required repair: Resolve safety-event alias/path and optional OpenSim manifest fields.
- Temporary handling: Map aliases in manifests, display proxy/simulation warnings, and mark unmatched or unmapped safety/embodiment views diagnostic-only.

## 9. Input Contract for This Phase

### 9.1 Input categories

| Input category | Representative records/artifacts | Phase 14 use | Status rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard-readable source records | `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PredictionRecord`, `CalibrationRecord`, `UncertaintyRecord`, `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `IHARQDecisionRecord`, `RegimeStateRecord`, `ReadinessContextRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, `TransitionRecord`, `StressProfileRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, Phase 13 optional outputs | Display, summarize, filter, warn, card, figure/table/export, and trace | Must remain owned by upstream layers and immutable from Phase 14 |
| Dashboard-readable evaluation artifacts | `EvaluationOutcomeRecord`, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, ablation summaries, matched operating-point tables, baseline sufficiency notes, stress/embodiment comparison reports | Evaluation and ablation pages, figures, tables, metric definitions, diagnostic labels | Must be labelled evaluation-only and not used as decision-time inputs |
| Dashboard-warning inputs | Claim-safety tags, limitation statements, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, `InvalidClaimFlag`, leakage warnings, missingness logs, negative-result notes, simulation-only/proxy-only/stress-only/embodiment-only labels, branch status notes | Warning banners, limitation cards, blocked-export decisions | Required for claim-facing exports; missing warnings block export |
| Dashboard-generated source-bundle inputs | Source bundles/cards from upstream phases, card templates, export templates, figure/table templates, dashboard page config | Card/view/export generation | Templates do not become evidence without source links |

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 14 follows a record-only derived-output chain:

```text
saved upstream records and manifests
→ schema/completeness/lineage validation
→ index and source-record join resolution
→ metric dictionary and matched-comparison linkage
→ diagnostic-only / missingness / warning-state assignment
→ DashboardMetricRecord generation
→ DashboardViewRecord generation
→ card generation and card-completeness validation
→ figure/table/export generation with artifact identity contract
→ claim-evidence and limitation linkage
→ artifact manifest and ReproducibilityManifest packaging
→ Phase 15 handoff
```

### 12.1 Record-only reading

Layer 10 reads records and manifests saved by upstream phases. It may derive dashboard summaries only from those records and declared metric definitions. If a computation would change an experimental result, alter a threshold, rerun a model, mutate a policy, reapply a stress profile, or replay an embodiment simulator, it is not a Phase 14 dashboard operation. It must either be performed in the responsible upstream phase with a new run identifier and output record or be excluded from thesis-ready Phase 14 exports.

### 12.2 Validation and lineage resolution

Phase 14 validates that consumed records have schemas, IDs, validation status, split role, source IDs, config hashes, seeds where applicable, warning flags, limitation tags, and producer-layer ownership. It builds lineage indexes that allow every figure/table/card/view to trace back to record IDs and configuration hashes. Failed joins are not silently repaired; they become missingness reports, diagnostic-only flags, blocked-export states, or open issue entries.

### 12.3 Metric and comparison linkage

For every metric-bearing dashboard output, Phase 14 requires a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or validated metric dictionary snapshot. For every comparative output, Phase 14 requires a matched-comparison key or a clear diagnostic-only/unmatched comparison label. This includes A0–A13 views, stress comparisons, embodiment comparisons, policy comparisons, baseline-sufficiency tables, and optional OpenSim comparisons.

### 12.4 Warning and claim-safety propagation

Phase 14 applies the strictest inherited claim-safety tags from source records and Layer 0. A dashboard page, card, figure, or table may only be thesis-facing if it preserves the warnings and limitations attached to its sources. If a source contains public-data-only, proxy-label, low-calibration, simulation-only, stress-conditioned, embodiment-proxy-only, MyoSuite/OpenSim-demo-only, diagnostic-only, future-work-only, or non-clinical tags, the derived artifact must carry those tags.

### 12.5 Export and packaging

Phase 14 exports a package for Phase 15 containing dashboard-derived records, cards, figures, tables, logs, artifact manifests, reproducibility manifests, metric dictionaries, matched-comparison indexes, negative-result indexes, and claim-evidence views. Every exported artifact must have an artifact identity contract.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Core validation gates

| Gate | Required check | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Saved-record-only gate | Dashboard reads only saved records, manifests, metric dictionaries, matched reports, and note indexes | Hidden recomputation blocks Phase 14 exit |
| Schema gate | Consumed records and produced Layer 10 records validate against schemas or declared schema-status candidates | Invalid records excluded or diagnostic-only; missing core schema blocks export |
| Source ownership gate | Source records remain owned by producing layers; Layer 10 outputs are derived | Owner ambiguity becomes warning/open issue; source mutation blocks export |
| Lineage gate | Every figure/table/card/view has source IDs, config IDs/hashes, run IDs, schema versions, and warning tags | Missing lineage blocks thesis-ready export |
| Metric dictionary gate | Every metric has definition, direction, unit, formula/source fields, and dictionary ID/snapshot | Undefined metrics diagnostic-only |
| Matched-comparison gate | Comparative claims have matched keys and matched reports, or accepted missingness and diagnostic-only status | Unmatched comparisons cannot support improvement claims |
| Negative-result gate | Negative/null/failure/missingness notes are indexed and visible | Hidden negative result blocks claim-facing export |
| Warning coverage gate | Required public-data/proxy/simulation/stress/embodiment/diagnostic/clinical-non-claim warnings appear in views/cards/exports | Missing warnings block unsafe export |
| Card completeness gate | Cards include source lineage, metrics, limitations, reproduction fields, warnings, and thesis usage | Incomplete cards cannot be claim-supporting |
| Export determinism gate | Repeated exports from same records/configs are stable or differences are versioned | Non-deterministic untracked exports blocked |
| Policy-update separation gate | Training/adaptation curves, update-enabled runs, disabled-update audits, and frozen-policy evaluation are separated | Mixed curves diagnostic-only or blocked |
| Stress/embodiment branch gate | Optional stress/embodiment/OpenSim views preserve branch status, proxy/simulation limitations, and source manifests | Optional branches hidden or promoted improperly block export |
| Layer 0 review gate | Claim-facing outputs pass Layer 0 limitation/forbidden-claim review | Missing review blocks Phase 15 handoff |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 14 is complete when it produces a traceable dashboard/export package in which every figure, table, card, view, screenshot, metric export, warning, and reproducibility artifact links to source records, configuration hashes, schema versions, run IDs, metric dictionary entries, matched-comparison records where required, negative-result notes where relevant, claim-evidence entries where claim-facing, and limitation tags.

The exit condition can be satisfied by a static export package if it includes the same traceability, warning, and reproducibility guarantees as an interactive dashboard.

### 13.3 Additional policy-learning gate

For contextual-bandit and RL pages, Phase 14 must display:

- `PolicyUpdateTrace` completeness;
- disabled-update audit visibility for frozen evaluation;
- `DashboardMetricRecord.policy_update_filter` values;
- separate training/adaptation curves and held-out frozen-policy evaluation curves;
- reward/config/stress/policy lineage;
- simulation-only warnings;
- diagnostic-only downgrades where trace, reward, or frozen/update lineage is incomplete.

### 13.4 Additional Layer 1–3 evaluation-slice gate

For the public-data/decoder/calibration slice, Phase 14 must display:

- Layer 1 ablation-readiness state;
- split/readiness and matched-comparison key completeness;
- A0–A4 lineage;
- metric dictionary references;
- Layer 3 matched operating-point exports;
- leakage warnings and threshold-selection split provenance;
- high-confidence-wrong and negative-result notes;
- claim-evidence linkage.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

Phase 14 must preserve matched-comparison keys; it may not create visual comparisons that imply fairness without matching evidence.

### 14.1 Required key families

| Key family | Fields / records | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| Data identity | `dataset_id`, `subject_id`, `session_id`, `trial_id`, `window_id`, `split_id`, `split_role`, `preprocessing_id`, `label_map_id` | A0–A13 where comparisons use shared data windows |
| Decoder/model identity | `model_id`, model family, label budget, training/calibration split, checkpoint/run ID | A0–A4 decoder and calibration views |
| Calibration/threshold identity | `calibration_id`, `threshold_registry_id`, selection split, operating point ID, reliability bin | A1–A3 and downstream threshold-aware views |
| IHARQ/evidence identity | `evidence_quality_id`, `iharq_decision_id`, action token, reason code, fallback/unsafe state | A5–A7 and policy-context views |
| Policy identity | `policy_id`, policy family, action-space version, cost/reward config, policy-update mode, frozen/update flag | A8–A11 and closed-loop/policy pages |
| Simulation identity | environment config, transition ID, episode/session ID, reward trace ID, simulator ID, seed | A8–A11 simulation pages |
| Stress identity | `stress_profile_id`, `stress_schedule_id`, intensity, stress family, injection target, seed, clean/stressed pair ID | A12 and stress-conditioned comparisons |
| Embodiment identity | `embodiment_mode_id`, command mapping ID, simulator branch, demo manifest ID, endpoint-error family, safety-event log ID | A13, Phase 12/13 pages |
| Evaluation artifact identity | `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` / manifest link | All claim-facing evaluation exports |
| Dashboard/export identity | `DashboardMetricRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, `CardRecord`, export artifact ID, checksum, config hash | All Phase 14 outputs |

### 14.2 Preservation rules

- If a visual comparison is matched, the dashboard view and exported figure/table must cite the matched-comparison ID or matched key set.
- If a comparison is unmatched but still useful for inspection, it must be labelled diagnostic-only or exploratory.
- If missingness is accepted, the accepted-missingness rationale must be visible in the `DashboardViewRecord`, card, table, and export manifest.
- If stress-conditioned or embodiment-conditioned comparisons are shown, clean/stressed or simulator-mode pairing must be explicit.
- If policy-update curves are shown, training/adaptation and held-out frozen evaluation must not share a visual or table without explicit separation and labels.
- If a key is unavailable because the registry leaves the entity unresolved, the open issue must be preserved rather than silently resolved.

| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | Display RL rollouts, safety/illegal-action warnings, and frozen evaluation | RL policy records, update traces, reward configs, safety events, metric dictionary, matched comparison |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Display stress profiles, sensitivity curves, matched clean/stressed comparisons | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifests, stress validity reports, stress metrics, negative-result notes |

### 15.1 Explicit evaluation artifact requirements

For every thesis-facing evaluation view, Phase 14 requires:

```text
EvaluationOutcomeRecord or equivalent source evaluation record where produced
MetricDictionaryEntry / metric dictionary snapshot
MatchedComparisonReport where comparison is claimed
NegativeResultNote when results are null, failed, incomplete, skipped, or diagnostic-only
DiagnosticOnlyFlag / diagnostic-only status where any evidence requirement is incomplete
```

A0–A13 may be displayed as an evaluation ladder or ablation dashboard, but they must not be described as artifact owners.
