## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 14 may support claims about:

```text
dashboard/read-only inspectability
record-to-figure traceability
card completeness and limitation visibility
artifact manifest completeness
reproducibility packaging
metric dictionary and matched-comparison visibility
negative-result visibility
diagnostic-only and missingness visibility
warning coverage and claim-safety review readiness
public EEG reliability evidence display
low-calibration evidence display
calibration and uncertainty visibility
IHARQ-style evidence verification display
temporal trust monitoring display
adaptive readiness-policy evaluation display
simulation-only closed-loop behavior display
stress-conditioned robustness display
simulation/proxy-only embodiment demonstration display
```

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 14 must not support or imply claims about:

```text
clinical BCI-FES validation
real patient safety
medical-device readiness
real rehabilitation efficacy
real muscle stimulation control
real deployment readiness
real assistive-control safety
real-time clinical dashboard readiness
patient-specific biomechanical validation
actual therapeutic benefit
real-world stress/fatigue diagnosis
```

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

Phase 14 must propagate the strictest applicable tags, including:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based where applicable
evaluation_only
simulation_only
stress_conditioned
embodiment_proxy_only
MyoSuite_OpenSim_demo_only
diagnostic_only where applicable
future_work_only where applicable
skipped_non_blocking where applicable
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

A Phase 14 output must be downgraded to diagnostic-only, blocked export, or limitation-only when:

- metric dictionary entries are missing;
- matched-comparison keys are missing for comparative claims;
- source-record lineage is incomplete;
- warning flags are absent;
- negative results are hidden;
- policy-update traces are incomplete;
- training/adaptation and frozen evaluation are mixed;
- stress or embodiment branch lineage is incomplete;
- optional OpenSim outputs are unmanifested or mapping limitations are absent;
- Layer 0 review has not passed;
- a figure/table/card would imply a forbidden clinical/deployment/medical claim.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

Phase 14 can display capability-tier readiness, but C0–C4 are not implementation phases, ablation IDs, artifact owners, or dashboard owners. They remain thesis-valid claim-maturity summaries and stopping-point labels.

| Tier | Phase 14 role | Claim-maturity handling |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Display and package public EEG, split, baseline, calibration, uncertainty, selective-prediction, reliability, high-confidence-wrong, and negative-result artifacts | Valid if Phases 0–3 records and exports are complete; dashboard does not create C0 evidence |
| C1 | Add IHARQ-lite and RegimeRisk pages/cards/exports where Phases 4–5 complete | Valid if IHARQ and temporal-trust evidence has matched metrics, warnings, and limitations |
| C2 | Add evidence-quality estimator, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, and learning-to-defer pages/cards/exports | Valid if pseudo-label, cost/coverage, and policy limitations are visible |
| C3 | Add simulated closed-loop, StressForge, contextual-bandit, and RL pages/cards/exports | Valid if simulation-only, stress-conditioned, update-trace, and frozen/update separation rules pass |
| C4 | Add Layer 9 embodiment, optional OpenSim, complete cards/figures/tables/manifests, and final traceability package | Valid only with proxy/simulation-only embodiment warnings and optional-branch status preserved |

Phase 14 may strengthen C4 readiness by packaging the full dashboard/cards/reproducibility artifact set. It must not make lower-tier thesis claims depend on optional C4 artifacts. If Phase 12 or Phase 13 is missing or diagnostic-only, C0–C3 remain unaffected, and C4 embodiment/OpenSim pages are marked incomplete, diagnostic-only, skipped, or future-work-only.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Negative-result visibility

Phase 14 must surface negative, null, incomplete, failed, skipped, unmatched, and diagnostic-only outcomes rather than hiding them. The negative-result page/index must include:

- failed or weak decoder baselines;
- calibration degradation or no calibration improvement;
- selective-prediction/high-confidence wrong failures;
- IHARQ fallback or unsafe-event burdens;
- RegimeRisk negative controls or weak temporal-trust findings;
- Adaptive-IHARQ or learning-to-defer underperformance;
- simulation reward/cost failures;
- stress robustness degradation;
- bandit/RL instability, reward leakage warnings, or update-trace failures;
- embodiment poor endpoint-error, blocked-command, safety-event, or mapping failures;
- Phase 13 OpenSim skip/future-work/failed replay/unmatched comparison notes;
- dashboard/export validation failures.

Each `NegativeResultNote` must link to affected records, metric dictionary entries, matched-comparison reports where applicable, diagnostic-only status, limitation tags, and Phase 15 relevance.

### 19.2 Baseline-sufficiency handling

Phase 14 must make baseline sufficiency visible. It must show whether simpler baselines are sufficient, whether advanced phases improve anything under matched conditions, and whether a negative result makes a lower-tier thesis stopping point more honest than an unsupported higher-tier claim.

Baseline-sufficiency display should cover:

- A0 raw decoder baseline;
- A1 calibrated decoder;
- A2 simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline;
- A3 uncertainty and selective prediction where produced;
- A4 longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls;
- IHARQ-lite versus simple confidence/fallback baselines;
- RegimeRisk-aware versus regime-unaware comparisons;
- learning-to-defer versus fixed deferral/fallback baselines;
- supervised policy versus rule-based policies;
- contextual-bandit/RL versus frozen supervised/simple policies;
- clean versus stressed comparisons;
- embodiment/no-embodiment or static-replay/MyoSuite/OpenSim branch comparisons where matched.

If a baseline is missing, the dashboard must show that gap and mark affected claims diagnostic-only or incomplete.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

### 20.1 Failure modes

| Failure mode | Risk | Required Phase 14 defense |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard becomes cosmetic | It looks complete but does not support scientific claims | Link every page to source records, metrics, claims, limitations, cards, ablations, and reproducibility artifacts |
| Dashboard becomes hidden experiment engine | It recomputes or retunes results outside upstream records | Enforce record-only reading and new-run requirement for any recomputation |
| Missing records are hidden | Thesis appears more complete than evidence allows | Show missingness/incomplete states on pages/cards/exports |
| Cards omit limitations | Cards overclaim or mislead | Card completeness checks and Layer 0 warning coverage required |
| Metric definitions are absent | Tables/figures become irreproducible | Require metric dictionary entries or diagnostic-only status |
| Matched-comparison keys are absent | Visual comparisons imply unfair improvements | Require matched reports or diagnostic-only labels |
| Policy updates are mixed with frozen evaluation | Adaptive methods look stronger than they are | Require update filters, trace cards, disabled-update audit views, and separate exports |
| Stress/embodiment warnings are absent | Proxy outputs appear clinically meaningful | Require stress/proxy/simulation/embodiment warnings in all derived artifacts |
| Optional OpenSim is promoted to core | Phase 13 absence/failure appears to invalidate lower-tier thesis | Display optional branch status and non-blocking skip/future-work handling |
| Manual figure edits break lineage | Thesis artifact no longer matches source records | Require export manager, checksums, artifact IDs, audit logs |
| Layer 0 review missing | Unsafe claim wording may enter thesis | Block claim-facing export until review passes |

### 20.2 Diagnostic-only rules

Phase 14 must mark the affected view/card/figure/table/export diagnostic-only when:

- a required source record is missing;
- source IDs or matched-comparison keys fail to join;
- source validation status is failed or unresolved;
- metric dictionary references are missing;
- comparison matching is incomplete;
- warning flags or limitation tags are missing;
- negative-result notes are missing for known failures;
- dashboard filters cannot be reproduced;
- source record ownership is ambiguous and unresolved;
- policy-update traces are missing for update-enabled views;
- disabled-update audit is missing for frozen evaluation views where required;
- stress profile/schedule/run-manifest lineage is missing;
- embodiment mode/command mapping/demo-manifest lineage is missing;
- Phase 13 OpenSim output manifest or mapping limitation is missing;
- Layer 0 review is absent;
- repository paths are unresolved without manifest mapping.

### 20.3 Missingness states

Phase 14 should use visible states such as:

```text
complete
incomplete_missing_source
incomplete_missing_metric_dictionary
incomplete_missing_matched_comparison
incomplete_missing_claim_evidence
incomplete_missing_warning
blocked_export
diagnostic_only
skipped_non_blocking
future_work_only
not_applicable_with_reason
stale_source_record
schema_validation_failed
```

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

Phase 14 should use the architecture-supported repository organization and manifest mapping. Concrete path finalization remains subject to `MC-009` where the registry has not confirmed exact homes.

| Storage family | Phase 14 expectation | Path status |
|---|---|---|
| Dashboard metric records | Store `DashboardMetricRecord` outputs under a dashboard metric record family | Architecture/registry-supported conceptual home; exact path governed by manifest and `MC-009` |
| Dashboard view records | Store `DashboardViewRecord` outputs under a dashboard view record family | Architecture/registry-supported conceptual home; exact path governed by manifest |
| Card records and files | Store `CardRecord` records and rendered cards under card record/card output families | Architecture supports `records/card_records/` and `cards/`-style homes; exact subpaths may remain confirmable |
| Static figures | Store dashboard/exported and thesis-ready figures with artifact IDs and checksums | Architecture supports `figures/dashboard_exports/` and thesis figure homes conceptually |
| Thesis tables | Store CSV/Parquet/Markdown/LaTeX table exports with table IDs | Architecture supports `thesis_tables/` conceptually |
| Dashboard app/static export | Store interactive app or static dashboard export package | Architecture supports `dashboard_app/`; static export is acceptable fallback |
| Manifests | Store artifact manifest, export manifest/package index, run registry links, metric dictionary export, claim-evidence view, reproducibility manifest | Architecture supports `manifests/`; exact file naming partly governed by registry issues |
| Logs | Store validation logs, warning logs, export logs, missingness logs, card-completeness logs, policy-update trace validation logs | Architecture supports `logs/` and validation/export logs conceptually |
| Claim-evidence views | Store claim-evidence view/manifest links with matrix/manifest alias caveat | `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` / `ClaimEvidenceManifest` ambiguity preserved |
| Negative-result index | Store index of `NegativeResultNote` entries and export-validation failures | Framework-supported; exact path via manifest |
| Open issue list | Store registry/open issue status used by dashboard and Phase 15 | Required to avoid hidden unresolved issues |

Every stored Phase 14 output must include or manifest-link:

## 23. Downstream Handoff Package

### 23.1 Handoff to Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

Phase 14 hands Phase 15 a traceable thesis artifact package containing:

- dashboard-derived metric records;
- dashboard view records;
- rendered dashboard/static export package;
- final static figures;
- thesis tables;
- rendered cards and card completeness report;
- artifact manifest;
- export manifest/package index;
- `ReproducibilityManifest`;
- metric dictionary exports/snapshots;
- matched-comparison report index;
- negative-result note index;
- diagnostic-only status list;
- claim-evidence views or manifest links;
- warning and limitation coverage report;
- open issue inventory;
- source bundle pointers for all thesis-used artifacts.

Phase 15 may use these outputs for thesis chapters only if the artifact identity contract, Layer 0 claim-safety review, metric dictionary, matched-comparison, negative-result, warning, and manifest requirements are satisfied.

### 23.2 Handoff to Layer 0 claim-safety review

Layer 0 receives:

- intended claim wording attached to figures/tables/cards;
- claim-evidence views and matrix/manifest links;
- limitation and warning coverage report;
- diagnostic-only and blocked-export lists;
- simulation/proxy/stress/embodiment/OpenSim warnings;
- forbidden-claim audit checklist;
- negative-result index;
- open issue inventory.

Layer 0 must block any dashboard/card/export output that implies clinical validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, or real deployment readiness.

### 23.3 Handoff to repository/reproducibility package

The repository/reproducibility package receives:

- generated artifact inventory;
- source record bundle index;
- configuration files and hashes;
- schema versions;
- seed and deterministic-replay notes;
- environment/tool version notes;
- scripts/pages used to generate artifacts;
- checksums/output hashes;
- validation logs;
- export logs;
- warning logs;
- open issue report;
- package index.

### 23.4 Handoff to reviewers/examiners

Reviewers and examiners receive a dashboard or static export package that can answer:

- what data, splits, and limitations were used;
- which baselines exist and whether they were sufficient;
- whether calibration and uncertainty improved reliability;
- how IHARQ and RegimeRisk changed readiness decisions;
- how learned policies were evaluated and whether policy updates were separated from frozen evaluation;
- how closed-loop simulation, stress, and embodiment were bounded;
- where negative results and diagnostic-only labels are visible;
- how every figure/table/card links to source records;
- which claims are allowed and which are explicitly forbidden.

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 14 is definition-of-done complete when all of the following are satisfied:

1. The combined Markdown file preserves Phase 0–13 predecessor sections above this Phase 14 section.
2. The section uses the official identity `Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards`.
3. Phase 0 inheritance is checked, including schemas, configs, validators, run IDs, config hashes, seeds, manifests, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, dashboard/export placeholders, policy-update trace fixtures, negative-result fixtures, and repository skeleton expectations.
4. All consumed source records from Phases 1–13 are either validated, explicitly missing, skipped, future-work-only, or diagnostic-only.
5. Layer 10 reads saved records only and does not mutate upstream records or recompute hidden experimental logic.
6. `DashboardMetricRecord` outputs are produced for dashboard metrics that have source records, filters, metric dictionary references where metric-bearing, matched-comparison references where comparative, warning flags, diagnostic-only status, and export/card links.
7. `DashboardViewRecord` outputs are produced for dashboard pages/panels with page IDs, metric IDs, filters, source links, warnings, completeness states, evaluation lineage, export references, and checksums where applicable.
8. `CardRecord` outputs and rendered cards include source records, metrics, limitations, warning flags, reproduction fields, artifact paths, and thesis usage references.
9. Every exported figure, table, screenshot, card, and dashboard page satisfies the artifact identity contract.
10. Metric dictionary entries or snapshots exist for every thesis-facing metric; otherwise affected outputs are diagnostic-only.
11. Matched-comparison reports or matched key sets exist for every comparative claim; otherwise affected comparisons are diagnostic-only.
12. Negative-result notes and missingness states are indexed and visible.
13. Baseline-sufficiency displays make clear whether simpler baselines are sufficient and whether advanced phases improve under matched conditions.
14. A0–A13 views are exposed as evaluation metadata only, with source-record lineage and explicit evaluation artifacts.
15. C0–C4 are displayed only as claim-maturity/stopping-point summaries, not phases or artifact owners.
16. Policy-update trace cards, disabled-update audit tables, and `policy_update_filter` fields are present where contextual-bandit/RL/update-enabled evidence appears.
17. Training/adaptation curves are separated from held-out frozen-policy evaluation curves in all pages, tables, figures, cards, and export manifests.
18. Stress-conditioned views preserve `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifest, seed, clean/stressed pairing, and stress-only/proxy warnings.
19. Embodiment views preserve embodiment mode, command mapping, endpoint-error, safety-event, reward-trace, demo-manifest, and embodiment-proxy limitations.
20. Phase 13 OpenSim outputs, if displayed, preserve optional branch status, output manifest, mapping limitations, comparison status, and non-clinical/non-blocking warnings.
21. Layer 10 dashboard-readable source records, dashboard-warning inputs, dashboard-generated derived outputs, dashboard-export manifest inputs, and not-dashboard inputs are separated.
22. Layer 0 claim-safety review passes for all claim-facing outputs.
23. Forbidden claims about clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, and deployment readiness are blocked.
24. Artifact manifest, export manifest/package index, and `ReproducibilityManifest` are generated and validated.
25. Export determinism, card completeness, warning coverage, missingness visibility, schema validation, and manifest integrity tests pass.
26. Repository/storage expectations are manifest-linked, and unresolved path/schema/name issues remain explicit instead of invented.
27. Open issues and confirmation requests are carried forward to Phase 15.
28. The Phase 15 handoff package is complete.

If the interactive dashboard is not implemented, Phase 14 can still be complete through a static export package if all lineage, card, figure/table, manifest, warning, diagnostic-only, negative-result, and Layer 0 review requirements pass. If any required lineage, metric, matched-comparison, warning, claim-evidence, or manifest requirement fails, affected outputs remain diagnostic-only or blocked and cannot support Phase 15 claim-facing use.

# Phase 15 — Final thesis integration

## 1. Phase Identity and Scope

| Field | Phase 15 value |
|---|---|
| Phase ID | `Phase 15` |
| Official phase name | `Final thesis integration` |
| Phase type | Final synthesis, manuscript traceability, claim-safety, and repository-release integration phase |
| Primary purpose | Convert validated implementation artifacts into defended thesis claims while preventing gaps between architecture, experiments, dashboard exports, limitations, and final writing |
| Primary layer participation | Layer 0 and Layer 10 are the main governance/read-export participants; Layers 1–9 remain source-evidence owners for the records they produced |
| Primary upstream phase | `Phase 14 — Dashboard and cards` |
| Hard upstream dependency | The highest completed capability tier must have validated records, metrics, figures, tables, cards, ablations, limitations, and manifests |
| Primary outputs | Thesis-ready architecture/method/evaluation/results/discussion sections; claim-to-artifact traceability matrix; `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`; negative-result register/index; artifact appendix; reproduction guide; limitation statements; final claim map |
| Primary consumers | Final thesis, defense slides, repository release, reproducibility appendix, examiner-facing artifact package, and future paper/reporting artifacts |
| Evidence-production boundary | Phase 15 produces synthesis and claim-traceability artifacts. It does not produce new empirical model results, recompute hidden dashboard logic, retune thresholds, retrain policies, generate new stress runs, rerun embodiment, or upgrade optional/stretch artifacts into core evidence. |
| Claim-safety boundary | Phase 15 may support bounded public EEG, low-calibration reliability, calibration/uncertainty visibility, evidence-verification, temporal-trust, adaptive-readiness, simulation-only, stress-conditioned, embodiment-proxy, dashboard/reproducibility, and final traceability claims. It must not support clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real deployment readiness, or real assistive-control safety. |

Phase 15 is the manuscript traceability gate. It must make the final thesis defensible at the highest completed and validated capability tier, while preserving diagnostic-only, optional-only, skipped, future-work, negative-result, and limitation labels from all prior phases. It is not a final opportunity to invent missing evidence. If a claim lacks a source record, metric dictionary entry, matched-comparison report, dashboard/card/export lineage, negative-result interpretation, or limitation statement, the claim must be narrowed, moved to future work, or removed.

| Framework for Generating the Execution and Evidence Plan | Governs the 26-section structure, source-grounding discipline, artifact lifecycle matrix, Phase 0 inheritance check, explicit evaluation artifacts, matched-comparison key preservation, frozen/update separation, negative-result handling, capability-tier governance, and handoff block requirements |

### 2.2 Architecture-grounded Phase 15 facts

Phase 15 is defined as the final thesis integration phase. Its precondition is that the highest completed capability tier has validated records, metrics, figures, tables, cards, ablations, limitations, and manifests. Its primary inputs are architecture sections, method descriptions, experiment configs, records, result manifests, ablation tables, metric dictionaries, matched-comparison reports, `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`, negative-result notes, stress results, cards, figures, limitations, failure taxonomy, repository manifest, and reproducibility guide. Its core tasks are to map every major thesis claim to evidence or limitation, write thesis chapters using saved artifacts, generate the claim-to-artifact matrix and reproduction guide, label public-data/proxy/simulation/embodiment/optional/future-work boundaries, and document negative results and failed or partial phases. Its exit condition is a manuscript and artifact package where the highest completed tier is clear, evidence is traceable, and unsupported claims are removed.

### 2.3 Registry-grounded Phase 15 facts

The registry treats `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` as a claim-evidence artifact and primary final claim linkage, but its exact schema/path remains a confirmation item. It also preserves `ClaimLedger`, `LimitationStatement`, `ScopeLabel`, and `InvalidClaimFlag` as Layer 0-governed candidate or draft-schema concepts, while `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` and `NegativeResultNote` are final evaluation/claim-safety artifacts. Layer 10 outputs such as `DashboardMetricRecord`, `DashboardViewRecord`, `CardRecord`, and `ReproducibilityManifest` are derived/read-export artifacts, not primary upstream empirical evidence. Metric dictionary entries and matched-comparison reports are required for thesis-facing metric and comparative claims.

All Phase 0–14 sections in the supplied combined Markdown file are preserved above this Phase 15 section. Phase 15 consumes their handoff state rather than rewriting their evidence. The most direct predecessor is Phase 14, which hands forward dashboard-derived metric records, dashboard view records, rendered dashboard/static export packages, final figures, thesis tables, rendered cards, artifact manifests, export manifests, `ReproducibilityManifest`, metric dictionary exports, matched-comparison report index, negative-result note index, diagnostic-only status list, claim-evidence views or manifest links, warning/limitation coverage report, open issue inventory, and source bundle pointers.

## 4. Architecture-Grounded Purpose

### 4.1 Purpose

Phase 15 converts the completed evidence system into a thesis-ready manuscript and artifact package. Its central role is to ensure that every thesis claim, figure, table, card, dashboard export, demonstration statement, and repository artifact can be traced back to validated upstream records, metric definitions, matched-comparison reports where required, claim-safety tags, negative-result notes, limitation statements, and reproducibility manifests.

### 4.2 Bottleneck controlled

Phase 15 controls the final bottleneck of claim drift. Without this phase, the thesis could accidentally:

- cite dashboard cards as if they were primary evidence;
- imply that optional Stretch C outputs are core evidence;
- claim performance improvement without matched-comparison support;
- omit negative or baseline-sufficient results;
- merge update-enabled training curves with frozen-policy evaluation curves;
- treat stress or embodiment outputs as real-world validation;
- hide incomplete, skipped, diagnostic-only, or future-work branches;
- weaken public-data, proxy-label, simulation-only, or non-clinical limitations;
- publish final claims that lack record/config/seed/manifest lineage.

### 4.3 Thesis evidence role

Phase 15 establishes that the architecture, implementation, experiments, dashboard, final demonstration, and limitations form one coherent defended contribution. It does not make every Stretch C branch mandatory. Instead, it makes the thesis valid at the highest completed and validated capability tier, with C0–C4 used only as claim-maturity and stopping-point summaries.

### 4.4 Non-goals

Phase 15 must not:

- create new official phases, layers, ablations, capability tiers, canonical records, or canonical interfaces;
- retrain decoders, refit calibration, retune thresholds, rerun IHARQ, retrain policies, rerun stress tests, rerun embodiment, or recompute hidden dashboard logic;
- overwrite validated upstream records;
- remove diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work, skipped, invalid, or negative-result labels;
- upgrade proxy/simulation/stress/embodiment evidence into clinical, real-patient, deployment, medical-device, rehabilitation, real muscle-control, or real assistive-control claims.

## 5. Primary Layers, Supporting Layers, and Module Participation

### 5.1 Layer participation

| Layer | Phase 15 role | Ownership boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Layer 0 — Claim-Safety and Scope Governance | Reviews final claim wording, limitation statements, `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`, diagnostic-only labels, invalid-claim flags, scope labels, and capability-tier summaries | Layer 0 audits and governs claims; it does not produce empirical evidence |
| Layer 1 — Public-Data and Protocol Anchor | Provides clean source-record lineage for datasets, windows, splits, preprocessing, labels, artifact flags, cards, validation, and manifests | Layer 1 source records remain immutable |
| Layer 2 — Decoder and Baseline Measurement Spine | Provides prediction evidence, decoder/baseline summaries, low-calibration curves, baseline sufficiency evidence, decoder cards, and failure indices | Layer 2 owns decoder evidence |
| Layer 3 — Calibration, Uncertainty, and Selective Prediction | Provides calibration, uncertainty, threshold, selective-prediction, leakage, reliability, and matched operating-point evidence | Layer 3 owns calibration/uncertainty/selective-prediction evidence |
| Layer 4 — IHARQ Evidence Verification | Provides IHARQ-lite decision, evidence-quality, combined-evidence, fallback, unsafe-event, trace, and comparison evidence | IHARQ remains separate from Adaptive-IHARQ |
| Layer 5 — RegimeRisk Temporal Trust Monitoring | Provides temporal-trust/regime-risk outputs, timelines, warnings, and temporal limitation evidence | RegimeRisk remains separate from IHARQ and policy learning |
| Layer 6 — Adaptive Readiness Policy Layer | Provides readiness-context, evidence-quality estimator, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, policy-action, pseudo-label/cost, and policy-update governance evidence | Layer 6 owns readiness-policy and policy-action records |
| Layer 7 — Simulated Closed-Loop Readiness Environment | Provides transition/session/episode/rollout/reward/environment diagnostic evidence and disabled-update audit outputs | Layer 7 owns simulation records and does not become real deployment evidence |
| Layer 8 — StressForge-Lite | Provides stress profiles, schedules, manifests, stress-conditioned comparison results, stress validity reports, and stress-only limitations | StressForge-Lite remains Layer 8-owned and bounded |
| Layer 9 — MyoSuite / OpenSim / Static-Replay Embodiment | Provides embodiment state/outcome records, command mappings, safety-event logs, demo manifests, optional OpenSim outputs, and proxy-only limitation evidence | Embodiment remains Layer 9-owned and simulation/proxy-only |
| Layer 10 — Dashboard, Cards, and Reproducibility Layer | Provides dashboard metrics/views, cards, static exports, figures, tables, export manifests, reproducibility manifests, warnings, and source-lineage bundles | Layer 10 outputs are derived/read-export artifacts, not primary evidence |

### 5.2 Module participation

| Module or module family | Phase 15 participation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Claim boundary checker / clinical non-claim guard | Checks every claim against allowed and forbidden classes | Required |
| Scope, readiness-status, and capability-tier labeler | Assigns core/target/stretch/optional/diagnostic/future-work and C0–C4 labels where supported | Required, with C0–C4 vocabulary confirmation caveat |
| Evidence provenance tracker / final evidence governance | Builds or validates `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` and claim-to-artifact mappings | Required, exact schema/path unresolved |

| Final demonstration contract modules | Demonstration scope gate, capability-tier synthesizer, demonstration-evidence matrix builder, claim-to-artifact ledger, negative-result interpreter, reproducibility acceptance checker, and stretch completion reporter | Required as synthesis modules where the final demonstration contract is used |
| Layer 10 export/manifest/card readers | Read dashboard exports, cards, static figures/tables, and reproducibility manifests | Required |
| Upstream evidence producers | Layers 1–9 remain producers of their own records | Read-only consumption by Phase 15 |
| Policy/stress/embodiment executors | Not executed by Phase 15 | `not_applicable_with_reason`: Phase 15 audits and cites saved artifacts only |

### 5.3 Boundary rules preserved

Phase 15 preserves the following boundaries:

- A0–A13 are evaluation-use metadata, not artifact owners.
- C0–C4 are capability-tier claim-maturity summaries and stopping-point labels, not implementation phases.
- Layer 10 may read/export/summarize but must not silently recompute hidden experimental logic.
- Layer 0 may approve, weaken, reject, or limit claims but does not produce empirical evidence.
- Optional Phase 13 OpenSim outputs may be used only as optional plausibility visualization or future-work appendix material unless validated under the architecture’s bounded rules.
- Negative results and baseline sufficiency are thesis evidence, not failures to hide.

| Stretch completion report | Architecture-supported final demonstration artifact | Phase 15 final demonstration synthesis | Thesis discussion/future work | Optional/stretch branch status, evidence support, diagnostic-only/future-work labels |
| `ClaimImpactMatrix` | Architecture-supported defensive-design/final-integration artifact; not a new empirical record | Phase 15 / Layer 0 claim-safety synthesis | Results, discussion, limitation section, claim-safety dashboard/export where present | Claim ID, missing/invalid evidence reason, weakened/narrowed/invalid/prohibited claim effect, repair or downgrade status |
| `ReproducibilityAuditChecklist` | Architecture-supported reproducibility audit artifact; may align with final-demo reproducibility readiness checklist | Phase 15 / Layer 10 reproducibility package | Repository release, examiner audit, reproducibility appendix | Required seeds, versions, hashes, manifests, schemas, figure/table source mappings, unresolved items |
| Limitation-language map / `ThesisLimitationLanguageMap` | Architecture-supported limitation-language artifact; exact file/schema may remain repository-mapped | Phase 15 / Layer 0 claim-safety review | Thesis limitation section, defense slides, cards, future reporting | Allowed wording, prohibited wording, evidence mode, strictest limitation tag, unresolved issue references |

### 10.2 Prepared outputs

| Prepared output | Purpose | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Defense slide evidence map | Converts final claim map into defense-friendly narrative | Prepared from thesis artifacts; not a primary evidence record |
| Repository release checklist | Confirms packaging, manifests, warnings, and reproducibility readiness | Prepared from artifact appendix and reproducibility checklist |
| Paper/reporting claim subset | Narrows thesis claims for future paper or report | Prepared only after Layer 0 claim review |

### 10.3 Output rejection rules

An output is not thesis-ready if it:

- lacks source-record lineage;
- lacks required metric dictionary entries;
- lacks matched-comparison support for a comparative claim;
- hides negative results;
- removes diagnostic-only or limitation labels;
- cites dashboard-derived outputs as primary evidence;
- cites stress/embodiment/OpenSim branches without proxy/optional limitations;
- mixes update-enabled training/adaptation evidence with frozen-policy evaluation;
- implies clinical, patient-safety, medical-device, rehabilitation, real muscle-control, deployment, or real assistive-control claims.

## 12. Evidence-Production Logic

Phase 15 evidence-production logic is a synthesis chain, not a new empirical pipeline:

```text
validated upstream records and manifests
→ metric dictionary and matched-comparison verification
→ dashboard/card/export lineage verification
→ negative-result and missingness inventory
→ claim-safety and limitation audit
→ capability-tier synthesis
→ claim-to-artifact mapping
→ manuscript chapter integration
→ reproduction guide and repository appendix
→ final thesis / defense / release package
```

### 12.1 Claim integration logic

For each major thesis claim, Phase 15 must identify:

1. claim ID and claim wording;
2. supported evidence mode, such as public-data, low-calibration, proxy-label, simulation-only, stress-conditioned, embodiment-proxy, dashboard/reproducibility, diagnostic-only, or future-work-only;
3. source records and producing layers;
4. metric dictionary entries for all metrics;
5. matched-comparison report where the claim is comparative;
6. ablation IDs A0–A13 where applicable, as evaluation-use metadata only;
7. dashboard metric/view/card/figure/table/export IDs where used;
8. negative-result notes or baseline-sufficiency notes where relevant;
9. limitation statements and forbidden claim classes;
10. final status: approved, weakened, diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work-only, rejected, invalid-due-to-leakage, invalid-due-to-claim-violation, or non-thesis-ready.

### 12.2 Manuscript integration logic

The thesis manuscript must be written from saved artifacts:

- Architecture and methods chapters describe the already-defined layers, phase order, record contracts, evaluation ladder, repository plan, and claim boundaries.
- Evaluation and results chapters cite validated records, metric dictionary entries, matched-comparison reports, dashboard/card/export artifacts, and negative-result notes.
- Discussion and limitations chapters explicitly report weak results, baseline-sufficient results, diagnostic-only outcomes, optional/stretch branch status, proxy/simulation/embodiment limitations, and unresolved registry issues.
- Reproducibility appendix cites schemas, configs, run IDs, config hashes, seeds, manifests, export packages, and reproduction guide.
- Defense package summarizes the same evidence without elevating claim strength.

### 12.3 Loopback logic

Phase 15 may create controlled loopback requests only when a claim lacks evidence or limitation. Allowed loopbacks are:

- add a missing artifact reference;
- rerun or regenerate a prior artifact only through the owning prior phase and with new run/manifest lineage;
- add a missing limitation or negative-result note;
- downgrade a claim to diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work-only, or removed.

Phase 15 may not loop back to tune on test outcomes, hide negative results, bypass ownership, or silently repair records inside the thesis.

## 13. Validation Gates and Exit Conditions

### 13.1 Validation gates

| Gate | What it checks | Failure handling |
|---|---|---|
| Claim-evidence gate | Every major claim maps to source records, metrics, ablations where applicable, figures/tables/cards, limitations, and manifests | Claim is weakened, diagnostic-only, future-work-only, or removed |
| Schema and manifest gate | All cited records/artifacts validate against schemas and appear in manifests | Artifact cannot support thesis-facing claim |
| Metric dictionary gate | Every metric in thesis figures/tables/cards has a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or metric dictionary reference | Metric is diagnostic-only |
| Matched-comparison gate | Every comparative claim has matched keys/report or explicitly states unmatched exploratory status | Comparative claim blocked or downgraded |
| Negative-result gate | Weak/null/baseline-sufficient/failed/diagnostic results have `NegativeResultNote` coverage and are visible | Claim-safety violation; thesis package incomplete |
| Dashboard lineage gate | Every figure/table/card/dashboard export links to saved source records, configs, seeds where applicable, and export manifests | Export blocked or regenerated from records |
| Layer 0 claim-safety gate | Claim wording avoids forbidden clinical/deployment/real-patient/medical-device/rehabilitation/muscle-control/assistive-control claims | Claim rejected or rewritten |
| Capability-tier gate | Highest claimed C0–C4 tier has required evidence and missing branch labels | Tier claim narrowed |
| Frozen/update separation gate | Adaptive, bandit, RL, simulation, stress, and embodiment feedback contexts separate training/adaptation from held-out frozen evaluation | Policy claim diagnostic-only or invalid |
| Optional/stretch branch gate | Phase 12/13/OpenSim/bandit/RL/stretch artifacts are not treated as core unless required evidence passes | Branch marked optional-only, skipped, or future-work-only |
| Repository/reproducibility gate | Reproduction guide, artifact appendix, checksums where feasible, environment/tool versions, configs, seeds, and manifests are present | Repository release claim weakened |

### 13.2 Exit condition

Phase 15 exits successfully when:

```text
Every major thesis claim is either supported by validated artifacts and explicit lineage,
or explicitly bounded by a limitation, diagnostic-only label, optional-only label,
future-work label, skipped branch status, or negative-result interpretation.
Unsupported claims are removed.
The highest completed capability tier is clear.
The manuscript, artifact appendix, reproduction guide, repository package,
dashboard/card exports, and claim-evidence matrix are mutually consistent.
```

### 13.3 Blocking failures

Phase 15 is blocked from final thesis release if:

- a core claim lacks source evidence and lacks a limitation statement;
- a comparative claim lacks matched-comparison support;
- a metric-bearing claim lacks metric dictionary support;
- the final manuscript contains forbidden clinical/deployment/real-patient/medical-device/rehabilitation/real muscle-control/real assistive-control wording;
- dashboard outputs are used without source-record lineage;
- negative results are omitted;
- update-enabled training and frozen evaluation are merged;
- an optional/stretch branch is represented as core evidence without validation.

## 14. Matched-Comparison Key Preservation

### 14.1 Required key families

Phase 15 must preserve matched-comparison keys from the original source records through final claims. Required keys include, where applicable:

```text
source_record_ids
run_id
config_hash
seed
schema_version
producer_module
phase_id
ablation_id
claim_safety_tags
validation_status
dataset_id
subject_id
session_id
trial_id
window_id
split_id
split_role
preprocessing_id
label_map_id
model_id
calibration_id
threshold_registry_id
policy_id
stress_profile_id
embodiment_mode_id
```

### 14.2 Comparison rules

| Comparison type | Required preservation | Diagnostic-only condition |
|---|---|---|
| A0/A4 baseline comparison | Dataset, subject, session, split, window, preprocessing, label map, model, seed/config where applicable | Missing matched keys or baseline-control lineage |
| A1–A3 calibration/uncertainty/selective comparison | Prediction, calibration, uncertainty, threshold, split role, metric dictionary, matched operating point | Test-tuned threshold, missing calibration lineage, missing metric dictionary |
| A5–A7 IHARQ/RegimeRisk comparison | IHARQ decision, evidence quality, regime state, threshold/baseline controls, cost/coverage keys | Unmatched coverage/cost or missing reason/action lineage |
| A8–A11 policy comparison | Readiness context, pseudo-label/cost config, policy ID, update trace, held-out split/session, frozen/update status | Missing pseudo-label manifest, update trace, or held-out frozen evaluation |
| A12 stress comparison | Clean/stressed pairing, stress profile/schedule/run manifest, seed, affected source records | Missing clean-paired run or stress-profile lineage |
| A13 embodiment comparison/demo | Embodiment mode, command mapping, safety-event IDs, endpoint/outcome IDs, demo manifest, optional OpenSim manifest | Missing mapping/demo/safety lineage or proxy-only limitation |
| Figure/table/card/export comparison | Source-record IDs, metric dictionary entries, dashboard metric/view/card IDs, export manifest IDs | Dashboard-only value with no source lineage |

### 14.3 Final claim linkage

A final claim may cite a matched-comparison result only when the `MatchedComparisonReport` or equivalent report identifies the matched keys and the metric dictionary defines the reported metric. If a comparison is unmatched, it may still appear in the thesis only as exploratory, diagnostic-only, or limitation evidence.

## 15. Ablation, Evaluation, and Explicit Evaluation-Artifact Linkage

### 15.1 A0–A13 linkage

A0–A13 remain evaluation-use metadata only. Phase 15 may claim that it summarizes, cites, or integrates records used by A0–A13. It must not say that an ablation produced a canonical source record.

| Ablation/evaluation ID | Phase 15 use | Required evaluation artifacts |
|---|---|---|
| A0 — raw decoder | Baseline decoder evidence and minimum public-data reliability spine | `PredictionRecord`, metric dictionary entries, baseline table, matched keys, negative notes where needed |
| A1 — calibrated decoder | Calibration quality and reliability visibility | `CalibrationRecord`, reliability diagrams, metric dictionary entries, negative notes |
| A2 — simple registered threshold / confidence-threshold baseline | Threshold and retained-coverage/retained-accuracy baseline | `SelectivePredictionRecord`, `ThresholdRegistryRecord`, matched operating-point table/report |
| A3 — uncertainty and selective prediction | Uncertainty/selective evidence where defined by Phase 3 records | Matched prediction/calibration/uncertainty/threshold/split keys, metrics, negative notes |
| A4 — longer-window, multi-window voting/averaging, and ordinary ensemble controls | Ordinary control/baseline sufficiency | Baseline comparison table, matched report, metric dictionary |
| A5 — IHARQ-lite | Evidence-verification claims | `IHARQDecisionRecord`, reason/action distributions, matched comparison, negative notes |
| A6 — IHARQ + evidence-quality estimator | Evidence-quality-enhanced IHARQ evidence | `EvidenceQualityRecord` with producer/variant tags, matched comparison |
| A7 — IHARQ + RegimeRisk | Temporal-trust context and RegimeRisk-linked readiness evidence | `RegimeStateRecord`, temporal reports, matched comparison where comparative |
| A8 — learning-to-defer | Deferral/cost/coverage evidence | `DeferralRecord`, pseudo-label/cost manifests, held-out evaluation |
| A9 — supervised Adaptive-IHARQ | Supervised readiness-policy evidence | `ReadinessContextRecord`, `PolicyActionRecord`, proxy-label/cost audit |
| A10 — contextual bandit | Update-enabled/frozen evaluation evidence where implemented | `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit, regret/adaptation/frozen evaluation tables |
| A11 — reinforcement-learning policy | RL stretch evidence where implemented | Reward config, policy records, training/frozen separation, held-out evaluation |
| A12 — StressForge stress tests | Stress-conditioned robustness evidence | `StressProfileRecord`, `StressScheduleRecord`, stress-run manifest, stress comparison report |
| A13 — Layer 9 embodiment demo | Simulation/proxy embodiment evidence where implemented | `EmbodimentStateRecord`, `EmbodimentOutcomeRecord`, safety-event logs, demo manifest, optional OpenSim manifest |

### 15.2 Explicit evaluation artifacts required by Phase 15

| Artifact | Required when | Phase 15 rule |
|---|---|---|
| `MetricDictionaryEntry` / metric dictionary | Any metric appears in thesis, table, card, or figure | Missing entry makes metric diagnostic-only |
| `MatchedComparisonReport` | Any comparative claim is made | Missing report blocks comparative claim |
| `EvaluationOutcomeRecord` where produced | Evaluation outcome is cited from a layer that produces it | Must preserve layer ownership and source IDs |
| `NegativeResultNote` | Result is weak, null, failed, baseline-sufficient, diagnostic-only, or incomplete | Must be included in negative-result register/index |
| `DiagnosticOnlyFlag` | Evidence lacks required lineage, metric, match, validation, or claim-safety coverage | Must remain visible in thesis and dashboard exports |
| `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` | Any major thesis claim is made | Must map claim to evidence or limitation |
| Final demonstration matrices | Final demonstration is included | Must read saved upstream artifacts only |

### 15.3 Evaluation claim discipline

Phase 15 may state evidence-supported comparisons only if they satisfy metric dictionary, matched-comparison, source-record, and claim-safety requirements. When IHARQ, RegimeRisk, Adaptive-IHARQ, bandit/RL, stress, or embodiment results do not improve over simpler baselines under matched conditions, the final thesis must describe the negative or baseline-sufficient result and narrow the claim accordingly.

### 16.1 Layer 10 input/output separation

| Category | Phase 15 examples | Phase 15 handling |

| Dashboard-readable source records | Layer 1–9 validated source and derived evidence records, evaluation artifacts, `MetricDictionaryEntry`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `NegativeResultNote`, `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` views | Read and cite through lineage; do not overwrite |

| Not-dashboard inputs | Raw EEG, model training internals, hidden notebook cells, unvalidated local computations, unmanifested screenshots | Not allowed as final evidence unless produced by the owning upstream phase and recorded |

### 16.2 Reproducibility obligations

Phase 15 must produce or finalize:

- reproduction guide;
- artifact appendix;
- repository release checklist;
- final card/export inventory;

- source-record bundle index;

### 16.3 Layer 10 restrictions

Layer 10 outputs may be cited only as derived representations of source evidence. Phase 15 must not allow final thesis text to imply that a dashboard page, card, figure, or export is itself the upstream empirical producer. If a dashboard export lacks source-record lineage or warning coverage, it must be regenerated from saved records by Phase 14 or excluded from Phase 15 claim-facing use.

## 17. Claim-Safety and Limitation Boundaries

### 17.1 Allowed claim types

Phase 15 may support bounded claims about:

- public EEG reliability evaluation;
- low-calibration neural-intent readiness evidence;
- calibration and uncertainty visibility;
- selective prediction and threshold behavior;
- IHARQ-style evidence verification;
- temporal trust monitoring through RegimeRisk;
- adaptive readiness policy evaluation under public-data/proxy-label constraints;
- learning-to-defer and cost-sensitive policy evaluation;
- simulation-only closed-loop readiness behavior;
- stress-conditioned robustness testing through StressForge-Lite;
- simulation-only/proxy-only embodiment demonstration through MyoSuite/OpenSim/static replay;
- dashboard/reproducibility traceability;
- final thesis evidence traceability and claim-safety governance.

### 17.2 Forbidden claim types

Phase 15 must not support claims about:

- clinical BCI-FES validation;
- real patient safety;
- medical-device readiness;
- real rehabilitation efficacy;
- real muscle stimulation control;
- real deployment readiness;
- real assistive-control safety;
- real-time clinical readiness;
- patient-specific biomechanics validation;
- therapeutic efficacy;
- validated physiological fatigue or medical drift diagnosis;
- real-world FES/exoskeleton safety.

### 17.3 Required limitation tags

The final claim package must preserve the strictest applicable tags, including:

```text
public_eeg_only
low_calibration_protocol
proxy_readiness
pseudo_label_based
evaluation_only
simulation_only
stress_conditioned
stress_only
embodiment_proxy_only
MyoSuite_OpenSim_demo_only
diagnostic_only
optional_only
future_work_only
skipped_non_blocking
non_thesis_ready
invalid_due_to_leakage
invalid_due_to_claim_violation
not_clinical_validation
not_real_patient_safety
not_medical_device_readiness
not_real_rehabilitation_efficacy
not_real_muscle_stimulation_control
not_deployment_readiness
not_real_assistive_control_safety
```

### 17.4 Claim downgrade conditions

A claim must be downgraded, rejected, or moved to future work when:

- source records are missing or invalid;
- metrics lack dictionary entries;
- comparative claims lack matched reports;
- limitations are missing;
- negative results are hidden;
- dashboard outputs lack source lineage;
- stress/embodiment/OpenSim evidence lacks proxy-only or optional labels;
- policy-update evidence lacks trace/audit/frozen-evaluation separation;
- the claim wording implies any forbidden clinical/deployment/real-world safety meaning.

### 17.5 Layer 0 review requirements

Before final thesis release, Layer 0 must review:

- final claim wording;
- claim-to-artifact matrix / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`;
- limitation map;
- negative-result register/index;
- diagnostic-only, optional-only, future-work, skipped, invalid, and non-thesis-ready statuses;
- C0–C4 capability-tier summary;
- final figures/tables/cards and captions;
- defense slide claim wording;
- repository README/release wording.

## 18. Capability-Tier Linkage and Claim-Maturity Governance

C0–C4 are not implementation phases, not ablation IDs, and not artifact owners. Phase 15 uses them only to summarize the highest validated thesis-ready stopping point.

| Capability tier | Architecture-defined evidence basis | Phase 15 governance |
|---|---|---|
| C0 | Phases 0–3: public EEG low-calibration reliability benchmark with standardized records, fixed splits, baseline decoders, calibrated uncertainty, selective-prediction baselines, reliability diagrams, and high-confidence-wrong audits | Minimum empirical spine; valid only if records, metrics, leakage checks, and limitations pass |
| C1 | Phases 0–5: IHARQ-lite evidence verification and RegimeRisk temporal-trust characterization with reason-coded readiness decisions and interpretable baseline comparisons | Minimum IHARQ/RegimeRisk contribution; comparative claims require matched cost/coverage |
| C2 | Phases 0–7: evidence-quality estimation, supervised Adaptive-IHARQ, learning-to-defer, cost-sensitive pseudo-label analysis, matched-cost/matched-coverage comparisons, and proxy-label limitations | Strong learned-readiness contribution; no real readiness-label claim |
| C3 | Phases 0–11: simulated closed-loop policy-learning evaluation, StressForge robustness tests, contextual bandit adaptation, optional RL, reward sensitivity, and simulation-only claim tags | Simulation-only stretch contribution; frozen/update separation required |
| C4 | Phases 0–15: maximum Stretch C artifact with Layer 9 simulated embodiment/static replay, optional OpenSim replay, Layer 10 read-only observability, cards, thesis figures, traceability matrix, repository manifest, and final claim-safety documentation | Full Stretch C synthesis; still simulation/proxy/non-clinical and not deployment-ready |

### 18.1 Highest-tier determination

Phase 15 must set the highest defensible tier by the weakest required evidence source. If C4 stretch branches are incomplete, the thesis remains valid at C0, C1, C2, or C3 as long as claims are narrowed and unfinished branches are classified honestly.

### 18.2 Tier claim restrictions

- C0 cannot imply IHARQ, RegimeRisk, adaptive policy, stress, or embodiment completion.
- C1 cannot imply learned policy or closed-loop simulation readiness.
- C2 cannot imply bandit/RL, stress-conditioned robustness, or embodiment completion unless those records pass.
- C3 cannot imply real deployment or embodiment validation.
- C4 cannot imply clinical, real patient safety, medical-device, real rehabilitation, real muscle-control, or real assistive-control safety.

## 19. Negative-Result and Baseline-Sufficiency Handling

### 19.1 Required negative-result handling

Phase 15 must include negative or limiting outcomes when:

- calibration does not improve ECE/Brier/NLL or reliability;
- selective prediction or thresholding is sufficient and advanced methods do not add value;
- longer windows, voting, averaging, or ensembles match IHARQ;
- IHARQ increases request, fallback, delay, or cost burden without sufficient benefit;
- RegimeRisk does not improve decisions and only characterizes temporal risk;
- supervised Adaptive-IHARQ or learning-to-defer is unstable, imbalanced, or proxy-label dominated;
- contextual bandit or RL does not improve held-out frozen evaluation;
- stress tests reveal fragility or only diagnostic robustness;
- embodiment mappings fail, produce unsafe blocked-command patterns, or remain proxy-only;
- OpenSim replay is skipped, incomplete, or only visualization;
- dashboard/export completeness is insufficient for claim-facing use.

### 19.2 Baseline-sufficiency rule

If a simpler baseline is sufficient under matched metrics, cost, coverage, or risk, the thesis must state that clearly. Baseline sufficiency is a valid scientific result and must not be hidden to make Stretch C appear stronger.

### 19.3 Negative-result register/index

The final negative-result register/index must be built from `NegativeResultNote` entries and linked to:

- affected claim IDs;
- source records;
- metric dictionary entries;
- matched-comparison reports;
- figures/tables/cards;
- limitation statements;
- fallback or downgraded claim status;
- final thesis discussion location.

## 20. Failure, Missingness, and Diagnostic-Only Rules

| Failure or missingness case | Phase 15 consequence |
|---|---|
| Missing source record lineage | Claim blocked or diagnostic-only |
| Missing schema validation | Artifact not thesis-ready |
| Missing metric dictionary entry | Metric diagnostic-only |
| Missing matched-comparison report for comparative claim | Comparative wording removed or diagnostic-only |
| Missing negative-result note for weak/null/failed outcome | Claim-safety gate fails |
| Missing limitation tag | Claim blocked until limitation added |
| Missing dashboard source lineage | Figure/table/card/export excluded |
| Hidden dashboard recomputation | Export invalid; Phase 14 repair required |
| Missing `PolicyUpdateTrace` for update-enabled evidence | Adaptive policy claim diagnostic-only |
| Missing disabled-update audit for frozen evaluation | Frozen-policy comparison invalid or diagnostic-only |
| Mixed training/adaptation and frozen evaluation curves | Policy claim invalid until separated |
| Missing stress profile/schedule/run manifest | Stress claim diagnostic-only |
| Missing clean/stressed pairing | Stress comparison invalid |
| Missing embodiment command mapping | Embodiment claim blocked |
| Missing safety-event log where safety events are claimed | Embodiment/stress safety claim blocked |
| Missing `Layer9EmbodimentDemoManifest` | A13/C4 embodiment claim diagnostic-only or optional-only |
| Missing Phase 13 OpenSim manifest where OpenSim is shown | OpenSim branch skipped/future-work-only/diagnostic-only |
| Unresolved repository path without manifest mapping | Reproducibility claim weakened |
| Forbidden claim wording | Claim rejected as invalid due to claim violation |

### 20.1 Diagnostic-only preservation

Diagnostic-only status must appear in:

- `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`;
- final claim map;
- negative-result register/index;
- thesis results/discussion text;
- captions or notes for affected figures/tables/cards;
- defense slides where affected outputs are shown;
- repository release notes or artifact appendix.

## 21. Repository and Storage Expectations

### 21.1 Repository expectations

Phase 15 must preserve the repository architecture without inventing unsupported paths. Where the architecture explicitly names final demonstration paths, they may be used as synthesis artifacts; otherwise, repository locations must be referenced through manifest mappings until `MC-009` is resolved.

Required repository/release package contents include:

- final manuscript source or compiled thesis artifact where applicable;
- architecture/method/evaluation/results/discussion/limitations chapter sources;
- artifact appendix;
- reproduction guide;
- `ClaimEvidenceMatrix` or matrix/manifest-linked equivalent;
- claim-to-artifact matrix;
- demonstration evidence matrix;

## 26. Phase Definition of Done

Phase 15 is definition-of-done complete when all of the following are satisfied:

1. The combined Markdown file preserves Phase 0–14 predecessor sections above this Phase 15 section.
2. The section uses the official identity `Phase 15 — Final thesis integration`.
3. The Phase 0 inheritance check is complete, including schemas, configs, validators, run IDs, config hashes, seeds, manifests, metric dictionary placeholders, claim-evidence placeholders, dashboard/export placeholders, repository skeleton expectations, and unresolved schema/path caveats.
4. All prior phase outputs required by the highest claimed capability tier are either validated, explicitly missing, diagnostic-only, optional-only, skipped, future-work-only, or non-thesis-ready.
5. Every major thesis claim appears in the claim-to-artifact matrix / `ClaimEvidenceMatrix`.
6. Every major claim maps to source records, metrics, ablations where applicable, figures/tables/cards, limitations, and manifests, or is explicitly bounded by a limitation.
7. Every thesis-facing metric has a `MetricDictionaryEntry` or metric dictionary reference; otherwise the metric is diagnostic-only.
8. Every comparative claim has matched-comparison support; otherwise the claim is diagnostic-only or written as exploratory/unmatched.
9. Every weak, null, failed, baseline-sufficient, diagnostic-only, or incomplete result has `NegativeResultNote` coverage and appears in the negative-result register/index.
10. Baseline sufficiency is reported rather than hidden when simpler baselines match or outperform advanced phases.
11. Dashboard/card/export artifacts used in the thesis have source-record lineage, config/hash references where applicable, warning coverage, and manifest links.
12. Layer 10 outputs are presented as derived/export artifacts, not primary upstream empirical evidence.
13. Layer 0 review has approved, weakened, rejected, or bounded every claim-facing output.
14. Forbidden claims about clinical BCI-FES validation, real patient safety, medical-device readiness, real rehabilitation efficacy, real muscle stimulation control, real assistive-control safety, and deployment readiness are absent.
15. Public-data, proxy-label, simulation-only, stress-conditioned, embodiment-proxy, optional, skipped, future-work, and diagnostic-only boundaries are visible in the thesis.
16. C0–C4 capability-tier status is reported only as claim-maturity/stopping-point summary.
17. Highest completed validated tier is clear.
18. Policy-update evidence preserves `PolicyUpdateTrace`, disabled-update audit, and training/adaptation versus frozen-evaluation separation where relevant.
19. Stress evidence preserves stress profile/schedule/run manifest, seed, clean/stressed pairing, and stress-only limitation tags.
20. Embodiment evidence preserves command mapping, safety-event logs, endpoint/outcome records, demo manifest, and proxy-only limitation tags.
21. OpenSim output, if shown, preserves optional branch status, output manifest, mapping limitations, and non-clinical/non-blocking warnings.
22. Artifact appendix and reproduction guide are complete enough to trace thesis figures/tables/cards to records, configs, seeds, manifests, and exports.
23. Repository release checklist, `ReproducibilityManifest`, `ReproducibilityAuditChecklist` or reproducibility readiness checklist, artifact manifest, export manifest, and package index are complete or unresolved items are listed explicitly.
24. Final demonstration evidence matrix, capability-tier summary, `ClaimImpactMatrix` where claim gaps exist, and limitation-language map where final limitation wording is formalized are produced where the final demonstration contract is used.
25. Open issues and confirmation requests are listed rather than silently repaired.
26. Unsupported claims are removed.

If Phase 15 cannot satisfy a required evidence link, it may still complete a lower-tier thesis by narrowing the highest completed capability tier and preserving unfinished branches as diagnostic-only, optional-only, skipped, or future-work-only. Phase 15 is not complete if unsupported or overbroad claims remain in the manuscript, defense package, repository release, or exported cards.

## CI-0. Preservation and no-drift statement

If any wording in this addendum appears to conflict with an already locked upstream authority, the locked authority remains controlling and this addendum must be interpreted as a candidate clarification requiring manual review.

The finalized Layer 1 package is treated as **method-selection/design-rationale authority for Layer 1 only**. It does not replace the Master Architecture Specification, the Canonical Registry, this document's existing phase/evaluation/playbook logic, the future Layer 1 nuts-and-bolts specification, the implementation build book, Layer 0 claim review, Layer 10 dashboard design, or the final paper/thesis evidence map.

## CI-5. Phase 1 evidence gates to carry forward

The following gates must be treated as Phase 1 / Layer 1 evidence gates for any selected or fallback dataset/protocol pair:

| Gate | Required evidence | Failure or uncertainty handling |
|---|---|---|
| Source/provenance gate | source/version/citation/license/access notes; source/provenance report; DatasetCard source fields | warn, diagnostic-only, fallback, exclusion, or NegativeResultNote depending on severity |
| Dataset metadata gate | subject/session/run/source-event/channel/sampling/timing metadata; metadata-completeness report | diagnostic-only or exclusion if identity cannot support split/window/readiness keys |
| Label/proxy-intent gate | LabelMapRecord, original labels, normalized labels, rest/no-action/excluded-label notes, Layer 0 claim tags | diagnostic-only or exclusion if labels are ambiguous or overclaim-prone |
| Preprocessing fit-scope gate | PreprocessingRecord and ValidationReport fit-scope audit | fail/downgrade if fitted transforms can see validation/test roles |
| Split and low-calibration gate | SplitRecord, split-role assignment, budget table, seed/config/hash evidence | fail/downgrade if subject/session/source-event/window leakage cannot be prevented |
| Window/source-event gate | WindowRecord, parent/source-event ID, overlap policy, timing checks | fail/downgrade if source-event lineage or timing cannot be recovered |
| Artifact/channel-quality gate | ArtifactFlagRecord where available, limitation notes when unavailable | warn/downgrade quality-sensitive claims; do not silently repair confirmatory evidence |
| Validation/leakage gate | ValidationReport plus leakage and matched-key completeness reports | block downstream thesis-ready use until passed or explicitly downgraded |
| Governance/card/manifest gate | DatasetCard, ProtocolCard, Layer1Manifest, readiness JSON, Layer 10 and Layer 0 fields | not thesis-ready if card/manifest/readiness/claim tags are incomplete |
| Live smoke-test gate | implementation-time loader/access/record-writing smoke test | remains pending here; do not claim live public EEG loading from method selection alone |

## CI-6. Future-layer evidence handoff rule

Future Layers 2–10 must consume Layer 1 through the produced records, cards, manifests, readiness JSON, ValidationReport, and claim tags. They must not reselect Layer 1 datasets, reinterpret source labels, repair split leakage, remove diagnostic-only status, or bypass missing-key warnings unless a formal method-selection reopen or registry/evaluation patch is accepted.

## E4. Phase 1 evidence gates

```text
source/provenance evidence;
metadata and hierarchy completeness;
contextual exact-one label coverage;
preprocessing fit authorization and inherited-transform separation;
split/source-event group disjointness and budget integrity;
parent-bounded window lineage and temporal-contamination checks;
quality/artifact evidence or explicit unavailable-quality limitation;
single canonical ValidationReport;
card/manifest/readiness reference and limitation consistency;
matched-key completeness for A0–A13 source readiness;
Layer 0 claim-tag completeness;
Layer 10 read-only visibility;
repeated-generation and digest consistency;
atomic publication or rollback.
```

Failure behavior is fail-closed. A failed prerequisite may produce a visible blocked, diagnostic-only, excluded, future-work, or negative-result disposition; it may not be silently repaired or omitted from the evidence denominator.

# Layer 1 bidirectional execution/evidence synchronization addendum — R19

## E7. Purpose and authority

R19 preserves R18 and makes the Phase 1 evidence contract explicitly two-way.

The synchronization is bidirectional in traceability and change propagation, but not symmetrical in authority. Architecture, Registry, Execution Plan, Experiment Protocol, Phase Playbook, Method Selection Register and the Layer 1 framework retain their respective normative domains. M10 may supply evidence-backed specialization and update proposals to those owners; it may not override them locally. Conversely, an accepted upstream change must be propagated into a versioned Layer 1 successor and all affected records, cards, manifests, readiness evidence, tests and downstream consumers.

## E8. Plan-to-Layer-1 direction

The Plan defines required evidence, evidence owners, Phase 1 entry/exit gates, matched-key completeness, negative-result visibility and downstream evidence lifecycle. M10 and the Build Book must materialize and validate those obligations without reclassifying supporting evidence as canonical.

## E9. Layer-1-to-Plan direction

M10 supplies the exact producer chain, 52 output families, source/adapter limitations, validation feasibility, atomic publication behavior and runtime gates. If a Plan-required output is not technically producible, the first response is an internal adapter/validator/transformation solution. If the expected evidence itself must change, the Plan and all dependent documents are synchronized before implementation proceeds.

## E10. Evidence change invalidation

Adding, removing or reclassifying evidence requires versioned updates to the output matrix, module contracts, ValidationReport checks, cards, manifest/readiness projections, Playbook exit gate and downstream evidence consumers. Previously published evidence remains immutable and is marked superseded or invalidated.

## E11. Complete current coverage

The 11 canonical plus 41 supporting output families are bidirectionally traced. Each has an authoritative producer, consumer set, validation mode, remaining gate and reverse synchronization rule in the R19 52-output matrix.

## E12. Current status

Design-level evidence coverage is complete. Live source execution, Build Book realization, final Protocol numerics, Layer 0 approval and final validation/freeze remain active gates.




## R20 bidirectional integrity and compatibility lock

**Compatibility set:** `L1-BISYNC-R20-20260714`  
**Preservation rule:** the complete R19 predecessor is retained byte-for-byte in this successor.

# R23 Layer 2 Nuts-and-Bolts Finalization Synchronization Addendum

## R23.1 Evidence-plan effect

The finalized M7 design supplies the missing Phase 2 internal evidence-production detail without altering phase identity, order, claim boundaries or downstream ownership. Phase 2 remains the baseline-decoder and measurement phase. Its design deliverable is now `GREEN-LIT — CURRENT STAGE COMPLETE` and `GREEN-LIT — HANDOFF READY`; live Phase 2 artifacts remain `GREEN-LIT TO BEGIN — FUTURE EXECUTION` when frozen Layer 1 inputs and implementation prerequisites exist.

## R23.2 Frozen Phase 2 intake

Phase 2 consumes, without mutation, the effective Phase 0 schema/config/run/seed/metric/manifest foundations and the finalized Layer 1 `DatasetRecord`, `WindowRecord`, `SplitRecord`, `PreprocessingRecord`, `LabelMapRecord`, optional `ArtifactFlagRecord`, cards, `ValidationReport`, `Layer1Manifest`, and `layer1_ablation_readiness_l1_v1.json`. Any incompatibility produces a visible blocked, unsupported, failed, excluded, conditional or diagnostic result; it never triggers silent repair, subject/session/channel/class dropping or a more permissive upstream interpretation.

## R23.3 Module-level evidence obligations

| Module | Evidence obligation | Required outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline trainer | Execute accepted branches under frozen splits/budgets/seeds and retain complete success/failure/resource evidence. | trained artifacts, checkpoints, training/validation/tuning/resource/failure logs, registry content |
| Prediction logger | Produce immutable canonical raw predictions with legal score/class/time/truth visibility. | `PredictionRecord`, inference and missing-output evidence |
| Low-calibration curve builder | Measure legal nested budgets without redesigning Layer 1 budgets. | `LowCalibrationCurveRecord`, support/failure summaries |
| Subject difficulty profiler | Produce descriptive common-support participant/session evidence. | `SubjectProfileRecord`, limitation/omission evidence |
| Model-family registry | Maintain immutable model/config/transform/checkpoint/provenance identity. | `ModelRegistryRecord`, failed/skipped/unsupported inventory, card-source fields |
| Ensemble comparison builder | Produce fixed ordinary A4 controls under matched conditions. | `EnsembleControlRecord`, disagreement, burden, missing/tie evidence |
| Compact SSL adapter | Qualify conditional pretrained branches and create offline immutable bundles. | model bundle, provenance, compatibility/resource/failure evidence; no canonical prediction writing |
| Downstream readiness validator | Validate referential closure and branch×consumer prerequisites. | `Layer2ReadinessReport`, schema/missing/staleness/blocking evidence |

Cross-cutting evaluation and release functions additionally produce `BaselineMetricRecord`, `MatchedComparisonReport`, `FailureCaseIndex`, `LeakageWarningRecord`, `NegativeResultNote`, `DiagnosticOnlyFlag`, Layer 10 source snapshots, Layer 0 limitation evidence and Phase 2 freeze/handoff inputs.

## R23.4 Phase 2 definition of done

Phase 2 is complete only when all fourteen established steps have visible terminal evidence: frozen-input verification; model/resource/seed/budget declaration; baseline execution; model/provenance registration; canonical prediction production; A0 evidence; low-label evidence; participant/session profiles; A4 ordinary controls; failure/missingness reconciliation; consumer-specific readiness validation; Layer 10 source preparation; Layer 0 limitation attachment; and immutable Phase 2 freeze/Phase 3 handoff.

Every planned branch/cell must terminate as success, failed, blocked, unsupported, skipped, excluded or diagnostic-only under the effective governed vocabulary. Missing branches remain in denominator, coverage and limitation reporting.

## R23.5 Handoff and invalidation

- C1 outputs become legal C2 inputs only after model, artifact, class/score, transform, checkpoint and reload validation.
- C1/C2 evidence becomes legal C3 input only through immutable IDs/versions/hashes and complete terminal evidence.
- C3 readiness controls later-layer consumption; no later layer infers missing upstream content.
- Corrections create successors, mark dependent products stale, and trigger dependency-aware regeneration.
- Layer 10 renders source snapshots without repair or hidden recomputation.
- Layer 0 receives limitations and evidence sufficiency but retains final claim authority.

## R23.6 Remaining future evidence gates

Final live record bytes, real EEG performance, checkpoint/licence access, hardware measurements, exact Protocol v1.0 run/statistical settings, Build Book implementation and final claim approval remain not-yet-due owner/evidence gates rather than current design defects.

# R24 Layer 2 Bidirectional Evidence-Plan Synchronization Addendum

## R24.1 Authority boundary

The Evidence Plan controls Phase 2 purpose, required evidence, entry/exit gates, definitions of done, handoff sufficiency and evidence-retention obligations. M8 controls internal algorithms that satisfy those obligations. Neither document may silently assume the other's authority.

## R24.2 Module evidence closure

| Official module | Required evidence supplied under M8 | Evidence-Plan completion condition | Reverse change effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline trainer | declared cells, configs, seeds, budgets, fit-scope, training/validation/resource/failure logs, artifacts/checkpoints | every planned cell has one visible terminal outcome and complete provenance | changed evidence obligation updates C1 logging, terminal accounting and release graph |
| Prediction logger | immutable `PredictionRecord`, inference/missing-output evidence, class/score/time/reference checks | all eligible models produce validated predictions or visible terminal failures | changed prediction evidence updates C2 and all downstream consumers |
| Low-calibration curve builder | legal budget curves, support, invalid/sparse budget reasons | every governed budget is valid or visibly terminal | changed support/curve evidence updates C2 and Protocol mappings |
| Subject difficulty profiler | descriptive common-support profiles and omission reasons | no unsupported diagnosis/routing; opportunity sets disclosed | changed profile evidence updates C2 and consumer readiness |
| Model-family registry | immutable model versions, artifacts, checkpoints, environment/licence/reload evidence | all claim-bearing predictions resolve to a valid model version | changed registry evidence updates C1/C2/C3 linkage |
| Ensemble comparison builder | fixed A4 controls, member identities, ties, missingness, disagreement and burden | matched complete denominators and visible unresolved/zero-member cases | changed A4 evidence updates C2 and Protocol |
| Compact SSL adapter | checkpoint/corpus/licence/overlap/input/resource qualification or blocked result | conditional branch never disappears and never bypasses C2 writer | changed qualification evidence updates C1 and claim scope |
| Downstream readiness validator | terminal reconciliation, failures, referential/staleness checks, consumer readiness, source bundles and limitations | complete immutable Phase 2 freeze/handoff or explicit no-freeze | changed gate updates C3 and later-phase entry |

## R24.3 Two-way evidence workflow

An M8 technical refinement is acceptable without an Evidence Plan successor when it changes only the internal way an existing evidence obligation is fulfilled and preserves the same producer, source, gate and output. A change to required evidence, definition of done, phase entry/exit, retention, source authority or downstream handoff requires an Evidence Plan successor and an M8 impact review.

An accepted Evidence Plan change invalidates all evidence products whose completeness predicate or source requirement changed. Old evidence remains immutable and is marked stale/superseded rather than repaired.

## R24.4 Current definition of done

Phase 2 is design-complete when all eight modules and cross-cutting functions have specified inputs, outputs, algorithms, validators, failures, provenance and handoffs; it is empirically complete only after live execution produces a reconciled terminal graph, validated records, source bundles, limitation evidence and an immutable Phase 2 freeze. M8 satisfies the first condition, not the second.
