## 6. Definition-of-done additions

A Phase 4 branch is claim-supporting only when:

1. source/branch/capability eligibility and visibility are frozen;
2. threshold applicability and support-scope state are recorded;
3. every decision has a complete trace and canonical action/reason path;
4. conditional records obey emission/cardinality rules;
5. A5/local rows are eligible and matched with denominators/attrition;
6. metrics are approved or explicitly blocked/diagnostic;
7. negative, null, adverse, unmatched and overconservative outcomes are preserved;
8. reverse dependency closure is current;
9. Layer 10 and Layer 0 handoff evidence exists;
10. Gates 4.1–4.11 and exit facets are explicitly recorded.

## 7. Exit facets

The Plan successor must keep these facets separate: method-selection complete; Registry/profile disposition; N&B design complete; implementation/build complete; project-instance record conformance; Protocol v1.0/run-matrix complete; empirical gates; Layer 10 export readiness; Layer 0 claim review; reviewer sign-off; BPCR/reopen status.

## 8. No-change lock

No new phase, module, owner, product family or global ablation is introduced. Detailed formulas, pseudocode, state machines, schema syntax, paths and commands remain Layer 4 N&B/Build Book/Protocol v1.0 responsibilities.

## 5. Evidence mode, status and downgrade rules

Each evidence-producing branch records one of `success`, `degraded`, `diagnostic-only`, `blocked`, `inapplicable` or `superseded`, together with the narrowest reason, source/config closure and controlled-reopen predicate. Optional absence cannot invalidate unrelated branches; required-source absence blocks the affected branch. Evaluation-only evidence cannot become primary runtime evidence.

## 6. Staged freeze facets

The Phase 5 handoff records distinct status for: method selection; Registry profile; Layer 5 Nuts-and-Bolts; Build Book implementation; Protocol v1.0; executed empirical evidence; dashboard/export; claim readiness. No facet implies completion of another.

## 7. Definition-of-done additions

- [ ] All 47 decisions have effective implementation/evidence dispositions and exact configuration identity.
- [ ] All 15 Registry packages have owner status; blocking vocabulary/physical-schema issues are explicit.
- [ ] Every official output is produced, explicitly inapplicable, blocked or diagnostic-only—never silently absent.
- [ ] Every output resolves to source records, decision cutoff, visibility, horizon/support, configuration and validation status.
- [ ] Primary A7 common support, variants, controls, metrics and negative-result routes are Protocol-ready.
- [ ] Layer 10 and Layer 0 handoffs are source-bound and claim-safe.
- [ ] All readiness facets remain separate.

## 8. Reverse propagation and correction

Grounded upstream defects create a BPCR or source-owner correction request, not an in-place edit. Accepted source successors invalidate all dependent Layer 5 views, records and A7 reports through source/config closure. Regeneration creates new immutable IDs.

## 9. No-change lock

No formulas, thresholds, code paths, final run counts, statistical constants, empirical results or claims are introduced by this addendum. These remain Nuts-and-Bolts, Build Book, Protocol v1.0, executed evidence and Layer 0 responsibilities.

## 6. Evidence status and omission policy

Every expected branch or artifact must be recorded as one of:

`success`, `degraded`, `diagnostic-only`, `blocked`, `inapplicable`, `superseded`.

Silent absence is invalid. A conditional artifact may be omitted only with an explicit predicate result, reason, source/configuration context and consumer impact.

## 1. Purpose and precedence

The authority order remains Architecture → Canonical Registry → Execution and Evidence Plan → Experiment/Ablation/Evaluation Protocol → Phase Execution Playbook → accepted Method Selection → Nuts-and-Bolts → Implementation Build Book → execution evidence. The Layer 5 R7 document is a detailed-design realization and cannot unilaterally change a superior authority. This successor therefore distinguishes: (a) clarification already supported by the authority stack, (b) authority-specific synchronization text, (c) Registry/Protocol/Build Book/project-instance/consumer/empirical/claim matters that remain owner-gated, and (d) controlled reverse-impact packets for any future proven contradiction.

The R34 Plan successor does not add, remove, or reorder any Phase 5 step or gate. It binds the already-authoritative Phase 5 execution structure to the finalized R7 products, owners, failure modes, and consumers.

## 3. Exact Gate 5.1–5.11 minimum-evidence binding

| Gate | Surface | Minimum accepted evidence | Failure effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1 | Upstream completeness and immutability | Closed-world intake manifest, required sources, lifecycle/source hashes, branch capability and no upstream mutation. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.2 | Temporal order and identity | Bitemporal times, authoritative partial order, source/key completeness/idleness, reset/epoch and strict-predecessor evidence. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.3 | Split, cutoff and visibility legality | Split isolation, four-zone field visibility, descendant exclusion and no future/outcome leakage. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.4 | A5 action and trace integrity | Seven stored tokens, alias mapping, complete IHARQDecisionRecord/IHARQTraceRecord and immutable regime_aware=false source. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.5 | State/trust/warning schema and finite values | Full RegimeStateRecord profile, conditional TrustStateRecord predicate, warning linkage, canonical vocab and finite/configured values. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.6 | Matched A5/A7 comparison | Exact common support, identical required matching factors, source/config identities, support-flow and clustered pairing. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.7 | Negative controls and local variants | Predeclared dependency graph, applicable component availability, structure-preserving/burden-matched controls, seeds and invariant checks. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.8 | Metric dictionary and denominators | Approved entries, evidence-mode/denominator/independent unit/horizon/support/attrition and event-level timing definitions. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.9 | Negative-result visibility | SESOI/equivalence, harm/overconservatism/inconclusive/invalid zones, notes/flags and claim impact. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.10 | Layer 10 source readiness | Read-only source bundle, complete lineage, hashes, warnings, cards/export references and no hidden computation. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |
| 5.11 | Layer 0 claim safety and release | Proxy/simulation/nonclinical tags, forbidden wording checks, staged freeze facets, reviewers and controlled reopen. | affected facet remains blocked, diagnostic-only, or unready; no unrelated readiness inheritance |

Gate passage is facet-specific. A passed design check does not imply Registry, Build Book, project-instance, consumer, empirical, deployment, clinical, or claim readiness. Failure blocks or downgrades only the dependent facet; unrelated readiness is not inherited.

## 4. Canonical and interface closure imported from R35

1. `MatchedComparisonReport` is the canonical evaluation-report family. “A7 MatchedComparisonReport” is descriptive shorthand for a `MatchedComparisonReport` carrying A7 comparison/configuration identity; it is not a separate canonical family.
2. The `RegimeCard` source-lineage bundle is an **existing governed card-lineage/manifest bundle**. Layer 5 owns source preparation and lineage closure; Layer 10 consumes it read-only for rendering/export. This creates neither a new record family nor Layer 10 recomputation authority.
3. The governed boundary inventory contains ten semantic interfaces. Canonical names and normalized aliases describe one semantic object and must not be double-counted.
4. Conditional products use explicit `produced`, `empty-valid`, `inapplicable`, `blocked`, `diagnostic-only`, or `superseded` status; silent omission is invalid.
5. Physical field names, schemas, nullability, API classes, storage paths, package pins, and project-instance mappings remain Registry/Build Book owner-gated unless already accepted.

The Plan uses the ten governed interfaces exactly as normalized in the Registry successor, including `Layer 4/5 Evaluation Export Interface` and `Repository Promotion Interface`.

## 5. Evidence production and absence rules

Every required or conditional output must be represented by a produced artifact or an explicit `empty-valid`, `inapplicable`, `blocked`, `diagnostic-only`, or `superseded` status with owner, reason, affected scope, source/configuration identity, and gate consequence. Missing required evidence cannot be converted into implicit success. Negative, adverse, null, inconclusive, overconservative, invalid, baseline-sufficient, and unsupported results remain visible.

## 6. Reverse-impact and regeneration

A future Layer 5 finding may not silently repair or reinterpret an upstream authority or Layers 1–4 source. It must emit a versioned reverse-impact packet containing the affected proposition, exact evidence, impacted records/interfaces/steps/gates/ablations/consumers, migration and compatibility consequences, earliest invalidated dependency, proposed owner action, and closure test. Accepted corrections create immutable successors and trigger dependency-based invalidation/regeneration from the earliest changed authority input. Rejection preserves the current authority and leaves the affected Layer 5 branch blocked, downgraded, inapplicable, or diagnostic-only as appropriate.

## 7. Final Plan maturity

The finalized R7 design is sufficient for Implementation Build Book intake. It is not evidence that any project-instance Phase 5 gate has passed. Protocol values, physical schemas, executable adapters, live artifacts, consumer acceptance, empirical A7 results, and Layer 0 claim review remain separately required.

## 3. Gate-facet discipline

A gate result is valid only for its declared facet and evidence scope. Design conformance cannot be inherited as physical-schema approval, Protocol freeze, Build completion, project-instance passage, consumer acceptance, empirical success, deployment readiness or claim authorization. A failed facet blocks or downgrades only dependent products, but the failure and its denominator/support remain visible.

## 4. Upstream-to-Layer 5 intake and Layer 5-to-upstream return

The Plan sends Layer 5 exact objectives, products, owner assignments, gate evidence and stop conditions. Layer 5 returns produced artifacts or explicit absence/failure states, source/config closure, affected decision IDs, consumer handoffs and reverse-impact packets. The Plan owner decides whether an authority successor is needed; Layer 5 cannot self-edit the Plan through implementation convention.

## 5. Freeze and re-entry

Step 15 may declare only facet-specific closure. Any accepted Architecture, Registry, Protocol, Playbook, Method Selection or Layers 1-4 correction re-enters at the earliest affected Phase 5 step. All downstream artifacts are invalidated transitively and regenerated in topological order; historical results remain attributable to their original compatibility set.

## 4. Activation and reverse synchronization

The R3 proposals are promoted from `OWNER-READY` to `FINAL_APPLIED` at the documentary level by this resolution. The corresponding R7 reverse-synchronization rows become active for document references, logical profiles, readiness, handoffs, limitations, and open-gate status. They do **not** close a physical, numerical, implementation, empirical, consumer, or claim gate without its required evidence.

## 5. Rollback

If a later owner rejects a specific physical or numerical realization, only the affected realization/profile and its descendants are invalidated. The accepted documentary obligations and the unaffected R7 decisions/designs remain controlling. A method or algorithm may change only through an explicit controlled reopen.

## Acceptance, compatibility and rollback

The owner must accept, reject or revise each clause individually or as an explicitly enumerated package. Partial acceptance activates only the named clauses. Every acceptance record must identify the effective version, scope, compatibility set, migration, rollback, dependent Layer 10 sections and consumer acknowledgments. Rejection leaves the controlling predecessor in force and the affected Layer 10 product blocked or downgraded.
